The four apparently independent statements of the left column — universal $c$, no faster-than-$c$, motion at $c$ through spacetime, length contraction — collapse to a *single* foundational principle on the right column: $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the universal rate of the universe's fourth-dimension expansion. The McGucken Principle does not introduce a new structure; it *names* what the four-budget identity has been describing for over a century without an underlying physical mechanism.

The "everything moves at $c$ through spacetime" reading, which has been *hand-wavy* in the technical literature since Greene's popularisation in 1999 and structurally invisible in the constraint-imposition reading of every standard textbook since 1905, is *not* hand-wavy on the McGucken framework. It is the *direct kinematic content* of the universe being in motion: every event of $M_G$ participates in the $x_4$-expansion at rate $ic$; every object on $M_G$ inherits this motion via the master equation; every Lorentz contraction is a rotation of spatial extent into the moving fourth dimension; every time dilation is a reduction of the coordinate-frame projection of the universally-moving $x_4$-direction; every mass-shell condition is the four-budget identity applied to four-momentum.

The structural completion is what has been missing from the literature. The McGucken Principle supplies it. Every subsequent appearance of the four-budget identity in this book — in the master equation of Chapter 5, the geodesic equation of Chapter 6, the four-velocity normalisation of every Killing-vector argument, the photon's null condition, the Schwarzschild stationary-observer derivation, the FLRW Friedmann equations, the Kerr energy-extraction, and the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy — should be read with this structural content in mind: the identity is the algebraic record of the universe's fourth dimension being in motion at universal rate $ic$, with every object on $M_G$ inheriting this motion via its proper-time normalisation. *That* is why every object moves at $c$ through spacetime, neither more nor less, with the only freedom being how the universal-rate four-budget is partitioned between the temporal and spatial sectors.

### 1.4.1.6 The deeper meaning of $E = mc^2$

The four-budget reading delivers, as its final structural payoff, the *physical content* of the rest-energy identity $E = mc^2$ — the most famous equation in physics, and one whose conventional account has been as algebraically opaque as the four-budget itself.

The standard derivation [Einstein 1905b] obtains $E = mc^2$ by computing the kinetic energy of a body emitting electromagnetic radiation in two reference frames and equating the loss of mass with the loss of energy, divided by $c^2$. The derivation is algebraically clean and observationally vindicated to extraordinary precision (nuclear binding energies, particle-antiparticle annihilation, mass-energy conversion in accelerators), but it offers no answer to the structural question: *why is the rest energy of a body equal to its mass times the squared speed of light, rather than some other combination of mass and a universal constant?* The standard answer — "because $c^2$ is the conversion factor between mass and energy units imposed by the Lorentz-invariant structure of spacetime" — is once again a *constraint reading*: the answer names the conversion factor without supplying a *mechanism* for why this particular conversion factor.

The McGucken-framework reading supplies the mechanism. At spatial rest, the four-budget identity (B) of Lemma 11 above asserts that the body's entire four-velocity is directed along the $x_4$-axis: in the local Lorentz frame at the event, $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ with $|u^0| = c$ (the temporal component, encoding the rate of $x_4$-advance per unit proper time) and $|\vec u| = 0$ (zero spatial component). The body is moving at the magnitude $|u| = c$ through spacetime, with the entire four-speed budget allocated to the $x_4$-direction. The mass $m$ of the body is the inertial content of this motion (Theorem 5.3.4 of Chapter 5, where the operational definition of inertial mass is recovered from the $x_4$-component of four-momentum at spatial rest).

The structural derivation of $E = mc^2$ from the four-budget identity:

(i) The four-momentum is defined as $p^\mu = m u^\mu$ along a massive timelike worldline. At spatial rest in the local Lorentz frame, $p^\mu = (mc, 0, 0, 0)$.

(ii) The energy in the local Lorentz frame is the time-component of four-momentum scaled by $c$: $E = c p^0$. (This identification follows from the standard relativistic-mechanics correspondence $p^0 = E/c$, equivalently the time-translation Killing-vector projection of the four-momentum at the asymptotically flat reference frame; cf. Theorem 5.3.4 of Chapter 5.)

(iii) Substituting $p^0 = mc$ at spatial rest: $E = c \cdot mc = mc^2$.

The McGucken-framework structural reading of the factor $c^2$: the time-component $p^0 = mc$ at spatial rest carries one factor of $c$ from the universal rate of $x_4$-advance (the McGucken Principle setting $u^0 = c$ at rest), and the energy-from-time-component identification $E = cp^0$ carries the second factor of $c$ from the standard relativistic-mechanics convention. The product $c^2$ records the two independent appearances of the universal rate in the four-momentum-to-energy chain: once in the four-velocity normalisation set by the McGucken Principle (the four-budget identity (B)), once in the four-momentum-to-energy conversion of relativistic mechanics. The McGucken-framework structural account of why $E = mc^2$ rather than some other functional combination of $m$ and a universal constant: both factors of $c$ trace to the same physical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the universal rate of $x_4$-advance from every event of $M_G$.

The magnitude of $E = mc^2$ — small masses releasing enormous energies in fission and fusion, particle-antiparticle annihilation producing gamma-ray bursts, nuclear binding energies vastly exceeding chemical binding energies — is the empirical signature of the universal $x_4$-advance content carried by every massive object on $M_G$. The conversion of mass to released energy in nuclear processes is the liberation of this $x_4$-advance content from a bound configuration into propagating spatial-sector modes (photons, particles), with the total four-budget content $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ preserved at every step.

The McGucken-framework reading of $E = mc^2$ is a structural account of the algebraic result rather than a new derivation: Einstein's 1905b derivation remains algebraically valid and empirically vindicated. The structural content is that the rest energy of mass $m$ scales as $c^2$ because the four-momentum-to-energy chain carries two factors of $c$, both descending from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the four-budget identity (B). The McGucken Principle supplies the structural content that the standard textbook derivation leaves as an unexplained dimensional coincidence.

## 1.5 The Two Channels of the McGucken Duality

The wavefront of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ has $c$ as its rate of expansion and $\hbar$ as its action per oscillation. Two structurally disjoint readings of this single wavefront are available. The Algebraic Channel reads its algebra: $\hbar$ as the action quantum, $i$ as the perpendicularity marker, the operator structure $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ on the wavefunction phase under $\psi \mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi$. The Geometric Channel reads its geometry: the spherical wavefront $M^+_p(t)$ at every event, the Huygens-Fermat path-integral over arriving radii, the McGucken Sphere geometry of the $x_4$-expansion. The two channels share no named intermediate machinery on the five load-bearing pivots of \S5 — the structural disjointness $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$ that follows is the empirical signature of one wavefront generating both readings.

The McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ admits exactly two structurally distinct readings, both of which are *necessary* (the principle forces both) and *sufficient* (each derives the full content of GR alone).

### 1.5.1 Algebraic Channel: The Algebraic-Symmetry Reading

**Definition 7 (Algebraic Channel).** Algebraic Channel is the reading of $dx_4/dt = ic$ that asks: what transformations leave the principle invariant?* Since $x_4$ advances at the same rate $ic$ from every spacetime event, in every spatial direction, at every time, the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is invariant under:

- translations along $x_4$ itself: $x_4 \mapsto x_4 + a_4$ for $a_4 \in \mathbb{C}$;
- translations along $x_1, x_2, x_3$: $x_j \mapsto x_j + a_j$ for $a_j \in \mathbb{R}$ and $j = 1, 2, 3$;
- translations along $t$: $t \mapsto t + a_0$ for $a_0 \in \mathbb{R}$;
- rotations of the spatial three-coordinates: $x \mapsto Rx$ for $R \in \mathrm{SO}(3)$;
- Lorentz boosts: $(t, x) \mapsto \Lambda(t, x)$ for $\Lambda \in \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, automatic from the $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the integrated identity $x_4 = ict$ producing the Lorentzian signature on the constraint surface.

**Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$).** The combined invariance group of $dx_4/dt = ic$ acting on $M_G$ is the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^4 \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ at the four-dimensional level.

*Proof.* By items (i)--(iii) of Definition 7, the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is invariant under the four-dimensional translation subgroup $\mathbb{R}^4$. By items (iv) and (v), it is invariant under the proper orthochronous Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$. The Lorentzian signature on the constraint surface arises from the pullback of the holomorphic quadratic form $g_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ on the complexified cotangent bundle along the embedding $\iota: (t, x_1, x_2, x_3) \mapsto (x_1, x_2, x_3, ict)$, producing $\iota^* g_E = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2$ (Theorem 4(a)). The full derivation of the Poincaré invariance group as the *structural product* of $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the embedding $\iota$ appears in [7, §2.2, Theorem 12]. The structural-priority statement --- that $dx_4/dt = ic$ *generates* the Poincaré group rather than being a representation of it --- is the content of [4, Theorem 1], where the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is established as the *father symmetry* from which Lorentz, Poincaré, Noether, Wigner, gauge, quantum-unitary, CPT, diffeomorphism, and supersymmetry all descend as theorems. The semidirect-product structure $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3) = \mathbb{R}^4 \rtimes \mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ follows from the standard composition of translations with Lorentz transformations [42]. $\square$

**Theorem 9 (Factorisation of Diff(M) via McGucken, imported from [2, §3]).** Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance of the gravitational action is factored by $dx_4/dt = ic$ into two physically distinct structural components:
(a) A kinematic symmetry: $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$-invariance of the matter action, where $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is the foliation-preserving subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ generated by vector fields $\xi^\mu = (\xi^0(x^0), \xi^i(x^0, x^j))$ with $\xi^0$ depending only on the time coordinate $x^0$.
(b) A constitutive identity: $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ enforced pointwise on every massive worldline.
Off shell, only $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ acts as a symmetry. On shell --- given the matter equations of motion --- the full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ is recovered, and the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4)\, T_{\mu\nu}$ follow from Lovelock uniqueness plus Newtonian matching.
*Proof of Theorem 9.* We follow the structure of [2, §3], expanding each step.

**Step 1 (the subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$).** The McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ fixes the rate of $x_4$-advance to $ic$ at every point of $M_G$. Under a diffeomorphism $\phi: M_G \to M_G$ generated by a vector field $\xi^\mu$, the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ requires $dx_4/dt = ic$ to be invariant. The constraint is that $\xi^0$ cannot depend on the spatial coordinates $x^j$ in a way that varies the rate at different points of the same spatial slice; otherwise the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ would be broken because $dx_4/dt$ would acquire spatial dependence. Hence $\partial \xi^0/\partial x^j = 0$ for $j = 1, 2, 3$, i.e., $\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)$ only. The spatial components $\xi^j$ are unconstrained because the spatial sector is deformable (Definition 5(b)). The vector field is therefore of the form $\xi^\mu = (\xi^0(x^0), \xi^j(x^0, x^k))$, which defines $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$.

**Lemma 9.1.** $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is a strict subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$.

*Proof of Lemma 9.1.* The general vector field on $M_G$ has $\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0, x^i)$ depending on all coordinates. Restricting $\xi^0$ to depend only on $x^0$ yields a strict subgroup, since vector fields with $\partial \xi^0/\partial x^j \neq 0$ are not in the McGucken subgroup. $\square$

**Step 2 (the constitutive identity).** By the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, every massive particle's worldline $x^\mu(\tau)$ on $M_G$ has $dx_4/dt = ic$. Parametrising by proper time $\tau$ via $d\tau^2 = -c^{-2} g_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu$, the four-velocity is $u^\mu = dx^\mu/d\tau$. The four-velocity budget identity
$$u^\mu u_\mu = g_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = -c^2$$
follows directly from the definition of $\tau$: indeed $g_{\mu\nu} u^\mu u^\nu = (dx^\mu dx_\mu)/d\tau^2 = -c^2$. The stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid of such particles is
$$T^{\mu\nu} = (\rho c^2 + p) \frac{u^\mu u^\nu}{c^2} + p\, g^{\mu\nu}, \tag{T}$$
with the constraint $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ enforced pointwise.

**Step 3 (Noether's second theorem applied to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$).** Apply Noether's second theorem [34, ref. 37] to the matter action $S_M[\phi, g_{\mu\nu}]$ invariant under $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$. Noether's second theorem is here the standard variational result applied to framework-derived inputs: the McGucken Lagrangian (Lemma 1 plus the derived least-action structure), the $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-symmetry, and the $+ic$ foliation all descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ ([2, Theorem 30$'$]; precise status in Remark 10.3.1.1). The variational theorem itself is general calculus of variations --- a tool, not re-derived from the Principle; what the Principle supplies are its inputs. Therefore the Algebraic Channel rests on no *physical* input external to $dx_4/dt = ic$ for this step.

The conserved currents associated with $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariance are *weaker* than those of full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ because the symmetry group is smaller. Specifically: (S) spatial diffeomorphism invariance ($\xi^j$ unconstrained, $\xi^0 = 0$) yields the spatial conservation law $\nabla_i T^{i\nu} = 0$ on each spatial slice $\Sigma_t$; (T-int) time-reparametrisation invariance ($\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)$, $\xi^j = 0$) yields the integrated time-conservation $\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\Sigma_t} T^{0\nu} \sqrt{h}\, d^3 x = 0$. The local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ in *all* four directions is *not* given by $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ alone because $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ is a strict subgroup (Lemma 9.1).

**Step 4 (on-shell enhancement).** Claim: given the matter equations of motion (relativistic energy equation and Euler equation) together with the constitutive identity (Step 2), the local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ holds in all four directions.

*Proof of the on-shell enhancement.* The perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor (T) gives, upon differentiation,
$$\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; \nabla_\mu\!\left[(\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\right] u^\nu \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\,\nabla_\mu u^\nu \;+\; g^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p. \tag{$\dagger$}$$

*Timelike projection.* Contract ($\dagger$) with $u_\nu$ and apply the constitutive identity $u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2$ together with its consequence $u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu = 0$ (from differentiating $u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2$, a constant on the constraint surface):
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[(\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\right] \;+\; 0 \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.$$
Expanding the first term:
$$-c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[\frac{(\rho c^2 + p) u^\mu}{c^2}\right] \;=\; -\nabla_\mu[(\rho c^2 + p) u^\mu] \;=\; -(\rho c^2 + p) \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;-\; c^2 u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho \;-\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.$$
Combining:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -(\rho c^2 + p) \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;-\; c^2 u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho.$$
Setting this to zero gives the *relativistic energy equation* (the perfect-fluid matter EOM for energy conservation along the flow):
$$u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho \;+\; (\rho + p/c^2)\, \nabla_\mu u^\mu \;=\; 0. \tag{Energy-EOM}$$
The timelike projection $u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ is therefore equivalent to the perfect-fluid energy equation, which is one of the matter EOMs.

*Spatial projection.* Project ($\dagger$) orthogonal to $u^\nu$ using the spatial projector $h^\nu_\lambda = \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda/c^2$ (with $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0$ and $h^\nu_\lambda h^\lambda_\sigma = h^\nu_\sigma$):
$$h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; (\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\,(h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda) \;+\; h^{\nu\mu} \partial_\mu p,$$
where the first term of ($\dagger$) drops out under the spatial projection because $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0$, and the third term contracts to $h^{\nu\mu}\partial_\mu p$ via $h^\nu_\lambda g^{\lambda\mu} = h^{\nu\mu}$. Setting this to zero gives the *relativistic Euler equation* (the perfect-fluid matter EOM for spatial momentum):
$$(\rho c^2 + p)\,\frac{u^\mu}{c^2}\, \nabla_\mu u^\nu \;=\; -h^{\nu\mu} \partial_\mu p, \tag{Euler-EOM}$$
where the projection $h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda \equiv \nabla_\mu u^\nu$ on the spatial subspace (using $u_\lambda \nabla_\mu u^\lambda = 0$) eliminates the redundant temporal component. The spatial projection $h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} = 0$ is therefore equivalent to the relativistic Euler equation.

*Span and conclusion.* The timelike-projector $-u^\nu u^\lambda/c^2$ and the spatial-projector $h^\nu_\lambda = \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda/c^2$ together span the full tangent space at every event:
$$-\frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; h^\nu_\lambda \;=\; -\frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; \delta^\nu_\lambda \;+\; \frac{u^\nu u_\lambda}{c^2} \;=\; \delta^\nu_\lambda.$$
Hence the vanishing of $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ on both subspaces implies $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ identically. On shell — given the relativistic energy equation (Energy-EOM) and the relativistic Euler equation (Euler-EOM) as the perfect-fluid matter EOMs — the local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ holds in all four directions. The matter action becomes invariant under arbitrary diffeomorphisms acting consistently on metric and matter, recovering the full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ on-shell. $\square$ (end of Step 4)

*Step 5 (Einstein field equations from Lovelock).** With $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ established, the geometric side of the field equations is forced by Lovelock's theorem [57, ref. 32]: *in four dimensions, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor built from the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and its first two derivatives, linear in second derivatives, is
$$L_{\mu\nu} = \alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} + \beta\, g_{\mu\nu}, \tag{Lovelock}$$
where $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g_{\mu\nu}$ is the Einstein tensor and $\alpha, \beta$ are constants. The structural priority of Lovelock as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ operates through the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6): the McGucken-Invariance Lemma restricts the allowed geometric structure to one in which $g_{\mu\nu}$ is the *deformable-sector* variable (spatial sector) coupled to matter through the universal Sphere geometry; the Lovelock uniqueness then applies to the divergence-free combinations on the four-dimensional manifold $M_G$. Setting $L_{\mu\nu} = \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}$ with $\kappa = 8\pi G/c^4$ and $\beta = \Lambda$ gives
$$G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{Einstein field equations}$$

The tag (the Einstein field equations) is the standard abbreviation for the Einstein Field Equations: the foundational dynamical equations of general relativity, relating the geometric curvature of spacetime (encoded in the Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu}$ and cosmological-constant term $\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}$ on the left) to the matter-energy content (encoded in the stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ on the right). They are GR T11 of the book's 24-theorem gravitational chain.
**Step 6 (Newtonian matching fixes $\kappa$).** In the weak-field static limit $g_{00} = -(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)$, $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$, the dominant component of (the Einstein field equations) at $00$ reduces to Poisson's equation $\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G \rho$. The coupling constant $\kappa = 8\pi G/c^4$ is forced by this matching. $\square$ (end of Theorem 9)

**Corollary 9.2.** The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations rests on no mathematical input external to $dx_4/dt = ic$ and Lovelock's theorem, plus the Newtonian matching condition fixing the coupling constant. The factorisation (a) of Theorem 9 (Diff-invariance) and (b) (constitutive identity) are both direct theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Noether's second theorem, used in Step 3, operates on framework-derived inputs --- which descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via [2, Theorem 30$'$], with the precise status stated in Remark 10.3.1.1 (the theorem itself is a standard variational tool, not re-derived from the Principle). The structural meaning is that the McGucken Principle is strictly stronger than Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance: the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ determines which diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$) and explains why the full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ is recovered on shell (because the four-velocity budget is consistent with arbitrary reparametrisation of the worldline).

The Algebraic Channel is the *invariance-group content* of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Through Noether's theorem (itself a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ per [4]), every continuous symmetry generates a conservation law: energy ($t$-translation), momentum (spatial translation), angular momentum (spatial rotation), four-momentum (Lorentz), stress-energy conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ (the on-shell enhancement of $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariance). The Algebraic Channel operates uniformly in Lorentzian signature; the structural reason established in [2, §5] is that the imaginary unit $i$ is *interior* to the unitary representations $\exp(-isp/\hbar)$, $\exp(-iHt/\hbar)$ and cannot be exteriorised without dissolving the algebraic content.

### 1.5.2 Geometric Channel: The Geometric-Propagation Reading

**Definition 10 (Geometric Channel).** Geometric Channel is the reading of $dx_4/dt = ic$ that asks: what does the principle generate when applied at every spacetime event?* The McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ of Definition 2 is the wavefront generated by $dx_4/dt = ic$ at $p$; by Proposition 3, every point of $M^+_p(t)$ is itself a source of a new McGucken Sphere; iterating this construction generates Huygens' Principle and the iterated-sphere path structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on $M_G$. Formally, Geometric Channel is the wavefront-functor $p \mapsto M^+_p(\cdot)$ of Definition 2, together with its iterated composition $M^+_p(\cdot) \circ M^+_q(\cdot)$ for $q \in M^+_p(\cdot)$ as in Proposition 3.

The Geometric Channel is the *wavefront content* of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations proceeds through four self-contained theorems, each derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$, culminating in the same equation (the Einstein field equations) that the Algebraic Channel produces. We state each as a numbered theorem with a complete proof.

**Theorem 11 (Geometric Second Law).** Given the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of any ensemble of $N$ particles is strictly monotonically increasing in coordinate time:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{3}{2}\, \frac{k_B}{t} > 0 \qquad \text{for all } t > 0.$$
*The monotonicity is exact, not statistical, and there is no Poincaré recurrence.

*Proof.* The proof proceeds in four steps from $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the strict monotonicity; the integrated form $x_4 = ict$ plays no role in the derivation.

*Step 1 (kinematic content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ projected onto the spatial slice).* By the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, $x_4$ advances at rate $ic$ from every spacetime event $p \in M_G$ in a spherically symmetric manner. Projecting this 4-dimensional spherical expansion onto the spatial three-slice at each event produces the McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ of radius $c\, \delta t$ about that event for any infinitesimal time interval $\delta t$ (Definition 2). Each particle in the ensemble is therefore displaced by $c\, \delta t$ in a direction $\hat{n}$ drawn from the uniform measure on $S^2$ at every Planck-time step $\delta t_p = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^5}$ (the fundamental time scale at which $x_4$ advances by one Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ [3, 4]).

*Step 2 (diffusion equation from isotropic step).* The probability density $P(\vec{r}, t)$ of a particle position evolves under iterated isotropic displacements with rms step size $c\, \delta t_p$ per step. The isotropy of each step is not an assumption but a consequence of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii) (Spherical symmetry): the $x_4$-expansion is spherically symmetric from every event, so the projected displacement direction $\hat n$ is drawn from the uniform measure on $S^2$ with no preferred spatial direction. The standard derivation of Brownian motion from isotropic random walks [41, Chandrasekhar 1943] --- here serving only as the computational lemma that turns the Principle-supplied isotropic step into a diffusion law --- applied with step size $c\, \delta t_p$ and step time $\delta t_p$ gives the diffusion coefficient
$$D = \frac{(c\, \delta t_p)^2}{6\, \delta t_p} = \frac{c^2\, \delta t_p}{6}$$
and the probability density satisfies the isotropic diffusion equation
$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} = D\, \nabla^2 P. \tag{Diff}$$

*Step 3 (Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of the Gaussian solution).* The fundamental solution of (Diff) with delta-function initial data $P(\vec{r}, 0) = \delta^3(\vec{r})$ is the Gaussian $P(\vec{r}, t) = (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\, \exp(-r^2/(4Dt))$. Direct evaluation of the Boltzmann--Gibbs differential entropy $S(t) = -k_B \int P \ln P\, d^3 r$ on this Gaussian gives
$$S(t) = \frac{3}{2}\, k_B \ln(4 \pi e D t) + \text{const}.$$

*Step 4 (strict monotonicity).* Differentiating with respect to $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{3}{2}\, \frac{k_B}{t} > 0 \qquad \text{for all } t > 0.$$
The monotonicity is *exact*, not statistical, because $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies the $+ic$ orientation (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (iii)): $x_4$ advances and does not retreat, so (Diff) propagates probability density forward in $t$ with no time-reversed branch in the physical dynamics. The textbook statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to this strict geometric Second Law when the $+ic$-oriented physical motion underlying the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is recognised. There is no Poincaré recurrence because $x_4$ does not recur. $\square$

**Theorem 12 (Bekenstein--Hawking area law from $x_4$-mode counting).** Given the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the identification of the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ as the fundamental $x_4$-advance wavelength, the entropy associated with a McGucken Sphere of area $A$ is
$$S = k_B\, \frac{A}{4 \ell_P^2} = k_B\, \frac{A c^3}{4 \hbar G}.$$

*Proof.* By the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the fourth dimension expands at rate $ic$ from every spacetime event. Quantising this expansion at the Planck scale, the fundamental wavelength of $x_4$-advance is $\ell_P$. The number of independent quantum modes of $x_4$-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere of area $A$ is one mode per Planck-area cell:
$$N_{\text{modes}} = \frac{A}{\ell_P^2}.$$
Identifying entropy with $k_B$ times the number of modes (one bit per mode): $S = k_B A/\ell_P^2$. This mode-counting argument fixes the *form* of the area law --- entropy proportional to horizon area in Planck units --- but not its numerical coefficient. The coefficient is $1/4$, and it is *derived* as an output of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at Theorem 15.4.3 of Chapter 15: the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost at the horizon supplies the Hawking temperature $T_H$ (Theorem 15.4.2), and integrating the first law $dE = T_H\, dS$ with the boundary condition $S(0) = 0$ yields $S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$, the factor $\tfrac14$ arising from the $\tfrac12$ of $\int M\,dM$ against the geometric factors carried by $r_s = 2GM/c^2$. No Bekenstein--Hawking input is used at any step (Remark 15.4.3.1). The present theorem therefore delivers the area law's form; Theorem 15.4.3 delivers its coefficient, and together they constitute GR T20. $\square$

**Theorem 13 (Unruh temperature from Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost).** Given the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and Theorem 4 (McGucken--Wick rotation), a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration $a$ experiences a temperature
$$T_U = \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B}.$$

*Proof.* This is part (c) of Theorem 4, restated as a standalone Geometric Channel input. The Wick rotation $t \mapsto -i\tau$ with $\tau = x_4/c$ (Theorem 4) converts the Lorentz boost in $(x, t)$ to a Euclidean rotation in $(x, x_4)$. Single-valuedness of the rotation on the Euclidean section requires period $2\pi$ in the Euclidean angle, giving $\Delta \tau_p = 2\pi c / a$. The KMS identification of imaginary-time period $\beta$ with inverse temperature $T^{-1}$ via $\hbar \beta c = \Delta \tau_p$ yields $T_U = \hbar/(k_B \beta) = \hbar a/(2 \pi c\, k_B)$. The KMS periodicity invoked here is not a bare external assumption: it is the $2\pi$-periodicity of the Euclidean $x_4$-circle traced by the accelerated worldline under the McGucken--Wick rotation (Theorem 4(c)), i.e. itself a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ read on the Euclidean section. It is listed among the thirty-four quantum-field-theoretic inputs that the Wick-rotation paper [3] derives as theorems of the Principle (cf. Theorem 15). It is taken as a standing input of the Geometric Channel here, alongside the Clausius relation, only in the sense that its full derivation is carried in [3] rather than repeated. $\square$

**Theorem 14 (Geometric Channel output: the Einstein field equations).** Given the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, Theorems 11--13, the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\, dS$, and the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences, the Einstein field equations
$$G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} = \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}$$
*hold at every spacetime point.*

*Proof.* The argument is Jacobson's 1995 thermodynamic derivation [37], applied to a local Rindler horizon at every spacetime event $p \in M_G$ and underwritten by the McGucken-framework Geometric Channel inputs (Theorems 11--13). The local Rindler horizon is not an external scaffold imposed on the manifold: by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii), $x_4$ expands spherically at rate $c$ from every event, and the null surface this expansion sweeps out is the McGucken Sphere's null cone (Definition 2); the local Rindler horizon through $p$ is precisely a patch of that Principle-generated null structure as seen by a uniformly accelerated observer. Consider an arbitrary spacetime point $p$ and a local Rindler horizon $H$ through $p$: a null hypersurface generated by a null congruence with affine parameter $\lambda$ and tangent vector $k^\mu$. The horizon is the boundary of the past of a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration $a$ in the local neighbourhood of $p$. The Rindler horizon-generating Killing vector $\chi^\mu$ is parallel to $k^\mu$ on $H$, with $\chi^\mu = -a\lambda\, k^\mu$ in the affine parametrisation [37, eq. (1)] — the Rindler-Killing-vector affine-parameter relation that supplies the factor of $a$ canceling against the Unruh temperature.

*Step 1 (heat flux through $H$).* The heat flux carried across $H$ by matter, defined as the boost-energy flux past the Rindler observer, is
$$\delta Q \;=\; \int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \chi^\mu\, d\Sigma^\nu \;=\; -\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, (a\lambda)\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA, \tag{Q-flux}$$
where $d\Sigma^\nu = k^\nu d\lambda dA$ is the null-congruence area-element-times-affine-parameter measure, and the minus sign comes from $\chi^\mu = -a\lambda k^\mu$.

*Step 2 (entropy change from the area law).* By Theorem 12, the entropy associated with the horizon $H$ at any cross-section is $S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$. The differential entropy change for an area variation $\delta A$ is
$$\delta S \;=\; \frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2}\, \delta A. \tag{S-area}$$
On a null congruence, the area variation along the congruence at parameter $\lambda$ relates to the expansion $\theta$ via $d(\delta A)/d\lambda = \theta\, \delta A$, equivalently $\delta A = -\int (d\theta/d\lambda) \lambda\, d\lambda\, dA$ in the focusing limit (Step 3 below).

*Step 3 (area change from Raychaudhuri).* The Raychaudhuri equation for the null congruence generating $H$ is
$$\frac{d\theta}{d\lambda} \;=\; -\tfrac{1}{2}\theta^2 \;-\; \sigma_{\mu\nu}\sigma^{\mu\nu} \;-\; R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu,$$
where $\theta$ is the expansion, $\sigma_{\mu\nu}$ the shear, and $R_{\mu\nu}$ the Ricci tensor. At the chosen event $p$ (with $\theta(0) = 0$ and $\sigma(0) = 0$ for the locally-stationary horizon), the leading-order behaviour is $d\theta/d\lambda = -R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$. The integrated area change up to affine parameter $\lambda$:
$$\delta A(\lambda) \;=\; \int_0^\lambda \theta(\lambda')\, dA\, d\lambda' \;=\; -\int_0^\lambda \lambda'\, R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu\, dA\, d\lambda', \tag{Ray}$$
where the second equality uses $\theta(\lambda) = \int_0^\lambda (d\theta/d\lambda')d\lambda' = -\lambda R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$ at leading order.

*Step 4 (Clausius relation).* Equate $\delta Q = T_U\, \delta S$ with $T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$ from Theorem 13. Substituting from (Q-flux), (S-area), and (Ray):
$$-\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, (a\lambda)\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c\, k_B} \cdot \frac{k_B}{4\ell_P^2} \cdot \left(-\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\right).$$
The factor $a$ on each side cancels; the factor $\lambda$ inside each integral cancels; the minus sign on each side cancels:
$$\int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{8\pi c\, \ell_P^2} \int_H R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA.$$
Using $\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3$:
$$\frac{\hbar}{8\pi c \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{\hbar c^3}{8\pi c \hbar G} \;=\; \frac{c^2}{8\pi G}.$$
But $T_{\mu\nu}$ has units of energy density and the integration $d\lambda\, dA$ has units of length × area = volume, while $R_{\mu\nu}$ has units of inverse area. For dimensional consistency on the contraction with null $k^\mu$ (which are dimensionless tangent vectors on the affine null congruence), the equality reads:
$$T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \quad \text{for all null } k^\mu, \tag{14.1}$$
with the remaining factor of $c^2$ coming from the unit-conversion between the energy-flux measure (which intrinsically carries $c$ from the relativistic $T_{\mu\nu}$ definition) and the inverse-area Ricci measure.

*Step 5 (conclusion: all null vectors → tensor identity).* Equation (14.1) holds for *every* null vector $k^\mu$ at *every* spacetime point. The Newman-Penrose-type completeness of null vectors in the tangent space, together with the symmetry of both $T_{\mu\nu}$ and $R_{\mu\nu}$, forces
$$T_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8\pi G}\bigl( R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R\, g_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \bigr),$$
where:
- the trace term $-\tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ is forced by the requirement $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (from Step 4 of Theorem 9, the on-shell enhancement), which by the contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ singles out the Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2}Rg_{\mu\nu}$ over the bare Ricci tensor;
- the cosmological-constant term $+\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}$ enters as an integration constant (allowed because $\nabla^\mu g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ identically).

Rearranging the conclusion gives (the Einstein field equations). $\square$

The Geometric Channel is *bi-signature*: it admits a Lorentzian reading (with oscillating phase weight $\exp(iS/\hbar)$ producing the Feynman path integral) and a Euclidean reading (with real positive measure weight $\exp(-S_E/\hbar)$ producing the Wiener process and horizon thermodynamics). The two are related by the McGucken--Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ of Theorem 4. ### 1.5.3 The Signature-Bridging Theorem

**Theorem 15 (Signature-Bridging Theorem, [2, Theorem 5.1]).** Let $\mathrm{SIG}_L$ denote the Lorentzian metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $\mathrm{SIG}_E$ the Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$. The McGucken--Wick rotation $t \mapsto -i\tau$ with $\tau = x_4/c$ (Theorem 4) is the unique coordinate identification on the real four-dimensional McGucken manifold that:
*(i) is induced by a single physical principle (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$);*

*(ii) maps Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures onto one another;*

(iii) preserves the physical content of $x_4$-expansion (the rate $c$ is invariant under the identification);
(iv) supports two independent derivations of $G_{\mu\nu}$ --- Algebraic Channel in $\mathrm{SIG}_L$ and the Geometric Channel in $\mathrm{SIG}_E$ --- that yield identical field equations.
Properties (i)--(iv) are jointly satisfied by no other coordinate identification known to physics. The standard Wick rotation of quantum field theory [56] is the formal shadow of (i)--(iv) when the physical reality of $x_4$ is suppressed.
*Proof.* Property (i) is the content of Theorem 4: the rotation arises from integrating the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ under the source-origin convention. Property (ii) is Theorem 4(a): the pullback $\iota^* g_E$ produces the Lorentzian line element on the constraint surface, and the substitution $t = -i\tau$ converts it to the Euclidean form. Property (iii) follows from the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6): the rate $c$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ does not depend on the metric, hence is preserved under the coordinate change. Property (iv) is the content of Theorem 9 (Algebraic Channel) and Theorem 14 (Geometric Channel): both derivations yield the same (the Einstein field equations).

Uniqueness: suppose $\phi: t \mapsto f(t, x)$ is another coordinate identification with properties (i)--(iv), with $\phi$ outputting the Euclidean coordinate $\tau$. Then $\phi$ must be induced by $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone (property (i)), preserve the rate $c$ (property (iii)), and map Lorentzian to Euclidean signature (property (ii)). Since $\tau = x_4/c$ by the choice of Euclidean coordinate (Theorem 4), and $dx_4/dt = ic$ on $M_G$ by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the differential of $\phi$ is fixed:
$$\frac{d\phi}{dt} \;=\; \frac{1}{c}\frac{dx_4}{dt} \;=\; \frac{1}{c} \cdot ic \;=\; i.$$
With the source-origin boundary condition $\phi(0) = 0$, integrating gives $\phi(t) = it = \tau$, equivalently $t = -i\tau$ — the McGucken-Wick rotation. Hence the identification is unique. $\square$

The Wick-rotation paper [3] establishes that thirty-four independent inputs of quantum field theory, QM, and symmetry physics --- including the Wick substitution itself, the convergence of the Euclidean path integral, the $+i\epsilon$ prescription, the Schrödinger-to-diffusion correspondence, Osterwalder--Schrader reflection positivity, the KMS condition, Gibbons--Hawking horizon regularity, the Hawking temperature, the Matsubara formalism, the canonical commutator $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$, the path-integral weight $e^{iS/\hbar}$, the Minkowski--Euclidean action bridge $iS_M = -S_E$, the U(1) gauge phase, the Dirac spinor structure, and the Born rule $P = |\psi|^2$ --- descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as theorems.

#### 1.5.3.1 The Wick Rotation as a Theorem of the McGucken Principle {#sec:channels-wick}

Both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is itself a theorem of the principle (Theorem 4). The principle contains the imaginary unit; the coordinate identification $x_4 = ict$ is already the Wick-rotated coordinate, with $i$ absorbed into the relationship between $x_4$ and the real time $t$. Integration of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along any worldline (null, timelike, spacelike) produces $x_4 = ic(t - t_0)$, with the imaginary unit appearing as a structural feature of the integration rather than as a separate analytic-continuation procedure.

### Are the Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel derivations of a given theorem related by a Wick rotation?

A natural reading of the dual-channel architecture is to ask whether the two derivations of a given theorem are *Wick rotations of each other* --- whether applying the Wick rotation to the Algebraic Channel derivation produces the corresponding Geometric Channel derivation, or vice versa. The answer is no, and the reasons are worth stating directly.

Applying the Wick rotation to the Algebraic Channel derivation produces a Wick-rotated Algebraic Channel derivation. The Algebraic Channel reasons through symmetry-group arguments --- the Lorentz and Poincaré groups, the action functional, the Euler-Lagrange equations, Noether's theorems, Lovelock uniqueness, operator algebra with canonical commutators. Wick-rotating the Algebraic Channel argument changes the signature of the metric, the form of the action functional, and the phase of the path integral, but it does not change the *mode of reasoning*. The argument is still algebraic-symmetry reasoning; it is just operating in Euclidean signature now.

Applying the Wick rotation to the Geometric Channel derivation produces a Wick-rotated Geometric Channel derivation. The Geometric Channel reasons through iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation, Huygens construction, mode-counting on the Sphere surface, Brownian-motion diffusion, Compton-phase rotation along $x_4$. The McGucken Sphere as a 2-surface with radius $c(t - t_0)$ and the iterated-Sphere flow at universal rate $c$ are signature-invariant geometric objects: the Sphere is the same Sphere whether one labels the time axis $t$ (Lorentzian) or $\tau = x_4/c$ (Euclidean). Wick-rotating the Geometric Channel argument transforms the time label but leaves the iterated-Sphere geometric content invariant.

The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations (Lovelock uniqueness from action variation, Algebraic Channel) and the Geometric Channel derivation (Jacobson's thermodynamic chain on the McGucken Sphere horizon, Geometric Channel) share no intermediate machinery. The Geometric Channel derivation uses the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$, the Bekenstein--Hawking area law $S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ as $x_4$-mode counting on the horizon sphere, the Unruh temperature $T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$ as the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost periodicity, and the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T_U \delta S$ integrated through the Raychaudhuri equation on a local Rindler horizon. None of these objects appears in the Algebraic Channel Lovelock-uniqueness derivation. The two derivations are *structurally disjoint* at the level of intermediate machinery --- the structural disjointness (dual-channel-disjoint) signature recorded in [1, Part VII]. The Wick rotation, applied to either derivation, does not produce the other.

What relates the two derivations is *common descent from the principle*. Both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel trace back to $dx_4/dt = ic$. The cross-channel agreement on the same observable theorem (here: the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$) follows from both channels deriving from the same principle, with no Wick-rotational relationship between the two derivation chains themselves.

### Where the Wick rotation does enter

The Wick rotation enters the framework at four distinct structural levels:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *As a theorem of the principle (Theorem 4)*. The Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is derivable from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the imaginary-unit content of the rate. It is built into the integration of the principle, with no need to be postulated as an external analytic-continuation device.

\item *Used internally by the Algebraic Channel during its own derivations*. The Algebraic Channel derivation of the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy uses the Gibbons--Hawking--York Euclidean Schwarzschild action --- a Wick rotation applied within the Algebraic Channel argument to make the partition-function-periodicity computation work. The Algebraic Channel is not strictly Lorentzian; it Wick-rotates internally when the algebraic argument requires Euclidean signature.

\item *Used internally by the Geometric Channel during its own derivations*. The Geometric Channel derivation of the Geometric Second Law uses the Wick-rotated Brownian-motion diffusion equation, with $x_4 \to ic\tau_E$ converting the iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation into a heat-equation reading on the deformable spatial sector. The Geometric Channel is not strictly Euclidean either; it Wick-rotates internally when the geometric argument requires Lorentzian signature for the wavefront reading.

\item *As the differential diagnostic between the two channels*. The Algebraic Channel objects (the algebraic content of the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, the Schrödinger time-derivative $i\hbar\partial_t$, the path-integral phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$) are signature-specific: they transform under the Wick rotation ($-c^2 \to +c^2$, $i\hbar\partial_t \to -\hbar\partial_\tau$, $e^{iS/\hbar} \to e^{-S_E/\hbar}$). The Geometric Channel objects (the McGucken Sphere as a 2-surface, the iterated-Sphere flow at universal $c$, the Sphere-mode count, the wavefront propagation) are signature-invariant. This is the QM corpus result [3, Theorem on Channel--Wick Asymmetry]: the Wick rotation acts as a structural diagnostic by transforming Algebraic Channel content while preserving Geometric Channel content.
\end{enumerate}

The first three are *uses* of the Wick rotation within or by the principle. The fourth is the differential response of the two channels' content under the rotation. None of the four is the standard "Wick-rotate Algebraic Channel to get Geometric Channel" relationship that the bridge framing would suggest, because that relationship does not hold: the two derivation chains are structurally disjoint at the level of their intermediate machinery, and the Wick rotation does not bridge between them.

### How each channel absorbs the imaginary unit

The two channels exploit the same dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- whose mere integrated coordinate shadow is the static identity $x_4 = ict$ --- through different absorptions of the imaginary unit:

- *Algebraic Channel* absorbs $i$ into the metric signature and operator coefficients: the Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$, the canonical commutator $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$, the Schrödinger time-derivative $i\hbar\partial_t$, the path-integral phase $e^{iS/\hbar}$.

- *Geometric Channel* absorbs $i$ into the rate of the fourth-dimension expansion: $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the active rate, the iterated-Sphere wavefront propagation at universal $c$, the Compton phase $\Phi = \exp(-imc^2\Delta\tau/\hbar)$ along worldlines.

Both readings produce the same observable predictions because both descend from the same principle.

### What is characteristic of each channel

**Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry reading):**
The Algebraic Channel reads the integrated shadow $x_4 = ict$ of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a coordinate label and derives theorems from the symmetry group of the label. The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, the Poincaré group $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$, the diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ and its factorisation, Noether's theorems, Lovelock's uniqueness, variational principles with action functionals, operator algebra with canonical commutators. The master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ in its Lorentzian-signature form is the standard Algebraic Channel reading; the Wick-rotated Euclidean form $|u^\mu|^2_E = +c^2$ is also the Algebraic Channel object, used internally when the partition-function argument requires Euclidean signature. The defining feature is the *mode of reasoning*: symmetry-group arguments with algebraic operations on tensor fields.

**Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation reading):**
The Geometric Channel reads $dx_4/dt = ic$ as an active wavefront expansion and derives theorems from the iterated-Sphere flow. The McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ as a 2-surface in 3-space with radius $c(t-t_0)$ centred at the source apex, Huygens-Feynman wavefront construction, Compton-phase uniformity $\Phi(q;p) = \exp(-i m c^2 \Delta\tau/\hbar)$ on the Sphere, proper-time integrals $\Delta\tau = \int dt' \sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ along worldlines, the iterated-Sphere composition of the Feynman path integral, the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy via mode-counting on the horizon Sphere. The defining feature is the *mode of reasoning*: geometric-propagation arguments with wavefront content on a 2-surface.

The Algebraic Channel/Geometric Channel distinction is *not* the Lorentzian/Euclidean distinction; both channels operate in either signature as the internal argument requires. The distinction is between *algebraic-symmetry reasoning on a coordinate label* and *geometric-propagation reasoning on an active wavefront*. These are different modes of reasoning, not different signature conventions.

### What each channel can and cannot derive alone

**Algebraic Channel alone** can derive every theorem of GR that depends on the symmetry-group structure (Einstein field equations via Lovelock, geodesic equation via variational principle, Killing-vector conserved quantities, Lorentz invariance of $c$ at the level of the metric, light cone causal structure). The Algebraic Channel cannot directly visualise what is dynamically active in the fourth dimension. It presents the metric signature as a given, the four-velocity normalisation as a constraint, and the imaginary unit $i$ as appearing in specific formulas without supplying a geometric content.

**Geometric Channel alone** can derive the iterated-Sphere structure of wave propagation, the Huygens-Feynman path-integral composition, the wavefront-realist reading of quantum mechanics, the geometric content of the active fourth-dimension expansion, the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy via mode-counting on the horizon Sphere, the Jacobson thermodynamic derivation of the Einstein field equations. The Geometric Channel cannot directly produce the operator-algebra structure of quantum field theory (canonical commutators, raising and lowering operators, S-matrix elements) without invoking Algebraic Channel reading at specific points.

**Together**, the two channels supply the complete dual-channel architecture: Algebraic Channel delivers the algebraic-symmetry content underlying GR and QM; Geometric Channel delivers the geometric-propagation content underlying the same theorems; the cross-channel agreement on observables (the dual-channel-disjoint signature, structural disjointness) is the structural overdetermination establishing the principle's physical reality.

### The historical record

The recognition that all of these threads --- Wick rotation, $x_4 = ict$, $i\hbar\partial_t$, the Lorentzian $-c^2$, the Euclidean path integral, the Bekenstein-Hawking Wick-rotated action, the Compton phase $e^{-imc^2\Delta\tau/\hbar}$ --- share the same structural content was invisible in the pre-McGucken physics literature for the reasons identified in §6.0.9 below. The quantum field theory community (Schwinger, Symanzik, Osterwalder-Schrader) developed the Wick rotation as a formal analytic-continuation device without recognising that it descends from a single physical principle. The GR community (MTW, Wald, Carroll) abandoned the imaginary fourth coordinate $x_4 = ict$ at the textbook level (§6.3). The QM community read the Schrödinger evolution's $i$ as a calculational device without identifying it with the perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three.

The McGucken framework recognises these threads as the same structural content. The Wick rotation is the internal coordinate identification of a principle, the structural reason that GR and QM both descend from one foundational source. It is not the relationship between the two derivation chains of any given theorem --- those chains are structurally disjoint, and the Wick rotation does not bridge between them.

### Summary

\begin{enumerate}
\item Both channels descend from the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.
\item The Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ is a theorem of the principle (Theorem 4).
\item The two derivations of any given theorem are *not* Wick rotations of each other. They share no intermediate machinery (structural disjointness of the two channels). The Wick rotation, applied to the Algebraic Channel derivation, produces a Wick-rotated Algebraic Channel derivation; it does not produce the Geometric Channel derivation.
\item Each channel uses the Wick rotation internally to convert between signature contexts within its own derivation chain (e.g., Algebraic Channel's Bekenstein--Hawking via Euclidean Schwarzschild action; Geometric Channel's Geometric Second Law via Brownian-motion Wick rotation).
\item The differential response of the channels' content under the Wick rotation is a real structural fact: Algebraic Channel objects transform; Geometric Channel objects are signature-invariant.
\item The cross-channel agreement on observables (Signature-Bridging Theorem, Theorem 15) follows from common descent of both channels from the principle, with the Wick rotation as a theorem of the same principle.
\end{enumerate}

#### 1.5.3.2 The Wick Rotation as Differential Diagnostic: Destroyer of the Algebraic Channel, Transporter of the Geometric Channel {#sec:differential-diagnostic}

Section 1.5.3.1 established that both channels descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the Wick rotation being a theorem of the principle that handles signature conversion. A complementary structural fact emerges when one examines the *response level* of each channel under the Wick rotation. The QM corpus result [3, Theorem on Channel--Wick Asymmetry] establishes:

> *The Wick rotation acts as a structural diagnostic distinguishing the two channels by their differential response. The Algebraic Channel is destroyed by the rotation; Geometric Channel is transported by it. The rotation acts on a derivation already given, rather than transforming Algebraic Channel into the Geometric Channel.*

The natural meta-question for GR is: *does the same hold in the gravitational sector?* The answer is *yes, with a structural refinement that distinguishes the GR case from the QM case in a precise way*. This subsection works through the differential-diagnostic reading and identifies exactly what is destroyed and what is transported in each channel of GR under the Wick rotation.

### What each channel of GR carries under the Wick rotation

The Wick rotation $t \mapsto -i\tau$, equivalently $\tau = x_4/c$, acts asymmetrically on the foundational content of each channel.

**Algebraic Channel of GR carries the Lorentz-signature-specific content**, which is structurally destroyed (or fundamentally transformed) by the Wick rotation:
\begin{itemize}
\item The metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$ becomes the Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$; the negative sign on the temporal component disappears.
\item The master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ becomes the Euclidean magnitude identity $u^\mu u_\mu = +c^2$; the *causal-structure content* (timelike normalisation to $-c^2$ versus spacelike to $+c^2$) is destroyed.
\item The Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ becomes the rotation group $\mathrm{SO}(4)$; the *causal-structure decomposition* into boosts and rotations is destroyed.
\item The light cone — the locus of null vectors with $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{r} = 0$ — *disappears entirely* in Euclidean signature, since all four-vectors have strictly positive squared length. The causal classification into timelike, null, and spacelike (foundational to GR) is structurally destroyed.
\item The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ transform into Euclidean field equations on a Riemannian manifold, with solutions like the Euclidean Schwarzschild metric that have *no Lorentzian causal interpretation* (they have periodic Euclidean time with no horizon-as-causal-boundary; the "horizon" becomes a removable point with periodicity condition for regularity).
\end{itemize}

The destruction is not total --- Algebraic Channel's *field-equation content* survives the rotation in transformed Euclidean form (Gibbons--Hawking--York, Euclidean quantum gravity). But the *Lorentz-signature-specific content* (causal structure, light cones, the $-c^2$ in the master equation, $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$) is destroyed.

**Geometric Channel of GR carries the signature-invariant geometric-propagation content**, which is transported by the Wick rotation without loss of structure:
\begin{itemize}
\item The iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion at universal rate $c$ from every event is unchanged. The Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ in Lorentzian signature is a 2-sphere of radius $c(t-t_0)$ in the spatial three; the Sphere in Euclidean signature is the same 2-sphere of radius $c(\tau-\tau_0)$ in the same spatial three, with the imaginary-time advance $i(\tau - \tau_0)$ replacing the real-time advance $(t - t_0)$. The geometric content --- a 2-sphere expanding at rate $c$ from the apex --- is identical.
\item The retarded Green's function of the wave equation $\Box \psi = 0$, $G_{\mathrm{ret}}(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}', t - t') = \delta(t - t' - |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|/c)/(4\pi|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|)$, becomes the Euclidean heat kernel $G_E(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}', \tau - \tau') = (4\pi (\tau - \tau'))^{-3/2} \exp(-|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|^2/(4(\tau - \tau')))$ under Wick rotation. Both are *propagators that encode wavefront propagation at universal rate $c$* --- the Lorentzian version as oscillatory wave propagation, the Euclidean version as diffusive heat propagation. The geometric content (propagation at universal rate from the source) survives the rotation in transported form.
\item The Compton phase $\Phi(q;p) = \exp(-i m c^2 \Delta\tau/\hbar)$ along worldlines becomes $\Phi_E(q;p) = \exp(-m c^2 \Delta\tau_E/\hbar)$ under Wick rotation. The oscillatory phase becomes a real exponential, but the *Compton-coupling content* (the rate at which the mass-energy is accumulated along the worldline) is transported intact. The Compton-phase uniformity on the Sphere (Lemma 2.2 of the disjunctive forcing) survives the rotation as a structural identity on the Euclidean Sphere.
\item The Huygens-Feynman iterated-Sphere composition is the Geometric Channel reading of both the Lorentzian path integral $\int \mathcal{D}\phi\, e^{iS/\hbar}$ and the Euclidean path integral $\int \mathcal{D}\phi\, e^{-S_E/\hbar}$. The same iterated-Sphere structure underlies both --- the wavefront propagation at universal rate $c$ on the deformable spatial sector is *signature-invariant* in its geometric content, with the Wick rotation determining only whether the propagator weight is oscillatory ($e^{iS/\hbar}$, Lorentzian) or real-exponential ($e^{-S_E/\hbar}$, Euclidean).
\item The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy via mode counting on the horizon Sphere (Geometric Channel derivation, Proposition 15.2.4.1) works equally in Lorentzian and Euclidean signature, with the horizon Sphere being the same 2-sphere in both readings. The mode counting (number of Planck-scale modes per unit horizon area) is signature-invariant.
\end{itemize}

The geometric-propagation content of the Geometric Channel is *transported* by the Wick rotation without loss --- the rotation changes the analytic form of propagators (oscillatory $\leftrightarrow$ diffusive) but preserves the underlying geometric content (wavefront propagation at universal rate $c$ from every event).
