## 1.8 The Tong Diagnostic: Four Open Questions in Quantum Field Theory and the McGucken Framework's Structural Readings {#sec:tong}

The orthodox foundations of quantum field theory carry four interlocking structural features that the orthodox tradition has named explicitly but has been unable to *explain*: (a) the *gauge redundancy* of every fundamental theory, in which one must introduce labels (the voltage $A_\mu$ in electromagnetism, the metric components $g_{\mu\nu}$ in general relativity, the overall phase of the quantum wavefunction) that are unmeasurable even in principle yet structurally required to write the laws of physics; (b) the *locality--unitarity tradeoff*, in which the same quantum field theory admits formulations in which locality is manifest but unitarity is hidden, or formulations in which unitarity is manifest but locality is hidden, with the gauge redundancy supplying the equivalence that makes both readings possible; (c) the *UV-cutoff that preserves all symmetries*, in which quantum field theory's infinities must be regulated by some Planck-scale structure that does not break Lorentz invariance, gauge invariance, or any other physical symmetry of the theory; (d) the *chirality structure of the Standard Model*, in which the left-handed and right-handed sectors interact differently with the weak nuclear force and the resulting theory cannot be placed on a discrete spatial lattice (Nielsen--Ninomiya, §1.7) yet must somehow be regulated at the Planck scale.

These four structural features have been observed, named, and articulated by working quantum field theorists for nearly a century without a foundational account explaining *why* they are present together. David Tong's 2025 *Mindscape* conversation on open questions in quantum field theory [Tong--Carroll 2025] articulates each of the four features in plain orthodox vocabulary and confesses, at multiple points, that the orthodox tradition does not know what generates them. Tong's confession is the cleanest contemporary statement of the *structural gap* that the McGucken Duality fills. The present subsection records this gap as a structural diagnostic — the *Tong Diagnostic* — and establishes that each of Tong's four orthodox puzzles is the operator-algebraic shadow of the Geometric Channel geometric content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on $M_G$, with the McGucken Duality supplying the dual-channel architecture that the orthodox tradition gestures at without recognising.

The structural payoff: every Tong puzzle dissolves into the Algebraic Channel/Geometric Channel signature of the McGucken Duality, with the dissolution validating the framework's claim to *foundational status* — the framework is not merely a reformulation of orthodox quantum field theory but the structural source from which the four Tong-diagnosed orthodox features descend. The novelty and necessity of the McGucken Duality is exhibited at exactly the points where orthodox quantum field theory is most articulate about its own unresolved questions.

### 1.8.1 The Tong diagnostic statements: orthodox quantum field theory's articulate confession

We record Tong's four confessions verbatim (with quotation marks indicating his words), in the order they appear in the *Mindscape* interview [Tong--Carroll 2025], and pair each with the McGucken-framework structural answer.

**Tong Confession 1 — Gauge redundancy** [Mindscape 0:37:54--0:38:00]. *"It's gauge redundancy. It's a redundancy in our description of the laws of physics. Tong's examples: the voltage $A_0$ in Maxwell's electromagnetism (overall value unmeasurable); the metric components $g_{\mu\nu}$ in general relativity (coordinate-dependent, unmeasurable in absolute terms); the overall phase of the quantum wavefunction $e^{i\alpha} \psi$ (unmeasurable, all observables invariant under multiplication by $e^{i\alpha}$). **Tong Confession 4 — Chirality structure** [Mindscape 0:57:10--1:04:54]. *"Theories that were left and right-handed, where they look different when viewed in the mirror, cannot be put on a spatial lattice. \ldots [String theory's] internal directions, Calabi--Yau manifolds or whatnot. ### 1.8.4 The novelty and necessity of the McGucken Duality, exhibited at the Tong-diagnostic points

The Tong Diagnostic is the cleanest contemporary articulation of orthodox quantum field theory's structural gaps. Each of the four confessions — gauge redundancy, locality--unitarity tradeoff, UV-cutoff symmetry-preservation, chirality structure — is named explicitly by Tong as a structural feature of the laws of physics that he does not understand, with the explicit observation that the orthodox tradition has not produced a foundational account of any of them. The McGucken Duality's two-channel architecture supplies, at full structural rigor, the foundational account that orthodox quantum field theory lacks.

The novelty of the McGucken Duality is exhibited at exactly the four points where Tong's orthodox vocabulary runs out:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Gauge redundancy is no longer mysterious.* It is the Algebraic Channel algebraic-symmetry shadow of the Geometric Channel McGucken-Sphere geometric content. The Algebraic Channel labels have no Geometric Channel referents because the Algebraic Channel operates with operator-algebraic structures (Hilbert spaces, gauge fields, vector potentials) while the Geometric Channel operates with geometric-propagation structures (McGucken Spheres, $x_4$-phase distributions, iterated-Sphere flows). The redundancy is a structural necessity of any theory descending from $(\mathrm{McP})$ via the McGucken Duality.

\item *Locality and unitarity are no longer in tension.* Locality is the Algebraic Channel manifest; unitarity is the Geometric Channel manifest. Both descend from $(\mathrm{McP})$; gauge redundancy supplies the equivalence between the two readings; the McGucken Duality's two-channel architecture is what allows both features to coexist in the same physical theory.

\item *The UV cutoff problem is solved.* The Planck-scale Lorentz-invariant $x_4$-quantization of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ + Proposition 2.2 is intrinsic to the principle, not imposed as a regulator, and preserves all the symmetries because the principle itself is Lorentz-invariant. The orthodox struggle with regulators (Pauli--Villars breaking gauge invariance, dimensional regularization continuing to non-integer dimensions, lattice cutoff breaking Lorentz invariance) is bypassed at the foundational level.

\item *The chirality structure is no longer mysterious.* The $\gamma^5$ chirality operator's defining imaginary unit $i$ is the same $i$ as in $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The chirality content of the Standard Model is the Algebraic Channel algebraic content of the perpendicularity marker, without compactification or singular Calabi--Yau features. The orthodox string-theory chirality derivation is one Geometric Channel geometric construction; the McGucken framework supplies the structurally disjoint Algebraic Channel construction.
\end{itemize}

The necessity of the McGucken Duality follows from the orthodox tradition's articulate confession of these four structural gaps. If the laws of physics did not exhibit the bi-channel architecture, none of the four Tong-diagnostic features would be present: gauge redundancy would not be needed (no Algebraic Channel--Geometric Channel label distinction); locality and unitarity would be manifest in the same formulation (no two-channel split); the UV cutoff problem would be solved by some other means; the chirality structure would not require compactification or singular manifolds in the orthodox derivation. The four features are *forced* by the dual-channel architecture, and their joint presence in the orthodox formulation of fundamental physics is the empirical signature that the underlying structural content of the laws of physics is the McGucken Duality.

The structural priority statement of \S1.8: *the Tong Diagnostic is the orthodox quantum field theory community's articulate confession of the McGucken Duality's necessity. Each of the four Tong confessions — gauge redundancy, locality--unitarity tradeoff, UV-cutoff symmetry-preservation, chirality structure — is the empirical signature of the Algebraic Channel/Geometric Channel structural feature of the McGucken Duality, with the four features jointly demonstrating that the laws of physics carry the dual-channel architecture and the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies the foundational source from which both channels descend. ## 1.9 Historical Context: Dual-Formulation Sightings in the Pre-McGucken Literature {#sec:history}

The structural fact that fundamental physics admits *two* parallel formulations — one algebraic-symmetric, one geometric-propagative — is not original to the McGucken framework. The historical record contains repeated sightings of dual-formulation structure across roughly two and a half centuries, with each major figure naming one half of a pair within the technical vocabulary of their own period without identifying a foundational principle from which both halves descend. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies that foundational principle. The present section records the historical context in narrative form, without claiming that each prior figure's dual-formulation observation maps exactly onto the Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel architecture of \S1.5 — that would be a structural-historical claim requiring detailed textual scholarship I have not done. What can be said with confidence is that the existence of *dual formulations* in foundational physics is a documented historical pattern, and the McGucken Duality is the latest entry in a long sequence.

The narrative below identifies eight clusters of sightings, with citations to primary sources or to standard secondary scholarship. The reader who wants the structural mapping of each sighting onto Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel is referred to the body of the textbook (Chapters 5--17) where each McGucken theorem is derived with its own audit. The historical narrative below is contextual, not load-bearing for the derivations.

### 1.9.1 Lagrange--Hamilton: the variational vs canonical formulations of classical mechanics

Lagrange's *Mécanique Analytique* (1788) developed mechanics from a variational principle on configuration-space trajectories; Hamilton's *On a General Method in Dynamics* (1834) reformulated the same mechanics canonically on phase space. The two formulations are related by the Legendre transform and are formally equivalent on standard cases. Hamilton himself recognised the depth of the equivalence through his *optico-mechanical analogy* of the 1830s, in which the variational principle of mechanics is shown parallel to Fermat's variational principle of geometric optics. The analogy is the earliest historical sighting of a structural pairing of "algebraic" (Hamiltonian canonical) with "geometric" (Lagrangian variational) formulations of the same physics. The standard secondary reference is Whittaker, *A Treatise on the Analytical Dynamics of Particles and Rigid Bodies* (1937, 4th ed., Cambridge); the optico-mechanical analogy is treated at length in Goldstein, *Classical Mechanics* (1980, 2nd ed., Addison-Wesley, Ch.\ 10), and in the historical study by Komorowski, *Lectures on Quantum Mechanics for Mathematicians* (arXiv:1907.05786, Appendix A.8). The optico-mechanical analogy was the explicit input to Schrödinger's wave-mechanical derivation in 1926 (\S1.9.2 below).

### 1.9.2 Schrödinger 1926: matrix mechanics, wave mechanics, and the Hamilton--Huygens correspondence

The most famous dual-formulation structure in twentieth-century physics is the parallel discovery of matrix mechanics (Heisenberg, Born, Jordan 1925) and wave mechanics (Schrödinger 1926), with their unitary equivalence established by Schrödinger 1926d (Annalen der Physik 79, 734--756) and rigorised by the Stone--von Neumann uniqueness theorem (Stone 1930, von Neumann 1931). The two formulations operate with structurally disjoint primitives: matrix mechanics with operator algebras on Hilbert space (Algebraic Channel--like in modern reading), wave mechanics with wavefunction propagation on configuration space (Geometric Channel--like in modern reading). Schrödinger himself, in his second 1926 *Annalen* paper, made the structural reading explicit. He wrote, on the relation between Hamilton's mechanics and wave propagation: "Hamilton's variational principle can be shown to correspond to the Fermat principle for wave propagation in configuration (q)-space, and the H-J equation expresses Huygens' principle for this wave propagation." This is Schrödinger explicitly identifying the dual-formulation pattern in 1926, by his own hand, in the paper that established wave mechanics. Schrödinger's identification of Hamilton-Jacobi $\to$ Huygens' principle is the closest historical sighting of what the McGucken framework now reads as a wavefront-based Geometric Channel reading of mechanics. The primary source is Schrödinger 1926b (Annalen der Physik 79, 489--527); a careful modern reconstruction is in the academic survey "The classical roots of wave mechanics: Schrödinger's transformations of the optical-mechanical analogy" (Academia.edu, arxiv reference 2103.02022).

### 1.9.3 Hertz 1894: the algebraic Maxwell theory

Heinrich Hertz's posthumously-published *Die Prinzipien der Mechanik in neuem Zusammenhange dargestellt* (Barth, Leipzig, 1894; English translation *The Principles of Mechanics Presented in a New Form*, Macmillan, London, 1899) is the canonical late-nineteenth-century work on mechanical-foundational reformulation. Hertz famously asserted that "Maxwell's theory is Maxwell's system of equations" — a frequently quoted statement read by some commentators as a turn toward an algebraic/operational reading of electromagnetism. The actual historical picture is more nuanced: modern scholarship (e.g., Mulligan, "The aether and Heinrich Hertz's *Principles of Mechanics*," *Physics in Perspective* 3 (2001), 136--164; Lützen, *Mechanistic Images in Geometric Form: Heinrich Hertz's Principles of Mechanics*, Oxford 2005) shows that Hertz remained committed to the ether as a mechanical substrate and viewed *Principles of Mechanics* as foundational groundwork for an eventual mechanical-geometric reduction of electromagnetism. The structural reading: Hertz formulated the equations algebraically while holding open a future geometric/mechanical reduction. The pattern — algebraic statement of the laws + suspended commitment about underlying geometric substrate — is the structural signature of a dual-formulation framework whose geometric half is held open.

### 1.9.4 Bohr 1928: complementarity

Niels Bohr's complementarity principle, set out in his Como lecture of September 1927 (published as "The Quantum Postulate and the Recent Development of Atomic Theory," *Nature* 121 (1928), 580--590, and reprinted in *Atomic Theory and the Description of Nature*, Cambridge 1934), asserts that quantum mechanical descriptions of phenomena require pairs of mutually exclusive but jointly necessary classical descriptions — wave and particle, position and momentum. Bohr's framing was epistemological: the descriptions are forced into mutual exclusion by the experimental arrangement. The McGucken framework offers a different reading — both descriptions are simultaneously available because each is a structurally disjoint reading of one wavefront — but the *fact* of dual-description structure at the foundations of quantum mechanics was named by Bohr nearly a century before McGucken. The standard scholarly treatment is Camilleri, *Heisenberg and the Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics: The Physicist as Philosopher* (Cambridge 2009); Held, "The meaning of complementarity," *Studies in the History and Philosophy of Modern Physics* 25 (1994), 871--893; Faye, "Niels Bohr: His Heritage and Legacy" (Springer 1991). Whether Bohr's "complementary descriptions" map cleanly onto Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel of the McGucken Duality is a question of structural interpretation, not a settled fact.

### 1.9.5 Wheeler--Feynman 1949 and Feynman 1948: retarded/advanced symmetry and the path integral

Wheeler and Feynman's absorber theory ("Interaction with the Absorber as the Mechanism of Radiation," *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 17 (1945), 157--181; "Classical Electrodynamics in Terms of Direct Interparticle Action," *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 21 (1949), 425--433) developed a fully time-symmetric formulation of classical electrodynamics. Feynman's 1948 path-integral formulation ("Space-Time Approach to Non-Relativistic Quantum Mechanics," *Rev. Mod. Phys.* 20 (1948), 367--387) reformulated quantum mechanics as a sum over paths weighted by the exponential of the classical action. Feynman explicitly identified his path integral with Huygens' principle for wave propagation, and the path-integral formulation has been read in much subsequent literature (e.g., the Komorowski survey cited above) as a geometric-propagation reading of quantum mechanics paralleling the operator-algebraic formulation. The McGucken framework's Geometric Channel / Algebraic Channel pairing — with the Geometric Channel operating on McGucken-Sphere wavefront geometry and the Algebraic Channel on operator algebras — has structural resonance with the path-integral / matrix-mechanics pairing, though again the exact mapping is a question requiring detailed structural-historical work.

### 1.9.6 Wightman 1956 and Haag--Kastler 1964: axiomatic quantum field theory

Algebraic quantum field theory developed in two axiomatic frameworks in the 1950s and 1960s: the Wightman axioms ("Quantum Field Theory in Terms of Vacuum Expectation Values," *Phys. Rev.* 101 (1956), 860--866), formulating quantum field theory in terms of operator-valued distributions at spacetime points; and the Haag--Kastler axioms ("An Algebraic Approach to Quantum Field Theory," *J. Math. Phys.* 5 (1964), 848--861), formulating quantum field theory in terms of abstract operator algebras assigned to spacetime regions. The two frameworks are equivalent on standard cases but operate with structurally disjoint primitive concepts (point-localised field operators vs region-assigned algebras). The standard reference is Haag, *Local Quantum Physics* (Springer 1996).

### 1.9.7 Geometric reformulations of quantum field theory: Penrose twistors, Ashtekar variables, Connes spectral triples

Several mature programs in the second half of the twentieth century have aimed at geometric reformulations of quantum field theory. Penrose's twistor program (Penrose 1967, "Twistor Algebra," *J. Math. Phys.* 8, 345--366; Penrose, *The Road to Reality*, Knopf 2004) reformulates spacetime quantum-field structure on twistor space. Ashtekar's connection-variable reformulation of canonical general relativity (Ashtekar 1986, "New Variables for Classical and Quantum Gravity," *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 57, 2244--2247) replaces the ADM metric variables with an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ connection. Connes's noncommutative geometry program (Connes, *Noncommutative Geometry*, Academic Press 1994; Chamseddine--Connes 1996, "The Spectral Action Principle," *Commun. Math. Phys.* 186, 731--750) reformulates geometry via the spectral triple $(\mathcal A, \mathcal H, D)$. Each of these programs is, in a broad sense, a geometric counterpart to the standard operator-algebraic formulation of quantum field theory; each is an instance of the dual-formulation pattern in twentieth-century foundational physics.

### 1.9.8 Gauge-gravity duality: 't Hooft and Maldacena

't Hooft's large-$N$ reformulation of gauge theory ("A Planar Diagram Theory for Strong Interactions," *Nucl. Phys. B* 72 (1974), 461--473) and Maldacena's AdS/CFT correspondence ("The Large $N$ Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity," *Adv. Theor. Math. Phys.* 2 (1997), 231--252) established the most famous gauge-gravity duality of the modern era: a gauge theory in $d-1$ dimensions is dual to a gravitational theory in $d$ dimensions. The standard textbook is Aharony, Gubser, Maldacena, Ooguri, Oz, "Large N field theories, string theory and gravity," *Phys. Rep.* 323 (2000), 183--386.

### 1.9.9 Wheeler's foundational-question methodology and the McGucken Principle

Wheeler's late-career programme — geons (Wheeler, "Geons," *Phys. Rev.* 97 (1955), 511--536), quantum foam (introduced in Wheeler's *Geometrodynamics*, Academic Press 1962), the "it from bit" programme (Wheeler, "Information, physics, quantum: The search for links," in *Complexity, Entropy, and the Physics of Information*, Addison-Wesley 1990) — was a sustained methodological insistence that physics has, at its base, a single foundational fact that can be stated simply and from which the structural features of the universe descend. Wheeler is the immediate pedagogical antecedent of the McGucken Principle. The present author was Wheeler's undergraduate student at Princeton in the late 1980s, with Wheeler's c.\ 1989--1990 problem sets on the geometric derivation of the Schwarzschild time-factor and on EPR / delayed-choice experiments being the original pedagogical setting in which the McGucken Principle was first developed. The dissertation appendix at UNC Chapel Hill (1998--1999) is the first written record of the principle.

The historical lesson of \S\S1.9.1--1.9.9 is *not* that each prior figure independently arrived at the McGucken Duality. It is that the pattern of dual formulation in foundational physics has been visible for two and a half centuries; that orthodox physics has named the pattern under various technical vocabularies without identifying a foundational principle from which both halves of each dual pair descend; and that the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ provides that foundational principle, with the dual-channel architecture of the laws of physics derivable as a theorem from a single equation in elementary calculus notation. Whether each historical dual-pair maps exactly onto Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel of the McGucken Duality is a structural question requiring case-by-case textual work, and is not claimed in advance of that work.

# 2. Mainstream Graduate Pedagogy of General Relativity {#sec:five}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

We anchor that posture in five representative graduate texts, then extract the foundational organisation they share --- an organisation that holds across the standard literature regardless of which representative texts one selects.

## 2.1 Five Representative Texts

The five texts below [26--30] span the range of mainstream graduate GR instruction, from the encyclopedic to the streamlined. Each descriptor records structural facts --- part/chapter organisation, metric signature, mode of presentation --- verified against publisher tables of contents and standard reference surveys; none of the books' text is reproduced here.

**(1) Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler, *Gravitation* (1973; Princeton reissue 2017).** "MTW." Ten parts, forty-four chapters, $\sim 1280$ pages. Organised on a two-track design (a core Track 1 and an advanced Track 2), deeply geometric and coordinate-free in the Wheeler school. Signature $(-,+,+,+)$ (Landau--Lifshitz spacelike convention). The field equations are approached through Chapter 17's "six routes to Einstein's geometrodynamics" --- a sequence of physical motivations, not an axiom. Almost nothing is labelled a theorem.

**(2) Wald, *General Relativity* (1984).** $\sim 490$ pages, abstract-index notation, signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Two parts: Part I (Fundamentals) runs Introduction, Manifolds and Tensor Fields, Curvature, Einstein's Equation, Homogeneous Isotropic Cosmology, and the Schwarzschild Solution; Part II (advanced topics) covers Lagrangian and Hamiltonian methods, causal structure, the singularity theorems, asymptotic flatness, quantum field theory in curved spacetime and Hawking radiation, black-hole thermodynamics, and spinors. This is the one text of the five that operates in explicit definition--lemma--theorem style downstream --- yet Einstein's equation itself is *posited*, motivated by limiting arguments, with the theorem--proof apparatus applied only to what follows from it.

**(3) Carroll, *Spacetime and Geometry* (2004; Cambridge reprint 2019).** Eight chapters plus appendices, $\sim 510$ pages, signature $(-,+,+,+)$: Special Relativity and Flat Spacetime, Manifolds, Curvature, Gravitation, the Schwarzschild Solution and Black Holes, More General Black Holes, Perturbation Theory and Gravitational Radiation, Cosmology. General relativity proper enters in Chapter 4, where the field equation is obtained twice --- by Newtonian-limit matching and by a variational derivation from the Einstein--Hilbert action. The text treats GR explicitly as a field theory in order to connect it to quantum field theory.

**(4) Weinberg, *Gravitation and Cosmology* (1972).** $\sim 685$ pages, five parts (Preliminaries; the General Theory of Relativity; Applications; Formal Developments; Cosmology). The field-theoretic outlier: signature $(+,-,-,-)$ and a deliberately anti-geometric stance --- Weinberg held that over-emphasis on geometry obscures the connections between gravitation and the rest of physics. The equivalence principle is taken as the foundational *postulate* and GR is built as the theory of a massless spin-2 field. The book does not treat black holes.

**(5) Schutz, *A First Course in General Relativity* (1985; 2nd ed. 2009).** $\sim 12$ chapters, signature $(-,+,+,+)$; the undergraduate-accessible entry point. A geometry-first review of special relativity, then vector and tensor analysis built up carefully from flat spacetime, curvature, the field equation, geodesic motion in Schwarzschild and the classical tests, closing with black holes including the Kerr solution and the Hawking effect. The gentlest of the five; the cosmology chapter was rewritten for the second edition.

## 2.2 What the Standard Texts Share

All five develop the same physical content: the Lorentzian manifold, the metric and Levi-Civita connection, the Riemann tensor and its contractions, the geodesic equation, the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\, T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$, the Schwarzschild solution, gravitational waves at linearised order, and FLRW cosmology; all but Weinberg treat black-hole horizons. Four of the five adopt the $(-,+,+,+)$ signature; Weinberg uses $(+,-,-,-)$. This common content is the stable core of graduate GR instruction across the wider literature (Hartle, Rindler, Stephani, Padmanabhan, and others), not an artefact of these particular five.

## 2.3 How Mainstream Pedagogy Is Organised

The standard texts vary along two axes --- philosophical stance and rigour of presentation --- while sharing a single foundational posture (§2.4).

*Stance.* MTW and Wald are geometric; Weinberg is anti-geometric; Carroll and Schutz are geometric but pragmatic.

*Rigour and mode of presentation.* Only Wald uses theorem--proof as its primary downstream mode; the others proceed by physical argument and worked example. MTW motivates the field equations through its "six routes"; Weinberg builds on explicitly stated principles; Carroll and Schutz are predominantly expository. Wald is also the only one of the five to treat the global techniques (Penrose diagrams, trapped surfaces, the Hawking--Penrose singularity theorems) and quantum field theory in curved spacetime in earnest.

The variation here is in *how the material is presented*, not in *what is taken as foundational*.

## 2.4 The Shared Foundational Posture

Beneath the stylistic variation, mainstream graduate GR pedagogy shares a single foundational posture, and it is this posture --- not any one book --- against which the present work defines its contrast:

> The standard texts introduce gravitation by *positing* a small cluster of physical principles --- the equivalence principle (typically in weak, Einstein, and strong forms), together with general covariance and a correspondence or minimal-coupling rule --- and present the Einstein field equation as a postulate *motivated* by limiting and consistency arguments rather than *derived* from a more primitive principle. The equivalence principle enters as an input, never as a theorem.

This is verifiable directly from the texts' own organisation. Wald presents Einstein's equation as a postulate motivated by limiting arguments. Weinberg makes the equivalence principle the foundational postulate. MTW reaches the field equations through motivational "routes." Carroll *derives* the field equation, but from the posited Einstein--Hilbert action together with Newtonian matching, not from anything deeper. Schutz bootstraps from the special-relativistic equivalence principle. No standard text derives the equivalence principle, and none derives the field equation from a single deeper physical principle. The posture is uniform across the literature.

## 2.5 Counting Foundational Posits

A coarse but useful way to summarise the posture of §2.4 is to count the free-standing principles each text posits before its derivations begin. These counts are *interpretive*: none of the texts presents a closed enumerated axiom list, and reasonable readers will bracket the totals by one or two depending on how the equivalence principle's three forms and general covariance are tallied. The table below should therefore be read as an estimate of foundational posits, not an exact census.

\begin{center}

What is *not* interpretive, and is verified, is the lower bound shared by every standard text: each posits at least the equivalence principle, and each posits the Einstein field equation as a starting point rather than deriving it. The McGucken entry of *one* records a fact about *this book's presentation* --- that the weak, Einstein, and strong equivalence principles appear here as theorems GR T3, GR T4, GR T5, and the field equation as the derived theorem GR T11, all downstream of the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The equivalence principle is counted as one principle for each book above; every text except Schutz distinguishes at least two forms, so counting each form separately raises every number above by one or two while leaving the McGucken count of one unaffected, since the three forms appear here as separate theorems rather than separate posits.

## 2.6 What the Survey Establishes, and What It Does Not

To keep the comparison referee-proof, two claims must be held distinct.

*Established by the survey.* Mainstream graduate GR pedagogy posits the equivalence principle (and typically general covariance and a correspondence/minimal-coupling rule) and posits the Einstein field equation, then derives its downstream results from these inputs. This is a verifiable statement about the structure of the standard texts, and it stands without hedging.

*Argued in this book, not established by the survey.* That deriving these posited principles --- the equivalence principle, the field equation --- as *theorems* from the single principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is preferable to taking them as inputs. This is a substantive claim about explanatory economy and structural priority. The survey establishes the *contrast* --- posited-principle pedagogy versus a derive-from-one-principle architecture --- but it does not, by itself, establish the *superiority* of the latter. The case for that preference is made on its own terms in the chapters that follow, where each posited principle of the standard pedagogy is exhibited as a theorem and the two structurally disjoint derivation channels are shown to converge (Chapters 5--17).

## 3.2 What "One Principle, Two Channels" Means as a Textbook Discipline

The discipline of this book is uncompromising. Every theorem of general relativity is to be derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ along *both* $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel. No auxiliary principles are admitted. No "minimal coupling," no "general covariance as an independent principle," no "equivalence principle as a separate posit" --- all of these appear as theorems (GR T3, T4, T5) downstream of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Einstein--Hilbert action, where it appears, is constructed as a theorem; the field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ are derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ in two independent ways (Lovelock route along the Algebraic Channel, Jacobson thermodynamic route along the Geometric Channel), neither route sharing intermediate machinery with the other. Both derivations have been completed in full above (Theorems 9 and 14).

The reader is encouraged to verify, theorem by theorem, that no second principle is admitted. The bibliography is provided so that every external mathematical input is traceable to a paper in the McGucken corpus where it is itself derived as a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and from there to the original mathematical source.

# 5. The McGucken Duality as Overdetermined Proof of $dx_4/dt = ic$ {#sec:overdetermination}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

The structural significance of the dual-channel architecture is *evidential*. The convergence of two structurally disjoint derivation chains on the same physical content is, historically, taken as evidence that the content expresses something real about physical reality, not an artefact of either chain. Three canonical historical examples:

(i) The Heisenberg matrix-mechanics and Schrödinger wave-mechanics formulations of quantum mechanics were shown by Dirac and Jordan to be equivalent; the convergence was taken as evidence that quantum mechanics expresses something real about the world.

(ii) The Hilbert and Einstein derivations of the field equations (independently, November 1915) used the variational principle and the Newtonian-limit route respectively; the convergence was taken as evidence that $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ expresses a physical law.

(iii) The Hawking and Bekenstein arguments for black-hole entropy used the four-laws-of-thermodynamics analogy and the information-theoretic bound respectively; the convergence on $S = k_B A/(4 \ell_P^2)$ was taken as evidence for the physical reality of horizon thermodynamics.

The McGucken Duality extends this historical pattern to all 24 theorems of GR (and all 23 theorems of QM in the companion volume) simultaneously. The structural fact that each theorem admits the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel derivation with operator-algebraic / symmetry intermediate machinery, *and* the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation with geometric / Sphere-based intermediate machinery, *and* the two share no named intermediate structure on the five load-bearing pivots, is an overdetermination of the underlying principle the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ at a scale without precedent in theoretical physics.

## 5.1 The Disjointness Predicate (structural disjointness of the two channels)

The formal statement of "structurally disjoint" used throughout this book is the following predicate, imported from [1, Part VII].

**Definition 17 (Dual-Channel-Disjointness, structural disjointness).** Let $T$ be a theorem of the McGucken framework. Let $\Pi_A(T)$ be the Algebraic Channel proof of $T$ and $\Pi_B(T)$ the Geometric Channel proof of $T$. Let $M(\Pi_A)$ be the set of named intermediate mathematical structures invoked in $\Pi_A$ (theorems, lemmas, definitions, identities) other than the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ itself; analogously $M(\Pi_B)$. The predicate
$$\mathrm{DCD}(T) :\iff M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$$
*holds when the two proofs share no named intermediate structure.*

**Definition 17-bis (Channel priority and the Import Asymmetry).** *Disjointness as stated in Definition 17 is a symmetric set-theoretic condition, but the two channels are not on a symmetric footing, and the audit condition that enforces $\mathrm{DCD}$ in practice is therefore one-directional.*

*The Geometric Channel is structurally prior to the Algebraic Channel.* The Geometric Channel reads $dx_4/dt = ic$ as what it physically is --- the *active spherical expansion of the fourth dimension at rate $c$ from every event* --- and derives its theorems from the iterated-Sphere wavefront flow that this expansion generates. The Algebraic Channel reads the *integrated shadow* $x_4 = ict$ as a coordinate label and derives its theorems from the symmetry group of that label (§1.5.2, "What is characteristic of each channel"). The shadow is cast by the expansion; the expansion is not cast by the shadow. Two independent structural facts record this priority:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *The Wick-rotation diagnostic* (§1.5.3.2). Under the McGucken--Wick rotation the Algebraic Channel's content is **destroyed** --- the Lorentzian signature, the master equation's causal normalisation, the boost/rotation decomposition of $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, and the light cone itself all fail to survive --- while the Geometric Channel's content is **transported** intact, the Sphere-flow wavefront persisting in either signature. A structure that survives the rotation which annihilates the other is the more foundational of the two.
\item *The direction of derivation.* Every named element of $M(\Pi_A)$ is in principle recoverable from the Geometric Channel, because the coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ on which the Algebraic Channel operates is itself the time-integral of the Geometric Channel's active expansion (Lemma 5.1.2.1). The converse fails: the Sphere-flow wavefront content is not recoverable from the symmetry group of a coordinate label, which retains no record of the expansion that produced it.
\end{enumerate}

*The Import Asymmetry Rule.* Consequently, in any dual-channel derivation:

\begin{itemize}
\item[(IA1)] *The Geometric Channel may not import Algebraic Channel machinery.* Such an import would have the primary structure borrowing from its own integrated shadow, inverting the derivational order, and it falsifies $\mathrm{DCD}(T)$ outright by placing a named element of $M(\Pi_A)$ inside $\Pi_B$. Where a Geometric Channel proof appears to need an Algebraic result, the correct repair is *not* to weaken the disjointness claim but to *supply the Geometric Channel with its own derivation of that result from the Sphere flow*. (Worked instance: Lemma 12.1.3.1a of Chapter 12 supplies the coordinate-period invariance of a photon from the congruence of successive wavefront histories under the static Sphere-flow map, replacing an earlier routing through the Algebraic Channel's Killing-vector/Noether conservation of $p_t$.)
\item[(IA2)] *The Algebraic Channel does not need to import Geometric Channel machinery, because once established it is self-sufficient.* The Algebraic Channel is erected from the Principle at the outset --- $dx_4/dt = ic$ integrates to the shadow $x_4 = ict$ (Lemma 5.1.2.1), the shadow forces the Minkowski line element through $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ (Lemma 5.1.2.2), the line element carries its isometry group, and the group carries the variational and operator machinery. From that point forward the Algebraic Channel derives its results *within its own machinery*: the master equation from the four-velocity algebra, the connection from metric compatibility and the cyclic-permutation identity, the curvature from the commutator of covariant derivatives, the field equations from Noether's second theorem and Lovelock's uniqueness. No step of this chain requires a wavefront, a Sphere, or a Huygens construction. There is no intermediate structure the Algebraic Channel must fetch from the Geometric Channel in order to proceed.

That a given Algebraic step *could* be obtained from the Geometric Channel instead --- which follows immediately from the shadow relation, every algebraic fact about the label being recoverable from the expansion that casts it --- does **not** make the Algebraic Channel dependent on the Geometric Channel. Possibility is not necessity. The Geometric route to an Algebraic result is an *available but unused* route: available because the Principle is rich enough to reach the same place twice, unused because the Algebraic Channel already possesses its own. An unexercised alternative creates no derivational dependency.

*Consequence.* The two derivation chains are therefore **fully independent as chains**, not merely disjoint as bookkeeping. Each proceeds from $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the theorem without at any point requiring the other, and $\mathrm{DCD}(T)$ records a structural fact about the Principle rather than an accident of how the proofs happen to have been written. It follows that when a written Algebraic Channel proof is found leaning on a named Geometric structure, the repair is *never* to withdraw the disjointness claim --- the independent Algebraic route always exists, by the self-sufficiency just described --- but to *write that route out explicitly*, exactly as (IA1) requires the Geometric Channel to be supplied with its own Sphere-flow derivation rather than permitted to borrow from its shadow. In both directions the correct response to an apparent entanglement is to derive, not to concede.
\end{itemize}

*What disjointness does and does not assert.* $\mathrm{DCD}(T)$ asserts that the two *derivation chains are fully independent*: each runs from $dx_4/dt = ic$ to $T$ without at any point requiring a named structure of the other. It does **not** assert that the two channels are ontologically independent --- they are not, and (2) above says why: the Algebraic Channel reasons about the integrated shadow of the very expansion the Geometric Channel reasons about directly. These two statements are consistent, and their conjunction is the precise content of the McGucken Duality. Both channels descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$, which is their shared root and is excluded from $M(\Pi_A)$ and $M(\Pi_B)$ by construction; the Algebraic Channel descends further, through the Principle's own integrated record. Yet neither chain, in reaching $T$, must pass through any step of the other.

The evidential force of an overdetermined proof is therefore not that two unrelated principles happen to agree --- there are no two principles --- nor that the same proof has been written twice in different notation. It is that a *single* principle, read along its primary geometric content (the active expansion, the Sphere wavefront) and read along the algebraic content of its own integrated record (the coordinate label, its symmetry group), forces the same theorem through two chains that share no intermediate step and require nothing of one another. That is a statement about the richness of $dx_4/dt = ic$: the Principle is deep enough to reach each theorem of general relativity twice, independently, from the two readings of itself.

**Theorem 17-ter (Content Asymmetry: structural sign-blindness of the Algebraic Channel on the $+ic$ orientation).** *Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote the symmetry group of the integrated coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ --- the Lorentz group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$, the Poincaré algebra $\mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$, the CPT operator, and the internal gauge groups --- these being the structures from which the Algebraic Channel derives its theorems. Then:*

*(a) $\mathcal{G}$ cannot distinguish $+ic$ from $-ic$. The orientation of the McGucken Principle lies in the kernel of the projection that carries the active expansion to its preserved label.*

*(b) Consequently the $+ic$ orientation, and every theorem whose derivation requires it --- the strict Second Law, the arrow of time, the irreversibility of measurement --- cannot descend along the Algebraic Channel alone. They descend along the Geometric Channel, where the expansion is read as an active process rather than as a preserved structure.*

*Proof.* (a) The Algebraic Channel takes as its object the label $x_4 = ict$, the time-integral of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Lemma 5.1.2.1), and derives its theorems from the transformations that *preserve* that label's structure. Now the involution $\iota: i \mapsto -i$ is a field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{R}$: it fixes every real number and reverses the imaginary unit. Under $\iota$ the label $x_4 = ict$ maps to $x_4' = -ict$, and the induced quadratic form is unchanged, since $(-ic)^2 = (ic)^2 = -c^2$. Every structure the Algebraic Channel builds on the label is therefore invariant: the Minkowski line element (Lemma 5.1.2.2 depends on $i^2 = -1$, which $\iota$ preserves), hence its isometry group $\mathrm{SO}^+(1,3)$ and its inhomogeneous extension $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)$, hence the operator algebra and the gauge structures erected upon them. The bare algebra does not select $+i$ over $-i$; that selection is invisible to it. Hence $\mathcal{G}$ is blind to the orientation, which is the claim.

The blindness is not an accident of this particular label but a structural consequence of what a symmetry *is*. A symmetry is by construction a *structure-preserving* automorphism: it declares two configurations equivalent when they differ by a group element, and it retains exactly what is common to the orbit. Preservation is the negation of change. The McGucken Principle, by contrast, asserts a *change*: the fourth dimension is *actively expanding*, at rate $c$, spherically, at every event --- a process, carrying a direction. The passage from the expansion to the symmetry group of its integrated label is therefore a projection from a process to a preservation structure, and a preservation structure has, by its nature, no slot in which to record process. The projection has a non-trivial kernel, and the generative content --- the fact *that* the expansion occurs, its direction, its rate, its ontological status as a real physical happening at every event --- lies in that kernel. What survives the projection is the endpoint; what is annihilated is the expanding.

(b) The $+ic$ orientation is exactly the content annihilated by the projection of (a). The Second Law in its strict geometric form (Theorem 11 of §1.5.2, $dS/dt = \tfrac{3}{2}k_B/t > 0$ with no Poincaré recurrence), the arrow of time, and the irreversibility of measurement each require the orientation as an input: each distinguishes $+ic$ from $-ic$, which by (a) no element of $\mathcal{G}$ can do. Therefore no chain of reasoning conducted entirely within the Algebraic Channel --- entirely within the symmetries of the label --- can produce them. They must, and do, descend along the Geometric Channel, where $dx_4/dt = ic$ is read as the active expansion it is, retaining the direction the label discarded. $\square$

**Remark 17-ter.1 (the shadow metaphor as a theorem, and where it exceeds the cave).** Theorem 17-ter is the shadow-projection relation stated as a proposition with a proof, rather than as an analogy. It is worth noting precisely where it *exceeds* the Platonic figure. In the cave, a static object casts a static shadow, and what the shadow loses is the object's three-dimensional shape --- a loss of *extension*. Here an *active expansion* casts a *symmetry group*, and what is lost is not merely a dimension of shape but the fact that the object was a *process producing something in real time* --- a loss of *generation*. The projection carries a happening into a structure whose defining property is that it does not change. Preservation cannot represent process; that is not a defect of any particular symmetry group but the content of the word.

**Remark 17-ter.2 (the general form: every labelling scheme has a kernel, and the kernel is where the generative content lived).** The asymmetry of Theorem 17-ter is an instance of a pattern with wide currency in mathematics, and recognising the pattern guards against mistaking the label for the thing. A labelling scheme captures snapshots; the process that produced the labels is not in the labels. A coordinate chart on a manifold retains the differential structure and forgets that the manifold was constructed by patching. A cohomology ring retains the topology and forgets the CW-complex that carried it. A character table retains the group's structure and forgets the group *action*. In each case the labelling operation is a projection with a non-trivial kernel, and in each case the kernel is precisely where the generative content resided. The McGucken case is the same operation applied at the foundation of physics: the coordinate label $x_4 = ict$ retains the Lorentzian geometry and forgets the expansion at $ic$ that produced it. The Algebraic Channel is the physics of the label; the Geometric Channel is the physics of the process. Both are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- but only one of them can see the $+$.

# 6. The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem and the Twelve-Test Empirical Triumph {#sec:disjunctive}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

Section 5 established the *structural* case for the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ through the dual-channel architecture: every theorem of GR admits two structurally disjoint derivations from one principle, and the convergence is an overdetermination at the formal level. This Section establishes two further cases that close the inferential loop.

**Section 6.1 (the formal-empirical bridge)** carries the **Disjunctive Forcing Theorem** of [25, §X.7]: a case-exhaustion proof that the *joint* empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity forces the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ uniquely. Five empirically settled strands of physics --- Tsirelson saturation in Bell tests, rotational invariance of entanglement correlations, the absence of any entanglement-distance limit out to satellite scales, Lorentz invariance of $c$ at parts in $10^{-20}$, and wavefront self-replication (Huygens' Principle) --- jointly constrain any candidate dynamics $\Pi$ of the four-dimensional manifold $M$ along three orthogonal structural axes. Five corresponding *failure modes* (Modes A--E) are individually excluded by the empirical record by orders of magnitude. The unique surviving configuration is the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.

**Section 6.2 (the empirical triumph)** reports the twelve-test cosmological record of [21,25]: McGucken takes first place in *every available ranking* against $\Lambda$CDM, $w$CDM, MOND, Verlinde's emergent gravity, and the other dark-sector frameworks, with *zero* free dark-sector parameters.

**Section 6.3 (the MTW resolution)** documents verbatim the passage in Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler [26, *Gravitation*, 1973] in which the authors explicitly identify the failure of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, to extend to curved spacetime and abandon the imaginary fourth coordinate. The McGucken framework supplies what they could not.

## 6.0 The Common-Sense Proof: *Just Think About It*

Before the formal machinery of Section 6.1, the disjunctive forcing of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ stands on its own at the level of plain reasoning. The argument is short enough to fit on a single page and rigorous enough that, once seen, it cannot be unseen. The full formal proof follows in Section 6.1; this section establishes the common-sense skeleton from which the formal proof is the case-exhaustion completion. The six-step argument is the structural prelude that motivates Theorem 26 (Section 6.1.5); the formal proof then closes each conceivable alternative by direct conflict with the experimental record.

### 6.0.1 Step 1: A photon is the same physical thing in any frame

In a Bell experiment at Aspect's lab (1982, meter scale), at the Hensen 2015 Nitrogen-Vacancy experiment (1.3 km, loophole-free), at the Yin 2017 Micius satellite link (1200 km, ground-to-orbit), and in the cosmic-microwave-background photons that have been travelling since recombination 13.8 billion years ago, *the same photon is the same physical thing*. Its propagation is governed by the same physical reality. This is the empirical content of $c$ being a constant of nature: the photon's properties --- its dispersion relation, its polarisation algebra, its wavefront structure --- do not depend on which laboratory, which century, or which gigaparsec-scale separation one is examining. The empirical record of Lorentz invariance from Michelson--Morley (1887) through Müller et al. (2003, $10^{-17}$ terrestrial isotropy) through Vasileiou et al. (2013, $|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-20}$ across cosmological distance) is one century of progressive verification of this single empirical fact.

### 6.0.2 Step 2: The Bell tests measure $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$, the Tsirelson bound, at the maximum allowed by quantum mechanics --- not lower

Hensen et al. 2015 report $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2.42 \pm 0.20$. The Big Bell Test 2018 [Big Bell Test Collaboration] confirms saturation across thirteen laboratories with human-randomness freedom-of-choice closure. The Micius satellite at 1200 km reports $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2.37 \pm 0.09$ [Yin et al. 2017]. *The bound is saturated, not approached.* Whatever the entangled photons share, they share it *perfectly* --- to within the few-percent precision floor of current detectors. The Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt{2}$ is the maximum that quantum mechanics permits, and the experimental record finds saturation at this maximum across thirteen orders of magnitude in spatial separation (from laboratory cm-scale to satellite Mm-scale).

### 6.0.3 Step 3: What do entangled photons share?

The entangled photons were emitted at the *same source event*. By the time they reach the detectors a thousand kilometres apart, what is the geometric thing they have in common? *They sit on the same expanding sphere of light from the source.* That sphere is what each one was riding outward on. Not a metaphorical sphere --- the actual locus of points reachable from the source at the velocity of light in the time since emission. This is what every textbook draws as the *light cone* and what Einstein wrote $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, to encode.

### 6.0.4 Step 3.5: The light cone is the McGucken Sphere, and the "null" terminology was always telling us this

The standard textbook object is the *light cone* --- the locus of spacetime events reachable from a source $p$ by a light ray, the surface $|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0|^2 = c^2(t - t_0)^2$. Every spatial slice of the future light cone at time $t > t_0$ is a 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_0)$ centred at the source. *This is the McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ of Definition 2.* The two are the same geometric object; the McGucken Sphere is the light cone read as the active wavefront of the fourth dimension's expansion. *Identifying them recognises what was already there.*

The vectors from the source to every point on the light cone are called *null vectors* in the standard formalism: they satisfy $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{r} = -c^2(t - t_0)^2 + |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}_0|^2 = 0$ in the Minkowski inner product. The word "null" was chosen carefully. It does *not* mean "zero" in the colloquial sense of nonexistence. It means "zero in some sense" --- specifically, *zero length under the spacetime inner product*. A null vector is a vector with zero spacetime length. Two events connected by a null vector are, by the metric, zero distance apart in spacetime. The events along a photon's worldline are all at zero spacetime distance from one another. *This was not McGucken's invention; it has been the standard formalism since Minkowski 1908.*

What the McGucken framework recognises is the *physical content* of the null formalism that the standard reading had left unconnected. If the radii from $p$ to every point on $M^+_p(t)$ are null vectors of zero spacetime length, then *every point on the McGucken Sphere is at zero spacetime distance from the source*. And since each pair of points on the Sphere can be connected via the source by two zero-length legs, every point on $M^+_p(t)$ is, in the metric sense, at *zero spacetime distance from every other point on the Sphere*. In three spatial dimensions, where we observe these points to be a thousand kilometres apart at the detectors, this zero spacetime separation manifests as what we call *nonlocality*. Two photons at the two detector ends of a Bell experiment are spatially separated by 1200 km in the Micius experiment, but they are at *zero spacetime distance from each other through the source*. The Bell-test correlations at the Tsirelson bound $2\sqrt{2}$ are the empirical signature of this fact. The "spooky action at a distance" that Einstein found so troubling [Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen 1935] *is not action at any distance at all* --- in the metric of spacetime, the distance was always zero.

This is common-sense the moment one accepts both quantum mechanics and relativity. Relativity told us, in the null-vector formalism that Minkowski wrote down in 1908, that the radii of every expanding light sphere are zero-length vectors. Quantum mechanics told us, in the Bell experiments from Aspect 1982 through Micius 2017, that entangled photons share an empirical connection at exactly the strength that this zero-spacetime-distance reading predicts. *Both pieces have been on the table for decades.* The recognition is just that they are the same fact. The fourth dimension's spherically symmetric expansion at $c$ defines a null-separated surface --- the McGucken Sphere, identical to the light cone --- and in three spatial dimensions we observe this null surface as nonlocality.

### 6.0.5 Step 4: A photon at the wavefront "knows about" the wavefront

This is what the Tsirelson saturation is telling us empirically. A photon does not lose its connection to the wavefront simply because it has travelled a long way. *The connection is the wavefront itself.* If the wavefront were a fuzzy thing of finite thickness, the connection would degrade over distance. The connection does not degrade --- Micius at 1200 km saturates the same Tsirelson bound as Aspect's meter-scale 1982 experiment. The wavefront is therefore not fuzzy. *It is a sharp surface* --- a true geometric sphere --- and every point on it shares the wavefront because the wavefront is what it is. The Bell tests are the empirical demonstration of this fact at experimental scales spanning thirteen orders of magnitude.

### 6.0.6 Step 5: The fourth dimension is what is doing the expanding

Look at where the sphere lives. *It lives in the three spatial dimensions.* Its centre is fixed at the source. Its radius grows at the velocity of light. *Something has to be advancing at $c$ to push the sphere outward.* Not the three spatial dimensions --- those are stationary; the sphere lives *in* them. The thing that advances at $c$ is what we have always called the *fourth coordinate*, and the rate of advance is exactly what Einstein wrote $x_4 = ict$ to record. By Einstein's own coordinate, $dx_4/dt = ic$. This is not a postulate. *It is what the geometry of the wavefront is doing.*

### 6.0.7 Step 5.5: Why the four-velocity budget is exactly $c$, finally explained

The four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ --- equivalently $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\mathbf{x}/d\tau|^2 = c^2$ in the McGucken numbering (Section 1.4.1, Lemma 11), with $|dx_4/d\tau| = c\gamma$ the magnitude of the imaginary $x_4$-component and $|d\mathbf{x}/d\tau| = \gamma v$ the spatial-component magnitude --- has been a textbook identity since Minkowski (1908). Every object in spacetime, massive or massless, moves at *exactly* $c$ through spacetime. Not less. Not more. *Exactly $c$.* This has been calculated, used, and taught for over a century, but it has never had a physical explanation. Why $c$? Why not $2c$, or $c/2$, or a value that varies object-to-object? Why exactly the speed of light, the same constant that appears in Maxwell's equations and in $E = mc^2$?

With $dx_4/dt = ic$, the answer becomes obvious. *The budget is $c$ because $c$ is what the fourth dimension is doing.* Every object's motion through spacetime is its participation in the fourth dimension's expansion. The total motion is the expansion itself, and the expansion is at $c$. Three consequences fall out immediately, all previously discussed at greater length in Section 1.4.1 and recapitulated here for the common-sense skeleton:

- **Nothing can move faster than $c$ through space** because the total budget is $c$. To have spatial speed greater than $c$, an object would need to draw on a budget larger than what the fourth dimension is providing --- and the fourth dimension is providing $c$ at every event, no more.

- **Nothing can move slower than $c$ through spacetime**, either. This is the symmetric statement that has been hiding in plain sight. An object at spatial rest is still moving at $c$ --- not at zero. All of its motion is concentrated in the fourth dimension's advance, and the fourth dimension's advance is at $c$. *There is no such thing as "stationary" in spacetime.* Every object is riding the fourth-dimension wavefront outward at the velocity of light. Massive particles at spatial rest are the limit case where the entire budget is in the timelike direction. This is exactly why $E = mc^2$ holds for a stationary mass: the energy is the *kinetic energy of the mass's participation in the fourth dimension's expansion* (Section 1.4.1.6).

- **Lorentz length contraction is rotation into the moving dimension, always accompanied by motion.** When we observe an object moving at high speed and see it foreshortened, we are observing it rotated into the fourth dimension. The rotation is by definition into the moving dimension, which is why foreshortening is always inseparable from motion. There is no foreshortening without motion, and no motion without rotation of the four-velocity into the fourth dimension. The Lorentz transformation is the rotation; the contraction is its spatial signature; the time dilation is its temporal signature. All three are consequences of the four-velocity budget being a fixed-magnitude rotation in $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$, with $x_4 = ict$ contributing the imaginary axis along which rest-frame proper time is recorded. Without the fourth dimension actually expanding at $c$, there is no reason for the rotation magnitude to be fixed at $c$, no reason for the rotation to be inseparable from motion, no reason for length contraction to be precisely $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$. With $dx_4/dt = ic$, all three follow. *The budget was always there; only now does it have a physical reason for being what it is.*

This is the kind of insight Wheeler called for: *the answer that, once seen, makes the old textbook identity finally make sense.*

And so the deeper meaning of $E = mc^2$ is seen. If $x_4$ is expanding past a mass at the velocity of light, the mass is then by definition moving at the velocity of light through spacetime, and thus intuitively would have to have a tremendous energy, as anyone familiar with objects colliding at high velocities would have to agree. *The factor $c^2$ is the algebraic signature of the universal four-momentum-to-energy chain*: at spatial rest, the four-velocity is $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local Lorentz frame (the entire four-budget directed into $x_4$-advance at universal rate $c$), the four-momentum is $p^\mu = m u^\mu = (mc, 0, 0, 0)$, and the energy is the time-component of four-momentum scaled by $c$: $E = c p^0 = m c^2$. Both factors of $c$ trace to the McGucken Principle: one from the universal rate of $x_4$-advance setting $u^0 = c$ at rest, one from the standard relativistic-mechanics convention $E = c p^0$. A kilogram of any matter, sitting on a desk, is at the full four-budget magnitude $c$ through spacetime, and the energy is $E = m c^2 = 9 \times 10^{16}$ joules. The energy was never hidden; it is the algebraic record of the mass's *compulsory participation in the universal $x_4$-expansion*. Einstein wrote the equation in 1905. The McGucken Principle supplies the structural content for why the right side carries two factors of the universal rate $c$.

### 6.0.8 Step 6: Just think about it

The fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner from every spacetime event. Massive particles at spatial rest are at absolute rest in the spatial three and are riding the fourth dimension outward at $c$. Photons are riding the wavefront, which is to say they are at absolute rest *on* the fourth dimension, surfing it (Ontology case (2) of the four-fold ontology, Memory of the corpus). The reason $E = mc^2$ is that the energy of a stationary mass is the energy of its participation in the fourth dimension's expansion. The reason entangled photons remain correlated at arbitrary spatial separation is that they share the wavefront --- the same spherical surface of the source --- and the wavefront is a single thing at zero spacetime distance from itself. The reason the cosmic microwave background has a preferred frame is that the universe-scale wavefront from the Big Bang is a definite spherical surface, and we move with respect to it. The reason quantum mechanics has its mysterious phase factor $e^{i\varphi}$ is that $\varphi$ is the angle of the perpendicular fourth axis. The reason the imaginary unit $i$ appears throughout physics is that the fourth dimension is perpendicular to the spatial three, and $i$ is the algebraic record of perpendicularity. The reason there is an arrow of time is that the fourth dimension advances; it does not retreat.

The Bell tests measuring $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$, the Micius bound at 1200 km, the GRB 090510 photon-timing isotropy to one part in $10^{20}$, the existence of light propagation at all --- these are five empirical demonstrations of the same single fact, that the fourth dimension is doing exactly what $dx_4/dt = ic$ says it is doing. *Anything else, and at least one of those experiments would have come out differently by orders of magnitude.* The mathematical body of Section 6.1 below formalises this commonsense argument as a case-exhaustion theorem: it classifies every alternative to "the fourth dimension is expanding at $c$ in a spherically symmetric manner from every event" into five exhaustive failure modes (A--E), and closes each one by direct conflict with one of the five experiments named above. *But the argument is right in the commonsense form.* Once you see what the wavefront is doing geometrically, you cannot un-see it. Einstein's $x_4 = ict$ is the integrated record of the fact. Wheeler's invocation that "behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it $\ldots$ we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?" applies precisely here.

*The fourth dimension is expanding.*

### 6.0.9 Why Nobody Saw This Before: The Historical Concealment of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel / $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel Pieces in Each Step of the Common-Sense Argument

A natural question arises: if the disjunctive-forcing argument is so direct --- if the light cone is the McGucken Sphere, if null vectors are zero-spacetime-distance vectors, if entangled photons share a single wavefront, if the Bell tests are the empirical signature of this --- *why did nobody see this before?* The pieces have been on the table for over a century: Minkowski's null cone (1908), Einstein's $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, coordinate (1908-1912), Eddington's "rotation into the fourth dimension" reading of Lorentz contraction (1920), the Wick rotation $t \mapsto -i\tau$ (1954), the Bell-test correlations from Aspect 1982 through Micius 2017. Each piece, individually, has been in the standard literature for decades. The recognition that they are the same fact is what was missing. This subsection traces the *structural* reasons for the historical concealment, and identifies for each step of the common-sense argument which McGucken channel (A or B) carries that step, and which channel was hidden in the standard pedagogy.

### The structural reason for the historical miss: two disjoint communities, two disjoint formalisms

The deep reason the disjunctive-forcing argument was not constructed before McGucken (1989--present) is that it *requires both quantum mechanics and relativity simultaneously*, in a register that was not available to either community in isolation. The relativity community, from Minkowski 1908 forward, had the null-vector formalism --- zero-spacetime-distance vectors on the light cone --- but lacked empirical access to entanglement correlations that would reveal what the zero-distance reading was telling them. The quantum-mechanics community, from Bell 1964 forward, had the empirical correlations but operated in a formalism (Hilbert-space algebraic structure) that had progressively abandoned the imaginary fourth coordinate $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The migration in graduate gravitation textbooks from $x^4 = ict$ to $x^0 = ct$ (documented in §6.3 and §6.4) erased the algebraic visibility of the perpendicularity of the timelike axis to the three spatial axes --- the very feature that the null-vector reading would later need.

Both pieces were on the table for decades, but in *different communities* who were not talking to each other in this register. The relativity community read null vectors as "light rays" and forgot the *metric content* (zero spacetime distance). The quantum-mechanics community read Bell-test correlations as "nonlocality" and forgot that the *spacetime metric makes the distance zero*. The recognition that the two readings are the same fact required someone fluent in both formalisms simultaneously, attentive to the metric content of null vectors, and willing to read $x_4 = ict$ as a *dynamical* statement $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than a static coordinate label.

### The seven near-misses of the historical record

**Einstein 1908--1912** wrote $x_4 = ict$ explicitly in his Zürich notebooks and the 1912 Manuscript on the Special Theory of Relativity [Einstein 1912]. He had the *integrated* identity. He never wrote its time-derivative $dx_4/dt = ic$. The reason: the coordinate identification served his purpose --- it made the metric signature work out --- and the dynamical reading was not necessary for what he was doing. Einstein was making spacetime *intervals* work; he was not asking what the fourth coordinate was *doing* dynamically. The dynamical reading was one step away and was not taken.

**Minkowski 1908** [Minkowski 1908] introduced "Raum und Zeit" with the unified spacetime formalism and the null cone. He wrote down null vectors with zero spacetime length. But Minkowski's framework was *geometrically static* --- the four-dimensional manifold was a frozen block (the "block universe"), not an actively-expanding structure. The light cone was the locus of events reachable by light, not the wavefront of an active expansion. *The null-vector formalism was there; the dynamical reading was not.*

**Eddington 1920** [55] got the closest of any pre-McGucken figure. In *Space, Time, and Gravitation* he wrote about Lorentz contraction as "rotation into the fourth dimension." He saw the *geometric content* of length contraction at the rotation level. But his fourth dimension was *static* --- a coordinate axis, not a moving dimension. So the rotation-into-the-fourth-dimension reading produced only the contraction, not the universal motion of every massive object at $c$ through spacetime. Eddington was one structural ingredient --- the dynamical content $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- away from the full picture, and never took the step.

**The Wick-rotation lineage (Wick 1954, Schwinger, Symanzik, Osterwalder-Schrader)**: The substitution $t \mapsto -i\tau$ was treated as a *formal analytic-continuation trick* on a complex $t$-plane [56], not as a coordinate identification on the real manifold $M_G$ with $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The physical content of $x_4$ was forgotten; the imaginary unit $i$ was reduced to an algebraic device. Theorem 4 of this book (the McGucken-Wick Rotation Theorem) restores the physical content: $\tau = x_4/c$ is a real coordinate identification on $M_G$, not a complex-analytic device.

**MTW 1973** [Misner-Thorne-Wheeler 1973]: Explicitly identified the failure of $x_4 = ict$ to extend to curved spacetime and *abandoned* the imaginary fourth coordinate. The textbook record from 1973 onward simply forgot the imaginary fourth coordinate existed. The MTW resolution is documented verbatim in §6.3 below; the McGucken framework supplies what MTW abandoned by promoting $dx_4/dt = ic$ from a static coordinate label to a dynamical physical principle.

**Greene 1999, 2004** [Greene 1999, 2004]: Came close with "everything moves at $c$ through spacetime" but could not supply a mechanism. Hand-wavy because Greene did not have $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a foundational principle --- only the algebraic consequence (the four-velocity budget identity). The structural diagnosis is in §1.4.1.2 above: Greene named the phenomenon without supplying the underlying physical content.

**The Bell-test community (Aspect 1982 through Yin 2017)**: Measured the empirical content --- Tsirelson saturation at arbitrary spatial separations --- but read it through the lens of "nonlocality" rather than "zero spacetime distance on the wavefront." The reading "spooky action at a distance" hides the structural fact: in the spacetime metric, the distance between the entangled photons through the source was always zero, and what Bell-test correlations measure is precisely this zero-distance connectivity, not action over any distance at all. The Bell-test community had the empirical signature of the McGucken framework's prediction but read it through a formalism (Hilbert-space nonlocality) that had abandoned the relevant spacetime-metric content.
