### What was hidden in each step's historical pedagogy

**Step 3 (Geometric Channel)** was hidden in the migration of QM pedagogy from the wavefront-realist reading of de Broglie 1924, Schrödinger 1926, and Peebles 1992 to the operator-algebra reading of von Neumann 1932 and the Copenhagen Interpretation 1927. The Copenhagen shift treated the wavefunction as a calculation device rather than as a physical wavefront; the geometric-propagation content was abandoned at the level of pedagogical framing. The Feynman path integral 1948 partially restored Geometric Channel (sum over paths, each path contributing $e^{iS/\hbar}$, with the iterated-Sphere structure visible in the path integral), but Feynman's reading was treated as an alternative formulation rather than as a structural twin of the standard Hilbert-space formalism. Peebles 1992's spherical-wavefront reading of the photon survived but was never developed into a foundational principle.

**Step 3.5 (Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel identification)** was hidden because the two channels were treated, in standard pedagogy, as if they were the same thing. The light cone (Algebraic Channel's null-vector content from Minkowski metric) and the wavefront (Geometric Channel's geometric-propagation content from Huygens-Feynman lineage) were both presented but never identified as the *same geometric object* read in two different formal languages. The standard pedagogy would say "the light cone is where light goes" (Algebraic Channel reading of the metric) and "the wavefront is the locus of constant phase" (Geometric Channel reading of wave propagation), without recognising that these are two readings of one object on the McGucken framework's $M_G$.

**Step 4 (Geometric Channel)** was hidden by the Copenhagen-Interpretation shift to "measurement collapse" language, which abandoned the wavefront-as-physical-object reading. The Bell tests starting from Aspect 1982 measured correlations that empirically demonstrated the wavefront's sharpness and single-thing nature, but the dominant interpretation framework (Copenhagen, "nonlocality," "spooky action") obscured the wavefront-realist reading. The reading "the wavefront is a single sharp surface and entangled photons share it because the surface is what it is" was structurally accessible only to wavefront-realist interpretations (de Broglie-Bohm, Peebles' spherical-wavefront reading), which were marginalised in the dominant pedagogy.

**Step 5 (Geometric Channel)** was hidden by MTW 1973's abandonment of $x_4 = ict$, documented verbatim in §6.3 below. The MTW resolution explicitly identifies the failure of $x_4 = ict$ to extend to curved spacetime and discards the imaginary fourth coordinate. The downstream textbook tradition (Wald 1984, Carroll 2004, Schutz 2009, Weinberg 1972) did not even engage the issue --- they migrated to the real coordinate $x^0 = ct$ without comment. The dynamical reading $dx_4/dt = ic$ was structurally inaccessible because the underlying coordinate $x_4 = ict$ had been removed from the formalism. The McGucken framework restores it by promoting it from a static coordinate label to a dynamical principle.

**Step 5.5 (Algebraic Channel)** was hidden by the *constraint-imposition reading* of the four-velocity budget identity (MTW, Wald, Carroll), documented in §1.4.1.2 above. The reading treats $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ as a *normalisation convention* defining proper time, providing no structural account of why the magnitude is exactly $c$. The Greene 1999 reading came closest to identifying it as a kinematic content of motion at $c$ through spacetime, but lacked the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ to supply a mechanism. The Algebraic Channel reading of the four-velocity budget as the algebraic content of the universe's fourth-dimension motion was structurally invisible until the McGucken Principle was articulated.

**Step 6 (both channels together)** was hidden by the absence of any dual-channel architecture in pre-McGucken pedagogy. Standard graduate textbooks (MTW, Wald, Carroll, Schutz, Weinberg) develop general relativity through a *single* derivation chain --- either the algebraic-symmetry route (Einstein-Hilbert action, Lovelock uniqueness) or the geometric-propagation route (Huygens, Jacobson thermodynamic chain). No standard textbook before McGucken (2026) develops GR through *two structurally disjoint* derivations from one principle. The dual-channel architecture is the load-bearing structural feature of the McGucken framework, and its absence in standard pedagogy is the structural reason that the dual-channel signature of the common-sense argument was invisible.

### The conclusion: structural concealment is concealable

The pieces of the disjunctive-forcing argument were on the table for over a century. Minkowski 1908 supplied the null-vector formalism. Einstein 1912 supplied $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Eddington 1920 supplied the rotation-into-the-fourth-dimension reading of Lorentz contraction. Aspect 1982 supplied the Tsirelson-saturation empirical signature. Bell 1964 supplied the empirical-test framework. Vasileiou 2013 supplied the Lorentz-invariance precision bound. Huygens 1690 supplied the iterated-Sphere structure under the name *Huygens' Principle*. Each piece was a Nobel-Prize-worthy contribution at the time of its appearance. The recognition that the pieces *fit together* required:

(i) Reading the null-vector formalism as the metric content of zero spacetime distance (Algebraic Channel; recovered by McGucken from the post-1908 standard literature);

(ii) Reading the Bell-test correlations as the empirical signature of zero spacetime distance on the wavefront (Geometric Channel; the wavefront-realist reading suppressed by the Copenhagen Interpretation);

(iii) Promoting Einstein's $x_4 = ict$ from a static coordinate to the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the McGucken step; not in any standard pre-McGucken source);

(iv) Recognising that the dual-channel architecture is *load-bearing* --- that GR and QM both descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ through two structurally disjoint theorem chains (Sections 5 and 6 of this Introduction; the central architectural insight of the McGucken corpus).

The McGucken framework's contribution is *not* the individual pieces, all of which were known. The contribution is the recognition that the pieces fit together along two structurally disjoint chains from one principle, with the disjointness being itself an overdetermined proof of the principle's physical reality. Wheeler's prediction --- "behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it $\ldots$ we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?" --- applies precisely here: once the pieces are seen to fit, the question "why didn't anyone see this before?" answers itself. The pieces were in *different communities*, *different formalisms*, and *different pedagogies*; the synthesis required someone fluent in all of them simultaneously, attentive to the metric content of null vectors, willing to read $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, dynamically, and bold enough to propose a dual-channel architecture for the entire foundational structure of physics.

### 6.0.10 Both Relativity and Quantum Mechanics Require Nonlocality: The Dual-Channel Crystallisation

The structural content of the recognition crystallises into a single dual-channel reading that captures what both relativity and quantum mechanics, jointly, have been telling us for over a century:

> *Relativity is $x_4$'s nonlocality, read along the Algebraic Channel.*
>
> *$x_4$'s nonlocality is relativity's null structure, read along the Geometric Channel.*

This is the dual-channel statement of the Bell-test / null-vector identification of §6.0.3 in its most compact form. Each line is a complete statement; together they declare the same fact in both registers.

**Reading the first line (Algebraic Channel).** The Algebraic Channel content of relativity --- the Minkowski metric, the Lorentzian inner product $\eta_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu$, the null condition $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{r} = 0$ on light-cone radii --- says that radii from any spacetime event $p$ to every point of its future light cone are null vectors of *zero spacetime length*. In the algebraic-symmetry register, this is what null-vector formalism asserts: two events connected by a null vector are zero distance apart in the spacetime metric, even though they are spatially separated in any spatial slice. The relativistic null structure *is* nonlocality, expressed in the Algebraic Channel vocabulary of the metric. The Algebraic Channel reading of "nonlocality" is the Algebraic Channel reading of "null structure": same fact, same machinery, called by two names that the standard literature has kept separated by community boundaries (the relativity community using "null cone," the quantum-foundations community using "nonlocality") rather than by structural distinction.

**Reading the second line (Geometric Channel).** The Geometric Channel content of $x_4$'s nonlocality --- the active expansion of the fourth dimension at rate $ic$ generating the McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ at every event, with every point of $M^+_p(t)$ sharing the same Compton phase along its radial null shadow from the apex $p$ (Lemma 2.2 of the disjunctive-forcing argument, §6.1 below) --- says that every point of the wavefront is at zero spacetime distance from the source, and through the source from every other point on the wavefront. In the geometric-propagation register, this is the iterated-Sphere wavefront whose every event hosts a fresh Sphere at rate $c$, with the Bell-correlation singlet $|\Psi^-\rangle$ shared identically across all detector positions $q \in M^+_p(t)$. The Geometric Channel reading of "$x_4$'s nonlocality" is the Geometric Channel reading of "relativity's null structure": same fact, same machinery, expressed in the wavefront-on-the-Sphere vocabulary.

**Cross-channel co-derivation.** Each line is *derived from the other* through the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 106 of [4], imported from [3CH, Theorem 1]). The Algebraic Channel's null-vector content (zero spacetime length of light-cone radii in the Minkowski metric) is the algebraic-symmetry image of the Geometric Channel's Sphere-uniformity content (constant Compton phase on the wavefront surface from every apex). The two derivations share no intermediate machinery: Algebraic Channel uses the Minkowski inner product and the null condition $\mathbf{r} \cdot \mathbf{r} = 0$; Geometric Channel uses the iterated-Sphere structure of Proposition 3 and the Sphere-surface Compton-phase identity of Lemma 2.2 (§6.1 below). The convergence on the same empirical content --- Bell-test correlations at Tsirelson saturation $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$ across spatial separations from laboratory cm-scale to satellite Mm-scale --- is the cross-channel verification of the joint principle.

**The compact statement of what both theories are saying.** Once the dual-channel crystallisation is stated, the empirical record of the last century becomes one fact in two voices. Aspect 1982, Hensen 2015, the Big Bell Test 2018, and Yin 2017 are the Geometric Channel (quantum-mechanical) empirical reading; Michelson--Morley 1887, Eddington 1919, Vasileiou 2013, and the operational performance of GPS are the Algebraic Channel (relativistic) empirical reading. Both empirical bodies, separated by community boundary and by historical pedagogy, are observations of the *same active expansion* of the fourth dimension at the velocity of light. Relativity sees this expansion as the null structure of spacetime; quantum mechanics sees this expansion as the nonlocality of the singlet wavefront. The McGucken framework supplies the underlying object --- $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- that both theories are describing in their respective registers. The empirical impossibility of separating "nonlocality" from "null structure" is the structural mark that they are the same fact; the dual-channel crystallisation is the statement of that mark.

**Empirical and structural integration.** The crystallisation closes the structural gap between general relativity and quantum mechanics that has stood since Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen 1935. Einstein's discomfort with "spooky action at a distance" was the symptom of reading Bell-correlation content through a formalism that had abandoned the null-vector metric content. The reconciliation is automatic in the dual-channel architecture: there is no action at any distance, because in the metric of spacetime the distance was always zero; the "spookiness" was the artefact of computing the correlation in spatial-distance units while the wavefront uses spacetime-distance units, and the two differ by the null condition. Reading either channel restores the consistency: Algebraic Channel reads "the null structure of relativity is the empirical content of nonlocality," and the Geometric Channel reads "the wavefront-on-the-Sphere of quantum mechanics is the geometric content of the null cone." Both readings are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

The full formal proof of the disjunctive forcing (Theorem 26 of §6.1.5 below) now closes the case-exhaustion: every structural alternative to $dx_4/dt = ic$ violates either the Algebraic Channel reading of the null structure (Lorentz-invariance violation, GRB 090510 bound) or the Geometric Channel reading of nonlocality (Tsirelson saturation violation, Bell-test bound) or both. The dual-channel crystallisation provides the structural skeleton that the case-exhaustion completes formally.

## 6.1 The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem

The proof is structured as a case-exhaustion theorem: enumerate the possible alternatives to $dx_4/dt = ic$ along three orthogonal axes, identify each as a *failure mode*, and exclude each failure mode by an empirically settled fact.

### 6.1.1 The five empirical strands

Five empirical strands constrain any candidate dynamics $\Pi$ of the four-dimensional manifold $M$:

**(i) Tsirelson saturation.** Bell-inequality experiments [Aspect 1982, Tittel et al. 1998, Pan group 2017, modern loophole-free Bell tests] measure the CHSH (Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt) correlation function and find violation of the classical Bell bound $|\mathrm{CHSH}| \leq 2$ up to the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt{2}$. Loophole-free Bell tests confirm saturation within a few percent of the maximal value.

**(ii) Rotational invariance of entanglement.** The angular dependence of entanglement correlations is the universal $E(\hat{a}, \hat{b}) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$, isotropic under $\mathrm{SO}(3)$, with no preferred spatial direction across all laboratory orientations tested.

**(iii) No entanglement-distance limit.** Bell tests at increasing spatial separation --- from meter scale (Aspect 1982) to 10 km (Tittel et al. 1998 across Lake Geneva) to $1200$ km (Pan group 2017, Micius satellite) --- continue to find $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$ within experimental error.

**(iv) Lorentz invariance of $c$.** The speed of light is isotropic and frame-invariant to the precision of gamma-ray-burst timing constraints [Vasileiou et al. 2013, GRB 090510]: $|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-20}$ across photon energies differing by an order of magnitude over gigaparsec distances.

**(v) Wavefront self-replication.** Every point on a wavefront radiates secondary spherical wavelets that combine to form the future wavefront --- Huygens' Principle [1690, formalized by Kirchhoff 1882]. Without this property, the wave equation $\Box \psi = 0$ admits no Green's-function solution and the manifold cannot extend past one Planck tick.

### 6.1.2 Classification of alternatives: three orthogonal structural axes

**Definition 18 (Classification of candidate $\Pi$).** Any candidate dynamics $\Pi$ of the fourth coordinate is classified along three orthogonal structural axes:
*Axis ($\alpha$): rate of $x_4$-advance.* The rate $dx_4/dt$ is either (a) direction-independent of magnitude $c$, or (b) direction-dependent.

*Axis ($\beta$): surface assignment.* The function $q \mapsto x_4(q; p)$ on the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_t(p)$ is either (a) the constant zero, (b) a stochastic variable with positive variance, (c) a deterministic non-constant angular function, (d) extended to a finite-thickness shell with smooth radial variation, or (e) undefined because forward propagation fails.

*Axis ($\gamma$): orientation.* The sign in $dx_4/dt = \pm ic$ is the foundational orientation of the Principle itself. It is *not* fixed by the thermodynamic arrow: the arrow is *derived from* the $+ic$ orientation as the Geometric Second Law (Theorem 11 of §1.5.2 of this Introduction; downstream Generalised Second Law $dS_{\text{ext}} + dS_H \geq 0$ at black-hole horizons, Proposition 15.2.6.1 / Theorem 15.5.2 of Chapter 15), and so cannot be what fixes it. The forward orientation $+ic$ is empirically anchored by the sign-asymmetric GPS asymmetry (Theorem 38, with the sign argument carried at Corollary 38.1 of §20.2: the budget partition and the dilation factor are both *even* in the rate and so cannot fix the orientation, whereas the GPS offset is *linear* in it --- an accumulation with a direction --- and the pre-launch correction, applied in one direction only and operational since 1978, measures the sign of $d\tau/dt$ and hence of the $x_4$-advance) --- directional where strands (i)--(v) are sign-symmetric --- and is reached independently from the deductive special-relativistic side; the thermodynamic arrow then follows as its downstream theorem.

The McGucken configuration is the unique alternative in which $\alpha$ =(a), $\beta$ =(a), and $\gamma = +$. Every other configuration is a failure mode.
### 6.1.3 The five failure modes

**Definition 19 (The five failure modes).** Departures from the McGucken configuration along axes ($\alpha$) and ($\beta$) are classified exhaustively as:

- *Mode A (random scatter):* with $\beta$-axis case (b): $x_4(q; p)$ is an i.i.d. random variable across surface points, mean $0$, variance $\sigma^2_{x_4} > 0$.
- *Mode B (systematic gradient):* with $\beta$-axis case (c): $x_4(q; p) = f(\hat{n})$, a deterministic non-constant function of the spatial direction $\hat{n}$ from $p$ to $q$.
- *Mode C (finite thickness):* with $\beta$-axis case (d): the surface is a shell of finite extent in $x_4$, with $x_4(q; p)$ varying smoothly with characteristic correlation length $L_{\mathrm{coh}} > 0$.
- *Mode D (rate-anisotropy):* with $\alpha$-axis case (b): the rate $dx_4/dt = ic(\hat{n})$ is direction-dependent.
- *Mode E (no self-replication):* with $\beta$-axis case (e): surface points do not generate new McGucken Spheres; Huygens' Principle fails.

**Lemma 20 (Exhaustiveness of Modes A--E).** Every configuration $\Pi$ of the fourth coordinate that differs from the McGucken Principle along axis ($\alpha$) or ($\beta$) is a member of, or a finite combination of, Modes A--E.

*Proof.* We separate axis ($\alpha$) and axis ($\beta$) cases.

*Axis $(\beta)$ alternatives.* A candidate surface-assignment function $q \mapsto x_4(q; p) : \Sigma_t(p) \to \mathbb{C}$ on the McGucken Sphere of apex $p$ falls into exactly one of the following four exhaustive cases by elementary set-theoretic disjunction:

(a) $x_4(q; p) \equiv 0$ identically on $\Sigma_t(p)$ --- this is the McGucken-Principle case, excluded by hypothesis (the candidate $\Pi$ differs from the McGucken Principle).

(b) $x_4(q; p)$ is defined everywhere on $\Sigma_t(p)$ as a random variable with positive variance --- Mode A (random scatter).

(c) $x_4(q; p)$ is defined everywhere on $\Sigma_t(p)$ as a deterministic non-constant function. The deterministic non-constancy occurs either at fixed sphere-radius (angular dependence: $x_4(q; p) = f(\hat{n})$ where $\hat{n}$ is the spatial direction from $p$ to $q$) --- Mode B (systematic gradient) --- or across a radial extent (the surface is replaced by a shell of finite thickness in $x_4$ with smooth radial variation) --- Mode C (finite thickness).

(d) $x_4(q; p)$ is not defined everywhere on $\Sigma_t(p)$ --- Mode E (no self-replication: surface points do not generate new McGucken Spheres).

These four cases (a)--(d) are *exhaustive and mutually exclusive* by the law of excluded middle applied to the propositions \{"$x_4(q; p) \equiv 0$"\}, \{"$x_4(q; p)$ everywhere defined with positive variance"\}, \{"$x_4(q; p)$ everywhere defined, deterministic, non-constant"\}, \{"$x_4(q; p)$ not everywhere defined"\}. The McGucken case is excluded by hypothesis; the remaining three non-McGucken cases align with Modes A, B/C, and E respectively.

*Axis $(\alpha)$ alternatives.* The rate $dx_4/dt$ is by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i) either (a$_\alpha$) direction-independent of magnitude $c$ (the McGucken case) or (b$_\alpha$) direction-dependent. Case (b$_\alpha$) is Mode D (rate-anisotropy). The axis ($\alpha$) classification is orthogonal to axis ($\beta$): direction-dependence of the rate is a property of how $x_4$-expansion proceeds, structurally distinct from the variation of the surface-assignment value.

*Finite combinations.* A candidate $\Pi$ that differs from the McGucken Principle along both axis ($\alpha$) and axis ($\beta$) is a *combination* of two failure modes (one along each axis). The combinations $\{A \cap D\}$, $\{B \cap D\}$, $\{C \cap D\}$, $\{E \cap D\}$ inherit the empirical exclusions of their component modes: if any single component mode is excluded by the empirical record, the combination is excluded. The lemma's phrase "finite combination of Modes A--E" covers all such finite intersections of axis-$(\alpha)$ and axis-$(\beta)$ alternatives.

Hence every non-McGucken configuration falls into Mode A, B, C, D, E, or a finite combination thereof. $\square$

### 6.1.4 The five failure-mode exclusions

Each failure mode is excluded by one of the five empirical strands.

**Proposition 21 (Mode A excluded by Tsirelson saturation).** Under Mode A with Sphere-locality deviation field $\delta : M^+_{p_s}(t) \to \mathbb{R}$ i.i.d. Gaussian, mean $0$, variance $\sigma^2_\delta > 0$, the CHSH operator on the singlet state shared via the McGucken Sphere of the source event satisfies
$$|\mathrm{CHSH}|_{\mathrm{Mode\, A}} \;=\; 2\sqrt{2} \cdot \exp(-\sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2),$$
and two-slit interference visibility satisfies $V_{\mathrm{Mode\, A}} = \exp(-\sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2)$. The empirical record bounds $\sigma_\delta \lesssim 0.226\, \hbar$.
*Proof (Compton-phase reading).* The Sphere-locality deviation field is the per-point excess proper-time accumulation along the radial null shadow relative to the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$-foundational value (identically zero under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$):
$$\delta(q; p_s) \;:=\; m c^2 \cdot \Delta\tau_{\mathrm{shadow}}(q; p_s),$$
with units of action. Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and Sphere-surface Compton-phase uniformity (the foundational Lemma 2.2 of the disjunctive-forcing argument: every point of $M^+_{p_s}(t)$ carries the same Compton phase $\Phi(q; p_s) = \exp(-i m c^2 \Delta\tau/\hbar) = 1$ along the radial null shadow), $\delta(q; p_s) \equiv 0$ identically.

Under Mode A, $\delta$ is i.i.d. Gaussian with positive variance. The detector-pair phase difference $\Delta\Phi := -(\delta(q_A; p_s) - \delta(q_B; p_s))/\hbar$ has variance $\mathrm{Var}(\Delta\Phi) = 2\sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2$. The standard Gaussian characteristic-function identity $\langle e^{iX} \rangle = \exp(-\mathrm{Var}(X)/2)$ for $X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, s^2)$ gives the dephasing factor $\langle e^{i\Delta\Phi} \rangle = \exp(-\sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2)$. The singlet correlation acquires this multiplicative dephasing factor, yielding the suppressed CHSH formula above. The bound: Hensen et al. 2015 reports $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2.42 \pm 0.20$, Big Bell Test 2018 confirms saturation. Requiring the McGucken value to remain within $\sim 5\%$ of $2\sqrt{2}$:
$$\exp(-\sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2) > 0.95 \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \sigma^2_\delta/\hbar^2 < -\ln 0.95 = 0.0513 \;\Longleftrightarrow\; \sigma_\delta \lesssim 0.226\, \hbar.$$

The McGucken value $\sigma_\delta = 0$ is the strict identity. The empirical bound is many orders of magnitude tighter than any "noisy fourth-dimension" hypothesis would predict, foreclosing Mode A. $\square$

*Remark (postulate honesty).* The i.i.d.\ Gaussian distribution is the defining feature of Mode A, not a derived consequence. The Gaussian is the maximum-entropy distribution on $\mathbb{R}$ at fixed variance $\sigma^2_\delta$ and mean $0$. Other zero-mean distributions with the same variance produce visibility/CHSH suppression factors of the same magnitude with at-most exponentially small corrections via the cumulant expansion $\langle e^{iX} \rangle = \exp(-\sigma^2/2 + \kappa_4/24 + \ldots)$ with higher cumulants $\kappa_n \to 0$ in the Gaussian limit. The bound is therefore conservative for the full family of Mode-A distributions.

**Structural Reading 1 (Mode B excluded by rotational invariance).** Under Mode B with $\delta(q; p_s) = g \cos\theta(q; p_s)$ a deterministic dipole in the spatial direction $\hat{n}(q; p_s)$, the spin-correlation function acquires the orientation-dependent phase factor $\exp(i g (\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)/\hbar)$, making $|\mathrm{CHSH}|$ oscillate with apparatus orientation relative to the gradient axis. The empirical record across decades and laboratory orientations finds no such anisotropy at the few-percent level, bounding $|g| \lesssim 3 \times 10^{-36}\, \mathrm{J \cdot s}$.

*Proof.* The Mode-B deviation field $\delta(q; p_s) = g \cos\theta(q; p_s)$, with $\theta$ the angle between $\hat{n}(q; p_s)$ and a fixed gradient axis $\hat{e}$, generates a per-detector phase shift in the Compton-phase reading
$$\Phi_{\mathrm{Mode\,B}}(q; p_s) = -\frac{\delta(q; p_s)}{\hbar} = -\frac{g \cos\theta(q; p_s)}{\hbar}.$$
For the two-detector measurement at events $q_1, q_2$ on the McGucken Sphere of the source $p_s$, the relative phase $\Delta\Phi := \Phi_{\mathrm{Mode\,B}}(q_1) - \Phi_{\mathrm{Mode\,B}}(q_2) = -(g/\hbar)(\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)$. The singlet-state CHSH correlation $E(\hat a, \hat b) = -\cos\theta_{ab}$ acquires the orientation-dependent multiplicative phase factor $\exp(i\Delta\Phi)$, modifying the CHSH operator value to
$$|\mathrm{CHSH}|_{\mathrm{Mode\, B}} = 2\sqrt{2} \cdot |\cos(g (\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2)/\hbar)|$$
on the optimally aligned axes (taking the real part of the dephasing factor; the imaginary part contributes a sub-leading correction). The expression oscillates with the projection $\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2$, which depends on the apparatus orientation relative to the gradient axis $\hat e$. *Anisotropy bound:* requiring that no anisotropy at the few-percent ($\sim 5\%$) precision level be observed across the laboratory rotations covered in the experimental record, one needs
$$|g/\hbar| \cdot |\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2|_{\max} \lesssim 0.05.$$
With $|\cos\theta_1 - \cos\theta_2|_{\max} = 2$ (cosines range over $[-1, 1]$), this gives $|g|/\hbar \lesssim 0.025$, equivalently $|g| \lesssim 2.6 \times 10^{-36}$ J$\cdot$s. Rounding conservatively to the order-of-magnitude foreclosure: $|g| \lesssim 3 \times 10^{-36}$ J$\cdot$s.

The strict McGucken value is $g = 0$ (no anisotropy at all, $\delta \equiv 0$). The empirical bound is many orders of magnitude tighter than any "gradient fourth-dimension" hypothesis would predict at scales near $\hbar$, foreclosing Mode B. $\square$

**Structural Reading 2 (Mode C excluded by satellite Bell tests).** Under Mode C with characteristic correlation length $L_{\mathrm{coh}}$, the CHSH function decays in vacuum as $|\mathrm{CHSH}|_{\mathrm{Mode\, C}}(L) = 2\sqrt{2} \cdot \exp(-L/L_{\mathrm{coh}})$. The Yin et al. 2017 Micius satellite Bell test at $L = 1200$ km, finding $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2.37 \pm 0.09$, forces $L_{\mathrm{coh}} > 2 \times 10^7$ m by the 5\%-suppression criterion (equivalently $> 3.7 \times 10^7$ m by the experimental-uncertainty criterion; see proof). The bound is many orders of magnitude above any candidate physical length scale (de Broglie $\sim 10^{-7}$ m, Compton $\sim 10^{-13}$ m, Planck $\sim 10^{-35}$ m). No physical thickness scale lives anywhere near this; Mode C is closed by orders of magnitude.

*Proof.* The geometric content of finite $x_4$-thickness: surface points separated by spatial distance $|q_1 - q_2| > L_{\mathrm{coh}}$ carry $x_4$-coordinate differences of order the thickness scale, dephasing coherent correlations. This decay is *intrinsic* --- it persists in perfect vacuum, independent of environmental coupling. We derive the bound on $L_{\mathrm{coh}}$ from the Micius observation $|\mathrm{CHSH}|_{\mathrm{obs}} = 2.37 \pm 0.09$ at $L = 1200$ km, in two equivalent forms.

*Form (a): 5\% suppression criterion.* Requiring that the exponential decay $\exp(-L/L_{\mathrm{coh}})$ remain within 5\% of unity (i.e., the observed CHSH stays within 5\% of the Tsirelson maximum):
\begin{align*}
\exp(-L/L_{\mathrm{coh}}) > 0.95 \;&\Longleftrightarrow\; L/L_{\mathrm{coh}} < -\ln(0.95) = 0.0513 \\
&\Longleftrightarrow\; L_{\mathrm{coh}} > 1200\,\mathrm{km}/0.0513 = 2.34 \times 10^7\,\mathrm{m}.
\end{align*}

*Form (b): experimental-uncertainty criterion.* Requiring that the deviation from the Tsirelson value $2\sqrt{2}$ remain below the experimental uncertainty 0.09 of the Micius measurement:
\begin{align*}
2\sqrt{2}\,[1 - \exp(-L/L_{\mathrm{coh}})] < 0.09 \;&\Longleftrightarrow\; \exp(-L/L_{\mathrm{coh}}) > 1 - \frac{0.09}{2\sqrt{2}} = 0.968 \\
&\Longleftrightarrow\; L_{\mathrm{coh}} > 3.7 \times 10^7\,\mathrm{m}.
\end{align*}

The two criteria give bounds in the $10^7$ m range. Order-of-magnitude foreclosure: no candidate physical length scale lives anywhere near this --- the de Broglie wavelength is $\sim 10^{-7}$ m, the Compton wavelength $\sim 10^{-13}$ m, the Planck length $\sim 10^{-35}$ m. The closest physical scale (de Broglie) is fourteen orders of magnitude shorter than the empirical bound. Mode C is therefore foreclosed by orders of magnitude regardless of which criterion is used to compute the bound. $\square$

**Structural Reading 3 (Mode D excluded by GRB photon timing).** Under Mode D with $dx_4/dt|_{\hat{n}} = ic(\hat{n})$, the McGucken Sphere is not a true 2-sphere, the Minkowski metric is not Lorentz-invariant, and photon dispersion appears at cosmological distance with frequency-dependent arrival times. Vasileiou et al.\ (2013) analysing GRB 090510 bounds $E_{\mathrm{LIV}} > 7.6\, M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$, equivalent to $|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-19}$ at GeV-scale photon energies, foreclosing Mode D at orders-of-magnitude precision.

*Proof.* Under Mode D, the rate $dx_4/dt$ depends on the spatial direction $\hat n$: $dx_4/dt|_{\hat n} = i\, c(\hat n)$ with $c(\hat n)$ a non-constant function of direction. The McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t_0 + dt)$ at apex $p$ then has *direction-dependent radius* $c(\hat n)\, dt$ rather than uniform radius $c\, dt$. The wavefront $\Sigma_t(p)$ is no longer a 2-sphere but a 2-surface deformed by $c(\hat n)$; equivalently, the metric signature is not invariant under the rotation subgroup $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ acting on the spatial slice. The standard model for Mode-D Lorentz-invariance-violating (LIV) photon dispersion (Kostelecký 2003, Amelino-Camelia 2013) parametrises the deviation as
$$\frac{|\Delta c|}{c} \;\sim\; \left(\frac{E_\gamma}{E_{\mathrm{LIV}}}\right)^{n},$$
where $E_\gamma$ is the photon energy, $E_{\mathrm{LIV}}$ is the LIV-onset energy scale (Planck-scale in standard quantum-gravity programmes), and $n = 1$ (linear) or $n = 2$ (quadratic) is the LIV order. The GRB 090510 photon arrival times across photon energies spanning $\sim 3$ orders of magnitude (MeV to $\sim 31$ GeV in the Fermi-LAT energy range) bound the rate of any frequency-dependent dispersion. The Vasileiou et al.\ 2013 analysis yields $E_{\mathrm{LIV}} > 7.6\, M_{\mathrm{Pl}}$ at the linear order. At the highest observed photon energy $E_\gamma \approx 31$ GeV and Planck mass $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} \approx 1.22 \times 10^{19}$ GeV:
$$\frac{|\Delta c|}{c} \;<\; \frac{E_\gamma}{E_{\mathrm{LIV}}} \;=\; \frac{31\,\mathrm{GeV}}{7.6 \times 1.22 \times 10^{19}\,\mathrm{GeV}} \;\approx\; 3 \times 10^{-19}.$$
This is the empirical bound on Mode D's directional rate variation: the rate of $x_4$-advance differs across spatial directions by at most $\sim 10^{-19}$ in relative magnitude at GeV-scale photon propagation through cosmological distances. The McGucken value is strictly $c(\hat n) = c$ (no variation); the empirical bound is many orders of magnitude tighter than any candidate directional anisotropy at sub-Planckian scales. Mode D is foreclosed. $\square$

*Remark.* Structural Reading 3 is the empirical signature of the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6, GR T2): the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is independent of the gravitational field. Mode D would amount to allowing gravitational potential to alter the rate of $x_4$-advance; the GRB timing bound is the empirical foreclosure of this possibility at the cosmological-photon-propagation level.

**Structural Reading 4 (Mode E excluded by the existence of forward time evolution).** Under Mode E with Huygens' Principle failed, the wave equation $\Box \psi = 0$ admits no Green's-function solution; the field is undefined for any $t > t_0 + \delta t$; the manifold does not extend past one Planck tick.

*Proof.* Under Huygens, every point on a wavefront at time $t$ is the apex of a new McGucken Sphere at $t + \delta t$. The future wavefront $\Sigma_{t+\delta t}(p)$ is the envelope of secondary spherical wavelets emitted from each point of $\Sigma_t(p)$. Under Mode E, these secondary wavelets do not exist; surface points are not Sphere-apexes. In PDE terms: the wave equation requires the Cauchy data on a spacelike hypersurface to determine the field at all future events through the Green's function $G(x, t; x', t')$, which is itself a solution of $\Box G = \delta^4(x - x')$ and represents the spherical wavelet emitted at $(x', t')$. The vanishing of $G$ under Mode E implies the wave equation has no Green's function, equivalently no solutions at all. Empirical content: light reaches us from distant sources; gravitational waves were detected at LIGO from black-hole mergers $1.3$ Gly away; any electromagnetic signal at all reaches its receiver. Mode E negates physics itself. $\square$

### 6.1.5 The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem

**Theorem 26 (The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem).** Let $\Pi$ denote any candidate dynamical principle governing the rate and direction of advance of the fourth coordinate $x_4$. Then
\begin{align*}
&\text{strands (i)--(v) all hold at the precision of experimental record} \\
&\qquad\implies\quad \Pi = (dx_4/dt = ic) \text{ with sphere-surface } x_4\text{-locality}.
\end{align*}
Equivalently, in contrapositive form: if $\Pi \neq (dx_4/dt = ic)$ along any of the three classification axes, then at least one of strands (i)--(v) must fail at a level already excluded by experiment by many orders of magnitude.
*Proof.* By case-exhaustion across the three classification axes.

*Step 1 (trichotomy of configurations).* Any candidate dynamics $\Pi$ is either (a) the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$, or (b) differs along axis ($\alpha$) (rate magnitude/isotropy), axis ($\beta$) (surface-assignment structure), or axis ($\gamma$) (sign of $ic$). The three axes are structurally independent: axis ($\alpha$) concerns the magnitude/isotropy of the rate, axis ($\beta$) the function-theoretic shape of the surface assignment, axis ($\gamma$) the binary sign $\pm ic$. A candidate $\Pi$ that differs from the McGucken Principle differs along at least one of the three axes.

*Step 2 (axis $(\gamma)$: the orientation is the foundational $+$, from which the arrow is derived).* The sign of $ic$ in $dx_4/dt = \pm ic$ is *not* fixed by the five empirical strands (i)--(v); strands (i)--(v) are CHSH-saturation, rotational invariance, distance-independence, $c$-isotropy, and Huygens propagation, all of which are sign-symmetric (insensitive to the substitution $+ic \to -ic$). Nor is it fixed by the thermodynamic arrow: the arrow is *derived from* the $+ic$ orientation as the Geometric Second Law (Theorem 11 of §1.5.2 of this Introduction) and its downstream Generalised Second Law at black-hole horizons (Proposition 15.2.6.1 / Theorem 15.5.2 of Chapter 15), so it is a *consequence* of the orientation, not its cause. The forward orientation $+ic$ is the foundational sign of the Principle, empirically anchored by the sign-asymmetric GPS asymmetry (Theorem 38, with the sign argument at Corollary 38.1) --- the engineered, decades-maintained pre-launch frequency offset, directional where strands (i)--(v) are sign-symmetric --- and reached independently from the deductive special-relativistic side. The remaining content of the theorem --- that the *magnitude/isotropy* of the rate and the *surface-assignment* structure are forced by strands (i)--(v) --- is what Steps 3--6 below establish.

*Step 3 (exhaustiveness of axis-$(\alpha)$ and axis-$(\beta)$ alternatives).* By Lemma 20, every $\Pi$ differing from the McGucken Principle along axis ($\alpha$) or ($\beta$) falls into Mode A, B, C, D, or E, or a finite combination thereof.

*Step 4 (each mode violates at least one strand).* By Propositions 21--25: $\Pi$ in Mode A $\implies$ strand (i) fails (Tsirelson saturation); $\Pi$ in Mode B $\implies$ strand (ii) fails (rotational invariance); $\Pi$ in Mode C $\implies$ strand (iii) fails (no entanglement-distance limit); $\Pi$ in Mode D $\implies$ strand (iv) fails (Lorentz invariance of $c$); $\Pi$ in Mode E $\implies$ strand (v) fails (wavefront self-replication).

*Step 5 (mixed configurations).* A configuration combining several modes (e.g., A and B simultaneously) inherits the empirical exclusions of each component mode: if any single component mode is excluded by the empirical record, the combination is excluded. The exclusion is not weakened by allowing mixed modes.

*Step 6 (conclusion).* Combining Steps 3--5: if any of strands (i)--(v) is to remain consistent with the experimental record, $\Pi$ cannot fall into any of Modes A--E, hence does not differ from the McGucken Principle along axis ($\alpha$) or ($\beta$). Combined with Step 2 (axis ($\gamma$) fixed by thermodynamic input at $+ic$), the only configuration consistent with strands (i)--(v) plus the empirical thermodynamic arrow is the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = +ic$ with sphere-surface $x_4$-locality. $\square$

*Remark on the orientation and the arrow.* The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem forces the rate magnitude/isotropy and the surface-assignment structure from strands (i)--(v). It does not fix the orientation, and it needs no sixth strand to do so: the forward orientation is the foundational $+$ of $dx_4/dt = +ic$, empirically anchored by the sign-asymmetric GPS asymmetry (Theorem 38, with the sign argument at Corollary 38.1) and reached independently from the deductive special-relativistic side. The thermodynamic arrow is *derived from* that orientation as the Geometric Second Law, not an input that selects it --- treating it as an input would be circular, using the arrow to fix the very sign whose consequence the arrow is. The structural content: $dx_4/dt = +ic$ is the unique configuration consistent with the joint empirical record of quantum mechanics and relativity, with the arrow of time following as a derived theorem.

**Corollary 26.1 (the formal-empirical bridge).** If one accepts the empirical content of quantum mechanics and relativity --- specifically the five strands (i)--(v) at the precision of the present experimental record --- then by Theorem 26 one accepts that $dx_4/dt = ic$. The conjunction "QM and relativity are correct" entails the conjunction "the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light from every spacetime event in a spherically symmetric manner." No other configuration of the four-manifold is consistent with the joint empirical record.

The Disjunctive Forcing Theorem complements the structural overdetermination of Section 5 (structural disjointness across all 47 theorems of GR + QM along Geometric and the Algebraic Channels) with a direct empirical-forcing argument: the joint experimental record of QM and relativity *forces* the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ by case-exhaustion at orders-of-magnitude levels of experimental precision.

### 6.1.6 The Asymmetry: Why $x_4$ and Not the Spatial Axes

Theorem 26 establishes that the rate of $x_4$-advance is $ic$, event-independent and direction-independent. It does not yet establish *why $x_4$ and not the spatial axes* undergoes this expansion. The question is a natural one: why is the asymmetry between the temporal sector (active expansion at universal rate $c$, gravity-rigid by the McGucken-Invariance Lemma) and the spatial sector (static, gravity-deformable) what it is, rather than the reverse, or some symmetric configuration? We give three independent forcings, each closing the question from a different angle of the McGucken machinery.

**Forcing 1 (Algebraic: four-velocity budget).** By the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (GR T1, Lemma 11 of Section 1.4.1) under the (the McGucken-Invariance Lemma) gauge $g_{x_4 x_4} = -1$, every system has a fixed four-velocity budget of magnitude $c$, partitioned as
$$|dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\mathbf{x}/d\tau|^2 = c^2,$$
with $|dx_4/d\tau| = c\gamma$ the magnitude of the imaginary temporal four-velocity component and $|d\mathbf{x}/d\tau| = \gamma v$ the spatial-three magnitude.
A massive system at spatial rest has $|d\mathbf{x}/d\tau| = 0$ and spends the full budget on $x_4$-advance at rate $ic$. A photon has $|dx_4/d\lambda| = 0$ (Massless-Lightspeed Equivalence) and spends the full budget on spatial motion at $c$, taking the null limit of the budget identity ($u^\mu u_\mu = 0$). The spatial axes do not "also" advance at $c$; their advance rate is the residual after $x_4$ takes its share, and at rest the residual is zero. The asymmetry between $x_4$ and the spatial axes is the algebraic content of the master equation: the universal $c$-budget is distributed between the temporal and spatial sectors, with the budget identity forcing the timelike $x_4$-axis to be the primary carrier of the universal motion and the spatial directions to be the residual.

**Forcing 2 (Geometric: signature of the Minkowski metric).** Under the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ (Theorem 4), the four-coordinate quadratic form on the constraint surface of $M_G$ is
$$ds^2 = -c^2\, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$
with the *temporal* term carrying the negative sign and the *spatial* three terms carrying positive signs. The asymmetry between $x_4$ (negative-sign axis, imaginary-rate via $x_4 = ict$) and the spatial three (positive-sign axes, real-rate at zero baseline rate) is the algebraic content of the Minkowski signature $(-, +, +, +)$. By Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$), the Minkowski signature is itself a theorem of the McGucken Principle via the integrated identity $x_4 = ict$ and the embedding $\iota: (t, \mathbf{x}) \hookrightarrow M_G$. The asymmetry between the temporal and spatial sectors is therefore *not* arbitrary; it is the geometric content of the imaginary-rate coordinate axis, which is forced by the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ with $i^2 = -1$ as the algebraic record of perpendicularity of $x_4$ to the spatial three.

**Forcing 3 (Empirical: the three spatial axes are not expanding).** This is the most direct forcing. We can *observe* the three spatial dimensions, and they are not expanding at the velocity of light from every event of $M_G$. If they were, the radius of every spatial Sphere would grow at $c$ in every spatial direction --- which would be empirically indistinguishable from the universe being made of expanding spherical bubbles in spatial position. We see no such phenomenon. The three spatial dimensions are *static* relative to our laboratory observations; we move *through* them at velocities much less than $c$, and we observe them at fixed extent (the metre stick is the metre stick, the radius of the Earth is the radius of the Earth, the distance to Andromeda is the distance to Andromeda). The cosmological-scale expansion of the universe at the Hubble rate $H$ is *not* a spatial-coordinate expansion at $c$ from every event; it is a cosmological-scale rescaling of the comoving spatial slice (FLRW cosmology, Chapter 14), which proceeds at the fractional rate $H \ll c/(\text{unit length})$ at every laboratory scale. The fourth dimension's expansion at $c$ is therefore *qualitatively distinct* from the three spatial dimensions' static configuration. *The asymmetry is forced empirically* by the observation that we live in a universe whose spatial dimensions do not exhibit the $c$-expansion that the fourth dimension does.

**The combined structural reading.** The three forcings agree: the asymmetry between $x_4$ and the spatial axes is forced (i) algebraically by the master equation's four-budget partition, (ii) geometrically by the Minkowski signature $(-, +, +, +)$, and (iii) empirically by the observed staticness of the three spatial dimensions. None of these is an independent postulate; each is a consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via different intermediate paths. The structural conclusion: the McGucken Principle is the *unique* foundational statement that produces all three forcings simultaneously, with the asymmetry between the temporal and spatial sectors being the kinematic content of "the fourth dimension is expanding at $c$ from every event, and the three spatial dimensions are not."

### 6.1.7 Necessity and Sufficiency of the Nonlocal Expansion for Quantum Mechanics, Relativity, and Thermodynamics {#sec:necessity-sufficiency}

Theorem 26 and the derivation chains of this book together answer a question sharper than either addresses alone: is the nonlocal expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$ both *necessary* and *sufficient* for quantum mechanics, relativity, and thermodynamics? Necessity and sufficiency are distinct claims with distinct proofs, supplied by distinct parts of the framework --- necessity by the empirical-forcing uniqueness proof (Theorem 26), sufficiency by the theorem chains --- and this subsection states the result with that distinction kept explicit. The full nonlocal expansion is the conjunction of all three.

**Proposition 26.2 (Per-axis necessity, and the insufficiency of either axis alone).** *Decomposed along the three axes of Definition 18:*

*(a) (Motion at $c$, axis $\alpha$.) The magnitude and isotropy of the $x_4$-advance rate is necessary: by Theorem 26 (Step 4, Mode D / Proposition 24), any rate-anisotropy violates strand (iv), the Lorentz invariance of $c$, at the level already excluded by GRB 090510 timing ($|\Delta c/c| \lesssim 10^{-20}$). It is not sufficient in isolation: the surface-locality structure alone does not fix the rate. The nonlocality is the imaginary face of the same single advance whose magnitude is the rate of (a).*

## 6.3 The MTW Resolution: What Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler Could Not See

A complementary historical observation closes Section 6. The principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the resolution of a specific problem that Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler explicitly identified, acknowledged, and *abandoned* in their canonical 1973 textbook on general relativity [26].

### 6.3.1 The verbatim acknowledgment in MTW (1973)

In their introductory treatment of spacetime geometry, Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler write [26, *Gravitation*, 1973]:

> "*If in a region where spacetime is flat, one can hide this structure from view by writing $(\Delta s)^2 = (\Delta x^1)^2 + (\Delta x^2)^2 + (\Delta x^3)^2 + (\Delta x^4)^2$, with $x^4 = ict$, no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold. If '$x^4 = ict$' cannot be used there, it will not be used here. In this chapter and hereafter, as throughout the literature of general relativity, a real time coordinate is used, $x^0 = t = ct_{\mathrm{conv}}$ (superscript 0 rather than 4 to avoid any possibility of confusion with the imaginary time coordinate).*"

The acknowledgment is precise about what was abandoned: not a mathematical curiosity but a specific geometric ontology in which the fourth dimension would be *structurally distinct* from the spatial three, encoded by the imaginary unit $i$. The reason for the abandonment is also precise: in 1973, no one had discovered how to make $x^4 = ict$ work in the curved-spacetime manifold of general relativity.

### 6.3.2 What MTW could not see: $x_4 = ict$ as the kinematic shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$

The McGucken framework resolves the MTW problem by recognising that $x_4 = ict$ is *not* the foundational object --- it is the *integrated kinematic shadow* of the more fundamental dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The principle and its integrated coordinate are *not* equivalent foundational starting points: the principle is the physical content; the integrated coordinate is its kinematic record at a particular moment.

This reinterpretation is the key to making $x^4 = ict$ work in curved spacetime. Within the symmetric-metric ontological commitment of MTW, the integrated coordinate $x^4 = ict$ is treated as a *static* label on the spacetime manifold; the question "how do we make this label work in curved spacetime?" reduces to "how do we maintain the imaginary unit $i$ throughout coordinate-transformation arbitrariness?" --- a question with no clean answer because the imaginary unit is not preserved under general coordinate transformations of a Lorentzian manifold.

Under the McGucken framework, however, $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the *physical principle*, not a coordinate label. The principle specifies that the fourth dimension expands at exactly the rate $ic$ at every event in spacetime, with $x_1 x_2 x_3$ being the bending and stretching geometry that responds to mass-energy (the invariant/deformable split of Section 1.4). The imaginary unit $i$ is the *directional content* of $x_4$'s perpendicular expansion away from the three spatial axes, rather than a coordinate-transformation artifact. The McGucken-Invariance Lemma (Lemma 6) is the formal statement: the rate $dx_4/dt$ is independent of the metric components $g_{\mu\nu}$, hence preserved under coordinate transformations *because it is invariant under coordinate transformations*. The MTW objection dissolves: $x_4 = ict$ "works" in curved spacetime precisely because it is the integrated shadow of an invariant dynamical principle, not a coordinate label transported by diffeomorphism.

The historical resonance is striking. Wheeler himself --- whose 1986 essay "How Come the Quantum?" articulated the structural-economy criterion for foundational physical theories --- supplied the recommendation letter for Elliot McGucken at Princeton (cited verbatim in the epigraph above). The principle that Wheeler co-authored away in 1973 returned, three decades later, as the foundational input of a framework that derives general relativity, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, the Standard Model Lagrangian, and the symmetry structure of physics from one geometric principle: the dynamical advance $dx_4/dt = ic$ that MTW could not extend to curved spacetime, and that the McGucken framework extends by promotion from static label to physical principle.

\medskip

### 6.3.3 The historical record: Einstein did *not* abandon $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. He used it, credited it, and revised five editions never repudiating it.

A persistent misconception in the secondary literature on relativity --- recently and forcefully restated in a popular AI-generated exposition that the present author was shown --- holds that *Einstein himself abandoned the $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, notation because it made it impossible to transition from the flat spacetime of Special Relativity to the curved spacetime of General Relativity.* The claim is structurally appealing because it appears to vindicate the modern Lorentzian-signature pedagogy by retroactively imputing it to Einstein's own judgment. The claim is, however, *demonstrably false* as a historical matter. The primary sources document the opposite: Einstein used $x_4 = ict$ continuously from 1908 through the end of his life, credited it explicitly as load-bearing for the development of general relativity, and incorporated it into the canonical exposition of GR in five revised editions of *The Meaning of Relativity* between 1922 and 1955 without repudiation.

This sub-subsection records the documentary evidence. The sub-subsection that follows (§6.3.4) records the chronology of community abandonment, which occurred *after* Einstein and was canonised by MTW in 1973. The sub-subsection §6.3.5 re-reads MTW's actual claim precisely and identifies the category error in the popular abandonment narrative. The sub-subsection §6.3.6 records how Einstein in fact made $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, work in his own canonical GR exposition (via local Cartesian frames), an empirical-historical fact that bears directly on the MTW objection. The sub-subsection §6.3.7 records the resolution: how the McGucken framework promotes $x_4 = ict$ from a static coordinate label to a dynamical principle that resolves the MTW diffeomorphism-invariance worry. The sub-subsection §6.3.8 records the structural-uniqueness argument: among all configurations of "moving and stationary dimensions," the configuration of three stationary spatial dimensions and one fourth dimension expanding at $c$ is the unique configuration consistent with quantum mechanics, relativistic non-locality, and special relativity simultaneously. The sub-subsection §6.3.9 records the historical pattern: the abandonment of $x_4 = ict$ is one of several instances of the community discarding mathematical structures later recognised as physical, a pattern that includes Heaviside's elimination of quaternions, Einstein's own retraction of $\Lambda$, the Wick-rotation literature, the Lorentz-Poincaré aether ontology, and Dirac's negative-energy solutions.

**Documentary evidence: Einstein's *Relativity: The Special and General Theory* (1916; English translation 1920).** Einstein's popular exposition of relativity --- the most widely read book on the subject during his lifetime, with multiple editions published over decades --- contains an explicit credit of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, as load-bearing for the development of general relativity. The passage, from the chapter "Minkowski's Four-Dimensional Space" of the German original and its standard English translation [Einstein 1920, *Relativity: The Special and General Theory*, translated by Robert W.\ Lawson, Methuen & Co.\ London; subsequent reprints by Crown, Henry Holt, and Penguin]:

\begin{quote}
"In order to give due prominence to this relationship, however, we must replace the usual time co-ordinate $t$ by an imaginary magnitude $\sqrt{-1} \cdot ct$ proportional to it. Under these conditions, the natural laws satisfying the demands of the (special) theory of relativity assume mathematical forms, in which the time co-ordinate plays exactly the same role as the three space co-ordinates. Formally, these four co-ordinates correspond exactly to the three space co-ordinates in Euclidean geometry. It must be clear even to the non-mathematician that, as a consequence of this purely formal addition to our knowledge, the theory perforce gained clearness in no mean measure. These inadequate remarks can give the reader only a vague notion of the important idea contributed by Minkowski. \textbf{Without it the general theory of relativity, of which the fundamental ideas are developed in the following pages, would perhaps have got no farther than its long clothes.}"
\end{quote}

The emphasis in the closing sentence is the present author's. The content of Einstein's claim is unambiguous: $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, was *load-bearing* for the development of general relativity. The sentence is preserved in every edition of the popular book throughout Einstein's life.

**Documentary evidence: Einstein's *The Meaning of Relativity* (1922; revised 1945, 1950, 1953, 1955).** Einstein's *Meaning of Relativity*, comprising the four Stafford Little Lectures delivered at Princeton University in May 1921 and published by Princeton University Press in 1922, is the canonical exposition of general relativity for the technical reader, written by Einstein himself in his own voice. It is *the* book Einstein wrote to be used. Five editions were published during his lifetime, with the final edition appearing in 1955, the year of his death. *In every edition Einstein uses $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$.* The relevant passages, verified from the Project Gutenberg digitisation of the 1922 first English edition (Adams translation, available at \url{https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/36276}):

*Lecture II, p.\ 33* (in the chapter on Special Relativity, immediately before transitioning to general relativity):

\begin{quote}
"Finally, with Minkowski, we introduce in place of the real time co-ordinate $l = ct$, the imaginary time co-ordinate $x_4 = il = ict$ ($\sqrt{-1} = i$)."
\end{quote}

This is Einstein, writing in his canonical GR exposition, *adopting* $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, as the working notation. The two subsequent lectures (Lecture III and Lecture IV) are titled "The General Theory of Relativity" and "The General Theory of Relativity (continued)", and they are written using exactly this notation. The notation persists through all five editions Einstein authorised before his death.

**Documentary evidence: Einstein 1916 *Annalen der Physik* foundational GR paper.** Einstein's 1916 foundational paper *Die Grundlage der allgemeinen Relativit{\"a}tstheorie* [Einstein 1916, Annalen der Physik 49, 769] does not use the $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, convention in its body --- it uses the real coordinate $x^0$ with explicit Lorentzian-signature metric --- but Einstein's *exposition* of the theory for both popular and technical audiences in the years immediately following ($1916$ popular book, $1922$ Princeton lectures) explicitly invokes $x_4 = ict$ as the structural device that made the four-dimensional language possible. The 1916 *Annalen* paper acknowledges Minkowski's four-dimensional formulation as essential: Einstein writes of the "splendid" Minkowski formulation that enabled the general theory's geometrical content. The popular-exposition reliance on $x_4 = ict$ is therefore not separate from the technical content; it is Einstein's own structural reading of what he had accomplished.

**Documentary evidence: Pauli's *Theory of Relativity* (1921).** Wolfgang Pauli's *Relativit{\"a}tstheorie* [Pauli 1921, Encyklop{\"a}die der mathematischen Wissenschaften V19; English translation Pauli 1958, *Theory of Relativity*, Pergamon Press; reprinted Dover 1981], composed when Pauli was twenty-one years old and authoritatively reviewed by Einstein himself, uses $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, throughout both the special-relativity and general-relativity sections. Einstein's review of Pauli's *Encyklop{\"a}die* article [Einstein 1922, Die Naturwissenschaften 10, 184] praised it without reservation: *"No one studying this mature, grandly conceived work would believe that the author is a man of twenty-one... whoever reads it would be in a position to learn the entire literature of the subject."* Einstein's endorsement of Pauli's $x_4 = ict$-based treatment is itself further documentary evidence that Einstein considered the imaginary-time-coordinate formulation a legitimate and useful framing of relativity, including general relativity.

**Documentary evidence: Sommerfeld 1909.** Arnold Sommerfeld's 1909 paper on the composition of velocities in relativity [Sommerfeld 1909, Annalen der Physik 33, 649] uses the imaginary-time formulation: "*Minkowski has taught us to interpret the Lorentz-Einstein transformation as a 'space-time rotation', i.e., as a transformation of the character of an ordinary rotation, not in space $xyz$ but in the four-dimensional manifold of the magnitudes $xyzl$, where $l = ict$ also means a length, namely the 'light path' multiplied by the imaginary unit.*"

The documentary record therefore shows: Minkowski (1908), Sommerfeld (1909), Einstein (1916 popular, 1916 *Annalen* via reference to Minkowski, 1920 English translation, 1922 *Meaning of Relativity* first edition, all subsequent editions through 1955), and Pauli (1921) --- the founding cohort of relativistic physics --- all use, credit, or endorse $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. None of them abandons it. Einstein continues to use and credit it for the remaining forty-seven years of his life after Minkowski's introduction.
