### 6.3.4 The chronology of community abandonment: a gradual post-Einstein process, not Einstein's own choice

The abandonment of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, was a gradual process in the research and pedagogical literature that occurred *after* Einstein's productive period and was canonised by MTW in 1973. The chronology is as follows.

\begin{itemize}
\item *1908 (Minkowski).* Minkowski introduces $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, at the 80th Assembly of German Natural Scientists and Physicians, Cologne. The address is published as *Raum und Zeit* (Space and Time) in 1909.

\item *1909 (Sommerfeld).* Sommerfeld uses $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, in his Annalen der Physik paper on velocity composition.

\item *1915 (Einstein-Hilbert).* Einstein completes the field equations of general relativity. Hilbert independently obtains the same equations from a variational principle. Both formulations are compatible with the imaginary-time notation in flat patches.

\item *1916 (Einstein, *Relativity: The Special and General Theory*).* Einstein's popular book credits $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, as load-bearing for general relativity (passage quoted above).

\item *1921 (Pauli).* Pauli's *Encyklop{\"a}die* article uses $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, throughout. Einstein reviews and praises the work.

\item *1922 (Einstein, *The Meaning of Relativity*, first edition).* Einstein's canonical technical exposition of general relativity for the educated reader adopts $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, on page 33 of Lecture II and uses it throughout the subsequent two lectures on general relativity.

\item *1930s--1940s (research-literature transition).* As tensor calculus on Lorentzian manifolds becomes the standard graduate-level formulation of GR, the metric-signature convention $(-, +, +, +)$ (or its negative) gradually replaces the imaginary-time notation in the research literature. The shift is not motivated by a discovered impossibility but by computational convenience: explicit metric signatures make the bookkeeping of tensor indices cleaner, and the imaginary-unit $i$ in coordinates introduces awkwardness when general (non-orthogonal) coordinate transformations are applied. The shift is gradual and not universal. Schwinger, Feynman, and Bargmann use real time coordinates throughout. Pauli's later editions of *Theory of Relativity* (translated into English in 1958) retain $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Bergmann's 1942 *Introduction to the Theory of Relativity* (Prentice-Hall), reviewed by Einstein himself in its preface, continues to use imaginary time in places.

\item *1945, 1950, 1953, 1955 (Einstein, revised editions of *The Meaning of Relativity*).* Einstein revises *The Meaning of Relativity* through five editions over thirty-three years, the last appearing in the year of his death. The imaginary-time formulation is retained throughout. The five editions add appendices on the cosmological constant, the generalised theory of gravitation, and Einstein's non-symmetric field-theory unification attempts --- *none of which retracts the $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, usage of the main body.* Einstein had three decades after 1922 to revise the book if he had come to consider $x_4 = ict$ inappropriate for general relativity. He did not.

\item *1960s (textbook transition).* Synge's *Relativity: The General Theory* (1960), Adler-Bazin-Schiffer's *Introduction to General Relativity* (1965), and Weinberg's *Gravitation and Cosmology* (1972) standardise on the real-coordinate formulation $x^0 = ct$ with explicit metric signature. The transition is now established in the graduate textbook canon.

\item *1973 (Misner-Thorne-Wheeler, *Gravitation*).* MTW canonises the abandonment with the verbatim passage of §6.3.1 above: *"no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold."*

\item *1984--2005 (post-MTW textbook canon).* Wald (1984), Carroll (2004), Schutz (1985, 2009), and the later editions of Weinberg do not even mention the imaginary-time coordinate. The graduate-student tradition forgets that $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, was ever a thing.
\end{itemize}

The chronology is unambiguous: **Einstein is not among the abandoners.** The community abandoned $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, over a period of roughly forty years after Einstein's 1922 *Meaning of Relativity*, with MTW 1973 the canonical moment. Einstein's own canonical GR exposition --- updated and revised five times under his own authorisation, the last in the year of his death --- continues to use $x_4 = ict$ throughout. The narrative that "Einstein abandoned $x_4 = ict$ because he realised it would not work in general relativity" is contradicted by every primary source bearing on the question.

\medskip

### 6.3.5 The MTW claim re-read precisely: a difficulty for the community, not an impossibility theorem

MTW's verbatim claim, restated for clarity: *"no one has discovered a way to make an imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold. If '$x^4 = ict$' cannot be used there, it will not be used here. In this chapter and hereafter, as throughout the literature of general relativity, a real time coordinate is used, $x^0 = t = ct_{\mathrm{conv}}$."*

Three observations about this claim:

**(i) The careful wording: "no one has discovered a way."** MTW do not write "it is impossible to make an imaginary coordinate work" --- they write "*no one has discovered a way*." This is the language of a research-community status report ("here is what we, the post-Einstein community, working in the modern tensor-calculus formulation, have failed to find"), not the language of a no-go theorem. The distinction is structurally precise. A no-go theorem would state that the imaginary coordinate is *inconsistent* with curved-spacetime structure. MTW make no such claim; they report that the community has *not found* a way. The status of the question after MTW 1973 is therefore: open, with the community having shifted attention elsewhere.

**(ii) Einstein had been making it work for fifty-seven years.** The empirical-historical fact is that Einstein, in *The Meaning of Relativity* (1922 first edition, 1945--1955 four subsequent revised editions), demonstrably used $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, in his exposition of general relativity. The book contains the field equations $R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} g_{\mu\nu} R = -\kappa T_{\mu\nu}$, the Schwarzschild exterior solution, the FLRW cosmological line element, the perihelion-precession derivation, and the light-deflection calculation --- all developed in a framework that uses $x_4 = ict$ where appropriate. Whether Einstein's exposition meets MTW's standard of "making the imaginary coordinate work in the general curved spacetime manifold" depends on what one means by "work": Einstein worked in *local Cartesian frames* (Riemann normal coordinates), with the imaginary-time content alive in the local-frame structure and the metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ governing transitions between local frames. This is documented in §6.3.6 below. MTW's worry is about *globally arbitrary diffeomorphisms* of the curved manifold; Einstein's working solution operates *locally*, with the metric tensor doing the bookkeeping between local frames.

*(iii) The "no one" of MTW's claim refers to "the modern community", not "all of history".** MTW write the passage in 1973, fifty-eight years after general relativity's completion. The "no one" who has discovered the way is the post-Einstein community working in the tensor-calculus formulation that became standard after 1930. The "no one" does not include Einstein himself, who manifestly made $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, work in his canonical 1922 exposition. The MTW passage is therefore best read as: *the modern community, working in the modern tensor-calculus formulation, has not found a way to extend Einstein's locally-Cartesian $x_4 = ict$ formulation to a globally diffeomorphism-invariant formulation, and we abandon it for that reason.
The category error in the popular abandonment narrative is therefore precise. The narrative conflates two distinct questions:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Question A*: Can the integrated shadow $x_4 = ict$ be used as a global coordinate label across all of curved spacetime (a question which, lacking the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ of which the shadow is the mere integrated form, MTW could only pose at the level of the label), invariant under arbitrary diffeomorphisms? MTW's reported answer: no one has found a way, so we abandon it.
\item *Question B*: Does $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, work as the foundational structural device on which general relativity is built, when used locally in Cartesian frames with the metric tensor governing transitions between such frames? Einstein's answer: yes, indispensably --- "without it the general theory of relativity... would perhaps have got no farther than its long clothes."
\end{itemize}

The popular narrative presents Question A's negative answer as if it implies Question B's negative answer. *It does not.* Question A's negative answer is a working-community status report on a specific technical convenience. Question B's affirmative answer is Einstein's own canonical structural reading of his theory. The two coexist without contradiction because they operate on different objects.

\medskip

### 6.3.6 How Einstein actually made $x_4 = ict$ (integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$) work in general relativity: local Cartesian frames

Einstein's working method in general relativity, articulated in *The Meaning of Relativity* (1922) and the 1916 popular book, uses $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, in *local* Cartesian frames at each event of the curved manifold, with the metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ governing transitions between such local frames. The structural reading is precise and technically clean.

**Step 1: At each event $p$ of the spacetime manifold $\mathcal{M}$, choose a Riemann normal coordinate frame.** This is always possible by the equivalence principle: at any event, there exists a local inertial frame in which the metric $g_{\mu\nu}(p) = \eta_{\mu\nu}$ (the flat Minkowski metric at $p$) and the Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^\lambda_{\mu\nu}(p) = 0$. In such a frame, locally at $p$, the geometry is indistinguishable from special-relativistic Minkowski space.

**Step 2: In this local frame, adopt Einstein's $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, convention.** The local Minkowski metric in $(x^1, x^2, x^3, x^4 = ict)$ coordinates is just the four-dimensional Euclidean metric $\delta_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, 1, 1)$, because $(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ provides the required negative sign automatically. The local line element at $p$ is
$$ds^2 = (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2 + (dx^4)^2$$
which expands to $ds^2 = (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2 - c^2 dt^2$ on substituting $x^4 = ict$, the Lorentzian-signature line element. Einstein's structural point in the popular book quote is precisely this: *"these four co-ordinates correspond exactly to the three space co-ordinates in Euclidean geometry"* --- locally, at each event, the imaginary-time formulation makes the four-dimensional structure Euclidean-formal, with the negative sign for time captured by the imaginary unit rather than by a non-trivial metric signature.

**Step 3: The metric tensor governs the transition between local frames at different events.** Where Einstein's locally-Cartesian-with-$x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, formulation meets curved spacetime is at the level of how local frames at different events relate. Einstein's *Meaning of Relativity* develops this through the Christoffel symbols, the geodesic equation, the Riemann curvature tensor, and the Ricci tensor --- all of which are real-valued objects governing the variation of the local Cartesian frame across the manifold. Locally, the imaginary unit $i$ encodes the perpendicular character of the time axis relative to the spatial three. Globally, the metric tensor encodes how the manifold curves between local frames. The two coexist.

**Step 4: The MTW worry is about formulating Step 3 with $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, as a global coordinate label.** If one attempts to make $x_4 = ict$ a global coordinate on the entire curved manifold rather than a local-frame label, then the imaginary unit $i$ must transport cleanly under arbitrary diffeomorphisms of the manifold, which is awkward because the diffeomorphism group does not naturally preserve the real/imaginary structure. This is the MTW worry. It is a worry about *Question A* of §6.3.5 above (global diffeomorphism-invariance), not about *Question B* (does the formulation work for GR's exposition).

The historical-technical point: Einstein worked at Step 1--Step 3 and found the formulation natural and load-bearing. The post-Einstein community attempted Step 4 (global diffeomorphism-invariant formulation), found it awkward, and abandoned the imaginary-time content entirely. MTW 1973 is the canonical statement of that abandonment. *Neither MTW nor the community ever claimed that Einstein's own Step 1--Step 3 usage was incorrect or unworkable.* They abandoned a *different* construction (Step 4) and the community lost track of the distinction.

This is a textbook example of the pattern Wheeler himself diagnosed in his 1986 essay "How Come the Quantum?" and elsewhere: *the community develops a tool, gradually loses sight of the conceptual structure that made the tool natural, and eventually discards the tool while keeping the diluted formalism.* The "no one has discovered a way" of MTW 1973 is the empirical signature of this process. Einstein had discovered the way --- the locally-Cartesian-with-$x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, way --- and used it throughout his canonical exposition. The community, working in the post-1930 modernised tensor-calculus formulation, lost sight of Einstein's locally-Cartesian construction and reported the global-diffeomorphism-invariance worry as if it were the entire question.

\medskip

### 6.3.7 The McGucken resolution: promoting $x_4 = ict$ from static coordinate label to dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$

The McGucken framework's resolution of the MTW worry is structurally elegant and inherits Einstein's own working method while extending it. The promotion: $x_4 = ict$ is *not* a static coordinate label requiring diffeomorphism-invariance; it is the *integrated kinematic shadow* of the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The principle is the physical content; the integrated coordinate is its kinematic record at a particular moment.

The structural-mathematical content of the promotion:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Invariance, not tensoriality.* The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is *invariant*: the rate is exactly $ic$ at every event of spacetime, in every coordinate system. The rate is therefore not a tensor that needs to be transported under diffeomorphisms; it is an invariant of the spacetime structure that takes the same value everywhere by physical principle (the McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$: $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event). This is structurally analogous to the role of $c$ in special relativity: the speed of light is the same in every inertial frame not because $c$ is a tensor with a particular transformation law but because $c$ is an invariant of the spacetime structure. The McGucken framework generalises this to general relativity: $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the same at every event of curved spacetime, not because it transforms in a particular way under diffeomorphisms but because it is an invariant of the manifold.

\item *The imaginary unit $i$ encodes perpendicularity, not a coordinate-transformation artifact.* On the static-coordinate-label reading abandoned by MTW, the $i$ in $x_4 = ict$ is a feature of how the coordinate $x_4$ is constructed, and it must somehow transport under diffeomorphisms (the awkward step). On the McGucken-Principle reading, the $i$ in $dx_4/dt = ic$ encodes the *direction* of $x_4$'s expansion: perpendicular to the three spatial axes, in the algebraic sense that the only Frobenius division algebra ($\mathbb{R}, \mathbb{C}, \mathbb{H}$) compatible with a single perpendicular axis is $\mathbb{C}$, with $i$ as the unit imaginary direction. The $i$ is therefore structurally analogous to the $i$ in Euler's formula $e^{i\theta}$, where $\theta$ specifies an angle of rotation and $i$ specifies the perpendicular-rotation direction. Perpendicularity is preserved under coordinate transformations in a precise sense (the McGucken-Invariance Lemma, §1.4 above); the $i$ is not a coordinate-transformation artifact, it is the directional content of perpendicular expansion.

\item *Curved spacetime as the deformation of the spatial three with $x_4$'s rate invariant.* Under the McGucken framework, curved spacetime arises from the deformation of $x_1, x_2, x_3$ in response to mass-energy, while the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ remains invariant. The metric tensor $g_{\mu\nu}$ encodes the spatial deformation, with the conformal-factor function $\psi(t, x)$ (developed in §6.7 and throughout this book) characterising how the spatial three contract near baryonic potentials. The $x_4$-axis is structurally *not* contracted; the rate of its expansion is *the same* at every event. This is the McGucken-Invariance Lemma in its physical-interpretive form: the invariant rate of $x_4$'s expansion is what survives the curvature of spacetime as a structural constant of the manifold, and the spatial three carry the curvature content.
\end{itemize}

The MTW worry dissolves under this resolution. The MTW worry was about diffeomorphism-invariance of the static label $x_4 = ict$. The McGucken framework does not present $x_4 = ict$ as a static label; it presents $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a dynamical invariant. Invariants do not need to satisfy diffeomorphism-transformation laws because they take the same value in every coordinate system by definition. The MTW worry is a worry about an object the McGucken framework does not assert as foundational.

What the McGucken framework *does* assert as foundational --- the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- is the foundational object whose existence Wheeler himself articulated in his 1986 essay "How Come the Quantum?" and across his collected writings: *"Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it --- in a decade, a century, or a millennium --- we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise?"* The McGucken framework's claim is that this idea is $dx_4/dt = ic$, the dynamical promotion of the same imaginary-time content Einstein used throughout his canonical GR exposition.

### 6.3.8 The structural-uniqueness argument: why three stationary spatial dimensions and one fourth dimension expanding at $c$ is the unique ontology consistent with QM, non-locality, and special relativity

A further structural-foundational argument supports the specific ontological configuration of the McGucken Principle. The argument addresses a question that the abandonment of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, obscured for the past half-century: *among all possible configurations of "stationary" and "expanding" dimensions, which configuration is consistent with the empirical content of physics?* The answer, on the McGucken framework: the configuration of three stationary spatial dimensions and one fourth dimension expanding at $c$ is *unique* in being simultaneously consistent with quantum mechanics, the empirical record of non-locality and entanglement, and special relativity. Every other configuration is empirically refuted.

The argument by case-exhaustion proceeds as follows. Consider a spacetime manifold with four dimensions, partitioned into "expanding" and "stationary" content. There are five qualitatively distinct cases:

**Case 1: Four stationary dimensions (no expansion).** The classical Newtonian-Galilean ontology. Refuted by special relativity: the empirical content of the Lorentz transformations (time dilation, length contraction, the $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$ Tsirelson saturation in quantum entanglement) requires a non-trivial spacetime structure beyond static four-dimensional Euclidean space. Refuted by the constancy of $c$ across reference frames, which has no structural source in a fully stationary four-dimensional manifold.

**Case 2: Four expanding dimensions (all four at rate $c$).** Symmetric expansion of all four axes at rate $c$. This configuration cannot reproduce the rotational invariance of three-dimensional space that is empirically established (Earth-based experiments, accelerator experiments, astronomical observations). If all four axes expanded equivalently, there would be no preferred subspace of three rotationally-equivalent axes; the three spatial dimensions would have no structural distinction from the fourth. The empirical fact that we observe $SO(3)$ rotational invariance among the spatial three but no $SO(4)$ rotational invariance including the time axis refutes the symmetric-four-axis configuration.

**Case 3: Two expanding, two stationary.** Various sub-cases: two spatial axes expanding and two spatial-or-temporal stationary; one spatial and one temporal expanding; etc. Each sub-case introduces a structural anisotropy in the spatial three (because only some spatial axes would expand), which conflicts with the observed isotropy of space across all empirical tests. The cosmic microwave background isotropy to one part in $10^5$ (after dipole subtraction) refutes any configuration in which the spatial three are not all on equal footing.

**Case 4: One spatial dimension expanding at $c$, three stationary (including time).** This configuration would single out one spatial direction as preferred, again conflicting with $SO(3)$ rotational invariance of space.

**Case 5: Three stationary spatial dimensions and one fourth dimension (not a spatial direction, distinct from the three) expanding at $c$.** *The McGucken configuration.* The three spatial dimensions are on equal footing (rotational invariance preserved), the fourth dimension is structurally distinct from the three (encoded by the imaginary unit $i$ as the perpendicular direction), and the expansion at $c$ supplies the structural content from which special relativity (the Lorentzian metric as the kinematic shadow of $x_4$ expansion), general relativity (the metric tensor governing how the spatial three deform around mass-energy while the $x_4$-rate remains invariant), quantum mechanics (the cogenerative cascade of the Hilbert space, Born rule, canonical commutator, uncertainty principle, and Schrödinger equation from $dx_4/dt = ic$), and the non-locality / entanglement structure of quantum mechanics (the McGucken Sphere mechanism, with "all non-locality begins as locality" as the testable principle) all descend as theorems.

**The structural uniqueness claim.** Of these five cases, *only Case 5 --- the McGucken configuration --- is simultaneously consistent with quantum mechanics, relativistic non-locality, and special and general relativity.* Cases 1--4 each fail at least one of these three empirical constraints. The McGucken configuration is therefore the unique configuration of "stationary" and "expanding" dimensions consistent with the empirical content of physics.

This argument is structurally analogous to (and complementary to) the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem of §6.1 of this Introduction (and §X.7 of [5]), which establishes that $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the unique configuration of the four-dimensional manifold consistent with five empirically settled features of physics (Tsirelson saturation $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$, rotational invariance of entanglement correlations under $SO(3)$, absence of fundamental entanglement-distance limit, Lorentz invariance of $c$, wavefront self-replication). The present argument is a more elementary case-exhaustion at the level of the dimensional configuration; the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem is the more sophisticated statement at the level of the precise principle.

The structural-historical significance of the case-exhaustion argument: *the configuration was visible to the early-twentieth-century community.* Minkowski's 1908 introduction of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, already implicitly singles out the fourth dimension as structurally distinct from the spatial three (via the imaginary unit $i$). Einstein's 1916 popular book and 1922 *Meaning of Relativity* preserve this structural distinction. Pauli's 1921 and Sommerfeld's 1909 expositions preserve it. The structural-uniqueness argument was, in a sense, *already visible* in the formulations Einstein and his contemporaries adopted. *What the post-Einstein community lost, in abandoning $x_4 = ict$, was the structural distinction between the three spatial dimensions and the fourth that the imaginary unit $i$ encodes --- not merely a formal convenience but the algebraic visibility of dimensional perpendicularity itself.* The modern $(-, +, +, +)$ metric-signature convention buries the structural distinction inside the minus sign of $g_{00}$; the imaginary-time formulation puts the structural distinction front and centre, where it can be seen and reasoned about.

That nobody saw the case-exhaustion uniqueness argument explicitly during the seven decades of post-Einstein abandonment is itself a structural-historical fact worth recording. The argument requires the imaginary-time formulation to be conceptually salient, because the structural distinction it argues for ($x_4$ as the unique expanding dimension distinct from the stationary spatial three) is encoded in the imaginary unit $i$. With $i$ buried inside $g_{00} = -1$ via the modern signature convention, the structural question "which dimension is expanding?" becomes invisible. The McGucken framework's restoration of the imaginary-time formulation as a dynamical principle restores the structural question to visibility. The case-exhaustion argument is then immediate.

### 6.3.9 The historical pattern: mathematical structure abandoned as artifact, later recognised as physical

The abandonment of $x_4 = ict$ between 1930 and 1973, and its restoration as the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ in the McGucken framework, is one instance of a recurring historical pattern in foundational physics. The pattern: *the community develops a mathematical structure for a specific problem, gradually loses sight of the structural content the mathematics encodes, eventually discards the mathematical structure as a formal artifact, and is later forced to recognise that the discarded structure encoded physical content.* Five historical instances of the pattern are worth recording for context:

**Instance 1: Heaviside's elimination of quaternions from Maxwell's equations (1880s).** Maxwell's *Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism* (1873) was written using quaternions, the four-component number system Hamilton introduced in 1843. Heaviside in the 1880s reformulated Maxwell's equations in three-dimensional vector calculus, eliminating the quaternion structure. The vector-calculus formulation became standard, and the quaternion structure was largely forgotten by the physics community for eighty years. Hestenes's geometric-algebra programme, beginning with *Space-Time Algebra* (1966), recognised that the quaternion structure encoded physical content the community had abandoned: the unification of complex numbers, spinors, vectors, and pseudovectors in a single algebraic structure that turns out to be natural for the Dirac equation, the electromagnetic field, and the spin geometry of physics. The mathematical structure Heaviside discarded as a formal artifact was, ninety years later, recognised as structurally essential.

**Instance 2: Einstein's cosmological constant $\Lambda$ (1917).** Einstein introduced the cosmological constant to allow a static cosmological solution to the field equations. After Hubble's 1929 discovery of cosmic expansion, Einstein retracted $\Lambda$, calling it his "biggest blunder." For the next sixty-nine years, the cosmological constant was treated as a formal artifact of Einstein's incomplete understanding. The 1998 discovery of accelerating cosmic expansion via Type Ia supernovae [Riess et al.\ 1998; Perlmutter et al.\ 1999] forced the community to recognise that $\Lambda \neq 0$ is physically real. The mathematical structure Einstein discarded as a blunder was, in fact, the physical content of dark energy.

**Instance 3: The Wick rotation (1954).** Wick introduced the imaginary-time rotation $\tau = it$ as a computational device for quantum field theory: rotating from Lorentzian to Euclidean signature makes path-integral computations tractable. The community treated it as a formal device with no physical content for two decades. Hawking's 1975 Euclidean derivation of black-hole thermodynamics, the Gibbons-Hawking 1977 boundary-term derivation, and the modern Euclidean quantum field theory framework recognised that the Wick rotation encodes physical content: the KMS condition identifying imaginary-time periodicity with inverse temperature, the Euclidean cigar geometry of the Schwarzschild horizon supplying the Hawking temperature, the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ as a coordinate identification on the real four-manifold whose fourth axis is physically expanding at $c$. The mathematical structure Wick introduced as a computational device was, decades later, recognised as encoding deep physical content of horizon thermodynamics and the QM-statistical-mechanics correspondence.

**Instance 4: The Lorentz-Poincaré aether ontology (1890s--1905).** Lorentz and Poincaré developed the Lorentz transformations within an aether-frame ontology: a privileged frame existed in which light propagated, and the Lorentz transformations described how clocks and rods behaved when moving relative to this frame. Einstein's 1905 special relativity recognised that the same mathematics did not require an aether: the Lorentz transformations are the kinematic content of the principle of relativity plus the constancy of $c$. The aether was discarded as ontologically superfluous. But the mathematics --- the Lorentz transformations themselves --- was preserved entirely, and is now the empirical core of relativistic physics. The case is structurally distinct from Cases 1--3 in that what was abandoned (the aether) was the ontological framing, not the mathematics; but it illustrates the same pattern of structural reinterpretation: the same mathematical content can carry different physical meanings depending on which ontological framework is brought to bear.

**Instance 5: Dirac's negative-energy solutions (1928).** The 1928 Dirac equation has both positive- and negative-energy solutions for the electron. Dirac initially considered the negative-energy solutions as a problem of the equation, then recognised in 1930 that they could be interpreted as a sea of negative-energy electrons whose absence appeared as a positive-energy positively-charged particle. Anderson's 1932 discovery of the positron confirmed the physical reality of antimatter. The mathematical structure Dirac initially considered as an artifact was forced to be physical by the equation itself.

**The pattern in all five instances.** The community develops a mathematical structure for a specific problem, gradually loses sight of the structural content, discards the structure as formal artifact, and is later forced to recognise that the discarded structure encoded physical content. The recognition comes either from new empirical observations (dark energy for $\Lambda$, positron discovery for Dirac's negative energies, weak-lensing data for $x_4 = ict$ via [5]'s twelve-test first-place finish) or from structural-mathematical reanalysis (Hestenes's geometric algebra for quaternions, Hawking's Euclidean derivation for the Wick rotation, the cogenerative cascade of [HBR] for $x_4 = ict$ via its promotion to $dx_4/dt = ic$).

The McGucken framework's relation to the $x_4 = ict$ abandonment is structurally the same as Hestenes's relation to the quaternion abandonment: the framework restores a mathematical structure the community discarded, with the explicit identification that the discarded structure encoded physical content. Specifically: the imaginary unit $i$ in Minkowski's 1908 $x_4 = ict$, used by Einstein throughout his life, encoded the perpendicular-expansion content of the fourth dimension that the McGucken framework promotes to the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The MTW 1973 abandonment is one step in the historical pattern; the McGucken framework is the next step, the recognition that the abandoned structure encoded physical content all along.

The Wheeler aphorism is the cri de coeur of this pattern. Wheeler, who supervised the present author at Princeton in the 1980s, articulated repeatedly that the foundational principle must be simple, must be already encoded in the mathematics the community already has, and must be visible once the conceptual framing is correct. *"Behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it --- in a decade, a century, or a millennium --- we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise? How could we have been so stupid?"* The McGucken framework's identification of $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the foundational principle Wheeler said must exist is structurally one step in the historical pattern of mathematical-structure-discarded-then-recognised-as-physical. The structure was visible to Minkowski, Sommerfeld, Pauli, and Einstein himself --- and remains in Einstein's canonical 1922 GR exposition that the post-1955 community gradually forgot how to read.

### 6.3.10 The paradoxes and contradictions of the MTW formulation: how the hard road was taken

The abandonment of $dx_4/dt = ic$ documented above (§§6.3.1--6.3.9) has structural consequences that extend across the entire post-1973 foundational-physics programme. Once the principle is denied, *every natural element it supplies as a theorem must be put back into the formulation by hand* --- with each restoration introducing its own conceptual difficulties, free parameters, additional postulates, and unresolved paradoxes. The history of post-1973 quantum gravity, cosmology, and foundations of physics is largely the history of this patching process. This sub-subsection records seven specific structural problems of the symmetric-block-universe MTW formulation, each of which the McGucken framework dissolves through the structural content of $dx_4/dt = ic$, and each of which the MTW community has had to address by adding postulates, parameters, or unresolved conjectures.

The taxonomy is summarised as follows. (1) The Gödel paradox: closed timelike curves in classical GR, requiring Hawking's chronology protection conjecture to defend the universe against itself. (2) The frozen block universe: the Wheeler--DeWitt equation's problem of time, sixty years unresolved. (3) Non-renormalizable infinities in perturbative quantum gravity, the structural failure that motivated the entire string-theory and loop-quantum-gravity programmes. (4) The speed of light $c$ as a fundamental constant inserted by hand via metric signature, with no derivation from any principle. (5) Quantum non-locality forced into the formulation as an empirical fact with no structural source. (6) The light cone added by hand via the metric signature, with no physical mechanism. (7) The arrow of time put in by hand via the Past Hypothesis, despite the underlying dynamical laws being time-reversal symmetric. After cataloguing the seven structural problems, the sub-subsection closes with the load-bearing question: *did the MTW community not see this pattern?*

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.1 The Gödel paradox: closed timelike curves and the chronology protection conjecture

Kurt Gödel, the greatest logician since Aristotle and Einstein's close friend at the Institute for Advanced Study at Princeton, discovered in 1949 a solution to Einstein's field equations describing a rotating universe [Gödel 1949, Reviews of Modern Physics 21, 447, *"An example of a new type of cosmological solutions of Einstein's field equations of gravitation"*]. The solution, now called the Gödel metric, possesses several remarkable features: it is spatially homogeneous (the universe looks the same at every point), it rotates around every point (no privileged geometrical axis), and --- most consequentially --- *it contains closed timelike curves (closed timelike curves)*. A closed timelike curve is a worldline that returns to its starting point in spacetime: a path along which a traveller could return to their own past, with all the paradoxes of time travel that this entails, including the grandfather paradox.

The Gödel solution is not a curiosity. *It is an exact solution of Einstein's field equations*, sitting at the same mathematical-physical level as Schwarzschild's exterior solution and the Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker cosmologies. It satisfies the equations of general relativity exactly, with a specific choice of cosmological constant matched to the density of pressureless dust. As Inference Review's exposition records [Richmond 2021, *"Time Travelers"*, Inference Review]: *"This exact solution of Einstein's general relativity equations contains closed timelike curves and therefore allows for a trip into the past, accompanied by all the paradoxes that arise from a possible violation of the principle of causality."*

Gödel's discovery has a striking historical-philosophical context. *Gödel sought, above all, to find support for his philosophical point of view on the illusory nature of time.* The argument, articulated in Gödel's 1949 companion paper *"A Remark about the Relationship between Relativity Theory and Idealistic Philosophy"* and his unpublished correspondence with Einstein at IAS, is structurally precise: if general relativity permits universes in which time travel is possible, then time as a flowing entity cannot be a fundamental feature of physical reality; *time must therefore be an illusion of the observing consciousness rather than a structural feature of the spacetime manifold*. Gödel's solution is the mathematical-physical exhibit for this philosophical position. The conclusion that Gödel drew from his exact GR solution is *exactly* the conclusion of the Kantian-idealist tradition he was attempting to vindicate: time as we experience it is a feature of the mind, not of the world. *General relativity --- in its symmetric-block-universe MTW formulation --- supports this conclusion by structural construction.*

The Gödel solution is not the only general-relativistic closed-timelike-curve solution. Willem Jacob van Stockum had already in 1937 found a rotating-cylinder solution with closed timelike curves [Van Stockum 1937, Proc.\ Roy.\ Soc.\ Edinburgh 57, 135], which predates Gödel and provides further evidence that closed timelike curves are not an isolated pathology but a *generic feature* of rotating-mass solutions to the Einstein field equations. The Tipler cylinder (Tipler 1974), Morris--Thorne traversable wormholes (Morris--Thorne 1988), the Kerr black hole interior (closed timelike curves inside the inner horizon), Gott cosmic strings (Gott 1991), and the Alcubierre warp drive (Alcubierre 1994) all generate closed timelike curves as exact solutions or sub-regions of the manifold. The structural pattern: *whenever rotation, sufficient mass-energy, or exotic stress-energy distributions are introduced into the Einstein field equations, closed timelike curves appear as legitimate solutions of the equations.*

The community's response to this structural problem is the *chronology protection conjecture*, proposed by Stephen Hawking in 1992 [Hawking 1992, Phys.\ Rev.\ D 46, 603, *"Chronology Protection Conjecture"*]. Hawking, recognising that the existence of GR solutions with closed timelike curves threatens the causal structure of physics, conjectured that *laws of physics beyond those of standard general relativity prevent the formation of closed timelike curves*. The Wikipedia summary, sourced from Hawking 1992: *"It seems that there is a Chronology Protection Agency which prevents the appearance of closed timelike curves and so makes the universe safe for historians."* The conjecture's structural status is precise: it is *not* a theorem of general relativity. It is an *additional postulate* needed to protect classical GR from its own closed-timelike-curve solutions. Hawking's argument invoked quantum-field-theoretic effects at the would-be Cauchy horizon of a closed timelike curve region: vacuum fluctuations diverge near the would-be closed timelike curve, destroying the spacetime structure before the closed timelike curve can form. *The argument requires quantum effects to save classical GR from a structural pathology of its own field equations.*

Subsequent work has sharpened the chronology protection conjecture and identified its difficulties. Deser, Jackiw, and 't Hooft (1992) [Deser-Jackiw-'t Hooft 1992, Phys.\ Rev.\ Lett.\ 68, 267] demonstrated the non-existence of closed timelike curves in acceptable three-dimensional spacetimes by showing energy-condition violations. Hawking-Ellis (1973) [Hawking-Ellis 1973, *The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time*, Cambridge University Press] had earlier noted that the Gödel solution violates standard energy conditions and might therefore be unphysical. Burghardt (2001) [Burghardt 2001, arXiv gr-qc/0106070] argued that the Gödel cosmos has a cut-off radius beyond which rotational velocity exceeds $c$, eliminating closed timelike curves as practically realisable. *Each of these results is a patch.* Each adds a constraint, an additional condition, or a quantum-gravity effect that classical GR alone does not supply, to defend the universe against its own field-equation solutions.

The McGucken framework's structural diagnosis of the Gödel paradox is direct and complete. *Closed timelike curves are structurally impossible in the McGucken framework.* The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies that $x_4$ advances monotonically at rate $+ic$ at every event of spacetime. The advance is *invariant* (same at every event, in every coordinate system) and *monotonic* (the sign of $ic$ is fixed). A closed timelike curve would require a worldline returning to its starting $x_4$-coordinate value, which violates the monotonic $+ic$ advance of $x_4$ along every worldline. The Gödel construction, the Van Stockum cylinder, the Tipler cylinder, and the traversable wormholes are all *symmetric-block-universe solutions* in which $x_4$ has no structurally privileged direction of advance; they exploit precisely the symmetric treatment of all four spacetime dimensions that the McGucken framework rejects.

The structural-historical reading: the Gödel paradox is the empirical signature of the MTW symmetric-block-universe formulation being structurally incomplete. The symmetric treatment of all four spacetime dimensions, with no privileged $x_4$-advance, is what permits closed-timelike-curve solutions to exist as mathematical objects. Hawking's chronology protection conjecture is the additional postulate needed to defend classical GR against its own structural defect. The McGucken framework's promotion of $dx_4/dt = ic$ from static coordinate label to dynamical principle eliminates the defect at the source. *The community's failure to see the structural diagnosis is itself an artifact of having denied $dx_4/dt = ic$ in 1973: with the principle absent from the formulation, the structural-asymmetry content needed to forbid closed timelike curves is also absent, and the community must either tolerate closed timelike curves (Gödel's idealist-philosophical position) or postulate a chronology-protection mechanism (Hawking's working response).*

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.2 The frozen block universe and the Wheeler--DeWitt problem of time

The canonical quantization of general relativity, undertaken by Bryce DeWitt (1967) [DeWitt 1967, Phys.\ Rev.\ 160, 1113, *"Quantum Theory of Gravity. I.\ The Canonical Theory"*] and John Wheeler (1968) [Wheeler 1968, in *Batelles Rencontres*, eds.\ DeWitt and Wheeler, Benjamin: New York], leads to the Wheeler--DeWitt equation:
$$\hat{H}\, \Psi[h_{ij}, \phi] = 0$$
where $\hat{H}$ is the Hamiltonian constraint, $h_{ij}$ is the three-metric on a spatial hypersurface, $\phi$ represents matter fields, and $\Psi$ is the "wave function of the universe." *The equation has no time-derivative term.* It is a constraint equation, not an evolution equation. The wave function $\Psi$ does not evolve in time; it satisfies a static constraint on the configuration space of all possible spatial three-geometries.

This is the *frozen formalism problem* of canonical quantum gravity. The Wikipedia entry on the Problem of Time records the structural statement precisely: *"The non-relativistic equation of quantum mechanics includes time evolution... In general relativity the energy operator becomes a constraint in the Wheeler--DeWitt equation... where the operator varies throughout space, but the wave function here, called the wave function of the universe, is constant."* Rotondo's 2022 *Universe* paper [Rotondo 2022, Universe 8, 580] makes the structural identification: *"The absence of an external time in the description of GR, which is inherited by its quantization, is sometimes referred to as the 'frozen formalism problem,' and constitutes only one among other difficulties in the definition of time in classical and quantum physics."* The recent preprint of Vasak 2025 [Vasak 2025, arXiv 2505.01358, *"Setting free the cosmic time in Quantum Universe"*]: *"The standard Wheeler--DeWitt approach to Quantum Cosmology leads to the problematic freeze of time."*

The problem has been open for sixty years. Karel Kuchař's 1992 review [Kuchař 1992, in *Proceedings of the 4th Canadian Conference on General Relativity and Relativistic Astrophysics*, World Scientific] catalogued the proposed solutions to the problem of time and found none satisfactory. Isham's 1993 review [Isham 1993, in *Integrable Systems, Quantum Groups, and Quantum Field Theories*, Kluwer: Dordrecht] reached the same conclusion. Anderson's 2017 monograph [Anderson 2017, *The Problem of Time*, Springer: New York] is a 900-page exposition of the unresolved status of the problem. *Sixty years after Wheeler and DeWitt, the canonical quantization of general relativity still does not admit a satisfactory definition of time evolution.*

The proposed solutions are themselves illuminating. The Page--Wootters proposal (1983) [Page-Wootters 1983, Phys.\ Rev.\ D 27, 2885] introduces a *relational* notion of time: time emerges from correlations between subsystems of the universe rather than as a fundamental parameter. Barbour's "Mach's principle" approach (Barbour 1999, *The End of Time*, Oxford University Press) eliminates time entirely from the foundational level: time is "an illusion" in Barbour's view, with the structure of "now" replacing the structure of time-evolution. Rovelli's relational quantum mechanics (Rovelli 2004, *Quantum Gravity*, Cambridge University Press) again eliminates time at the foundational level, with relations between observables replacing absolute time. Each of these proposals is an attempt to *make sense of the absence of time* in the Wheeler--DeWitt formulation, with the structural commitment that time is not a fundamental feature of the universe but an emergent or illusory phenomenon.

This is precisely Gödel's philosophical position of 1949 (§6.3.10.1 above), restated as a working programme of post-1968 quantum gravity. *The MTW symmetric-block-universe formulation, when quantized, produces a framework in which time does not exist as a fundamental physical quantity.* The frozen-formalism problem and the Gödel-illusory-time philosophy are *the same structural problem* viewed from two different angles --- classical (Gödel 1949) and quantum (Wheeler--DeWitt 1967--1968).

The McGucken framework's resolution of the frozen-formalism problem is structural and complete. *The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is itself the equation of motion of $x_4$*, with time-evolution built into the foundational principle by construction. The principle is *not* a constraint of the form $\hat{H} = 0$; it is a *dynamical equation* specifying the rate of $x_4$'s advance at every event. The Algebraic Channel--Geometric Channel cogeneration of quantum mechanics from $dx_4/dt = ic$ (the [HBR] cascade) produces the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t \psi = \hat{H} \psi$ with an explicit time-derivative term, in which $t$ is the integrated kinematic shadow of $x_4 = ict$ along the worldline of the observer. The quantum-mechanical time-evolution is recovered as a theorem, not added as an additional postulate. *The frozen-formalism problem dissolves because the McGucken framework starts with a dynamical principle, not with a symmetric block-universe metric and a constraint algebra.*

The structural-historical reading: the frozen-formalism problem is the empirical signature, in the quantum-gravity domain, of the same structural defect that produced the Gödel paradox in the classical domain. *Both* are consequences of the MTW symmetric-block-universe treatment of all four dimensions on equal footing. The McGucken framework's promotion of $x_4$ to a dynamically-expanding direction at rate $ic$ dissolves both problems simultaneously --- as it must, because they are two readings of the same structural defect.

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.3 Non-renormalizable infinities in quantum gravity

The third structural problem of the MTW formulation is the non-renormalizability of perturbatively-quantized general relativity. The structural fact is recorded in every standard quantum field theory textbook: *the perturbative quantization of GR is non-renormalizable*, with new ultraviolet divergences appearing at each order in the loop expansion that require infinitely many counter-terms to absorb. Goroff and Sagnotti (1986) [Goroff-Sagnotti 1986, Nucl.\ Phys.\ B 266, 709] demonstrated the explicit 2-loop UV divergence in pure gravity. Deser's 1999 review [Deser 1999, arXiv gr-qc/9911073, *"Infinities in Quantum Gravities"*]: *"there is no viable nonghost quantum field model that includes general relativity"* --- even 11-dimensional supergravity, the unique highest-dimensional supergravity, suffers from 2-loop infinities despite its high degree of supersymmetry.

The structural source of the non-renormalizability is well-understood. Newton's gravitational constant $G$ has dimensions of inverse mass-squared in units where $\hbar = c = 1$, which by simple power-counting makes the perturbative expansion non-renormalizable. As Hossenfelder's review records [Hossenfelder 2017, *"Minimal Length Scenarios for Quantum Gravity"*, Living Reviews in Relativity]: *"It is not that we cannot quantize gravity, but that the attempt to do so leads to a perturbatively non-renormalizable and thus fundamentally nonsensical theory. The basic reason is that the coupling constant of gravity, Newton's constant, is dimensionful."* The theory's predictive content collapses at the Planck scale, where infinitely many counter-terms become equally important.

The community's response has been the development of full-machinery quantum-gravity programmes intended to *solve* the non-renormalizability problem. String theory (Green-Schwarz-Witten 1987 *Superstring Theory*, Polchinski 1998 *String Theory*) replaces point particles with extended one-dimensional objects, with the extended structure regulating the UV divergences. Loop quantum gravity (Rovelli 2004, Ashtekar-Lewandowski 2004) replaces smooth spacetime with discrete spin-network states, again regulating the UV divergences. Asymptotic safety (Weinberg 1979, Reuter 1998, Niedermaier-Reuter 2006) attempts to identify a non-trivial UV fixed point in the renormalization-group flow. Causal-set theory (Sorkin 1991, Bombelli-Lee-Meyer-Sorkin 1987) replaces continuous spacetime with discrete causal sets. *Each of these programmes is an attempt to supply, at the foundational level, a structural feature that regulates the UV behaviour.* None has produced confirmed empirical predictions in the half-century of its development.

The structural reason the MTW formulation produces non-renormalizable infinities is precise. The continuous Lorentzian-manifold treatment of spacetime treats spacetime as smooth at all scales, with no intrinsic quantum scale built into the foundational structure. The quantum scale ($\hbar$) and the gravitational scale ($G$) enter as *independent* fundamental constants, with their combination ($\sqrt{\hbar G/c^3} = \ell_P$, the Planck length) emerging dimensionally but not structurally. The Planck scale is *not* built into the manifold structure; it must be put in by hand or recovered as the scale where the theory breaks down.

The McGucken framework's structural treatment of the quantum scale is fundamentally different. *The quantum nature is built into the foundational principle.* The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies that $x_4$ expands at rate $ic$ from every event. The Born rule, Hilbert space, canonical commutator, uncertainty principle, and Schrödinger equation derive from this principle through the cogeneration cascade ([HBR]). In particular, $\hbar$ is *not* an independent fundamental constant in the McGucken framework. *It is the foundational wavelength of the $x_4$-oscillation per period*, proportional to the Planck length. [5] §I.5 establishes this explicitly: $\hbar$ is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- the McGucken Sphere expands with a wavelength that sets the action $h$, and $\hbar = h/2\pi$ is the action carried per cycle of the $x_4$-oscillation. The Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ is the natural scale of the $x_4$-oscillation; it is built into the foundational structure of the principle.

The structural consequence: *the McGucken framework does not suffer from non-renormalizable UV infinities*, because the quantum scale is built into the foundational structure of the manifold rather than added by hand. The UV behaviour of the theory is regulated at the Planck scale by the foundational $x_4$-oscillation wavelength, with no need for the string-theoretic extended-object regulator, the loop-quantum-gravity discrete-spin-network regulator, the asymptotic-safety UV fixed point, or the causal-set discreteness. The Planck scale is *theorem* in the McGucken framework, not *postulate*.

The structural-historical reading: the non-renormalizability problem of post-1968 quantum gravity is the empirical signature of the MTW formulation having stripped the quantum scale from the foundational level. With $\hbar$ buried inside the metric structure (as the natural scale of quantum field theory-in-curved-spacetime path-integral weights $e^{iS/\hbar}$) rather than built into the structure of $x_4$'s expansion, the community is forced to develop entire research programmes to recover the Planck-scale regulation that the McGucken framework supplies as a structural feature of the foundational principle.

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.4 The speed of light $c$ as a hardcoded constant rather than a derived quantity

The fourth structural problem of the MTW formulation is the status of $c$ itself. In the MTW formulation, $c$ is a *fundamental constant inserted by definition* via the metric signature $(-,+,+,+)$ or its negative, with $g_{00} = -c^2$ providing the speed-of-light boundary between timelike and spacelike intervals. *There is no derivation of $c$ from any principle.* The Stanford Gravity Probe B FAQ records the standard position: *"The invariance of the speed of light in all uniformly moving reference frames is a postulate of special relativity, it does not derive from special relativity, which only then states how observers will experience/measure space and time given the invariance of the speed of light."*

The structural fact: $c$ is a fundamental constant of the standard formulation. Uzan's catalogue of the 22 fundamental constants of the Standard Model and general relativity [Uzan, "Varying constants, gravitation and cosmology," Living Reviews in Relativity 14, 2] lists $c$ as one of three fundamental dimensional constants alongside $G$ and $\hbar$. The standard formulation supplies *no structural reason* for why $c$ takes the particular value it does, or even for why a single universal $c$ exists at all. The constancy of $c$ across reference frames is an empirical fact, codified as a postulate.

The McGucken framework derives $c$ as a *theorem* of the foundational principle. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies that the fourth dimension expands at rate $ic$ at every event; $c$ is the magnitude of this rate. The constancy of $c$ across reference frames is a structural consequence of the invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$: the rate is the same at every event of spacetime, in every coordinate system, *by physical postulate*. [5] §I.5 records this explicitly: $c$ is the substrate's wavelength-per-period ratio $\ell_*/t_*$ in the foundational $x_4$-oscillation, with $\ell_* = \ell_P$ identified via Schwarzschild self-consistency. The framework derives both $c$ and $\hbar$ as theorems and retains only $G$ as a fundamental dimensional constant input.

The structural significance: *the McGucken framework reduces the count of fundamental dimensional constants from three ($c, \hbar, G$) to one ($G$).* This is the kind of foundational-parsimony achievement that Einstein, Hilbert, Dirac, and Wheeler all articulated as the hallmark of a correct foundational theory (§6.11.5 above). The MTW formulation, having abandoned $dx_4/dt = ic$, has no analogous foundational-parsimony content; $c$ remains an independent fundamental constant, inserted by hand into the metric signature.

The Wheeler aphorism's structural content is precisely this: *behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful*. The MTW formulation requires three independent fundamental constants because it has no foundational-derivation structure for them. The McGucken framework requires one. The structural-historical reading: $c$ entered the MTW formulation as a postulate because the community had abandoned the principle ($dx_4/dt = ic$) that supplies $c$ as a theorem. The patch was successful in the sense that the empirical content of relativity was preserved; it was unsuccessful in the structural sense that $c$ remained an unexplained fundamental constant, with no foundational derivation.

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.5 Quantum non-locality forced into the formulation by hand, with no structural source

The fifth structural problem of the MTW formulation is its inability to supply quantum non-locality from any foundational principle. The empirical fact of quantum non-locality is established at extraordinary precision: Bell-CHSH inequality violations to $4.5\sigma$ and $5.3\sigma$ in the Renou-Li-Chen 2025 experiments, Tsirelson saturation $|\mathrm{CHSH}| = 2\sqrt{2}$ confirmed across all loopholes by Hensen et al.\ 2015 and Giustina et al.\ 2015, and the Micius satellite Bell test confirming entanglement at 1200 km separation [Yin et al.\ 2017]. *Quantum non-locality is among the most well-established empirical facts of physics.* The MTW formulation, however, has no structural source for this empirical fact. The Lorentzian manifold of GR is local --- causal influences propagate at $c$ or below --- and quantum mechanics is *added on top* of the local Lorentzian-manifold structure as a separate theory, with non-locality entering as an empirical fact of the quantum-mechanical layer.

The problem is not just terminological. *General relativity and quantum mechanics, in the MTW formulation, do not share a foundational source for their respective structural commitments.* GR's commitments to the Einstein field equations, the local-causal-influence structure, and the equivalence principle are not derived from the same foundational principle as QM's commitments to the Hilbert space, the Born rule, the canonical commutator, and the non-local entanglement structure. The two theories are joined operationally --- quantum field theory in curved spacetime --- but their non-locality structures have no shared foundational origin. The Marolf 2014 nonlocality constraint [Marolf 2014, arXiv 0808.2845] is one attempt to identify the structural requirement that a candidate quantum-gravity theory must satisfy if it is to reproduce the empirical non-locality of QM while respecting the local-causal structure of GR; the constraint is satisfied by no known framework other than the McGucken framework's McGucken Sphere mechanism.

The McGucken framework's structural treatment of non-locality is *derivation, not postulate*. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ generates the *McGucken Sphere*: the spherically symmetric wavefront of $x_4$'s expansion at $c$ from each event. Entangled particle pairs, prepared at a common origin event, share the same McGucken Sphere by construction. The apparent non-locality at later measurement events --- the "spooky action at a distance" of Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen --- is the *kinematic record* of the shared McGucken Sphere wavefront from the common origin. *All non-locality begins as locality*: this is the structural-physical principle that the McGucken framework establishes as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (see [GR-QM-Th] §7 and the Marolf-response content of §6.10.11.5 of this Introduction). The non-locality is *derived* from the foundational principle; it is not added on top of an a-priori-local Lorentzian manifold.

The structural-historical reading: the inability of the MTW formulation to derive quantum non-locality is the empirical signature of the same defect that produced the Gödel paradox and the frozen-formalism problem. The MTW formulation treats spacetime as a Lorentzian manifold with local causal structure built in, with no foundational principle supplying the non-locality content. Quantum non-locality is therefore *forced into* the formulation as an empirical fact, with no structural source. The McGucken framework's promotion of $x_4 = ict$ to the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, generating the McGucken Sphere as the foundational wavefront, supplies the structural source. The non-locality is *built into* the foundational principle from the start.

#### 6.3.10.6 The light cone added by hand via metric signature, with no physical mechanism

The sixth structural problem of the MTW formulation is the status of the light cone itself. In the MTW formulation, the light cone is the locus of events $p$ such that $ds^2 = g_{\mu\nu} dx^\mu dx^\nu = 0$, with the Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$ ensuring that the locus is a three-dimensional cone in spacetime. *The light cone is therefore added by hand via the metric signature*: it has no physical mechanism, no derivation from any principle. The boundary between timelike and spacelike intervals is structurally just where the metric quadratic form vanishes, and the metric signature is itself a postulate of the formulation.

The McGucken framework supplies the light cone as a *physical-mechanism theorem*. The McGucken Sphere is the spherically symmetric wavefront of $x_4$'s expansion at rate $c$ from each event. *The light cone is the integrated history of the McGucken Sphere over time.* Photons ride the wavefront of the McGucken Sphere: their worldlines are the boundary of the $x_4$-expansion-reachable region from each event. The light cone has therefore a *physical mechanism* on the McGucken framework: it is the kinematic record of the $x_4$-expansion at rate $c$, viewed as a hypersurface in spacetime. The boundary between timelike and spacelike intervals is the boundary between events that are inside the McGucken Sphere expansion and events that are outside. The Lorentzian signature of the metric is the kinematic shadow of $x_4$'s expansion at rate $ic$, integrated to give $x_4 = ict$ and squared to give the negative sign in $ds^2$.

The structural-historical reading: the MTW formulation supplies the light cone via the metric signature without a physical mechanism, because it has abandoned the principle ($dx_4/dt = ic$) that supplies the physical mechanism. The light cone exists in the MTW formulation as a *mathematical structure* but not as a *physical object* with a generative mechanism. The McGucken framework restores the physical mechanism: the light cone is the McGucken Sphere's history, the boundary of $x_4$'s expansion-reachable region.

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.7 The arrow of time put by hand via the Past Hypothesis

The seventh structural problem of the MTW formulation is the arrow of time. The empirical fact: time has a direction. Eggs break but do not unbreak; ice cubes melt but do not unmelt; the universe expands but does not unexpand; we remember the past but not the future. *The arrow of time is among the most basic empirical facts of physics.* The structural problem: the underlying dynamical laws of physics (Newtonian mechanics, Maxwell's electrodynamics, general relativity, quantum mechanics, the Standard Model) are all *time-reversal symmetric* (or, in the case of the weak interaction, CPT-symmetric with no fundamental T-asymmetry). There is no structural source in the underlying laws for the empirical asymmetry of time.

The standard response is the *Past Hypothesis*, coined by David Albert in his 2000 book *Time and Chance* [Albert 2000, Harvard University Press]. Albert's formulation, as quoted in the philosophical literature: *"the world first came into being in whatever particular low-entropy highly condensed big-bang sort of macrocondition it is that the normal inferential procedures of cosmology will eventually present to us."* Sean Carroll has been the most prominent advocate [Carroll 2010, *From Eternity to Here*, Dutton]: the universe began in a special low-entropy state, with the arrow of time being the direction of entropy increase from that initial low-entropy condition. Boltzmann had articulated the structural-statistical content of this argument in the 1870s. Penrose 1979 [Penrose, in *General Relativity: An Einstein Centenary Survey*, Cambridge University Press] sharpened the cosmological-state interpretation in the Weyl Curvature Hypothesis.

The Past Hypothesis is *structurally an additional postulate added by hand*. It is not a theorem of any of the underlying dynamical laws. As Carroll, Albert, Lebowitz, Goldstein, North, and others working on the foundations record explicitly: *the underlying laws are time-reversal symmetric; the empirical arrow of time requires an additional postulate about the special initial condition of the universe.* Feynman's 1965 *Character of Physical Law* lectures put the same point characteristically: *"We therefore conclude that the universe is not a fluctuation, and that the order is a memory of conditions when things started. This is not to say that we understand the logic of it."* The "we do not understand the logic of it" is the load-bearing admission: the Past Hypothesis is not a derivation, it is an assumption.

The McGucken framework supplies the arrow of time as a *theorem* of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The McGucken Principle has a *sign choice*: the rate is $+ic$, not $-ic$. *This single sign choice generates the arrow of time at every event of spacetime.* The structural content: $x_4$ advances monotonically at rate $+ic$ at every event, in every coordinate system, by physical postulate. The advance is *one-directional*: the sign is fixed. From this single one-directional advance, all five arrows of time derive:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *The thermodynamic arrow* (entropy increases): derived from the cogeneration of $\mathcal{H}$, the Hilbert space, by the iterated McGucken Sphere construction, with the entropy of any closed subsystem increasing monotonically as $x_4$ advances (see [6] Theorems 9 and 17; the strict Second Law $dS/dt = (3/2) k_B/t$ is itself a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$).

\item *The cosmological arrow* (the universe expands rather than contracts): derived as the integrated cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere expansion from the Big Bang apex, with the FLRW scale factor $a(t)$ increasing monotonically (see [5] §I).

\item *The radiative arrow* (retarded rather than advanced solutions to wave equations are physical): derived as the structural consequence of the McGucken Sphere expanding outward from each emission event, with the retarded Green's function being the natural solution to the wave equation on the manifold (see [GR-QM-Th] §7).

\item *The quantum-mechanical arrow* (wavefunction collapse forward in time, not backward): derived from the cogeneration of the Born rule and the measurement postulate from $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the projection of the wavefunction at the measurement event being the structural consequence of the monotonic $x_4$-advance (see [HBR] §4 and §6 of this Introduction).

\item *The psychological arrow* (we remember the past, not the future): derived as a special case of the thermodynamic arrow applied to neural-tissue subsystems --- memory is the increase of correlation between brain-state and external-event records, which increases monotonically as $x_4$ advances.
\end{enumerate}

*All five arrows of time are derived from the single sign choice $+ic$ rather than $-ic$ in the McGucken Principle.* The Past Hypothesis is not needed as an additional postulate. The arrow of time is a *theorem* of the foundational principle, not an *assumption* about the initial condition of the universe.

The structural-historical reading: the Past Hypothesis is the empirical signature, in the foundations-of-physics domain, of the same structural defect that produced the Gödel paradox, the frozen-formalism problem, the non-renormalizability problem, and the unsourced status of $c$, quantum non-locality, and the light cone in the MTW formulation. *All seven structural problems are consequences of the symmetric-block-universe treatment of spacetime that abandoned $dx_4/dt = ic$.* With the foundational principle restored, all seven problems dissolve. The arrow of time is derived from the sign choice; the light cone is the McGucken Sphere's history; non-locality is the shared-origin McGucken Sphere; $c$ is the rate of $x_4$-expansion; UV infinities are regulated by the foundational $x_4$-oscillation wavelength at the Planck scale; the frozen-formalism problem dissolves because the principle is itself a dynamical equation; and closed timelike curves are forbidden by the monotonic $+ic$ advance.

\medskip

#### 6.3.10.8 The "hard road" framing: every natural element put back by hand, and the question of why nobody saw this

The seven structural problems catalogued above (§§6.3.10.1--6.3.10.7) form a uniform pattern. *Every natural element supplied by $dx_4/dt = ic$ as a theorem must be put back into the MTW formulation by hand, with each restoration introducing its own difficulties, free parameters, additional postulates, or unresolved paradoxes.*

\begin{itemize}
\item Closed timelike curves appear as legitimate solutions of the Einstein field equations $\rightarrow$ Hawking's chronology protection conjecture is needed to defend the universe against itself (1992).

\item The canonical quantization of GR loses time evolution $\rightarrow$ the Page--Wootters relational time, the Barbour Mach's-principle elimination of time, the Rovelli relational-QM elimination of time, the Vasak scalar-time-field extension --- all attempts to recover time from a frozen formalism (1968--2025).

\item Perturbative quantum gravity is non-renormalizable $\rightarrow$ string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety, causal sets --- four major research programmes spanning half a century to recover the Planck-scale regulation that the foundational principle would supply (1968--2026).

\item The speed of light $c$ has no derivation $\rightarrow$ $c$ is added as a fundamental constant in the metric signature, listed among Uzan's 22 fundamental constants of the Standard Model + GR (1900s--present).

\item Quantum non-locality has no structural source on the Lorentzian manifold $\rightarrow$ non-locality is added as an empirical fact of QM with no derivation from foundational principles, with Marolf's 2014 constraint articulating the structural requirement that no standard framework satisfies (1935--present).

\item The light cone has no physical mechanism $\rightarrow$ the light cone is the locus where the metric vanishes, with the Lorentzian signature itself a postulate (1908--present).

\item The arrow of time has no structural source in the time-reversal-symmetric underlying laws $\rightarrow$ the Past Hypothesis is added as an additional postulate about the initial condition of the universe (Boltzmann 1870s, Albert 2000, Carroll 2010).
\end{itemize}

The history of post-1973 foundational physics is the history of this patching process.* Each patch is its own substantive research programme; each programme has its own working physicists, conferences, and textbooks; each programme has produced extensive technical results without resolving its foundational problem. The chronology protection conjecture is still a conjecture, not a theorem. The problem of time in quantum gravity has been open for sixty years. Non-renormalizable quantum gravity has driven five decades of string theory and loop quantum gravity without producing confirmed empirical predictions. The Past Hypothesis remains an unexplained assumption. *Each is the empirical signature of the same structural defect: the abandonment of $dx_4/dt = ic$ in 1973.
The structural diagnosis is precise: *the MTW community took the hard road*. They abandoned a principle ($dx_4/dt = ic$, in its static-coordinate-label form $x_4 = ict$) that supplied each of the seven elements as a theorem. They then had to put each element back into the formulation by hand, with each restoration introducing additional postulates, free parameters, or unresolved conjectures. The cumulative consequence is that the post-1973 foundational-physics programme is structurally a *patching* programme rather than a *derivation* programme: a programme of accommodating empirical facts that have no foundational source, rather than deriving them as theorems of a single principle.

The Wheeler aphorism, restated for the present context: *"behind it all is surely an idea so simple, so beautiful, that when we grasp it... we will all say to each other, how could it have been otherwise? How could we have been so stupid?"* The "how could we have been so stupid" is Wheeler's diagnosis of the patching pattern. Wheeler himself co-authored MTW. Wheeler himself participated in the 1973 abandonment of $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Wheeler himself articulated repeatedly, across the decades that followed, the conviction that the right foundational principle must already be encoded in the mathematics the community has and must be visible once the conceptual framing is correct.

*Why did the MTW community not see this pattern?* The structural answer, drawn from the documentary evidence catalogued above (§§6.3.3--6.3.9), is that the community had abandoned the conceptual salience of the imaginary-time formulation by 1973 --- with $i$ buried inside $g_{00} = -1$ via the modern signature convention, the structural questions "which dimension is expanding?" and "what is the foundational source of the arrow of time, the light cone, quantum non-locality, $c$, and the Planck scale?" became invisible. The community's working tools --- tensor calculus on Lorentzian manifolds with real coordinates and explicit metric signatures --- were precisely the tools optimised to *not see* the structural-asymmetry content that the imaginary unit $i$ in $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, encodes.

This is the same pattern that produced the Heaviside-quaternions abandonment (1880s) and its Hestenes-geometric-algebra recognition (1966+), the Wick-rotation formal-device abandonment (1954) and its Hawking-Euclidean-thermodynamics recognition (1975+), the Einstein-$\Lambda$ abandonment (1929) and its dark-energy recognition (1998), the Dirac-negative-energy artifact reading (1928) and its Anderson-positron-discovery recognition (1932), and the Lorentz-Poincaré-aether ontological-framing reading (1890s) and its Einstein-special-relativity recognition (1905). *The community repeatedly discards mathematical structures that encode physical content, then is forced to recognise the content later, often after a generation has passed.* The McGucken framework's identification of $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the foundational principle restores the content of $x_4 = ict$ that was discarded in 1973. The seven structural problems of the MTW formulation catalogued in this sub-subsection are the empirical signature of the discarded content's structural necessity; the foundational principle is needed to dissolve them simultaneously.

The MTW community took the hard road. The hard road, fifty-three years on (1973--2026), has produced seven open problems, four major research programmes (string theory, loop quantum gravity, asymptotic safety, causal sets) each with its own unresolved foundational issues, and a foundational-physics literature dominated by patches rather than derivations. The easy road, available since Minkowski 1908, was not seen because the community discarded the conceptual structure ($x_4 = ict$ with the imaginary unit $i$ as load-bearing) that made the easy road visible. The McGucken framework restores the easy road by promoting $x_4 = ict$ from a static coordinate label to the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the seven structural problems dissolving simultaneously as the foundational principle generates each natural element as a theorem.

That nobody in the MTW community saw this, even though Wheeler himself articulated the foundational-simplicity programme repeatedly across the post-1973 decades, is the structural-historical fact that the present sub-subsection records. *They had the conceptual content in hand --- Einstein, Minkowski, Pauli, Sommerfeld all used $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, continuously through the 1950s* (§§6.3.3, 6.3.4 above). The community lost the conceptual content during the post-1930 modernization of GR pedagogy, with MTW 1973 the canonical moment of formal abandonment. The hard road that followed --- seven open problems, four major research programmes, fifty-three years of unresolved foundational issues --- is the empirical signature of what the community lost when it abandoned $x_4 = ict$. The McGucken framework is the explicit attempt to restore what was lost, with the seven structural problems dissolving as the foundational principle is restored.
