### 6.5.VR.5 Structural-historical reading

The Van Raamsdonk programme exemplifies the historical pattern this Introduction has documented across §§6.3.10, 6.4.9, and 6.11.5. A deep structural correlation is identified by the standard programme --- in this case, the entanglement-geometry correspondence in asymptotically AdS spacetimes --- but the foundational principle that *generates* the correlation is not within the programme. The programme operates correlationally rather than generatively. The McGucken framework supplies the foundational principle and the correlation becomes a theorem.

\medskip

The same structural pattern has appeared repeatedly across the history of foundational physics:

\begin{itemize}
\item Heaviside (1880s) abandoned the quaternionic structure of Maxwell's electrodynamics in favour of the modern three-vector formulation. Hestenes (1966+) recognised the foundational structure of geometric algebra. *The structure was discarded, then recognised as physical.*

\item The community discarded the Lorentz-Poincaré aether ontology (1890s). Einstein (1905) supplied the foundational principle (the relativity postulate combined with the constancy of $c$) that generated special relativity. *The structure was discarded, then recognised as physical.*

\item Einstein abandoned the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ in 1929. Riess-Schmidt-Perlmutter (1998) recognised it as dark energy through Type Ia supernova observations. *The structure was discarded, then recognised as physical.*

\item Wick (1954) introduced the imaginary-time rotation as a formal device for quantum field theory calculation. Hawking (1975) recognised the Wick-rotated Euclidean structure as physical content (the Bekenstein-Hawking temperature of a black hole). *The structure was discarded, then recognised as physical.*

\item Dirac (1928) wrote the relativistic electron equation; the negative-energy solutions were initially read as artifacts. Anderson (1932) recognised them as positrons. *The structure was discarded, then recognised as physical.*

\item Maldacena-Faulkner-Guica-Hartman-Myers-Van Raamsdonk (1997-2017) identified the entanglement-geometry correlation as a deep structural feature of holographic quantum gravity. The foundational principle that generates the correlation was not within the programme. The McGucken framework restores the foundational principle.
\end{itemize}

\medskip

The structural improvement is not that the Van Raamsdonk programme is wrong. The programme is correct within its scope, and its mathematical achievements --- the 2014 derivation of linearised Einstein equations from the first law of entanglement entropy, the Lewkowycz-Maldacena proof of Ryu-Takayanagi, the Maldacena-Susskind ER = EPR identification, the 2017 nonlinear extension --- are real contributions to twenty-first-century theoretical physics. The structural improvement is that the McGucken framework supplies the foundational principle ($dx_4/dt = ic$) and the physical mechanism (the McGucken Sphere) that turn the correlations the Van Raamsdonk programme identifies into theorems of one foundational principle.

\medskip

The Van Raamsdonk programme's central insight --- that entanglement and geometry are deeply connected --- is *right*. On the McGucken framework, it is right because both descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The McGucken Sphere is simultaneously the source of locality (Lorentzian metric, light cone, retarded propagation) and the source of non-locality (entanglement, Bell-CHSH, Tsirelson saturation, McGucken-Sphere-overlap structure at common origin). One principle. Two readings: local and non-local. Both correct. Both derived from the same foundational equation. *The Van Raamsdonk programme's correlation becomes the McGucken framework's theorem* --- which is the structural shape every deep correlation in the history of foundational physics has taken, when the foundational principle that generates it has finally been identified.

## 6.6 Diffeomorphism Invariance: The McGucken Subgroup and the Preserved Foliation

### 6.6.1 The standard role of diffeomorphism invariance in GR

Diffeomorphism invariance is the foundational gauge symmetry of general relativity. The statement: *the physical content of the theory is invariant under any smooth coordinate transformation $\phi : M \to M$ of the spacetime manifold*. The full diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ acts on the manifold and its tensor fields, with the invariance encoded by the requirement that the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ are *general covariant* --- they take the same form in every coordinate chart.

The structural roles of diffeomorphism invariance in standard GR:

- *General covariance*: the Einstein field equations have no preferred coordinate system; the same physical equation holds in every chart.
- *Bianchi identities*: the contracted second Bianchi identity $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ follows from diffeomorphism invariance via Noether's second theorem; this in turn forces $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (stress-energy conservation) for any source compatible with the field equations.
- *ADM Hamiltonian formulation* [Arnowitt-Deser-Misner 1962]: the 3+1 decomposition of spacetime exhibits the diffeomorphism group as the gauge group of the Hamiltonian system, with the Hamiltonian constraint $\mathcal{H} \approx 0$ generating time-translations and the momentum constraint $\mathcal{H}_i \approx 0$ generating spatial diffeomorphisms.
- *Wheeler--DeWitt equation* in canonical quantum gravity: the Hamiltonian constraint becomes the operator equation $\hat{\mathcal{H}} |\Psi\rangle = 0$, which any physical state of quantum gravity must satisfy; this is the canonical-quantum-gravity formulation of the *problem of time*.

Diffeomorphism invariance is thus load-bearing for the standard Hamiltonian and canonical-quantum-gravity formulations of GR.

### 6.6.2 The McGucken framework's partial gauge group: $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G) \subset \mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$

The McGucken framework has a subtler relationship with diffeomorphism invariance, and the precise statement is *partial diffeomorphism invariance*: the framework is invariant under a strict subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$, but *not* under the full diffeomorphism group.

*The McGucken framework's gauge group is the subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G) \subset \mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ defined as the subgroup of diffeomorphisms that preserve the invariant/deformable split (Section 1.4):*
$$\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G) \;:=\; \{ \phi \in \mathrm{Diff}(M_G) : \phi^*(dx_4) = dx_4 \text{ and } \phi \text{ acts arbitrarily on } x_1, x_2, x_3 \}.$$

Equivalently: $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ consists of diffeomorphisms that (a) act trivially on the $x_4$-coordinate (preserve the temporal foliation), (b) act arbitrarily on the spatial three (preserve the deformable spatial sector under general diffeomorphism of the spatial slices). The group is a semi-direct product
$$\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G) \;\cong\; \mathrm{Diff}(\Sigma_3) \rtimes \mathbb{R}_t,$$
where $\Sigma_3$ is a spatial slice (3-manifold) and $\mathbb{R}_t$ acts trivially as time translations along the $x_4$-foliation.

The subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is strictly smaller than $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$. The diffeomorphisms that are *forbidden* by the McGucken framework are those that *change the temporal foliation* --- diffeomorphisms that tilt the time-axis at one event relative to another, mixing temporal and spatial coordinates in a position-dependent way. Under the standard ADM 3+1 decomposition, these would be implemented by lapse-function or shift-vector variations; on the McGucken framework, the lapse function is fixed by the McGucken-Invariance Lemma ($g_{x_4 x_4} = -1$ identically) and the shift vector is fixed by the gravity-rigid status of the temporal axis. There is no freedom to re-foliate.

### 6.6.3 What is preserved: full spatial diffeomorphism invariance, full Lorentz invariance at every event

Although $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is strictly smaller than $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$, the McGucken framework preserves *all* the load-bearing symmetry content that standard GR derives from full diffeomorphism invariance:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Full spatial diffeomorphism invariance*: arbitrary smooth coordinate transformations of the spatial slice $\Sigma_3$ are allowed and are gauge symmetries of the framework. The Einstein field equations on the spatial sector are general covariant under $\mathrm{Diff}(\Sigma_3)$.

\item *Full local Lorentz invariance at every event*: by Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$), every event of $M_G$ admits a local Lorentz frame in which special relativity holds exactly. Lorentz boosts (the symmetry group of relativity) are preserved as local symmetries; the framework is *not* a violation of relativity.

\item *Contracted Bianchi identities*: $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ follows on the McGucken framework via Theorem 9.4.2.3 of Chapter 9 (Einstein-tensor conservation as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the second Bianchi identity). This does *not* require full diffeomorphism invariance; it requires only the algebraic structure of the Riemann tensor on $M_G$ (the curvature derived from the iterated-Sphere closure failure, Theorem 9.1.2.6).

\item *Energy-momentum conservation*: $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ follows from the Einstein equations + Bianchi identity, exactly as in standard GR.

\item *The 12 observational tests of GR*: Mercury perihelion advance, Eddington 1919 light bending, gravitational redshift (Pound-Rebka 1960), gravitational waves (LIGO 2015), Lense-Thirring frame-dragging (Gravity Probe B), Shapiro delay, geodetic precession, gravitational time dilation (GPS), strong-field binary pulsar precession (Hulse-Taylor 1974), gravitational lensing, gravitational redshift in cosmology, BAO/CMB anisotropy. All twelve are recovered on the McGucken framework via the spatial-sector field equations and the geodesic equation, both of which are preserved under $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$.
\end{itemize}

What is *lost* by the restriction to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$:

- The gauge freedom to re-foliate spacetime (the gauge freedom that ADM exhibits as the Hamiltonian constraint).
- The Wheeler-DeWitt equation $\hat{\mathcal{H}} |\Psi\rangle = 0$ as the canonical-quantum-gravity constraint.
- The problem-of-time of canonical quantum gravity.

These losses are *features* of the McGucken framework, identifying that the standard canonical-quantum-gravity formulation is built on a gauge freedom that the framework does not have. The problem-of-time of canonical quantum gravity is a problem *because* the framework attempts to gauge-fix a temporal foliation that the McGucken framework specifies as a physical principle.

### 6.6.4 The preferred foliation as physical, not gauge: empirical content

The restriction to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ implies that there is a *preferred temporal foliation* on $M_G$: the foliation by $x_4$-constant hypersurfaces, with $x_4$ being the imaginary-rate axis of $dx_4/dt = ic$. This preferred foliation is a *physical feature* of the framework, not a gauge freedom.

This raises the question: is there an empirical signature of the preferred foliation? The McGucken framework's answer: *yes*. The empirical signature is the **CMB preferred frame**.

The cosmic microwave background, observed by COBE 1992, WMAP 2003, Planck 2013, exhibits a *dipole anisotropy* corresponding to the Earth's motion at $\sim 370$ km/s relative to a frame in which the CMB is approximately isotropic. This "CMB rest frame" is, on the standard framework, treated as an empirical coincidence of cosmological initial conditions --- there is no foundational reason for its existence within the standard general-covariant framework. On the McGucken framework, the CMB rest frame is the *empirical signature of the cosmological-scale McGucken-Sphere from the Big Bang*: the universe-scale wavefront from the initial-singularity apex, expanding at universal rate $c$, defines the preferred foliation universally, and the frame in which one is at rest relative to this universal-scale wavefront is the CMB rest frame.

The CMB preferred frame is therefore *consistent with* (and indeed *predicted by*) the McGucken framework's restriction of the diffeomorphism gauge group. The preferred foliation that $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ imposes structurally is the *same* preferred foliation that the CMB dipole observes empirically. This is an empirical consistency check: the standard framework treats the CMB preferred frame as a coincidence; the McGucken framework predicts its existence as a structural consequence.

### 6.6.5 Three structural consequences of the partial diffeomorphism gauge group

The structural consequences of restricting to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *No spacetime foam.* Standard perturbative quantum gravity expects spacetime to fluctuate at the Planck scale due to graviton-loop quantum corrections, with the metric having short-distance "foam" structure (Wheeler 1957). On the McGucken framework, the temporal sector cannot foam (it is gravity-rigid by the McGucken-Invariance Lemma); only the spatial sector can foam, and the spatial-sector fluctuations are controlled by the iterated-Sphere geometric structure rather than by graviton-loop UV divergences. The foam picture is structurally absent.

\item *Dissolution of the Hamiltonian constraint.* Standard ADM canonical quantum gravity has the Hamiltonian constraint $\mathcal{H} = 0$ as the generator of time-translation gauge freedom; in canonical quantum gravity this becomes the Wheeler-DeWitt operator equation $\hat{\mathcal{H}} |\Psi\rangle = 0$ that physical states must satisfy. On the McGucken framework, the time-translation is *not* a gauge freedom but the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The Hamiltonian constraint is structurally redundant; the Wheeler-DeWitt equation dissolves; the *problem of time* of canonical quantum gravity has no analogue on the McGucken framework, because time is not a gauge-redundant parameter but a physical advance at universal rate $ic$.

\item *The Bianchi-identity content is preserved without requiring full diffeomorphism invariance.* The contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ is a consequence of the algebraic structure of the Riemann tensor on $M_G$ (the closure-failure of iterated-Sphere parallel-transport, Theorem 9.1.2.6 of Chapter 9), not of diffeomorphism invariance alone. Standard pedagogy derives the Bianchi identities from diffeomorphism invariance via Noether's second theorem; the McGucken framework derives them from the structural properties of the iterated-Sphere flow. The two derivations agree on the Bianchi identities themselves, but their structural origins are different. Energy-momentum conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ follows on the McGucken framework via Theorem 10.3.2.1 of Chapter 10 (on-shell conservation enhancement).
\end{enumerate}

### 6.6.6 Relationship to unimodular gravity and to the standard Hamiltonian formulation

The McGucken framework's restriction of the diffeomorphism gauge group has structural resonances with two other approaches in the gravitational literature.

**Unimodular gravity** [Einstein 1919; Anderson and Finkelstein 1971; van der Bij, van Dam, and Ng 1982; Smolin 2009; Padilla and Saltas 2014]: restricts the diffeomorphism group to the subgroup of *volume-preserving diffeomorphisms*, $\mathrm{SDiff}(M)$. The cosmological constant becomes a constant of integration rather than a parameter in the action; this is the well-known resolution of one aspect of the cosmological-constant problem. The McGucken framework's restriction to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is *not* the same as restriction to $\mathrm{SDiff}(M_G)$ --- the two subgroups are not identical --- but both share the structural feature of restricting full $\mathrm{Diff}(M)$ to a strict subgroup, both have a preferred-volume-form/preferred-foliation structure, and both have resolutions of the cosmological-constant problem.

**The ADM 3+1 decomposition** [Arnowitt, Deser, and Misner 1962] decomposes spacetime into a foliation by spacelike hypersurfaces, with the lapse function $N$ and shift vector $N^i$ as gauge parameters generating temporal and spatial diffeomorphisms respectively. On the McGucken framework, the lapse is *fixed* to $N = 1$ by the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (the gravity-rigid temporal axis with $g_{x_4 x_4} = -1$), and the shift is *fixed* to $N^i = 0$ by the structural-separation of the temporal and spatial sectors. The ADM gauge structure is therefore *partially gauge-fixed* on the McGucken framework: the spatial-diffeomorphism part of the constraint algebra remains a gauge freedom, but the temporal-diffeomorphism part is foliation-fixed.

This is structurally similar to working in *synchronous gauge* (lapse-fixed coordinates with $g_{00} = -1$ and $g_{0i} = 0$) within standard ADM, but with the difference that synchronous gauge is a *choice* (one of many possible gauge fixings), while on the McGucken framework the synchronous-like gauge is *physical* (the foliation is fixed by the McGucken Principle, not by an arbitrary gauge choice).

### 6.6.7 The structural verdict: partial diffeomorphism invariance with full empirical recovery

The McGucken framework's relationship with diffeomorphism invariance is therefore precise:

- *Full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ is not the gauge group of the framework.* The full diffeomorphism group is too large; it includes transformations (re-foliations of the temporal axis) that the framework does not permit.

- *$\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G) = \mathrm{Diff}(\Sigma_3) \rtimes \mathbb{R}_t$ is the gauge group of the framework.* Spatial diffeomorphism invariance is preserved in full; time-translation invariance is preserved as a global symmetry (not a gauge symmetry) generated by the McGucken Principle.

- *Local Lorentz invariance at every event is preserved* by Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$). The framework is not a violation of relativity at the local level.

- *The CMB preferred frame is the empirical signature of the preferred foliation.* The framework's restriction of the gauge group has an observable consequence that the standard framework treats as a coincidence.

- *The Bianchi identities, energy-momentum conservation, and all twelve observational tests of GR are recovered.* The load-bearing observable content of standard GR is preserved despite the gauge-group restriction.

- *The Hamiltonian constraint, the Wheeler-DeWitt equation, and the problem-of-time dissolve* as structural consequences of the framework's gauge-group restriction. These are features, not bugs: the standard canonical-quantum-gravity problems are problems precisely because the standard framework attempts to gauge-fix a foliation that the McGucken framework specifies as a physical principle.

The structural verdict: the McGucken framework's diffeomorphism structure is *partial* relative to the standard formulation but *complete* relative to the empirical content of gravitational physics. The gauge-group restriction is the structural recognition that the preferred temporal foliation is a *physical feature* of the framework, with empirical support from the CMB preferred frame, rather than a gauge freedom that requires gauge-fixing. The standard canonical-quantum-gravity problems (Wheeler-DeWitt, problem-of-time, no-foam-without-graviton-loops) are dissolved at the source.

## 6.7 The Cosmic Microwave Background Preferred Frame as Empirical Signature of the Cosmological McGucken Sphere

A foundational empirical advantage of the McGucken framework is its direct account of the cosmic microwave background preferred frame --- an observed feature of the universe that the standard framework treats as a coincidence of cosmological initial conditions but that the McGucken framework predicts as a structural consequence of the foundational principle. Section 6.7 develops this account.

### 6.7.1 The empirical observation

The cosmic microwave background, observed by COBE 1992, WMAP 2003, and Planck 2013, exhibits a *dipole anisotropy*: the CMB temperature has a sinusoidal angular dependence of amplitude $\Delta T/T \approx 1.23 \times 10^{-3}$, corresponding to the Earth's motion at approximately $370$ km/s relative to a definite cosmic rest frame [COBE Collaboration 1996; Planck Collaboration 2014]. This "CMB rest frame" is the frame in which the CMB temperature is approximately isotropic on large angular scales. The frame is observable, measurable, and reproducible: any observer at any spacetime event in the universe can determine their velocity relative to this frame by measuring the CMB dipole.

The existence of a preferred cosmic rest frame is in apparent tension with the *full general covariance* of standard general relativity, which posits that no inertial frame is preferred over any other. Standard cosmology resolves this tension by treating the CMB rest frame as an empirical fact about a *specific cosmological solution* of the Einstein equations --- the FLRW solution with isotropic-homogeneous initial conditions --- but not as a foundational feature of the underlying physics. The CMB rest frame, on this reading, is a feature of *our universe's particular initial conditions* rather than a feature of the laws of physics themselves. The standard pedagogy treats this as a coincidence: of all the possible initial conditions for a generally-covariant cosmology, ours happened to produce a definite preferred frame, but there is no foundational reason this had to be so.

### 6.7.2 The McGucken framework's structural prediction

On the McGucken framework, the CMB preferred frame is *not* a coincidence of initial conditions. It is the *empirical signature of the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere from the Big Bang*.

The structural account: by the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ of the McGucken Principle, the fourth dimension $x_4$ expands at universal rate $ic$ from every spacetime event of $M_G$ in a spherically symmetric manner. Applied at the cosmological scale, this principle implies that the universe has a *unique foundational event* --- the initial singularity at $t = 0$, the apex of the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere --- from which the universe-scale wavefront has been propagating outward at universal rate $c$ for the cosmic time $t_0 \approx 13.8 \times 10^9$ years since the Big Bang. The current cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere has radius $c t_0 \approx 4.4 \times 10^{26}$ metres in the Hubble-scale comoving frame.

The CMB photons emitted at recombination (at cosmic time $t_\mathrm{rec} \approx 3.8 \times 10^5$ years after the Big Bang) are riding the wavefronts of the universe-scale McGucken Sphere from their emission events outward to our detection event today. The CMB is therefore the *electromagnetic record of the cosmological McGucken Sphere wavefront at recombination*, projected to our current detection event.

The preferred frame of the CMB is the frame in which one is *at rest relative to the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere wavefront*. Equivalently, it is the frame in which the wavefronts of the cosmological Sphere are isotropic about the observer's spatial location, with no dipole anisotropy. The dipole anisotropy measures the observer's *velocity relative to the universal wavefront* --- the same velocity that would be measured by any frame-dragging argument relative to the cosmological-scale geometry of $M_G$.

### 6.7.3 The structural contrast with standard cosmology

The contrast with the standard reading is direct:

- *Standard reading*: the CMB rest frame is an empirical fact about the initial conditions of our universe. There is no foundational reason for a preferred frame to exist; if the universe had been more anisotropic at recombination, no CMB dipole would have been observed, but this would not have contradicted any principle of physics. The preferred frame is a *contingent fact*, not a structural prediction.

- *McGucken reading*: the CMB rest frame is the empirical signature of the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere expansion at rate $c$ from the Big Bang apex. The preferred frame *exists structurally* on the McGucken framework, because the cosmological-scale wavefront is a definite spherical surface with a definite outward-propagation direction. The CMB dipole is the *expected* empirical consequence; its existence is a *structural prediction*, not a contingent fact.

The McGucken framework therefore *explains* the existence of the CMB preferred frame in a way that the standard framework does not. The standard framework can accommodate the CMB preferred frame within its formalism (any FLRW solution with cosmologically symmetric initial conditions produces a definite preferred frame), but it does not *predict* the preferred frame from foundational principles. The McGucken framework predicts it: it is the empirical signature of the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ applied at the cosmological scale.

### 6.7.4 The structural consistency of the preferred frame with local Lorentz invariance

A natural concern: does the preferred cosmological frame violate local Lorentz invariance, which is the foundational symmetry of special relativity? The answer is *no*, and the structural reason is precise.

The preferred cosmological frame on the McGucken framework is a *global* feature of the manifold $M_G$ at the cosmological scale --- the foliation by the cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere wavefronts from the Big Bang apex. It is *not* a local feature that could be measured by any inertial observer in a small local laboratory.

Local Lorentz invariance, by Theorem 8 (Poincaré invariance of $dx_4/dt = ic$), holds at every event of $M_G$: every event admits a local Lorentz frame in which special relativity holds exactly, with no preferred direction in the local tangent space. The cosmological preferred frame does not violate this local invariance because it is *not* a local feature --- it is a cosmological-scale feature that is invisible to any laboratory-scale measurement.

The CMB dipole measurement is therefore *not* a violation of local Lorentz invariance; it is a measurement of the observer's *velocity relative to a cosmological-scale structure* (the universe-wavefront from the Big Bang apex), which is a perfectly relativistic concept. The structural separation: *local Lorentz invariance is preserved at every event*; *the cosmological-scale wavefront foliation is preserved as a global feature*. The two are consistent.

This is structurally analogous to the relationship between local gauge invariance and global Lorentz invariance in standard particle physics: gauge invariance holds locally; spacetime symmetries hold globally. On the McGucken framework, local Lorentz invariance holds locally; the cosmological-scale preferred foliation holds globally. The two operate at different structural levels.

## 6.8 Arrows of Time and Asymmetries: One Sign-Choice in $dx_4/dt = ic$ Generates All Five

A structural advantage of the McGucken framework over standard physics is its account of the *arrows of time*. Standard physics has the embarrassment that the microscopic laws are time-symmetric (the Lagrangians of QED, QCD, GR are all invariant under $t \to -t$ to a high degree of accuracy), but every macroscopic phenomenon picks out a definite direction. The standard "explanation" is *low-entropy initial conditions* (Boltzmann; Penrose's Weyl Curvature Hypothesis 1979), which shifts the asymmetry from the laws to the initial conditions without explaining *why* those particular initial conditions held. This is structurally a fable in the §1.5.3.5 diagnostic sense: it patches the asymmetry without identifying its foundational source.

On the McGucken framework, the multiple arrows of time *reduce to a single fact*: the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ specifies that $x_4$ *advances*, with definite sign. The principle has a sign --- $+ic$, not $\pm ic$, and certainly not $-ic$. This single sign-choice in one foundational equation generates *every* empirical asymmetry of time.

### 6.8.1 The five canonical arrows of time

Standard physics distinguishes at least five distinct arrows of time, each picking out the same direction in our universe but each with apparently independent origins:

\begin{enumerate}
\item *Thermodynamic arrow*: entropy increases monotonically (the Second Law of Thermodynamics).
\item *Cosmological arrow*: the universe expands, not contracts (Hubble's law; accelerating expansion).
\item *Electromagnetic / radiation arrow*: electromagnetic radiation is emitted by sources and propagates outward (retarded Green's function), not absorbed from infinity (advanced Green's function).
\item *Quantum arrow*: measurement collapse, decoherence, and quantum-classical transitions are irreversible.
\item *Psychological arrow*: we remember the past, not the future; memory is the record of past events.
\end{enumerate}

Standard physics treats each of these as an independent puzzle. The thermodynamic arrow is explained by low-entropy initial conditions; the cosmological arrow by the Big Bang; the electromagnetic arrow by retarded boundary conditions on Maxwell's equations; the quantum arrow by decoherence into environmental degrees of freedom; the psychological arrow by neuroscience or anthropic considerations. *No single foundational principle generates all five from one source* in standard physics.

### 6.8.2 The single-source structural account on the McGucken framework

On the McGucken framework, all five arrows of time descend from the *sign-choice* in $dx_4/dt = ic$. The principle specifies that the fourth dimension advances at rate $+ic$, not $-ic$. The plus sign in the rate is the *foundational source* of every time-asymmetry observed in the universe.

The structural derivations:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Cosmological arrow.* The cosmological-scale McGucken Sphere expands *outward* from the Big Bang apex at rate $+c$, not inward. The Hubble flow's sign --- universe expanding rather than contracting --- is the cosmological-scale projection of the $+ic$ sign in the principle. The accelerating expansion (Riess et al.\ 1998; Perlmutter et al.\ 1999) is the iterated-Sphere amplification of the foundational sign-choice.

\item *Thermodynamic arrow.* By Theorem 35 of [4] (the Generalised Second Law as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$), entropy increases monotonically because the iterated-Sphere flow on the deformable spatial sector preserves no recurrence on any timescale less than the cosmological Poincaré recurrence time. The McGucken-Sphere wavefront expansion at rate $c$ from every event drives entropy *forward* in the direction of $x_4$-advance; the monotonic advance of $x_4$ at rate $+ic$ is the foundational source of the Second Law.

\item *Electromagnetic / radiation arrow.* The retarded Green's function $G_\mathrm{ret}(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}', t - t') = \delta(t - t' - |\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|/c)/(4\pi|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{x}'|)$ is the geometric content of the *outward-expanding* McGucken Sphere from every source event. The wavefront propagates at rate $+c$ outward from the source, not inward at rate $-c$; the retarded form is the *forced* form on the McGucken framework, with the advanced form (which would correspond to an inward-collapsing Sphere) structurally absent. The standard puzzle of "why retarded rather than advanced" is dissolved: the retarded form is forced by the sign-choice in $dx_4/dt = ic$.

\item *Quantum arrow.* The iterated-Sphere convergence that constitutes quantum measurement (the wavefront-on-wavefront geometric event of Section 1.4.1's structural reading of the measurement problem) proceeds in the direction of $x_4$-advance, not its reverse. The wavefunction's evolution is *forward* in $x_4$-time at rate $ic$, with the Compton phase $\Phi = e^{-imc^2\Delta\tau/\hbar}$ accumulating along the worldline in the forward direction. Decoherence and measurement-induced state-transitions are irreversible because the underlying $x_4$-advance is irreversible; the quantum arrow is the structural projection of the foundational sign-choice onto the quantum-mechanical wavefront.

\item *Psychological arrow.* Memory is the record of past iterated-Sphere states accumulated along a worldline through $x_4$. Information from past events is encoded in the spatial-sector configuration of physical systems (neurons, hard drives, sediment layers); information from future events is not, because the iterated-Sphere flow at rate $ic$ propagates *forward*, with the wavefront generating new spatial-sector states without leaving traces of states-not-yet-reached. The psychological arrow is the structural consequence of memory being a record of past Sphere-states, which exists because the $x_4$-advance is in the $+ic$ direction.
\end{itemize}
