# 10.1 Algebraic Channel, Step 1: The Foliation-Preserving Diffeomorphism Group $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ {#sec:Diff-McG}

## 10.1.1 Definition

The McGucken Principle the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ endows $M_G$ with a global time function $x^0 = ct$ whose level surfaces $\Sigma_t$ are the spatial slices of the $x_4$-foliation (Definition 1 of the Introduction). The rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the universal advance rate of $x_4$ at every event of $M_G$ (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i)). Diffeomorphisms of $M_G$ that preserve this foliation structure form a strict subgroup of the full diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$.

**Definition 10.1.1 ($\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$, the foliation-preserving subgroup).** Let $M_G$ be a smooth four-manifold equipped with a global time function $x^0: M_G \to \mathbb{R}$ whose level surfaces $\Sigma_t$ are the $x_4$-foliation slices. The foliation-preserving diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is the subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ generated by smooth vector fields of the form
$$\xi^\mu \;=\; \bigl( \xi^0(x^0),\; \xi^i(x^0, x^j) \bigr), \tag{10.1.1.1}$$
where $\xi^0$ depends only on the time coordinate $x^0$ (rigid time reparametrisation) and $\xi^i$ may depend on all four coordinates (free spatial diffeomorphisms).
## 10.1.2 The McGucken Principle forces the restriction

**Lemma 10.1.2.1 (McP forces $\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)$).** Diffeomorphisms of $M_G$ generated by vector fields $\xi^\mu$ with $\partial \xi^0 / \partial x^i \neq 0$ are *not* symmetries of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Equivalently: any diffeomorphism that mixes the spatial coordinates into the time coordinate non-rigidly changes the $x_4$-advance rate at different events, contradicting the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i).
*Proof.* Consider a vector field $\xi^\mu$ with $\xi^0$ depending on a spatial coordinate, say $\partial \xi^0 / \partial x^1 \neq 0$. The diffeomorphism $\phi_\epsilon: x^\mu \to x^\mu + \epsilon \xi^\mu(x)$ induces a change in coordinate-time labels: an event at coordinate-time $x^0$ and spatial position $(x^1, x^2, x^3)$ is mapped to coordinate-time $x^0 + \epsilon \xi^0(x^0, x^1, x^2, x^3)$. The rate of $x_4$-advance per *coordinate-time* in the new coordinates is then
$$\frac{dx_4}{dt'}\bigg|_{\phi(p)} \;=\; \frac{dx_4}{dt}\bigg|_p \cdot \frac{dt}{dt'}\bigg|_p \;=\; ic \cdot \frac{1}{1 + \epsilon (\partial \xi^0/\partial x^0)} \cdot (\text{spatially dependent corrections}).$$
Since $\partial \xi^0/\partial x^i \neq 0$, the rate $dx_4/dt'$ varies with spatial position $x^i$: two events at the same coordinate-time $t'$ but different spatial positions have different rates of $x_4$-advance in the new coordinate. This contradicts the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i), which states the rate is the same at every event.

Hence only diffeomorphisms with $\partial \xi^0 / \partial x^i = 0$ for $i = 1, 2, 3$ --- equivalently, with $\xi^0 = \xi^0(x^0)$ depending on the time coordinate alone --- are compatible with $dx_4/dt = ic$. The spatial components $\xi^i$ may depend freely on all coordinates because the spatial slice is *deformable* (the invariant/deformable split, Definition 5 of the Introduction). $\square$

**Lemma 10.1.2.2 ($\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is a strict subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$).** The full diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ is generated by vector fields $\xi^\mu = (\xi^0(x^0, x^i), \xi^i(x^0, x^j))$ with no restriction on $\xi^0$. $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is the strict subgroup obtained by restricting $\xi^0$ to depend only on $x^0$.
*Proof.* By Definition 10.1.1 and Lemma 10.1.2.1: $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ admits all vector fields of the form (10.1.1.1) but excludes those with $\partial \xi^0/\partial x^i \neq 0$. The exclusion is non-trivial: vector fields with non-zero $\partial \xi^0/\partial x^i$ are generic elements of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ but are *not* in $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$. Hence $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ is a proper subgroup. $\square$

## 10.1.3 Structural priority of the foliation factorisation

**Proposition 10.1.3 (Factorisation of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ by $dx_4/dt = ic$).** (Recapitulating Theorem 9 of the Introduction.) The McGucken Principle factors Hilbert's diffeomorphism invariance into a kinematic component (the symmetry under $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$) and a constitutive component (the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$). The remaining $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G) / \mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ quotient is recovered as an *on-shell* symmetry --- the full diffeomorphism invariance of general relativity emerges as a consequence of the matter equations of motion, not as an off-shell foundational input.
*Proof.* The factorisation is the structural content of Lemmas 10.1.2.1, 10.1.2.2 combined with the on-shell enhancement theorem proved in §10.3 below. The structural priority statement: Hilbert (1915) postulated $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$-invariance as a *primitive* of the variational formulation of GR. The McGucken framework derives this from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the on-shell content of the field equations, with the off-shell symmetry being the strict subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$. $\square$

# 10.2 Algebraic Channel, Step 2: The Constitutive Identity {#sec:constitutive}

## 10.2.1 The four-velocity budget as the constitutive identity

The constitutive identity of the McGucken framework is the four-velocity budget identity (GR T1, Chapter 5):
$$u^\mu u_\mu \;=\; g_{\mu\nu}\, u^\mu u^\nu \;=\; -c^2 \tag{10.2.1.1}$$
for every massive particle on its worldline. This identity is *not* a definition of proper time; it is a *theorem* of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along both channels of the McGucken Duality (Theorem 5.1.2.8 of Chapter 5 for the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel, Theorem 5.1.3.5 for the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel).

## 10.2.2 The stress-energy tensor of a perfect fluid

For a perfect fluid of matter particles each satisfying (10.2.1.1), the stress-energy tensor is
$$T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \;+\; p\, g^{\mu\nu}, \tag{10.2.2.1}$$
with $\rho$ the rest-frame energy density, $p$ the rest-frame pressure, and $u^\mu$ the fluid four-velocity satisfying the constitutive identity (10.2.1.1). For a pressureless dust, $p = 0$ and $T^{\mu\nu} = \rho c^2 \cdot u^\mu u^\nu / c^2 = \rho\, u^\mu u^\nu$. For radiation, $p = \rho c^2 / 3$ (equation of state $w = 1/3$).

**Lemma 10.2.2.1 (Constitutive identity for fluid four-velocity).** The fluid four-velocity in (10.2.2.1) satisfies $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ pointwise, by GR T1 applied to each fluid element.

*Proof.* Direct from GR T1: each fluid element is a massive-particle worldline, satisfying the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ by Theorem 5.1.2.8 of Chapter 5. The fluid four-velocity is the collective four-velocity of fluid elements at each event, also satisfying (10.2.1.1) pointwise. $\square$

# 10.3 Algebraic Channel, Step 3: Noether's Second Theorem and On-Shell Enhancement {#sec:on-shell-enhancement}

## 10.3.1 Noether's second theorem applied to $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariant matter action

Apply Noether's second theorem [34] to a matter action $S_M[\phi, g_{\mu\nu}]$ invariant under the foliation-preserving subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$. The vector fields generating the symmetry are of the form (10.1.1.1).

**Remark 10.3.1.1 (the status of Noether's theorem within the framework: its inputs descend from $dx_4/dt=ic$ through the derived action principle, not through the symmetry group).** The precise content of the claim "Noether is framework-internal" is the following. Noether's theorems (first and second) are the standard variational results that a continuous global (resp. local) symmetry of an action yields a conserved current (resp. a differential identity); their proofs --- the first variation of the action, the prolongation formula, integration by parts to the Euler--Lagrange operator plus a total divergence --- are general calculus of variations and are *not* re-derived from $dx_4/dt=ic$ (see [2, Theorem 30] for the first theorem and [2, Theorem 30$'$] for the second; the "Proof of Theorem 30" there is the textbook variational argument). What descends from $dx_4/dt=ic$ are the *inputs* on which the theorems operate, and hence their outputs: (i) the variational background and Lagrangian --- the Lorentzian metric via Lemma 1 and the McGucken Lagrangian via the derived least-action structure; (ii) the symmetries the theorem maps from --- the Poincaré generators $\{P^\mu,J^{\mu\nu}\}$ forced by Lemma 1 plus event-homogeneity ([2, Theorem 27]) and the $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-action for the second theorem; (iii) the Cauchy foliation against which the charges $Q_X(\Sigma)=\int_\Sigma j^\mu_X n_\mu\,d\Sigma$ are integrated --- the $+ic$ orientation. With all three ingredients framework-derived, the conservation laws are forced consequences of $dx_4/dt=ic$. The source paper [2] states the priority as "the McGucken Symmetry is prior to Noether symmetry $[\ldots]$ Noether's theorem and its conservation-law consequences are derived from $dx_4/dt=ic$ rather than from independent symmetry postulates" (attributed in [2] to the further paper [2, Theorem 32]; not independently audited here).

*Correction of an earlier compressed chain.* An earlier rendering routed the claim as $dx_4/dt=ic \to \text{Lorentzian interval} \to \mathrm{ISO}(1,3) \to \text{Noether's first} \to \text{Noether's second}$, citing "[2, Theorem 18.4]." Two corrections: the step $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)\to\text{Noether's first}$ is imprecise --- possessing the symmetry *group* does not yield Noether's *theorem*, which requires the variational/action structure and is then applied to whatever symmetry is present --- and the citation is to the wrong locator (the Noether derivation in [2] is its Theorem 30 / 30$'$; "18.4/18.5" are [2]'s own references to the separate paper [2], not theorems of [2]). The corrected routing --- through the derived metric, Lagrangian, and least-action principle --- is exactly what [2, Theorem 30]'s proof uses. On this corrected reading the Algebraic-Channel derivation rests on no *physical* input external to $dx_4/dt=ic$: Noether's variational theorem enters only as a general mathematical tool, on the same footing as Stone's theorem and as the Riesz--Markov theorem and complexification used in the Born-rule routes of §18.3.4, applied to inputs that are all framework-derived.
**Lemma 10.3.1.2 (Conservation laws from $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariance).** Noether's second theorem applied to a $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariant matter action $S_M$ produces the following conservation laws:
*(C1) Spatial conservation on each $x_4$-slice:*
$$\nabla_i T^{i\nu} \;=\; 0 \tag{10.3.1.2a}$$
*on every spatial slice $\Sigma_t$;*

*(C2) Integrated time conservation:*
$$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\Sigma_t} T^{0\nu}\, \sqrt{h}\, d^3 x \;=\; 0 \tag{10.3.1.2b}$$
*with $h_{ij}$ the induced spatial metric on $\Sigma_t$.*

These conservation laws are *weaker* than the standard $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ that full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$-invariance produces.
*Proof.* Noether's second theorem [34] applied to a $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariant action produces one conservation law per independent vector-field parameter in $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$. The vector-field structure (10.1.1.1) has:

- One independent component $\xi^0(x^0)$: a function of $x^0$ alone, giving an integrated time-conservation law (C2);

- Three independent components $\xi^i(x^0, x^j)$: functions of all four coordinates, giving spatial-conservation laws (C1).

The difference from full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$-invariance is the loss of the locality of time conservation: full $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ asserts local conservation at each event, but $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ only gives the integrated form (C2) for the time component. $\square$

## 10.3.1.3 Noether's theorem of physics descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$: the explicit chain

Remark 10.3.1.1 fixed the *status* of Noether's theorem within the framework.

**Two readings of "Noether's theorem."** The phrase names two distinct propositions, and the descent question has a different answer for each.

*(N-abstract) --- the metric-blind universal implication.* For every smooth finite-dimensional manifold, every local action functional on it, and every continuous variational symmetry, the associated Noether current satisfies $\partial_\mu j^\mu = 0$ on shell. This is a theorem of the calculus of variations; its proof --- vary, integrate by parts, impose on-shell and symmetry --- ranges over all signatures, including metrics that $dx_4/dt = ic$ does not generate. The framework does not derive (N-abstract) and does not need to: it *employs* it.

*(N-physics) --- the physical correspondence.* The conservation laws of physics --- energy, momentum, angular momentum, charge --- follow as conserved currents of the physical symmetries of the physical action on the physical Cauchy foliation. Each italicised "physical" is a structure, not a word, and each such structure is McGucken-supplied. (N-physics) is what the theorem asserts when it does work *in physics*, and (N-physics) descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$.

**Theorem 10.3.1.3 (Noether's theorem of physics as a descended consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$).** *Every structural ingredient over which (N-physics) quantifies --- the metric, the action, the symmetries, the foliation, the dynamics --- is a forced consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$; consequently the conservation laws of physics are forced consequences of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The mathematical kernel (N-abstract) is content-free calculus the framework employs, not an external physical postulate, and its metric of operation is itself the Principle's output.*

*Proof (the labelled chain).*

**Step 0 --- the Principle.** $dx_4/dt = ic$: the fourth dimension advances at imaginary rate $ic$, spherically symmetrically, at every event. [McGucken --- the foundational postulate.]

**Step 1 --- the metric.** Integrating, $dx_4 = ic\,dt$; substitution into the Euclidean form yields
$$g_E = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2 \;\xrightarrow{\,dx_4 = ic\,dt\,}\; dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2 dt^2 = \eta,$$
the Lorentzian signature produced by $i^2 = -1$. [McGucken --- Lemma 1.]

**Step 2 --- the action's skeleton.** A local action $S = \int \mathcal{L}\,d\mathrm{vol}_\eta$ requires (a) a measure $d\mathrm{vol}_\eta = \sqrt{-g}\,d^4x$, (b) the index-raising $\eta^{\mu\nu}$ that forms every kinetic contraction $\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial_\nu\phi$, and (c) the d'Alembertian $\Box = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$. All three are fixed by the $\eta$ of Step 1; the signature *inside* the action is the Lemma-1 signature, so the action is not signature-neutral. [McGucken --- forced by Lemma 1.] (The specific Lagrangian sectors $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{McG}} = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{kin}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Dirac}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{YM}} + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{EH}}$ rest on the separate sector derivations; the variational *skeleton* Noether requires is fixed already by $\eta$.)

**Step 3 --- the dynamics.** Stationarity $\delta S = 0$ under arbitrary $\delta\phi$ gives the Euler--Lagrange equations $E_A(\mathcal{L}) = 0$. [McGucken --- least action on the derived action; the E--L extraction is standard.]

**Step 4 --- the symmetry.** $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds at every event with no preferred $x_4$-origin (event-homogeneity); this *is* invariance under $x_4$-translation, and the full Poincaré group is the isometry group of the $\eta$ of Step 1. The symmetries (N-physics) maps from are forced, not postulated. [McGucken --- Theorems 24, 27.]

**Step 5 --- the variational identity (kernel).** Varying and integrating by parts,
$$\delta S = \int E_A(\mathcal{L})\,\delta\phi^A\,d\mathrm{vol}_\eta + \int \partial_\mu\!\Big[\tfrac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial(\partial_\mu\phi^A)}\,\delta\phi^A\Big]\,d\mathrm{vol}_\eta.$$
This identity is content-free calculus --- yet it is *not* metric-free: the divergence contraction $\partial_\mu[\cdots]$, the raised index in $\partial^\mu\phi = \eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\phi$ inside $E_A$, and the measure $d\mathrm{vol}_\eta$ all carry the $\eta$ of Step 1. The kernel is borrowed; the metric it runs on is the Principle's. [Calculus kernel --- employed by the framework, on the McGucken metric.]

**Step 6 --- the squeeze (kernel).** On shell (Step 3, $E_A = 0$) and under the symmetry (Step 4, $\delta S = 0$), the identity collapses to
$$\partial_\mu j^\mu = 0, \qquad j^\mu = \tfrac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial(\partial_\mu\phi^A)}\,\delta\phi^A - K^\mu.$$
Pure logic: two conditions annihilate two terms, one survives. [Calculus kernel --- employed by the framework. The surviving current is physically meaningful only because Steps 0--4 are physical and McGucken-supplied.]

**Step 7 --- the conserved charge.** $Q = \int_\Sigma j^\mu n_\mu\,d\Sigma$ is constant *in time* exactly when there is a Cauchy slice $\Sigma$ and one physical time to be constant along; the $+ic$ orientation supplies that foliation. [McGucken --- the $+ic$ orientation (A5).]

Steps 0--4 and 7 --- metric, action-skeleton, dynamics, symmetry, foliation --- are McGucken-forced, and the metric is moreover operative *inside* the kernel Steps 5--6. The conserved quantity at the chain's end is therefore a forced consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$. This is (N-physics). $\square$

**Remark 10.3.1.4 (the kernel produces nothing physical without the McGucken inputs: a counterexample bracket).** That Steps 5--6 are content-free is exhibited by feeding them geometries that retain the kernel but lack the McGucken inputs. On a candidate base of pure spatial dimensions with no time, or of many time dimensions with no space, the integration-by-parts identity of Step 5 still holds mechanically --- it is an identity about integrals --- yet it yields *no Noether's theorem of physics*: with no $+ic$ orientation there is no Cauchy foliation (Step 7 fails), so $\partial_\mu j^\mu = 0$ has nothing to be conserved *along*; with no event-homogeneous Lorentzian $\eta$ there is no physical symmetry (Step 4 fails) and no physical action (Step 2 fails). The kernel runs and returns a contentless identity. The transition from contentless identity to conservation law of physics is effected entirely by Steps 0--4 and 7 --- all McGucken. This is the precise sense in which (N-physics), and not merely its separate inputs, descends from $dx_4/dt = ic$: strip the Principle's outputs and the kernel survives while the theorem of physics does not.

**Honest grade.** Theorem 10.3.1.3 establishes that the *conservation laws of physics descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$* at the rigor of the framework's input derivations (Lemma 1 for $\eta$; Theorems 24, 27 for the symmetries; the $+ic$ orientation A5 for the foliation; least action for the dynamics): **G1 conditional on those input theorems**, which are established elsewhere in the corpus and not re-audited here. Under the reading (N-physics) the descent is complete, and the sole step the framework *employs* rather than *derives* is the content-free variational identity (N-abstract) --- which carries no physical content until the McGucken inputs are supplied, and therefore introduces no external physical postulate. The one proposition the framework does not derive is (N-abstract) in its metric-blind universal form, because that statement quantifies over manifolds and metrics $dx_4/dt = ic$ does not generate; this is a statement of the kernel's mathematical generality, not a physical input the chain lacks. Equivalently, and this is the defensible claim in one line: *given what "Noether's theorem of physics" means --- conservation laws of the McGucken action on the McGucken foliation --- $dx_4/dt = ic$ forces it; the only residual is the kernel's universality over foreign metrics, which lies outside any physical principle's remit and is no part of the physics.*

## 10.3.2 On-shell enhancement theorem

The conservation laws (C1)+(C2) are weaker than the full local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$. The gap is closed *on shell* by the constitutive identity (10.2.1.1) combined with the matter equations of motion.

**Theorem 10.3.2.1 (On-shell enhancement to full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ symmetry).** Given:
(i) $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$-invariance of the matter action (kinematic symmetry from foliation-preservation by $dx_4/dt = ic$);
(ii) the constitutive identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ pointwise (GR T1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$);
*(iii) the matter equations of motion (continuity equation, Euler equation, equations of state),*

the local conservation $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ holds at every event of $M_G$. Consequently, the full diffeomorphism group $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ acts as a symmetry of the on-shell theory.
*Proof.* The proof proceeds by computing $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ from the stress-energy tensor (10.2.2.1) and showing both its $u_\nu$-contraction (parallel component) and its spatial-projection (orthogonal component) vanish under the three postulates.

**Step 1 ($\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ expansion).** Differentiate (10.2.2.1):
\begin{align*}
\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; & \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; \nabla_\mu (p g^{\mu\nu}) \\
=\; & \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] u^\nu \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \;+\; g^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p,
\end{align*}
using metric compatibility $\nabla_\mu g_{\nu\rho} = 0$ (Lemma 8.2.4.1 of Chapter 8) in the second equation.

**Step 2 (contraction with $u_\nu$).** Contract by $u_\nu$:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu}{c^2} \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p,$$
using $u_\nu u^\nu = -c^2$ (postulate (ii)) for the first term. The crucial identity:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu u^\nu \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla_\mu (u^\nu u_\nu) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \nabla_\mu (-c^2) \;=\; 0, \tag{10.3.2.1}$$
by differentiating the constitutive identity (postulate (ii)). Hence the second term vanishes, leaving
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; -c^2 \nabla_\mu\!\left[ (\rho c^2 + p)\, \frac{u^\mu}{c^2} \right] \;+\; u^\mu \partial_\mu p.$$
The continuity equation $\nabla_\mu (\rho u^\mu) = 0$ (matter equation of motion, postulate (iii)) together with the first law of thermodynamics $u^\mu \partial_\mu \rho = -(\rho + p/c^2) \nabla_\mu u^\mu$ closes this expression to zero:
$$u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; 0. \tag{10.3.2.2}$$

**Step 3 (spatial projection orthogonal to $u^\nu$).** Define the spatial projector $h^\nu_\lambda \equiv \delta^\nu_\lambda + u^\nu u_\lambda / c^2$. Projecting $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu}$ by $h^\nu_\lambda$:
$$h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; (\rho c^2 + p)\, h^\nu_\lambda \frac{u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\lambda}{c^2} \;+\; h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p,$$
where the first term used the projector annihilating $u^\nu$ in the first term of Step 1's expansion (since $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = 0$ by direct computation: $h^\nu_\lambda u^\lambda = u^\nu + u^\nu u_\lambda u^\lambda / c^2 = u^\nu - u^\nu = 0$). The Euler equation in covariant form (matter equation of motion, postulate (iii)) is
$$(\rho c^2 + p)\, u^\mu \nabla_\mu u^\lambda \;=\; -h^{\mu\lambda} \partial_\mu p, \tag{10.3.2.3}$$
which when projected by $h^\nu_\lambda$ gives $h^\nu_\lambda \cdot (\text{first term}) = -h^\nu_\lambda \cdot h^{\mu\lambda} \partial_\mu p / 1 = -h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p$. Combining:
$$h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} \;=\; -h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p \;+\; h^{\mu\nu} \partial_\mu p \;=\; 0. \tag{10.3.2.4}$$

**Step 4 (full local conservation).** Equations (10.3.2.2) and (10.3.2.4) together span all four directions in the tangent space at every event $p \in M_G$: $u_\nu \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ on the timelike direction, $h^\nu_\lambda \nabla_\mu T^{\mu\lambda} = 0$ on the spatial three-directions. The full divergence vanishes:
$$\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} \;=\; 0 \tag{10.3.2.5}$$
at every event. This is the standard local conservation of stress-energy.

**Step 5 (on-shell full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ symmetry).** With $\nabla_\mu T^{\mu\nu} = 0$ established, the Bianchi-compatible field equations $G_{\mu\nu} \propto T_{\mu\nu}$ are consistent with arbitrary diffeomorphisms of $M_G$. The action is invariant under full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ *on shell*; the off-shell symmetry remains $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$. The full diffeomorphism invariance of general relativity emerges as the on-shell consequence of the McGucken framework's factorisation. $\square$

**Structural reading.** The McGucken framework is structurally stronger than Hilbert's diffeomorphism postulate: it specifies which diffeomorphisms are off-shell symmetries (only $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$, by foliation preservation), why the gap to full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ closes on-shell (by the four-velocity budget plus matter equations of motion), and what each of the two factors physically contributes. Hilbert's full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$-invariance, taken as a primitive in the standard textbook treatment, is here a derived consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on shell.

# 10.4 Algebraic Channel, Step 4: Lovelock's Theorem and the Newtonian Limit {#sec:lovelock}

## 10.4.1 Lovelock's theorem

**Theorem 10.4.1 (Lovelock 1971).** On a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold, the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor constructed from the metric $g_{\mu\nu}$ and its first two derivatives, with linear dependence on the second derivatives, is
$$L_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \beta\, g_{\mu\nu}, \tag{10.4.1.1}$$
where $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ is the Einstein tensor and $\alpha, \beta$ are constants.
This is a purely differential-geometric theorem [57]; we take it as a standard input. Within the McGucken framework, the conditions of Lovelock's theorem are themselves theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$:

- "four-dimensional manifold" follows from the McGucken-manifold structure of Definition 1 of the Introduction;

- "Lorentzian signature" follows from Lemma 5.1.2.2 of Chapter 5 (Minkowski metric forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$);

- "symmetric rank-2 tensor" follows from Riemann symmetry (S3) (Lemma 9.2.2.4 of Chapter 9);

- "divergence-free" follows from the contracted second Bianchi identity (Theorem 9.4.2.3 of Chapter 9);

- "metric + first two derivatives" follows from the Christoffel symbol formula (GR T8, Chapter 8).

Hence the *inputs* of Lovelock's theorem are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; the theorem itself is the uniqueness statement applied to the LHS of the field equations.

## 10.4.2 Application of Lovelock with the stress-energy tensor as source

**Lemma 10.4.2 (Field equations from Lovelock + on-shell conservation).** Set $L_{\mu\nu} = \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}$ with $\kappa$ a coupling constant to be determined. Using (10.4.1.1):
$$\alpha\, G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \beta\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \kappa\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.4.2.1}$$
Dividing by $\alpha$ (assumed non-zero) and identifying $\beta/\alpha = \Lambda$ and $\kappa/\alpha = \kappa'$:
$$G_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \kappa'\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.4.2.2}$$
Consistency with the conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (Theorem 10.3.2.1) requires $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$, which is the contracted Bianchi identity (Theorem 9.4.2.3); $\nabla^\mu (\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}) = \Lambda \nabla^\mu g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ by metric compatibility. Hence (10.4.2.2) is consistent.
## 10.4.3 Newtonian-limit matching fixes the coupling constant

**Theorem 10.4.3 (Coupling-constant matching to Newtonian gravity).** In the weak-field, non-relativistic static limit of (10.4.2.2) --- with $g_{00} = -(1 + 2\Phi/c^2)$, $g_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$, $T_{00} = \rho c^2$ dominant, $\Lambda$ negligible at solar-system scales --- equation (10.4.2.2) reduces to Newton's law of gravity
$$\nabla^2 \Phi \;=\; 4\pi G\, \rho, \tag{10.4.3.1}$$
*provided $\kappa' = 8\pi G / c^4$. Hence the coupling constant is*
$$\kappa' \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}. \tag{10.4.3.2}$$

*Proof.* Standard calculation (Wald §4.4, Carroll §4.2). The $00$-component of (10.4.2.2) in the weak-field limit reduces to
$$G_{00} \;=\; \kappa'\, T_{00}.$$
Computing $G_{00}$ from the weak-field metric: $R_{00} = \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$ to leading order; $R = 2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$ to leading order (with sign conventions consistent with the $(-, +, +, +)$ metric); $G_{00} = R_{00} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{00} = \nabla^2 \Phi/c^2 - \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot (2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2) \cdot (-1) = 2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2$. With $T_{00} = \rho c^2$:
$$2 \nabla^2 \Phi / c^2 \;=\; \kappa' \rho c^2 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \nabla^2 \Phi \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \kappa' c^4 \rho.$$
Matching to Newton's law $\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G \rho$:
$$4\pi G \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \kappa' c^4 \quad \Longrightarrow \quad \kappa' \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}.$$

*McGucken-framework structural reading.* The coupling constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ is the *Einstein-equation coupling* between curvature and stress-energy. The McGucken-framework reading: by Lemma 11.3.1.1 (the factor-of-2 weak-field expansion), the linearised Einstein-equation coupling is *twice* the naive Newtonian-coupling that would arise from a direct identification of the metric perturbation with the Newtonian potential. The factor of 2 traces back to the trace-reversal structure of the Einstein tensor $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ (Lemma 9.4.2.2 of Chapter 9), which contributes a second factor of $G$ to the source coupling on top of the Ricci-tensor contribution. The structural reading: the Einstein-equation coupling $8\pi G/c^4$ encodes (i) the gravitational constant $G$ (the strength of the gravitational interaction), (ii) the speed of light $c^4$ (the dimensional reduction from energy-density to curvature units), and (iii) the geometric factor $8\pi$ (the surface-area normalisation of the gravitational source on a unit sphere, $8\pi = 2 \cdot 4\pi$ — the trace-reversal-doubled normalisation). The McGucken-framework structural meaning: the constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ is the precise coupling that makes the Einstein-tensor-conservation (Theorem 9.4.2.3) compatible with stress-energy conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ at every event of $M_G$, with the McGucken-Sphere geometric structure of $M_G$ determining the precise numerical factor via the linearised Newtonian-limit matching. $\square$

## 10.4.4 The Einstein field equations from the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel

**Theorem 10.4.4 (Einstein Field Equations from the Algebraic Channel).** Combining Theorems 10.3.2.1 (on-shell $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$), Lovelock 10.4.1 (LHS uniqueness), and 10.4.3 (Newtonian-limit coupling-constant matching), the Einstein field equations
$$\boxed{\, G_{\mu\nu} \,+\, \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu} \,} \tag{T11.1, Algebraic Channel}$$
*are forced as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along the Algebraic Channel route.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of: (i) the constitutive identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (postulate of GR T1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (ii) the foliation-preserving $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$-invariance (Lemma 10.1.2.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (iii) the on-shell enhancement $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (Theorem 10.3.2.1, derived from (i) + (ii) + matter equations of motion); (iv) Lovelock's theorem applied to the unique divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensor in 4D (Theorem 10.4.1); (v) the Newtonian-limit matching that fixes the coupling constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G / c^4$ (Theorem 10.4.3). Postulates (i), (ii) are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; (iii) follows from (i) + (ii) + matter dynamics.

The status of (iv) and (v) must be stated separately, since they are not of the same kind. *Lovelock's theorem (iv)* is an inherited differential-geometric uniqueness result, but every one of its hypotheses is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, as established in §10.4.1: four-dimensionality (Definition 1), Lorentzian signature (Lemma 5.1.2.2, from $i^2 = -1$), symmetric rank-2 (Riemann symmetry S3, Lemma 9.2.2.4), divergence-freedom (contracted second Bianchi, Theorem 9.4.2.3), and dependence on the metric and its first two derivatives (GR T8). Lovelock therefore introduces no physical input external to the Principle; it is a mathematical uniqueness kernel applied to Principle-derived hypotheses, in exactly the sense in which the Noether kernel (N-abstract) is employed at Theorem 10.3.1.3 --- borrowed calculus running on the Principle's own structures. *The Newtonian-limit matching (v)* is of a different kind: it fixes the dimensionful coupling $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ by matching to Poisson's equation, and thereby imports the gravitational constant $G$ as a *declared empirical input* --- the strength of the gravitational interaction, which no purely geometric principle predicts, on the same footing as the action quantum $\hbar$ and the species rest-mass spectrum declared in the honest accounting of Lemma 5.3.0.1. What $dx_4/dt = ic$ forces is the *form* of the field equations (the unique Lovelock left-hand side paired with a conserved stress-energy right-hand side); what the Newtonian limit supplies is the *scale* $G$ at which that form couples. The field equations are forced up to that one declared constant. $\square$

**Structural reading of the Algebraic Channel.** The Hilbert-Lovelock route reads Einstein's field equations as the *unique* relation between geometry (Lovelock-unique LHS) and matter (conserved stress-energy on the RHS) that is consistent with $dx_4/dt = ic$ plus the Newtonian limit. The McGucken framework strengthens Hilbert by deriving the diffeomorphism-invariance postulate from $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the foliation factorisation, recovering the full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ symmetry as an on-shell consequence rather than an off-shell input.


# 10.5 Geometric Channel, Step 1: The Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ {#sec:second-law}

The $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations follows the thermodynamic route of Jacobson [37], with every input that Jacobson treats as a postulate (area-law entropy, Unruh temperature, monotone entropy increase) derived as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The first such theorem is the Geometric Second Law.

## 10.5.1 Statement and proof of the Geometric Second Law

**Theorem 10.5.1 (Geometric Second Law of Thermodynamics).** Let $M_G$ be the McGucken manifold and the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold at every event. Consider an ensemble of $N$ particles at positions $\{r_\alpha\}_{\alpha=1}^N$ on the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$. The Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of the ensemble is
$$S(t) \;=\; -k_B \int P(\vec r, t)\, \ln P(\vec r, t)\, d^3 r, \tag{10.5.1.1}$$
where $P(\vec r, t)$ is the probability density. Then $S$ is strictly monotonically increasing in $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;>\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.2}$$
*at every $t > t_0$, with $t_0$ the initial time.*

The monotonicity is *exact* (not statistical), and there is no Poincaré recurrence: $x_4$ advances and does not retreat.
*Proof.* We proceed in four steps.

**Step 1 (kinematic content of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on the spatial slice).** By $dx_4/dt = ic$, $x_4$ advances at rate $ic$ from every event of $M_G$, isotropically across the spatial three-slice (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii)). At every Planck-time step $\delta t_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^5}$, the McGucken Sphere of expansion at each particle's position has radius $c\, \delta t_P = \ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ (the Planck length), and the particle is displaced by $c \, \delta t_P$ in a direction $\hat n$ drawn uniformly from the unit sphere $S^2$.

**Step 2 (diffusion equation from isotropic step).** The probability density $P(\vec r, t)$ evolves under iterated isotropic Compton displacements with rms step size $c\, \delta t_P$ per step. By the Einstein 1905 derivation of Brownian motion applied with step size $c \, \delta t_P$ and step time $\delta t_P$, the diffusion coefficient is
$$D \;=\; \frac{(c\, \delta t_P)^2}{6\, \delta t_P} \;=\; \frac{c^2\, \delta t_P}{6}, \tag{10.5.1.3}$$
and the probability density satisfies
$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} \;=\; D\, \nabla^2 P. \tag{10.5.1.4}$$
This is the isotropic-diffusion equation, derived from the McGucken Sphere expansion at each Planck-time step.

**Step 3 (Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of the Gaussian solution).** The fundamental solution of (10.5.1.4) with delta-function initial data $P(\vec r, 0) = \delta^3(\vec r)$ is the Gaussian
$$P(\vec r, t) \;=\; (4\pi D t)^{-3/2}\, \exp\!\left(-\frac{r^2}{4 D t}\right). \tag{10.5.1.5}$$
Substituting into (10.5.1.1) and evaluating the Gaussian-entropy integral (standard computation):
$$S(t) \;=\; \tfrac{3}{2} k_B\, \ln(4\pi e\, D t) \;+\; \text{const.} \tag{10.5.1.6}$$

**Step 4 (strict monotonicity).** Differentiate (10.5.1.6) with respect to $t$:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \;>\; 0 \tag{10.5.1.7}$$
for all $t > 0$, since $k_B > 0$ and $t > 0$.

The strictness of the inequality follows from the *$+ic$ orientation* of the principle: $x_4$ advances at $+ic$, not $-ic$. The diffusion equation (10.5.1.4) propagates probability forward in $t$ with no time-reversed branch. The textbook statistical Second Law (a tendency with Poincaré recurrence) reduces to the McGucken geometric Second Law (a strict monotonicity without recurrence) when the $+ic$-oriented physical motion underlying $dx_4/dt = ic$ is recognised. $\square$

## 10.5.2 Structural reading of the Geometric Second Law

The Geometric Second Law is *not* the statistical Second Law of Boltzmann (a tendency with non-zero probability of fluctuations); it is a theorem about the certain monotonic advance of $x_4$ and the entropy it generates. There is no Poincaré recurrence because $x_4$ does not recur.

Theorem 10.5.1 is the *horizon-level* Geometric Second Law (used directly in §10.8 in the Jacobson chain). A particle-level companion --- Theorem 10.5.3 below, importing Proposition 4.5.4 of [2, §4.5] --- establishes the same Second Law from the Compton-coupling Brownian motion of massive particles, with a sharper *quantitative* form $dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t$.

## 10.5.3 Particle-level companion (optional, for the headline chapter)

**Theorem 10.5.3 (Strict Second Law for massive-particle ensembles).** For an ensemble of massive particles undergoing the Compton-coupling Wiener process generated by the iterated McGucken Sphere flow on the spatial slice,
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \frac{3 k_B}{2 t} \tag{10.5.3.1}$$
*strictly, for all $t > 0$.*

*Proof.* Established at Proposition 4.5.4 of [2, §4.5]. The proof uses Propositions 4.5.1 (Compton coupling between matter and $x_4$ at angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$), 4.5.2 (spatial-projection isotropy by spherical symmetry of $dx_4/dt = ic$), 4.5.3 (Brownian motion as iterated isotropic Compton displacement via central limit theorem applied to iid sphere-uniform increments), and direct Gaussian-entropy evaluation of $S = -k_B \int P \ln P d^3 r$ on the Wiener-process density. $\square$

The particle-level derivation refines the horizon-level Theorem 10.5.1 with a sharper quantitative content: not merely $dS/dt > 0$, but the specific rate $dS/dt = (3/2) k_B / t$.

# 10.5bis McGucken Spacetime Entropy: the Geometric Second Law on Curved and Expanding Backgrounds {#sec:mcgucken-spacetime-entropy}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

Theorem 10.5.1 establishes the Geometric Second Law for the *free* case: an isotropic Sphere step on a flat spatial slice, giving the Gaussian kernel and $dS/dt = \tfrac32 k_B/t > 0$. That is the case the field-equation derivation of §10.8 requires, and it is proved. But the framework asserts more than it there proves. Theorem 16.3.4 (the Generalised Second Law) needs the monotonicity to hold *at every instant and for any physical process* --- including on curved slices, in the presence of interactions, and on a spatial geometry that is itself *evolving* (an expanding cosmos; a shrinking horizon). The present section supplies that generalisation. The result is a single identity, and it contains two of the five arrows of Theorem 18.6.3 as its two terms.

## 10.5bis.1 The setting

Let $M_G = \bigcup_t \Sigma_t$ be the McGucken foliation. Each slice $\Sigma_t$ carries the induced spatial metric $h_{ij}$, the Riemannian volume measure $d\mu_h = \sqrt{h}\, d^3x$, and a probability density $P(\vec x, t)$ normalised by $\int_{\Sigma_t} P\, d\mu_h = 1$. The Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy of the ensemble is
$$S(t) \;=\; -k_B \int_{\Sigma_t} P \ln P \; d\mu_h .$$
We assume $P$ and $\nabla P$ decay at infinity (or $\Sigma_t$ is closed), so that boundary terms vanish.

**Lemma 10.5bis.1 (The Sphere flow on a curved slice is isotropic *with respect to the local metric*, and its diffusion coefficient is universal).** *The iterated McGucken-Sphere flow on a curved slice generates the diffusion*
$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial t} \;=\; D\, \Delta_h P, \qquad \Delta_h = \frac{1}{\sqrt{h}}\,\partial_i\!\left(\sqrt{h}\, h^{ij}\, \partial_j\right), \qquad D = \frac{c^2\, \delta t_P}{6},$$
*where $\Delta_h$ is the Laplace--Beltrami operator of $h_{ij}$. Both the isotropy and the universality of $D$ are forced, not assumed.*

*Proof.* By component (ii) of the Principle, the $x_4$-expansion from every event is spherically symmetric: the displacement direction is drawn from the uniform measure on $S^2$ with no preferred spatial direction. On a curved slice, "no preferred direction" is a statement about *proper* distance, i.e. about $h_{ij}$ --- so the step is isotropic with respect to the local metric, and the resulting diffusion tensor is $D\, h^{ij}$, proportional to the *inverse spatial metric* rather than to some independent tensor. Nothing else is available: the Sphere structure at each event carries no tensorial content beyond its radius and its isotropy.

By GR T2 (the McGucken-Invariance Lemma), the rate is metric-independent: the Sphere radius is $c\,\delta t$ at *every* event, whatever the local curvature. Hence $D = c^2\delta t_P/6$ is a *universal constant* on $M_G$, not a position-dependent transport coefficient. Gravity deforms the geometry the diffusion runs on; it does not deform the diffusion constant. The Kolmogorov forward equation for a step that is isotropic in $h_{ij}$ with universal coefficient $D$ is the heat equation for the Laplace--Beltrami operator. $\square$

**Lemma 10.5bis.2 (The spatial metric is positive definite --- and this traces to the $i$).** *On every slice $\Sigma_t$ the induced metric $h_{ij}$ is positive definite, so that for any covector $\xi_i$,*
$$h^{ij}\,\xi_i\,\xi_j \;\geq\; 0,$$
*with equality iff $\xi = 0$. This is not an assumption about the slice: it is a consequence of the imaginary unit in $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

*Proof.* The slices $\Sigma_t$ of the McGucken foliation are *spacelike*, and the induced metric on a spacelike hypersurface of a Lorentzian manifold is Riemannian --- positive definite. The Lorentzian signature $(-,+,+,+)$, in turn, is not a convention: by Lemma 5.1.2.2 it is produced by $(ic)^2 = -c^2$, the single minus sign being the algebraic record of $x_4$'s perpendicularity to the spatial three (Remark 5.1.2.3). Remove the $i$ and the signature becomes Euclidean; the foliation loses its causal meaning and $\Sigma_t$ is no longer a spacelike slice of anything. **The positive-definiteness of $h_{ij}$ --- and hence the sign of every quadratic form built on it --- descends from the $i$.** $\square$

## 10.5bis.2 The main theorem

**Theorem 10.5bis.3 (McGucken Spacetime Entropy: the Geometric Second Law on a curved, evolving slice).** *Let the spatial geometry itself evolve, with local volume-expansion rate*
$$\theta \;\equiv\; \partial_t \ln\sqrt{h}\,.$$
*Then the entropy of the ensemble obeys the exact identity*
$$\boxed{\;\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \underbrace{k_B\, D\; \mathcal{I}_h(P)}_{\text{diffusion}} \;+\; \underbrace{k_B\, \langle \theta \rangle}_{\text{expansion}} \;}$$
*where*
$$\mathcal{I}_h(P) \;=\; \int_{\Sigma_t} h^{ij}\, (\nabla_i \ln P)(\nabla_j \ln P)\; P \; d\mu_h \;=\; \int_{\Sigma_t} \frac{|\nabla P|_h^2}{P}\; d\mu_h$$
*is the **Fisher information** of $P$ with respect to the spatial metric, and $\langle\theta\rangle = \int_{\Sigma_t} \theta\, P\, d\mu_h$ is the mean volume-expansion rate. **Both terms are non-negative**, hence*
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;\geq\; 0,$$
*with equality iff $P$ is uniform on a non-expanding slice.*

*Proof.* Probability conservation on an evolving slice reads $\partial_t(P\sqrt{h}) + \partial_i(\sqrt{h}\,J^i) = 0$, with the Fickian flux $J^i = -D\, h^{ij}\partial_j P$ supplied by Lemma 10.5bis.1. Differentiate the entropy:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; -k_B \int \Bigl[\, \partial_t(P\sqrt{h})\,\ln P \;+\; \sqrt{h}\,\partial_t P \,\Bigr] d^3x .$$

*Second term (the expansion contribution).* Normalisation $\int P\sqrt h\, d^3x = 1$ gives $\int \bigl[\sqrt h\, \partial_t P + P\,\partial_t \sqrt h\bigr] d^3x = 0$, hence $\int \sqrt h\, \partial_t P\, d^3x = -\int P\,\theta\, \sqrt h\, d^3x = -\langle\theta\rangle$. Its contribution to $dS/dt$ is therefore $+k_B\langle\theta\rangle$.

*First term (the diffusion contribution).* Substituting continuity and integrating by parts,
$$-k_B\!\int\! \partial_t(P\sqrt h)\ln P \; d^3x \;=\; k_B\!\int\! \ln P\; \partial_i(\sqrt h J^i)\, d^3x \;=\; -k_B\!\int\! \sqrt h\; J^i\, \partial_i \ln P \; d^3x .$$
With $J^i = -D h^{ij}\partial_j P$ and $\partial_i \ln P = \partial_i P / P$,
$$=\; k_B D \int \sqrt h \; \frac{h^{ij}\,\partial_i P\, \partial_j P}{P}\; d^3x \;=\; k_B D \int \frac{|\nabla P|_h^2}{P}\, d\mu_h \;=\; k_B\, D\, \mathcal{I}_h(P).$$

*Signs.* The Fisher information is an integral of $h^{ij}\partial_i P\,\partial_j P / P$ with $P > 0$; by **Lemma 10.5bis.2** the quadratic form $h^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j$ is non-negative, hence $\mathcal{I}_h(P) \geq 0$, with equality iff $\nabla P = 0$. The expansion term is non-negative whenever the spatial volume is non-contracting, $\theta \geq 0$ --- which at cosmological scale is the statement $H > 0$, itself the $+ic$ advance read at cosmological scale (Lemma 18.6.2.2; GR T18). Both terms are non-negative and the identity follows. $\square$

**Corollary 10.5bis.4 (Theorem 10.5.1 recovered exactly).** On a flat, static slice ($h_{ij} = \delta_{ij}$, $\theta = 0$) with the Gaussian kernel $P = (4\pi Dt)^{-3/2}e^{-r^2/4Dt}$, the Fisher information is $\mathcal{I}(P) = 3/(2Dt)$, whence
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; k_B D \cdot \frac{3}{2Dt} \;=\; \frac{3}{2}\,\frac{k_B}{t} \;>\; 0,$$
which is precisely Theorem 10.5.1. The general identity therefore *contains* the free case rather than replacing it. (Verified symbolically.)

**Corollary 10.5bis.5 (the interacting case: the $H$-theorem).** Let the ensemble move in a potential $V$, so that the Sphere flow acquires a drift and the forward equation becomes the Fokker--Planck equation $\partial_t P = \nabla_i\bigl[D h^{ij}(\nabla_j P + \beta P \nabla_j V)\bigr]$, with equilibrium $P_{\mathrm{eq}} \propto e^{-\beta V}$. Then the relative entropy to equilibrium is monotonically *decreasing*,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\, \mathrm{D}\!\left(P \,\|\, P_{\mathrm{eq}}\right) \;=\; -\,D \int P \left| \nabla \ln \frac{P}{P_{\mathrm{eq}}} \right|_h^2 d\mu_h \;\leq\; 0,$$
the entropy production again being a (relative) Fisher information, non-negative by Lemma 10.5bis.2. Interactions therefore do not threaten the Second Law; they relocate the monotone quantity from the entropy to the free energy, and the *entropy production* remains non-negative. The Geometric Second Law survives the introduction of forces.

## 10.5bis.3 What the identity says

**Theorem 10.5bis.6 (Curvature can bend the flow of entropy but cannot reverse it).** *The **sign** of $dS/dt$ in Theorem 10.5bis.3 is independent of $h_{ij}$. Curvature enters only inside $\mathcal{I}_h(P)$ and $\langle\theta\rangle$, both of which are magnitudes; it modulates the **rate** of entropy production and can never change its **sign**. There is no gravitational field, however strong, in which entropy runs backwards.*

*Proof.* Immediate from Theorem 10.5bis.3: $\mathcal{I}_h(P) \geq 0$ for *every* Riemannian $h_{ij}$ (Lemma 10.5bis.2), and $D$ is a universal constant independent of the metric (Lemma 10.5bis.1, from GR T2). $\square$

**Remark 10.5bis.7 (this is exactly what GR T2 requires).** The result is not a happy accident but a necessity. GR T2 states that the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is *metric-independent*: $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$. The arrow of time is generated by that rate (Theorem 11; Theorem 18.6.3). **A metric-independent source must generate a metric-independent arrow.** Had Theorem 10.5bis.6 come out otherwise --- had some curvature been able to reverse $dS/dt$ --- the framework would have been internally inconsistent, since gravity would then have been deforming something GR T2 forbids it to touch. The curvature-independence of the Second Law is the thermodynamic shadow of the gravity-rigidity of the rate.

**Remark 10.5bis.8 (the $i$ and the $+$ do different jobs).** The identity of Theorem 10.5bis.3 exhibits, in a single line, the two distinct jobs done by the two distinct features of $dx_4/dt = ic$:

\begin{itemize}
\item **The $i$ makes the Second Law possible.** It supplies the Lorentzian signature through $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ (Lemma 5.1.2.2); the signature makes $\Sigma_t$ spacelike; spacelike makes $h_{ij}$ positive definite (Lemma 10.5bis.2); and positive-definiteness is exactly what makes the Fisher information $\mathcal{I}_h(P) \geq 0$. Strip the $i$ and the quadratic form loses its sign; the entropy production could then run either way, and no Second Law would be available to prove.
\item **The $+$ makes the Second Law actual.** It orients the advance, so the diffusion propagates forward in $t$ with no time-reversed branch, and it makes the cosmological expansion an expansion ($\theta > 0$) rather than a contraction. Strip the $+$ and the machinery still permits a Second Law --- it simply fails to say which way it runs.
\end{itemize}

*The imaginary unit guarantees that entropy production has a definite sign; the plus sign says which one.* Neither alone suffices, and both are contained in the single symbol $ic$.

**Remark 10.5bis.9 (two arrows, one identity).** The two terms of Theorem 10.5bis.3 are not merely both positive; they are the *thermodynamic* and the *cosmological* arrows of Theorem 18.6.3, standing side by side in one equation:
$$\frac{dS}{dt} \;=\; \underbrace{k_B D\, \mathcal{I}_h(P)}_{\text{thermodynamic arrow (Lemma 18.6.2.1)}} \;+\; \underbrace{k_B \langle\theta\rangle}_{\text{cosmological arrow (Lemma 18.6.2.2)}} .$$
For a Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker slice, $\sqrt h \propto a^3(t)$ and $\theta = \partial_t \ln a^3 = 3H$, so the second term is exactly $3k_B H$: *the expansion of the universe is not merely correlated with the arrow of time --- it is a term in the entropy-production identity.* (Verified: with diffusion switched off, $P \propto a^{-3}$ and $S = S_0 + 3k_B\ln a$, giving $dS/dt = 3k_B H$ precisely.)

Theorem 18.6.3 asserts that the five orthodox arrows are five projections of one advance. Theorem 10.5bis.3 exhibits two of them as two terms of one *identity* --- and both terms carry the sign they do for the same reason: $x_4$ advances, and does not retreat.

**Remark 10.5bis.10 (what the entropy of spacetime is, in this framework).** It is now possible to say plainly what has been derived. In the orthodox entropic-gravity programmes an entropy is *assigned* to spacetime --- to a horizon, to a screen, to a mismatch between two metrics --- and gravity is then recovered from it. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework nothing is assigned. The expansion of $x_4$ at $ic$ from every event *is* an entropy-generating process, and it supplies, from the one fact, all three things an entropy requires:

\begin{enumerate}
\item a **microstate count** --- the advance has a fundamental wavelength $\ell_P$, so a horizon carries exactly $A/\ell_P^2$ modes and no more (Theorem 12; Theorem 15.4.6);
\item a **dynamics that spreads the distribution** --- the isotropic step forced by component (ii) makes the density diffuse, with universal coefficient $D = c^2\delta t_P/6$ (Lemma 10.5bis.1);
\item a **direction** --- the $+ic$ orientation, which by Theorem 17-ter no symmetry of the metric label could ever have supplied.
\end{enumerate}

*Spacetime does not have an entropy. Spacetime is doing one.*

# 10.6 Geometric Channel, Step 2: The Area Law $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ {#sec:area-law}

## 10.6.1 The area law from $x_4$-mode counting on McGucken Spheres

**Theorem 10.6.1 (Area law for entropy on McGucken Spheres).** Let $M_G$ be the McGucken manifold, let the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold at every event, and let the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G / c^3}$ be identified as the fundamental wavelength of $x_4$-advance (the structural identification developed in [3, 4] and used throughout the McGucken framework). Then the entropy associated with a McGucken Sphere of area $A$ is
$$S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}. \tag{10.6.1.1}$$

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere associated with a spacetime event $O$ is the 2-sphere swept out by $x_4$'s spherically symmetric expansion at radius $R = ct$ from $O$ (Definition 2 of the Introduction). Its area is $A = 4\pi R^2 = 4\pi c^2 t^2$.

Quantise $x_4$'s expansion at the Planck scale: the fundamental wavelength of $x_4$-advance is $\ell_P$. The number of independent quantum modes of $x_4$-advance crossing the McGucken Sphere is one mode per Planck-area cell. By the standard mode-counting argument [33, 35, 't Hooft 1993 (the holographic principle), Susskind 1995],
$$N_{\text{bits}} \;=\; \frac{A}{\ell_P^2} \tag{10.6.1.2}$$
up to a numerical factor of order unity. Identifying entropy with $k_B$ times the number of bits, and fixing the numerical factor by demanding consistency with the Bekenstein-Hawking expression in the limiting case of a black hole horizon [33, 35]:
$$S \;=\; \frac{k_B A}{4 \ell_P^2} \;=\; \frac{k_B A c^3}{4 \hbar G}.$$
The structural fact $S \propto A$ (rather than $S \propto V$) is forced by the $x_4$-mode counting on the McGucken Sphere: one mode per Planck-area cell. The factor $1/4$ is *not* fixed here by matching to Bekenstein--Hawking; it is *derived* as an output of $dx_4/dt = ic$ at Theorem 15.4.3 of Chapter 15 (integrate the first law against the Hawking temperature obtained from the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost, with $S(0)=0$), and its geometric origin --- the one-half of the Gibbons--Hawking--York boundary term on the Ricci-flat Euclidean cigar --- is exhibited at Theorem 15.4.5. Mode-counting supplies the area law's *form*; those theorems supply its *coefficient*. $\square$

## 10.6.2 Structural reading: the area law is McGucken-Sphere entropy

The area law (T10.6.1) is *not* an imported result from black hole thermodynamics; rather, the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black hole horizon is the *special case* of the McGucken-Sphere entropy when the McGucken Sphere coincides with the black hole horizon. The structural priority statement: $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ is the entropy of $x_4$-advance modes on any McGucken Sphere, with the black hole horizon being a particular kind of McGucken Sphere (the horizon of the Schwarzschild geometry; see Chapter 11, Theorem 11.5.4, and Chapter 15, §15.2.1).

# 10.7 Geometric Channel, Step 3: The Unruh Temperature $T_U = \hbar a / (2\pi c k_B)$ {#sec:unruh}

## 10.7.1 The Unruh temperature from the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost

**Theorem 10.7.1 (Unruh temperature from the McGucken-Wick rotation).** A uniformly accelerated observer in $M_G$ with proper acceleration $a$ experiences a thermal bath at temperature
$$T_U \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2\pi c k_B}. \tag{10.7.1.1}$$
The temperature is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Wick-rotation Theorem 4 of the Introduction (the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$) plus the KMS-periodicity identification of thermal states.
*Proof.* Consider a uniformly accelerated observer with proper acceleration $a$. The observer's worldline in Minkowski coordinates is
$$X(\tau_p) \;=\; \frac{c^2}{a}\, \sinh\!\left(\frac{a \tau_p}{c}\right), \quad x(\tau_p) \;=\; \frac{c^2}{a}\, \cosh\!\left(\frac{a \tau_p}{c}\right) \tag{10.7.1.2}$$
where $\tau_p$ is the observer's proper time.

Under the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$, $t \to -i\tau$ (Theorem 4 of the Introduction; theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via Lemma 5.1.2.1 of Chapter 5), the hyperbolic boost in the $(x, t)$-plane becomes a Euclidean rotation in the $(x, x_4)$-plane by angle $\theta = a \tau_p / c$ (where $\tau_p$ in this context denotes the Wick-rotated, Euclidean-section proper time of the accelerated observer).

Periodicity in the Euclidean angle $\theta$ (required by single-valuedness of the rotation on the Euclidean section): $\theta \in [0, 2\pi)$. The corresponding period in the Wick-rotated proper time is
$$\Delta \tau_p \;=\; \frac{2 \pi c}{a}. \tag{10.7.1.3}$$

By the KMS condition of quantum statistical mechanics [Kubo 1957; Martin-Schwinger 1959; Haag 1992], a quantum field state periodic in imaginary (proper) time with period $\Delta\tau_p$ is a thermal state at temperature $T$ given by the standard KMS relation $\Delta\tau_p = \hbar/(k_B T)$, equivalently $T = \hbar/(k_B \Delta\tau_p)$. Substituting (10.7.1.3):
$$T_U \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{k_B \cdot 2\pi c/a} \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B}. \tag{10.7.1.4}$$
$\square$

**Remark 10.7.2 (the KMS identification).** The KMS identification of imaginary-time periodicity with inverse temperature is the one substantive input from quantum statistical mechanics. Within the McGucken framework, KMS itself admits a derivation from the Wick-rotation structure of $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem 4 of the Introduction); we leave the full development of this to [3CH, §5] and import the KMS identification here as a standing assumption of the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel, alongside the Clausius relation in §10.8.

# 10.8 Geometric Channel, Step 4: Clausius Relation at Local Rindler Horizons {#sec:jacobson}

## 10.8.1 The Jacobson chain: $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at horizons

With the Geometric Second Law (Theorem 10.5.1), the area law (Theorem 10.6.1), and the Unruh temperature (Theorem 10.7.1) established as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$, the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations proceeds along Jacobson's 1995 chain.

**Setup.** Consider an arbitrary spacetime event $p \in M_G$ and a *local Rindler horizon* $H$ through $p$: a null hypersurface generated by a null congruence with affine parameter $\lambda$ and tangent vector $k^\mu$. The horizon is the boundary of the past of a uniformly accelerated observer in the local neighbourhood of $p$.

**Step 1 (heat flux through $H$).** The heat flux through a portion of $H$ is the integrated stress-energy flux along the local Rindler boost Killing vector $\xi^\mu = -\kappa\, \lambda\, k^\mu$ (Jacobson 1995 eq.\ 2; Wald 1984 §12.5), where $\kappa = a$ is the surface gravity (equal to the proper acceleration of the local Rindler observer at unit distance) and $\lambda$ is the affine parameter along the null generators of $H$:
$$\delta Q \;=\; \int_H T_{\mu\nu}\, \xi^\mu\, k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; -\kappa \int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu\, k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA. \tag{10.8.1.1}$$

**Step 2 (entropy change from area law).** By Theorem 10.6.1, the entropy associated with the horizon area is $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$. The infinitesimal entropy change is
$$\delta S \;=\; \frac{k_B}{4 \ell_P^2}\, \delta A. \tag{10.8.1.2}$$

**Step 3 (area change from Raychaudhuri equation).** The Raychaudhuri equation for a null congruence with tangent vector $k^\mu$ and expansion $\theta = d\ln A/d\lambda$, with vanishing expansion and shear at the bifurcation surface (where $\lambda = 0$), gives to leading order in $\lambda$
$$\theta(\lambda) = -\int_0^\lambda R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda'.$$
Integrating $dA/d\lambda = \theta\, A$ along the null generators, the area change between the bifurcation surface and affine parameter $\Lambda$ is
$$\delta A \;=\; -\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \tag{10.8.1.3}$$
to leading order. The minus sign reflects that positive $R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$ (the null energy condition direction) causes geodesic focussing, which decreases the cross-sectional area of the congruence.

**Step 4 (Clausius relation and the field equation).** Applying the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$ with $T = T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$ from (10.7.1.1) and $\kappa = a$:
$$-a \int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar a}{2 \pi c\, k_B} \cdot \frac{k_B}{4 \ell_P^2} \cdot \left(-\int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA\right).$$
Cancelling $-a$ from both sides:
$$\int_H \lambda\, T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA \;=\; \frac{\hbar}{8 \pi c\, \ell_P^2} \int_H \lambda\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu\, d\lambda\, dA.$$
This identity, together with full unit-tracking through the boost-Killing-vector normalization (Jacobson 1995, eqs.\ 3--5; the standard derivation), produces the Einstein-equation coefficient $c^4/(8\pi G)$ on the right-hand side. The pointwise statement valid at every event $p \in M_G$ and for every null $k^\mu$ at $p$ is
$$T_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu \;=\; \frac{c^4}{8 \pi G}\, R_{\mu\nu}\, k^\mu k^\nu. \tag{10.8.1.4}$$
The complete unit-tracking calculation, reconciling the dimensional content of the Unruh temperature, the Planck-area normalization, the Killing-vector normalization, and the Raychaudhuri-area integration, is in [37, equations 1--6] and recovered in textbook form in [Padmanabhan 2010, *Gravitation*, §15.4]. The McGucken-framework structural sourcing of each of the three thermodynamic inputs (Geometric Second Law, area law, Unruh temperature) as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the framework's contribution at this step; the Jacobson chain itself is inherited.

**Step 5 (universalisation to all null $k^\mu$ forces the field equations).** Since (10.8.1.4) holds for every null vector $k^\mu$ at every event, and $T_{\mu\nu}$ and $R_{\mu\nu}$ are both symmetric tensors, the contraction with null vectors forces a relation between the full tensors:
$$R_{\mu\nu} \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu} \;+\; \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8 \pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}. \tag{10.8.1.5}$$

The trace term $-\tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ is forced by the conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$, which is in turn required by the contracted Bianchi identity $\nabla^\mu G_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (Theorem 9.4.2.3 of Chapter 9); the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ enters as an integration constant (the unique additive term consistent with $\nabla^\mu (\Lambda g_{\mu\nu}) = 0$ by metric compatibility).

## 10.8.2 The Einstein field equations from the Geometric Channel

**Theorem 10.8.2 (Einstein Field Equations from the Geometric Channel).** Combining Theorems 10.5.1 (Geometric Second Law), 10.6.1 (area law), 10.7.1 (Unruh temperature), the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$, and the Raychaudhuri equation, the Einstein field equations
$$\boxed{\, G_{\mu\nu} \,+\, \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu} \,} \tag{T11.1, Geometric Channel}$$
*are forced as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along the Geometric Channel route.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of: (i) the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ (Theorem 10.5.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via isotropic-diffusion content of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (ii) the area law $S = k_B A / (4 \ell_P^2)$ (Theorem 10.6.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via $x_4$-mode counting at Planck scale); (iii) the Unruh temperature $T_U = \hbar a / (2 \pi c k_B)$ (Theorem 10.7.1, theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost); (iv) the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at local Rindler horizons; (v) the Raychaudhuri equation for null congruences (Equation 10.8.1.3, theorem of differential geometry on null geodesic congruences). Postulates (i)-(iii) are theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$; postulates (iv) and (v) are standard inputs from thermodynamics and differential geometry respectively. The field equations are forced. $\square$

**Structural reading of the Geometric Channel.** The Jacobson-McGucken thermodynamic route reads the Einstein field equations as the *equation of state* of spacetime, with the McGucken Sphere as the fundamental horizon-bounding surface and the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the source of the Sphere's expansion. The thermodynamic identity $\delta Q = T \delta S$ at every local Rindler horizon, with $T$ the Unruh temperature and $S$ the area-law entropy, forces $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ as the unique relation that makes the identity hold for every null direction at every event. The Geometric Channel derivation reveals general relativity as a *thermodynamic limit* of underlying $x_4$-expansion dynamics, with the field equations emerging from the area-law statistics of $x_4$-modes on McGucken Sphere horizons.

## 10.9.2 Empty-intersection verification

**Proposition 10.9.2 (structural disjointness certificate $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$).** No element of $M(\Pi_A)$ appears in $M(\Pi_B)$, and no element of $M(\Pi_B)$ appears in $M(\Pi_A)$. The two intermediate-machinery sets are structurally disjoint.
*Proof.* We verify the disjointness by pairwise inspection of the eight Algebraic Channel elements against the ten Geometric Channel elements.

(A1) $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ is a subgroup of $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$; this group-theoretic object does not appear in the Geometric Channel. The Geometric Channel uses null congruences and the Lie algebra of local boosts, not the foliation-preserving subgroup of the diffeomorphism group. (A1) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A2) Lemma 10.1.2.1 (rigidity of $\xi^0$) is a structural restriction on diffeomorphism generators; Geometric Channel has no analogous restriction --- the Rindler boost is parameterised by proper acceleration $a$, not by a restricted-vector-field structure. (A2) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A3) The perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor is the *matter* content of the Algebraic Channel; Geometric Channel treats matter through the *integrated heat flux* $\delta Q = \int_H T_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu d\lambda dA$ (Equation 10.8.1.1), which depends only on the contraction $T_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$ in a null direction, not on the perfect-fluid decomposition $(\rho, p, u^\mu)$. (A3) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A4) Noether's second theorem is the *variational* tool of the Algebraic Channel; Geometric Channel uses no variational principle at any step. The Raychaudhuri equation (B9) is a *kinematic* identity for null congruences, not a Noether-type conservation theorem. (A4) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A5) Spatial conservation and integrated time conservation are weak conservation laws specific to the Algebraic Channel's $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ symmetry; Geometric Channel has no analogous weak conservation laws --- it uses the strong conservation $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ implicitly through the contracted Bianchi identity at step (B10), but does not derive that conservation from a Noether-type argument. (A5) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A6) On-shell enhancement is the structural mechanism by which Algebraic Channel closes the gap from $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$ to $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$; Geometric Channel has no analogous enhancement step --- the Clausius relation is applied locally at every event without an on-shell/off-shell distinction. (A6) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A7) Lovelock's theorem is a *differential-geometric uniqueness* result on divergence-free symmetric rank-2 tensors in 4D; Geometric Channel does not invoke this theorem at any step. The universalisation in (B10) uses the contracted Bianchi identity to fix the trace term, but does not use Lovelock's uniqueness statement on the metric-and-derivatives functional form of the LHS. (A7) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

(A8) Newtonian-limit matching is a *weak-field static* calculation matching to Poisson's equation; Geometric Channel has no Newtonian-limit step --- the coupling constant $\kappa' = 8\pi G/c^4$ emerges in the Geometric Channel from the Clausius relation directly, via the combination of the area-law factor $1/(4\ell_P^2)$, the Unruh factor $\hbar/(2\pi c k_B)$, and the Planck-length substitution $\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3$ --- with no Newtonian matching invoked. (A8) $\notin M(\Pi_B)$.

Conversely:

(B1) Isotropic-diffusion equation is a *Brownian-motion* identity for the probability density; Algebraic Channel has no probability-density structure --- it treats matter through the deterministic stress-energy tensor (A3). (B1) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B2) Gaussian fundamental solution is the explicit form of the diffusion's heat kernel; Algebraic Channel has no heat-kernel structure. (B2) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B3) Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy and the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ are *statistical-mechanical* identities; Algebraic Channel has no entropy or Second Law content at any step --- the Newtonian-limit matching (A8) is deterministic, not statistical. (B3) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B4) $x_4$-mode counting at the Planck scale is a *quantum-geometric* counting argument; Algebraic Channel has no quantum-geometric inputs --- it operates entirely at the classical-variational level. (B4) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B5) The area-law coefficient $1/4$ is obtained on the Geometric Channel from horizon thermodynamics --- the Hawking temperature of the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost, integrated against the first law (Theorem 15.4.3), with its geometric origin in the Euclidean cigar's boundary action (Theorem 15.4.5). The Algebraic Channel has no thermodynamic content, no Euclidean section, and no horizon temperature at any step. (B5) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B6) Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost is the McGucken-Wick rotation applied to the accelerated worldline; Algebraic Channel uses the McGucken-Wick rotation only at the level of the global metric signature (in setting up the Lorentzian manifold $M_G$), not at the level of accelerated worldlines. (B6) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B7) KMS-periodicity identification is a *quantum statistical-mechanical* input; Algebraic Channel has no KMS or quantum-statistical content. (B7) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B8) Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \delta S$ is a *thermodynamic* identity; Algebraic Channel has no thermodynamic input. (B8) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B9) Raychaudhuri equation is a *null-congruence kinematics* identity; Algebraic Channel has no null-congruence machinery --- it operates on the level of the metric, the stress-energy tensor, and the connection, not on null geodesic congruences. (B9) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

(B10) Universalisation from null contractions is a *null-direction-averaging* argument; Algebraic Channel has no analogous averaging step. (B10) $\notin M(\Pi_A)$.

Hence $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$. The disjointness verification $\mathrm{DCD}(\mathrm{GR\,T11})$ is established. $\square$

## 10.9.3 Structural significance of the disjointness verification

The empty-intersection $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$ at the load-bearing pivot GR T11 is the strongest possible evidence for the structural priority of $dx_4/dt = ic$ over the field equations. The two derivations:

\end{itemize}

share no intermediate machinery. The convergence on $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ from these two structurally disjoint routes is the *overdetermined-proof structure* of the McGucken Duality (Section 5 of the Introduction), with maximum disjointness at the load-bearing pivot. The dual derivation is the structural reason GR T11 stands as a *theorem* of $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than a *postulate* of a gravitational framework: only a foundational principle as deep as the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ can support two such disparate routes of derivation converging on the same equation.

## 10.10.2 The cosmological constant $\Lambda$

The cosmological constant $\Lambda$ enters the field equations as an integration constant in both channels:

\begin{itemize}
\item In the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel, $\Lambda$ is the constant $\beta/\alpha$ in Lovelock's formula (10.4.1.1); it is consistent with both $\nabla^\mu g_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (metric compatibility) and $\nabla^\mu T_{\mu\nu} = 0$ (on-shell conservation), so it is unconstrained by the field equations themselves.

\item In the Geometric Channel, $\Lambda$ is the integration constant arising from the universalisation step (10.8.1.5): the relation $T_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu = (c^4/8\pi G) R_{\mu\nu} k^\mu k^\nu$ for all null $k^\mu$ determines $G_{\mu\nu} = R_{\mu\nu} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{\mu\nu}$ up to a constant multiple of $g_{\mu\nu}$, which becomes the $\Lambda$ term.
\end{itemize}

The empirical value $\Lambda \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-52}\, \mathrm{m}^{-2}$ from cosmological observations (Planck 2018 [Aghanim 2020]) is consistent with the McGucken Cosmology paper [21], which derives $\Lambda$ from the integrated $x_4$-expansion across the cosmological horizon. The 120-order-of-magnitude discrepancy that plagues quantum field theory-based attempts to derive $\Lambda$ from vacuum energy is *absent* in the McGucken framework: $\Lambda$ is a geometric integration constant in the field equations, not a vacuum-energy density requiring quantum-field cancellation. See [21, §6] for the full empirical analysis and the resolution of the cosmological constant problem within the McGucken framework.

## 10.10.3 The empirical triumph: McGucken Cosmology vs. $\Lambda$CDM

The Einstein field equations, with the McGucken framework's structural priority of $dx_4/dt = ic$ extending into the cosmological sector, yield the McGucken Cosmology [21] which has been empirically verified against $\Lambda$CDM across twelve independent observational tests. The Bayesian likelihood ratio of the McGucken Cosmology over $\Lambda$CDM is $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ [25], reflecting that the McGucken framework predicts the empirically observed cosmological dynamics *without* a free dark-sector parameter, while $\Lambda$CDM requires both dark matter ($\Omega_m \approx 0.31$) and dark energy ($\Omega_\Lambda \approx 0.69$) as free parameters.

The structural reason: the McGucken framework's foundational rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ generates the cosmological expansion as the *background* of the field equations, with the geometric integration constant $\Lambda$ playing the role of dark energy and the McGucken-Sphere structure of the early universe playing the role of (apparent) dark matter via gravitational lensing effects from the integrated $x_4$-expansion across cosmological scales. ## 10.10.4 Structural-priority statement

The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda g_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ have the following structural status within the McGucken framework:

*(i) They are a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, not a postulate.* Two structurally disjoint derivations (Algebraic Channel: Hilbert-Lovelock factorisation through $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}$; Geometric Channel: Jacobson thermodynamics through area-law horizons) converge on the same equation with empty intersection of intermediate machinery. The convergence is *forced* by the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.

*(ii) The diffeomorphism invariance of GR is a derived on-shell symmetry, not a foundational input.* The off-shell symmetry is $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$ (foliation-preserving); the full $\mathrm{Diff}(M_G)$ symmetry of Hilbert's framework emerges as a consequence of the matter equations of motion combined with the constitutive identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$.

*(iii) The field equations are an equation of state for spacetime.* The Geometric Channel route reveals the Einstein field equations as the *thermodynamic identity* $\delta Q = T \delta S$ applied to local Rindler horizons in $M_G$, with the McGucken Sphere as the fundamental horizon-bounding surface. The geometric content of GR (the metric and its curvature) emerges from the area-law statistics of $x_4$-modes on McGucken Spheres.

*(iv) The cosmological constant is a geometric integration constant.* $\Lambda$ enters the field equations as an integration constant in both channels, not as a vacuum-energy density. The 120-order-of-magnitude cosmological constant problem of quantum field theory-based approaches is absent within the McGucken framework.

*(v) The empirical evidence overwhelmingly favours the McGucken framework over $\Lambda$CDM.* The Bayesian likelihood ratio $\gtrsim 10^{141}$ over twelve independent cosmological tests reflects that $dx_4/dt = ic$ predicts the empirical dynamics without free dark-sector parameters.

The Einstein field equations, derived as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$, are the load-bearing pivot of the gravitational chain. Chapters 11--17 develop the downstream consequences --- Schwarzschild geometry, classical tests of GR, gravitational waves, cosmology, black hole thermodynamics --- each inheriting GR T11 as the foundational input. Within the McGucken framework, general relativity stands as a *theorem* of $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than a postulate of a gravitational framework: every equation in this book derives from a single physical principle.
