## 11.4.2 Quantitative prediction: GPS atomic-clock dilation

The GPS satellite atomic clocks at altitude $r_{\text{GPS}} \approx 26{,}600\, \text{km}$ from Earth's centre, with Earth's mass $M_\oplus = 5.972 \times 10^{24}\, \text{kg}$ and $r_\oplus = 6{,}371\, \text{km}$:

- Earth's $r_s$: $r_s^\oplus = 2 G M_\oplus/c^2 = 8.87\, \text{mm}$;
- Surface clock factor: $\sqrt{1 - r_s^\oplus/r_\oplus} \approx 1 - r_s^\oplus/(2 r_\oplus) \approx 1 - 6.96 \times 10^{-10}$;
- GPS clock factor: $\sqrt{1 - r_s^\oplus/r_{\text{GPS}}} \approx 1 - 1.67 \times 10^{-10}$;
- Differential (GPS faster): $5.29 \times 10^{-10}/$day $\times 86400$ s$/$day $= 45.7\, \mu$s/day.

This is the *gravitational* contribution. The special-relativistic time-dilation contribution from GPS satellite orbital velocity ($v \approx 3.87\, \text{km/s}$) is $\sim -7.2\, \mu$s/day (satellite clocks run slower due to motion). Net effect: GPS clocks run $\sim 38\, \mu$s/day faster than surface clocks --- corrected in the GPS satellite firmware to maintain coordinate-time synchrony. Without the correction, GPS positioning accuracy would degrade by $\sim 10$ km/day. The empirical verification of GR T13 is thus *continuous and daily* in the operation of the global positioning system.

# 11.5 Structural Relationship to Downstream Theorems

## 11.5.1 GR T14 (Gravitational Redshift)

The gravitational redshift (GR T14, Chapter 12) is derived from GR T13 by the following one-line argument. GR T13 supplies the proper-time-to-coordinate-time ratio at radial coordinate $r$:
$$\frac{d\tau(r)}{dt} \;=\; \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$$
A photon emitted by a stationary atom at radial coordinate $r_1$ has frequency $\nu_{\text{em}}$ measured by an observer at rest at $r_1$ (the emitter's local frame), where $\nu_{\text{em}}$ is the atomic transition frequency in proper time. The same photon, propagating outward along a null geodesic to radial coordinate $r_2 > r_1$, is received by a stationary observer at $r_2$ (the receiver's local frame) with frequency $\nu_{\text{rec}}$ measured in the receiver's proper time. Because (i) the photon's coordinate-time period is conserved along the null geodesic in the static Schwarzschild metric (the Killing vector $\partial_t$ is timelike outside the horizon, hence the photon's $\partial_t$-projection $p_t$ is conserved along the geodesic, hence the coordinate-time period $T_{\text{coord}} = 1/\nu_{\text{coord}}$ is invariant along the geodesic), and (ii) each observer's proper-time period is related to the coordinate-time period by the local time-dilation factor $d\tau/dt = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ of GR T13, the receiver's proper-time period $T_{\text{rec}} = T_{\text{coord}} \cdot \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$ and the emitter's proper-time period $T_{\text{em}} = T_{\text{coord}} \cdot \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$ give the frequency ratio
$$\nu_{\text{rec}} \;=\; \frac{1}{T_{\text{rec}}} \;=\; \frac{1/T_{\text{coord}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\text{coord}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}}, \qquad \nu_{\text{em}} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\text{coord}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}}$$
hence by elimination of $\nu_{\text{coord}}$:
$$\nu_{\text{rec}} \;=\; \nu_{\text{em}} \cdot \frac{d\tau_1}{d\tau_2} \;=\; \nu_{\text{em}} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}} \;<\; \nu_{\text{em}}.$$
The frequency shift is the *redshift* (lower frequency at higher altitude). In the weak-field limit $r_s \ll r_1, r_2$ the ratio expands to first order in $r_s/r$ as $\sqrt{(1-r_s/r_1)/(1-r_s/r_2)} \approx 1 - (r_s/2)(1/r_1 - 1/r_2) = 1 - (GM/c^2)(1/r_1 - 1/r_2) = 1 + (\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)/c^2$ with Newtonian potential $\Phi(r) = -GM/r$, giving the standard weak-field formula $\Delta \nu/\nu \approx (\Phi_2 - \Phi_1)/c^2$ with the sign convention that climbing out of a potential well decreases frequency.

## 11.5.2 GR T15 (Light Bending) and GR T16 (Mercury Perihelion)

GR T12 supplies the metric for GR T15 (null geodesics in Schwarzschild metric, bending angle $\delta\phi = 4GM/(b c^2)$ for impact parameter $b$, verified by Eddington 1919 and refined by Shapiro radio observations) and GR T16 (timelike geodesics in Schwarzschild metric, perihelion advance of $43''/$century for Mercury, verified by Le Verrier 1859 and explained by Einstein 1915). Both will be developed in Chapter 12 along both channels.

## 11.5.3 GR T17 (Gravitational Waves) and GR T18 (FLRW Cosmology)

GR T11 with linearised perturbations around Minkowski yields GR T17 (gravitational waves), the dynamical analogue of GR T12's static solution. GR T11 with the FLRW homogeneous-isotropic ansatz yields GR T18 (FLRW cosmology), the cosmological analogue. Both will be developed in subsequent chapters.

## 11.5.4 Singularity-free Schwarzschild geometry: the Kruskal interior is not part of $M_G$

The standard Kruskal--Szekeres maximal extension of the Schwarzschild metric extends the exterior $r > r_s$ across the horizon and into the interior region II, in which the coordinate $\partial_r$ acquires timelike character (its constant-$r$ surfaces become spacelike) and the curvature singularity at $r = 0$ is reached in finite proper time of order $r_s/c$ for radial infallers. The construction is summarised in Kruskal (Phys. Rev. 119, 1743) and Szekeres (Publ. Math. Debrecen 7, 285), and is standard in any graduate text (Wald §6.4, MTW §31.4--31.6, Carroll §5.7).

The Vanquishing paper [20] establishes that the Kruskal interior region II is *not* part of the McGucken manifold $M_G$, because the role swap of $\partial_r$ from spatial (in the exterior) to timelike (in the interior) is structurally inconsistent with the foundational axioms of the McGucken framework. The argument is *axiomatic*: it forecloses the interior by foundational commitment rather than by smoothing the curvature.

### 11.5.4.1 The foundational axioms of the McGucken framework, restated

The three axioms used in the foreclosure argument are all stated in or following directly from $dx_4/dt = ic$:

*(A1)* The fourth dimension advances at the invariant rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every spacetime event of $M_G$. The advance is unaffected by the presence of mass: $x_4$-expansion proceeds at rate $ic$ at every event, including events near a mass concentration. The wavelength $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ of one quantum of $x_4$-advance is therefore the same at every event. (This is the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i) of the Introduction, recovered as the McGucken-Invariance Lemma in GR T2.)

*(A2)* Mass affects the *spatial* geometry $x_1, x_2, x_3$ --- it bends and curves the spatial three directions. Gravitational time dilation is the projection of invariant proper-time $x_4$-advance onto a distant observer's coordinate time through the stretched spatial geometry; $x_4$'s rate does not change near a mass. (This is the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel reading of GR T13 from §11.2.)

*(A3)* Any momentum-energy carried in $x_4$ has no rest mass. Photons travel at $|v| = c$ in space and have $dx_4/d\tau = 0$ on null worldlines (they ride the wavefront, at absolute rest in $x_4$); massive matter at spatial rest has $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ with the entire four-speed budget directed into $x_4$-advance. (This is the four-budget partition of GR T1 with the massless/massive boundary cases of GR T6, Chapter 7.)

These are not separate postulates beyond $dx_4/dt = ic$: (A1) is the principle itself; (A2) is the content of the principle for how mass acts on geometry; (A3) is the photon-and-massive-matter ontology forced by the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ together with (A1).

### 11.5.4.2 Theorem 11.5.4: Schwarzschild geometry on $M_G$ has natural boundary at $r = r_s$

**Theorem 11.5.4 (Singularity-free Schwarzschild geometry).** Under the axioms (A1), (A2), (A3), the Schwarzschild geometry of a mass $M$ as realised on the McGucken manifold $M_G$ consists of the exterior region $r > r_s = 2GM/c^2$ only. The Kruskal interior region II and the curvature singularity at $r = 0$ are not part of $M_G$. The geometry has a natural boundary at the horizon $r = r_s$, where the spatial stretching of $\partial_r$ becomes infinite, and beyond which the manifold does not extend on the McGucken framework.

*Proof.* The Kruskal interior region II requires the coordinate direction $\partial_r$ to acquire timelike character and $\partial_t$ to acquire spacelike character at $r < r_s$ --- the *role swap*. We show that this role swap is structurally inconsistent with (A1), (A2), and (A3), through three structurally independent arguments.

*Inconsistency 1: from (A2).* The axiom (A2) identifies spatial directions by the property that mass bends and curves them. In the exterior Schwarzschild geometry, the radial direction $\partial_r$ is stretched by the factor $(1 - r_s/r)^{-1/2}$, with the stretching becoming infinite at $r \to r_s^+$. By (A2), the radial direction is therefore *spatial* on $M_G$ --- the identification is forced by the axiomatic content of how mass acts. The identification holds wherever mass is present and acting, which includes the entire region in which mass affects the geometry, not only $r > r_s$. The Kruskal extension's reinterpretation of $\partial_r$ as timelike for $r < r_s$ requires $\partial_r$ to cease being a spatial direction and become a timelike one. By (A2), this reinterpretation is barred: the radial direction was identified as spatial by the axiom of how mass acts, and that identification is *primitive* on the McGucken framework, with metric signature derived from it rather than the reverse. The metric coefficient changing sign at $r = r_s$ does not redefine which direction is spatial on $M_G$, because spatiality is fixed by (A2) independently of the local metric signature.

*Inconsistency 2: from (A1).* The axiom (A1) identifies the timelike direction by the property that $x_4$-expansion proceeds along it at the invariant rate $ic$. With the integrated kinematic shadow $x_4 = ict$ (descending from the dynamical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$), the timelike direction on $M_G$ is the $x_4$-axis (equivalently $\partial_t$ up to the factor $ic$) at every event of $M_G$. Inside the standard Kruskal interior region II, the metric coefficient $g_{tt} = -(1 - r_s/r)c^2$ would change sign at $r = r_s$ so that $\partial_t$ becomes metric-spacelike at $r < r_s$. There are two readings of this within the McGucken framework:

- *Reading (i):* $\partial_t$ continues to carry $dx_4/dt = ic$ but is metric-spacelike in the interior. This decouples the metric-signature notion of timelike from the axiomatic-McGucken notion. Under this reading, the standard physical interpretation of Kruskal-interior worldlines as "timelike in the metric-signature sense" no longer aligns with the master-equation condition $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, since the latter requires the four-velocity to point along the *axiomatic* timelike direction $x_4$, which is absent from region II in any reading consistent with (A1).

- *Reading (ii):* The carrier of $dx_4/dt = ic$ inside the horizon is something other than $\partial_t$. This directly contradicts (A1), which states that $x_4$-advance is along the $x_4$-axis at every event of $M_G$ without exception.

Reading (ii) is barred by (A1) directly; reading (i) leaves the interior region II structurally orphaned --- no massive worldline can extend into region II in the master-equation timelike sense, because the master equation requires alignment along the axiomatic timelike direction $x_4$, and this direction does not extend into region II under (A1). The Kruskal interior's promotion of $\partial_r$ to the new "timelike direction" inside the horizon is therefore barred even under reading (i) by Inconsistency 1.

*Audit caveat on Inconsistency 2.* Inconsistency 2 as stated is a *structural mismatch* rather than a strict logical contradiction in the same sense as Inconsistencies 1 and 3 --- reading (i) is internally consistent with (A1) in a narrow logical sense, but leaves the interior physically unintelligible by orphaning the master-equation four-velocity. The argument's strength is the combination: reading (i) is barred by Inconsistency 1 (which forecloses the alternative timelike axis); reading (ii) is barred by (A1) directly. The combined argument is unambiguous; we record the asymmetry for transparency.

*Inconsistency 3: from (A3).* The axiom (A3) states that any momentum-energy carried in $x_4$ has no rest mass; the contrapositive is that massive matter must carry its momentum-energy timelike along $x_4$, with the entire four-speed budget directed into $x_4$-advance at rate $ic$ in the rest frame. The Kruskal interior region II, in the standard reading, has massive infallers with timelike worldlines whose proper time accumulates along the decreasing-$r$ direction --- that is, along $\partial_r$, not along $x_4$. By (A3), a massive worldline cannot be timelike along anything other than $x_4$ at rate $ic$; the only timelike direction along which massive momentum-energy can flow is $x_4$. A massive infaller traversing region II with proper time accumulating along $\partial_r$ (and not along $x_4$) violates (A3): either the worldline carries rest mass while being timelike along the spatial direction $\partial_r$ (prohibited by (A3) plus Inconsistency 1), or the worldline is massless (contradicting the assumption that it is a massive infaller).

*Conclusion.* The three inconsistencies are structurally independent. (A2) fixes $\partial_r$ as spatial. (A1) fixes $x_4$, not $\partial_r$, as the carrier of $dx_4/d\tau = ic$, and forbids the metric-signature flip of $\partial_t$ at the horizon from being read as a change in the axiomatic timelike direction. (A3) prohibits massive worldlines from being timelike along non-$x_4$ directions. Each axiom alone bars the Kruskal role swap; together they do so unambiguously. The McGucken manifold $M_G$ does not extend past $r = r_s$. The classical curvature singularity at $r = 0$ lies in region II by construction of the Kruskal extension and is therefore not in $M_G$. $\square$

### 11.5.4.3 The maximum curvature on $M_G$ is finite and mass-bounded

**Corollary 11.5.4.4 (Finite maximum curvature on $M_G$).** The Kretschmann scalar $K = R_{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}R^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}$ of the Schwarzschild geometry on $M_G$ attains its maximum value at the horizon $r = r_s$:
$$K_{\max} \;=\; K(r_s) \;=\; \frac{48\, G^2 M^2}{c^4\, r_s^6} \;=\; \frac{48\, G^2 M^2}{c^4 \, (2GM/c^2)^6} \;=\; \frac{3 c^8}{4 G^4 M^4}. \tag{11.5.4.1}$$

*Proof.* The Kretschmann scalar of the Schwarzschild geometry is $K(r) = 48 G^2 M^2/(c^4 r^6)$ (standard textbook result; see MTW §31.2 for derivation). The function $K(r)$ is monotonically decreasing in $r$. Since by Theorem 11.5.4 the McGucken manifold $M_G$ consists of only the exterior $r > r_s$, the curvature on $M_G$ is bounded above by its value at the lower boundary $r = r_s$. Substituting $r_s = 2GM/c^2$:
$$K_{\max} \;=\; \frac{48 G^2 M^2}{c^4 \cdot (2GM/c^2)^6} \;=\; \frac{48 G^2 M^2 \cdot c^{12}}{c^4 \cdot 64 G^6 M^6} \;=\; \frac{48 \cdot c^8}{64 G^4 M^4} \;=\; \frac{3 c^8}{4 G^4 M^4}. \quad \square$$

**Remark 11.5.4.5 (mass scaling of the maximum curvature).** The maximum curvature on $M_G$ is finite and inversely proportional to $M^4$: a solar-mass black hole has $K_{\max} \sim 1.6 \times 10^{-13}$ m$^{-4}$; a stellar-mass black hole of $10\, M_\odot$ has $K_{\max} \sim 1.6 \times 10^{-17}$ m$^{-4}$; a supermassive black hole of $10^6\, M_\odot$ has $K_{\max} \sim 1.6 \times 10^{-37}$ m$^{-4}$ (using the formula $K_{\max} = 3 c^8/(4 G^4 M^4)$ of (11.5.4.1) with $G = 6.674 \times 10^{-11}$ m$^3$/(kg s$^2$), $c = 2.998 \times 10^8$ m/s, $M_\odot = 1.989 \times 10^{30}$ kg). In every case the curvature is bounded above and arbitrarily small for large $M$, in contrast to the standard Schwarzschild--Kruskal interior in which $K(r) \to \infty$ as $r \to 0$. The infinity at $r = 0$ is foreclosed by the axiomatic restriction of $M_G$ to $r > r_s$, rather than regulated by smoothing.

### 11.5.4.4 Structural status of the foreclosure

Theorem 11.5.4 is *conditional* on (A1), (A2), (A3) being foundational. A reader who accepts these axioms as foundational accepts the theorem; a reader who challenges the axioms is challenging the foundation of the McGucken framework rather than the theorem. The axioms (A1)--(A3) are not independent postulates beyond $dx_4/dt = ic$ within the framework: (A1) is the principle itself, (A2) is the content of the principle for how mass acts on geometry (the Geometric Channel reading of GR T13 from §11.2), and (A3) is the photon-and-massive-matter ontology forced by the master equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ together with (A1) (the boundary cases of the four-budget partition, GR T6 of Chapter 7).

The structural reading: the McGucken framework's foreclosure of the Kruskal interior is *not a curvature-regulation mechanism* (it does not smooth the singularity at $r = 0$ or replace it with a regular core); it is an *axiomatic-manifold-restriction mechanism*. The manifold $M_G$ ends at $r = r_s$, and the locus where the divergence would lie is not in $M_G$. The horizon is a genuine geodesic boundary of the manifold, not a coordinate artifact to be analytically continued past. Full content of the proof and discussion is given in the companion paper [20].

The Big Bang singularity is treated by a structurally analogous argument in §14.4 below: the FLRW scale factor's contraction is bounded below by the requirement that one quantum of $x_4$-advance be accommodated, with the spatial manifold reaching minimum extent at $t \sim t_P = \ell_P/c$ rather than contracting to a point at $t = 0$. The Big Bang argument is structurally less complete than the Schwarzschild argument because it rests on the additional input of Hypothesis 1 (the Planck-spacing $x_4$-lattice), as noted in §14.4.

## 11.6.3 Structural-priority statement

GR T12 and GR T13 open the *observational sector* of the gravitational chain. The structural priority statement at the chapter level:

The Schwarzschild solution is the radial profile of $x_4$-advance rates around a spherically symmetric mass distribution, with the gravitational time dilation it predicts being the structural consequence of the four-velocity budget partition: at lower potential, more of the budget is consumed by binding, leaving less for $x_4$-advance per coordinate time. Birkhoff's theorem (uniqueness) follows from the Gauss-law content of the spherical symmetry, which depends only on the total enclosed mass.
The standard textbook treatment (Wald §6.1, Carroll §5.2, MTW §31.2) derives the Schwarzschild solution by direct ODE-solving from the vacuum field equations on a spherically symmetric ansatz; the gravitational time dilation is then extracted from the metric. The McGucken framework provides a *structural reading* alongside this calculation: time dilation is budget-partition consumption, the gravitational radius $r_s$ is the radius at which the entire budget is consumed by binding (giving zero $x_4$-advance per coordinate time and the event horizon of a black hole, developed in subsequent chapters), and the factor of 2 in $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ has the structural origin in the relativistic correction to the budget partition.

The observational sector of the gravitational chain has now been opened. The Schwarzschild solution governs all observational tests of GR exterior to spherically symmetric masses; the time-dilation prediction of GR T13 has been verified to one part in $10^{15}$ by laboratory experiments and is the daily operational verification of GR in the GPS satellite system. Chapter 12 will develop GR T14 (gravitational redshift) and GR T15 (light bending) along both channels; Chapter 13 will develop GR T16 (Mercury perihelion advance) and GR T17 (gravitational waves), completing the classical-tests sector.

# 12.0 Chapter Overview

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

**Notation and abbreviations used in this chapter.** For reader convenience, the following terms are defined here once for the chapter; readers familiar with them may skip this block.

- $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- the *McGucken Principle* (occasionally abbreviated McP), the foundational physical principle of the framework: the fourth spacetime dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event. The imaginary unit $i$ records the perpendicularity of the temporal direction $x_4$ to the three spatial directions. Stated as the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ of §1.1.

- $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ --- the *four-velocity budget identity* (Theorem GR T1), occasionally referred to as the *budget* or *budget partition*. In plain words: every massive particle has a fixed allowance of four-speed equal to $c$, distributed between time-direction advance and spatial-direction motion. A particle at rest spends its whole budget on time-advance ($x_4$-direction at rate $c$); a particle moving spatially at speed $v$ spends part on spatial motion, leaving less for time-advance; a photon spends all of its budget on spatial motion at $c$, with zero time-advance.

- $[\hat{q}, \hat{p}] = i\hbar$ --- the *canonical commutation relation* of quantum mechanics (occasionally abbreviated the canonical commutation relation): position and momentum operators on a Hilbert space of quantum states do not commute; their commutator equals $i\hbar$. This is the formal heart of quantum mechanics, producing the Heisenberg uncertainty principle and forcing quantum states into a Hilbert space rather than a classical phase-space.

- **the McGucken-Invariance Lemma** --- the *McGucken-Invariance Lemma* (Theorem GR T2): the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is independent of the spacetime metric, $\partial(dx_4/dt)/\partial g_{\mu\nu} = 0$. The rate is *gravity-rigid* --- the same at every event regardless of local gravitational potential, curvature, or stress-energy.

- **structural disjointness** --- *Dual-Channel Disjointness*: the predicate $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$, asserting that the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel's intermediate machinery set $M(\Pi_A)$ and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel's intermediate machinery set $M(\Pi_B)$ share no named structure other than $dx_4/dt = ic$ itself.

- **EP** --- *Equivalence Principle*, in three forms: **the Weak Equivalence Principle** = weak equivalence principle (all massive test particles fall along the same geodesic, GR T3); **the Einstein Equivalence Principle** = Einstein equivalence principle (local physics is special-relativistic at every event, GR T4); **the Strong Equivalence Principle** = strong equivalence principle (the Einstein Equivalence Principle extends to events with macroscopic gravitational self-energy, GR T5).

- **QM, quantum field theory** --- *quantum mechanics* and *quantum field theory* respectively.

- **GR** --- *general relativity*. The 24 theorems of the gravitational chain are labelled GR T1 through GR T24.

- **BH** --- *black hole*. The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy is written $S_{\mathrm{BH}}$ (subscript abbreviation only; the framework derives the result as Theorem GR T20).

- **FLRW** --- *Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker* (the homogeneous-and-isotropic cosmological model derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as Theorem GR T18).

- **CMB** --- *cosmic microwave background*.

- **transverse-traceless gauge** --- *transverse-traceless* gauge: the standard gauge for gravitational-wave perturbations in the linearised field equations (GR T17), in which the perturbation $h_{\mu\nu}$ is divergence-free and traceless, leaving two physical polarisations $h_+$ and $h_\times$.

- **KMS** --- *Kubo--Martin--Schwinger* periodicity: the quantum-statistical-mechanics criterion identifying a periodically-identified Euclidean time direction with a thermal state at the corresponding inverse temperature $\beta = \hbar/(k_B T)$.

- **conformal field theory** --- *conformal field theory*: a quantum field theory invariant under conformal (angle-preserving) transformations.

\bigskip


This chapter continues the *observational sector* of the gravitational chain by developing two of the classical tests of general relativity. GR T14 is the gravitational redshift: photons emitted at lower gravitational potential appear at lower frequency to distant observers. GR T15 is the bending of light: photons passing near a massive body are deflected from their straight-line paths by an angle dependent on the mass and the impact parameter. Both theorems are verified by direct astronomical observation to high precision.

**Theorem GR T14 (Gravitational Redshift).** Let $M_G$ have the Schwarzschild metric (T12.1) exterior to a spherically symmetric mass $M$, and let the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold at every event. A photon emitted at frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ by a stationary source at radial coordinate $r_1 > r_s$ and received by a stationary observer at radial coordinate $r_2 > r_1$ is observed at frequency
$$\boxed{\, \nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}}. \,} \tag{T14.1}$$
For $r_2 > r_1$ (climbing out of the potential well), $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} < \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ (redshift). The fractional shift in the weak-field limit is
$$\frac{\Delta \nu}{\nu} \;\equiv\; \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{em}} - \nu_{\mathrm{rec}}}{\nu_{\mathrm{em}}} \;\approx\; \frac{\Phi_2 - \Phi_1}{c^2} \;=\; \frac{GM}{c^2}\left(\frac{1}{r_1} - \frac{1}{r_2}\right) \;>\; 0, \tag{T14.2}$$
with $\Phi(r) = -GM/r$ the Newtonian gravitational potential. The redshift has been verified by Adams (1925, Sirius B white-dwarf spectroscopy), Pound--Rebka (1959, $\gamma$-ray transit through Harvard tower), and astronomical observations of stellar redshifts in clusters and at galactic centres.
**Theorem GR T15 (Bending of Light by a Massive Body).** Let $M_G$ have the Schwarzschild metric (T12.1) exterior to a spherically symmetric mass $M$. A photon following a null geodesic in this metric with impact parameter $b \gg r_s$ is deflected from its asymptotic straight-line path by a total angle
$$\boxed{\, \delta\phi \;=\; \frac{4 G M}{b\, c^2} \;=\; \frac{2 r_s}{b}, \,} \tag{T15.1}$$
to leading order in $r_s/b$. For a photon grazing the Sun's limb ($b = R_\odot$, $M = M_\odot$): $\delta\phi = 1.75''$ (arcseconds). The deflection has been verified by:
*- Eddington 1919 (solar eclipse expedition to Príncipe, $1.61'' \pm 0.30''$);*

*- Shapiro radio observations 1971+ (verified to $\sim 0.1\%$ precision);*

- Very Long Baseline Interferometry observations of quasars (precision $\sim 10^{-4}$);
*- Gravitational lensing observations of distant galaxies behind cluster lenses (matter distribution reconstruction at all scales);*

- Direct imaging of the Event Horizon Telescope's $M87^*$ and $\mathrm{Sgr\,A^*}$ photon rings (verified to $\sim 10\%$ precision at $b \sim 5 r_s$).
The two theorems are connected: GR T14 is the *temporal* content of the Schwarzschild metric acting on photons (redshift = time dilation of photon frequency); GR T15 is the *spatial* content of the same metric acting on photons (bending = geodesic deflection in curved spatial geometry). Together they demonstrate that the Schwarzschild metric describes a unified spacetime curvature affecting both the temporal and spatial sectors of null worldlines.

The chapter is organised in six sections: §12.1 derives GR T14 along both channels; §12.2 derives GR T15 along both channels; §12.3 establishes the structural relationship between the two theorems (both are manifestations of the same Schwarzschild metric on null geodesics, with redshift the temporal sector and bending the spatial); §12.4 records the experimental verifications and modern observational refinements; §12.5 records the downstream structural relationships to GR T16 (Mercury perihelion, Chapter 13) and to gravitational lensing and Event Horizon Telescope imaging; §12.6 carries the disjointness verification for both channels and the structural-priority statement.


# 12.1 Theorem GR T14: Gravitational Redshift {#sec:GR-T14}

## 12.1.1 Statement of GR T14

**Theorem GR T14 (Gravitational Redshift).** Let $M_G$ have the Schwarzschild metric (T12.1) exterior to a spherically symmetric mass $M$. A photon emitted by a stationary source at radial coordinate $r_1 > r_s$ with frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ in the source's rest frame, and received by a stationary observer at radial coordinate $r_2$ in the observer's rest frame, is observed at frequency
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}}. \tag{T14.1}$$

For $r_2 > r_1$ (the observer above the source in the potential well), $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} < \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$: the photon is *redshifted*. For $r_2 < r_1$ (the observer below the source), $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} > \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$: the photon is *blueshifted*. In both cases, the frequency shift reflects the difference in proper-time rates between the emission and reception events.

## 12.1.2 $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel derivation: from gravitational time dilation applied to photon frequency

**Claim 12.1.2.** GR T14 follows from $dx_4/dt = ic$ by the algebraic-symmetry route directly from GR T13 (gravitational time dilation, Chapter 11) applied to the photon frequency.

### Step 1: Photon as a clock at the source.

**Lemma 12.1.2.1 (Photon emission frequency as proper-time rate).** A photon emitted with frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ in the rest frame of a stationary source at radial coordinate $r_1$ has a proper-time period $T_{\mathrm{em}} = 1/\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$. The corresponding coordinate-time period at the source location is
$$dt_{\mathrm{em}} \;=\; \frac{T_{\mathrm{em}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}} \;=\; \frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}}. \tag{12.1.2.1}$$

*Proof.* In three steps from $dx_4/dt = ic$ and GR T13.

*Step 1: Proper-time period of one photon oscillation.* In the local rest frame of the stationary source at radial coordinate $r_1$, the photon's oscillation period is the inverse of its emitted frequency: $T_{\mathrm{em}} = 1/\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$. This is the *proper-time* period --- the time elapsed on the source's clock between successive wave-crest events of the photon emitted at the source's location. The proper-time character of $T_{\mathrm{em}}$ is the McGucken-framework content of "in the rest frame of the source": by GR T13 (Theorem 11.2.2.2 of Chapter 11), the source's clock advances at the proper-time rate $d\tau$, and the photon's emission frequency is measured against this proper-time interval.

*Step 2: Conversion from proper-time to coordinate-time via GR T13.* By Theorem 11.2.2.2 of Chapter 11 (gravitational time dilation along the Algebraic Channel), the proper-time interval $d\tau$ at radial coordinate $r$ is related to the asymptotic-observer's coordinate-time interval $dt$ by
$$d\tau \;=\; \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, dt, \quad \text{equivalently} \quad dt \;=\; \frac{d\tau}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}}.$$
The $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel reading of this relation (Theorem 11.2.3.3): the proper-time rate of $x_4$-advance is *invariant* at every event by $dx_4/d\tau = ic$, but the coordinate-time projection of this advance is reduced at lower potential by the binding-induced consumption of the asymptotic-frame Sphere-expansion rate.

*Step 3: Application to the emission event.* At the source location $r_1$, the photon's proper-time period $T_{\mathrm{em}} = 1/\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ corresponds to a coordinate-time period
$$dt_{\mathrm{em}} \;=\; \frac{T_{\mathrm{em}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}} \;=\; \frac{1}{\nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}},$$
which is (12.1.2.1). The coordinate-time period is *longer* than the proper-time period because the source clock runs slow as observed from the asymptotic frame: the same number of photon oscillations occupies more coordinate-time seconds when viewed from infinity, by the factor $1/\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$. This is the structural content of the gravitational redshift derived in §12.1. $\square$

### Step 2: Coordinate-time period invariance under static metric.

**Lemma 12.1.2.2 (Coordinate-time period of photon is conserved along its null worldline).** In the static Schwarzschild metric, where $g_{\mu\nu}$ is independent of $t$, the coordinate-time period $dt$ between two successive wave crests of a photon is the same at every event along the photon's null worldline.

*Proof.* In two steps.

*Step 1: Killing-vector conservation from staticity.* The Schwarzschild metric (T12.1) is static: $\partial_t g_{\mu\nu} = 0$. By Noether's theorem applied to the time-translation Killing vector $K^\mu = (\partial_t)^\mu = (1, 0, 0, 0)$, the quantity $K_\mu p^\mu = g_{tt} p^t$ is conserved along any null geodesic of $M_G$, where $p^\mu$ is the photon four-momentum. In particular, $p_t = g_{tt} p^t$ is conserved. The coordinate-time period $dt$ between successive wave crests is related to the photon frequency in *coordinate-time* parameterisation by $dt_{\text{coord}} = 1/\nu_{\text{coord}}$, with the coordinate-time frequency $\nu_{\text{coord}}$ being the dual of the conserved $p_t$. Hence $\nu_{\text{coord}}$ (and equivalently $dt$) is constant along the photon worldline.

*Step 2: McGucken-framework structural reading.* The conservation of the coordinate-time period along the photon's worldline is the *McGucken-framework expression of the static-spacetime time-translation symmetry*. The static Schwarzschild background has the temporal Killing direction $K^\mu_{(t)}$ as a symmetry of $M_G$ (the iterated McGucken-Sphere expansion is the same at each cosmic-time slice on the static background, by GR T2 — the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i)'s universal rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ at every event of $M_G$). The photon four-momentum's projection onto this symmetry direction is the asymptotic-time-translation conserved charge $E = -K_{(t)\mu} p^\mu$ (Lemma 12.2.2.1), which has the dimensional content of *energy* — the asymptotic-observer's measurement of the photon's energy. The conservation of $\nu_{\text{coord}} = dt^{-1}$ along the photon's worldline is the equivalent statement in frequency units: the coordinate-time frequency, dual to the conserved $p_t$, is the same at every event of the worldline. The structural reading: the gravitational redshift (Theorem 12.1.3.4) is the difference between the *coordinate-time* frequency (conserved along the photon's worldline) and the *proper-time* frequency (measured by local observers at different radial coordinates with different time-dilation factors). The photon "doesn't lose energy" along its worldline — the energy projection onto the asymptotic-frame Killing direction is conserved; the *appearance* of redshift is the differential between the coordinate-time and proper-time foliations at the emission and reception events. $\square$

### Step 3: Reception frequency from coordinate-time period and reception-event gravitational time dilation.

**Theorem 12.1.2.3 (Gravitational Redshift from the Algebraic Channel).** At the reception event $(t_2, r_2)$, the photon's proper-time period in the observer's rest frame is
$$T_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}\, dt, \tag{12.1.2.2}$$
where $dt$ is the same coordinate-time period from (12.1.2.1) (by Lemma 12.1.2.2). The received frequency is
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \frac{1}{T_{\mathrm{rec}}} \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}\, dt} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}}, \tag{T14.1}$$
*recovering the gravitational redshift formula.*

*Proof.* (12.1.2.2) is the application of GR T13 at the reception event with the appropriate proper-time period. Substituting (12.1.2.1) for $dt$ yields (T14.1). $\square$

**Conclusion of the Algebraic Channel derivation.** GR T14 along the Algebraic Channel is the algebraic consequence of: (i) gravitational time dilation at the emission and reception events; (ii) coordinate-time period conservation along the static Schwarzschild metric's null geodesics (Noether/Killing). The ratio of proper-time rates at the two events generates the frequency shift.

## 12.1.3 Geometric Channel derivation: from McGucken-Sphere $x_4$-advance phase integral

**Claim 12.1.3.** GR T14 follows from $dx_4/dt = ic$ by the geometric-propagation route via the integrated $x_4$-advance phase along the photon's null worldline.

### Step 1: Photon phase as integrated $x_4$-advance.

**Lemma 12.1.3.1 (Photon phase from $x_4$-advance).** A photon's quantum-mechanical phase is the integrated $x_4$-advance along its worldline, weighted by the rest-mass-energy frequency $\omega = mc^2/\hbar$. For a photon (zero rest mass), the phase reduces to the integrated electromagnetic frequency:
$$\Phi_\gamma(\lambda) \;=\; \omega \cdot t \;=\; 2\pi \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, t, \tag{12.1.3.1}$$
*where $t$ is the coordinate-time elapsed along the null worldline.*

*Proof.* By the McGucken framework reading of quantum phase (Chapter 5; recall Lemma 5.1.3.2 of Chapter 5 and the de Broglie-Compton frequency identification of [6]): every quantum particle's phase evolves at rate $\omega = \mathcal{E}/\hbar$ along its worldline, with $\mathcal{E}$ the particle's energy. For photons, $\mathcal{E} = h \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$, so the phase evolves at rate $\omega = 2\pi \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ per coordinate-time second (in the source's rest frame), with the rate appearing as the coordinate-time content along the photon's null worldline. $\square$

### Step 1a: Coordinate-period invariance from static Sphere-flow congruence (Geometric Channel machinery).

**Lemma 12.1.3.1a (Coordinate-period invariance of the photon wavefront, from the iterated Sphere flow).** *On the static exterior of a spherically symmetric source, two successive wave crests of a photon emitted from $r_1$ separated by coordinate-time interval $\Delta t$ arrive at any $r_2 > r_s$ separated by the same coordinate-time interval $\Delta t$. The coordinate-time period of the photon is therefore invariant along its null worldline. The derivation uses only the iterated McGucken-Sphere flow and the staticity of the exterior; it invokes no Killing vector, no Noether current, and no conserved momentum component.*

*Proof.* By Lemma 7.2.3.2 of Chapter 7, a photon is a rider of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront: at every apex event it advances to the surface of the local Sphere of radius $c\,dt$, with the entire four-budget in the spatial sector. Its worldline is therefore an integral curve of the iterated Sphere flow at the null boundary (Lemma 7.2.2.1a(ii)).

Consider the Sphere-flow structure on the static exterior. At any spatial point $(r, \theta, \varphi)$ with $r > r_s$, the local McGucken Sphere has radius $c\,dt$ (universal rate, GR T2 --- Lemma 11.1.3.1), and its embedding into the spatial slice is governed by the spatial metric $g_{ij}(r)$, which by staticity is *independent of $t$*. Hence the Sphere-flow map that carries a wavefront from the slice $\Sigma_t$ to the slice $\Sigma_{t + dt}$ is *the same map* at every $t$: the iterated-Sphere flow on the static exterior is invariant under the coordinate-time translation $t \mapsto t + \Delta t$.

Now let $\gamma_1$ be the null Sphere-flow history of the first wave crest, emitted at $(t_e, r_1)$, and $\gamma_2$ that of the second crest, emitted at $(t_e + \Delta t, r_1)$. Both crests are emitted at the *same spatial point* $r_1$ and ride the *same* Sphere-flow structure. Because that structure is invariant under $t \mapsto t + \Delta t$ (previous paragraph), $\gamma_2$ is the rigid coordinate-time translate of $\gamma_1$: at every step of the iterated-Sphere construction, the Sphere that crest 2 rides at coordinate time $t + \Delta t$ is the exact time-translate of the Sphere that crest 1 rode at coordinate time $t$, with the same radius $c\,dt$ and the same spatial embedding. The two wavefront histories are therefore *congruent*, differing only by the rigid shift $\Delta t$ in the coordinate-time label.

Consequently, if crest 1 reaches radial coordinate $r_2$ at coordinate time $t_r$, crest 2 reaches $r_2$ at coordinate time $t_r + \Delta t$. The reception events are separated by the same coordinate-time interval $\Delta t$ as the emission events. The coordinate-time period of the photon is invariant along the null worldline. $\square$

**Remark 12.1.3.1b (why this is Geometric Channel machinery, not an Algebraic import).** The Algebraic Channel establishes the same invariance at Lemma 12.1.2.2 by an entirely different route: the time-translation Killing vector $K^\mu = (\partial_t)^\mu$ of the static metric, Noether's theorem, and the conservation of $p_t = g_{tt}p^t$ along the null geodesic. Lemma 12.1.3.1a invokes none of that apparatus. It uses only (i) the photon as Sphere-wavefront rider (Lemma 7.2.3.2), (ii) the universal Sphere radius $c\,dt$ at every event (GR T2), and (iii) the $t$-independence of the spatial embedding, which makes the Sphere-flow map itself time-translation-congruent. The invariance is read off the *congruence of two wavefront histories* --- a Huygens statement about the iterated Sphere construction --- rather than off a conserved charge. The two channels reach the same invariance from structurally disjoint machinery, which is what the disjointness certificate of §12.1.4 requires; the earlier routing of the Geometric Channel through Lemma 12.1.2.2 was an inadvertent import of Algebraic machinery and is corrected here.

### Step 2: Universal coordinate-time advance vs. potential-dependent proper-time advance.

**Lemma 12.1.3.2 (Coordinate-time vs. proper-time at reception).** The proper-time rate at the reception event (radial coordinate $r_2$) per coordinate-time second is $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$ (by GR T13 at the reception event). The observer at $r_2$ measures the photon's frequency by counting oscillations per *proper-time* second:
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{coord}} \cdot \frac{(\text{coordinate-time second})}{(\text{proper-time second at } r_2)} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}}, \tag{12.1.3.2}$$
where $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ is the coordinate-time frequency (oscillations per coordinate-time second).
*Proof.* In two steps.

*Step 1: Direct conversion.* The observer at $r_2$ counts wave crests per local proper-time second. One proper-time second at $r_2$ corresponds to $1/\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$ coordinate-time seconds. Hence the count of oscillations per proper-time second is the count of oscillations per coordinate-time second divided by the time-dilation factor: $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} = \nu_{\mathrm{coord}} / \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$.

*Step 2: McGucken-framework structural reading.* The conversion between coordinate-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ and proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}}$ at the reception event is the McGucken-framework four-budget projection factor at $r_2$: the proper-time rate at the reception event is the universal $dx_4/d\tau = ic$ (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i)), but the coordinate-time-foliation projects this rate by the factor $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$ (GR T13 at the reception event — Theorem 11.2.2.2). The local observer counts more wave crests per proper-time second than per coordinate-time second by the inverse of this projection factor, because the proper-time second is *shorter* than the coordinate-time second at $r_2$ (lower potential, more time-dilation). The structural reading: the apparent frequency shift at the reception event is the algebraic content of the four-budget coordinate-frame projection, not a property of the photon itself. The photon's coordinate-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ is conserved along its worldline (Lemma 12.1.2.2); the proper-time-frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}}$ depends on the *local-frame projection factor* at the reception event. $\square$

### Step 3: Source-event coordinate-time frequency.

**Lemma 12.1.3.3 (Source coordinate-time frequency from emission proper-time frequency).** Similarly at the source: the emitter at $r_1$ produces the photon at proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ in its rest frame, but the coordinate-time frequency along the photon's worldline is
$$\nu_{\mathrm{coord}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}} \cdot \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}. \tag{12.1.3.3}$$

*Proof.* In two steps.

*Step 1: Direct conversion at emission.* The emission proper-time interval $T_{\mathrm{em}} = 1/\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ corresponds to coordinate-time interval $T_{\mathrm{em}}/\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$. The coordinate-time frequency is the inverse of this: $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}/T_{\mathrm{em}} = \nu_{\mathrm{em}} \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$.

*Step 2: McGucken-framework structural reading.* The conversion at the source is dual to the reception-event conversion of Lemma 12.1.3.2: the proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ at the source's rest frame is converted to coordinate-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ along the photon's worldline by multiplication by the source's *local-frame coordinate-frame projection factor* $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$. The emitter produces oscillations at proper-time rate $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ in its rest frame; in the asymptotic-observer's coordinate-time foliation, these oscillations appear at the *slower* coordinate-time rate $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}} = \nu_{\mathrm{em}} \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1} < \nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ (the coordinate-time second is *longer* than the proper-time second at $r_1$, so fewer oscillations fit per coordinate-time second). Combined with Lemma 12.1.3.2's reception-event conversion, the gravitational redshift formula (Theorem 12.1.3.4):
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}}/\nu_{\mathrm{em}} \;=\; \sqrt{(1 - r_s/r_1)/(1 - r_s/r_2)}$$
emerges as the *ratio of the two local-frame coordinate-frame projection factors* at the emission and reception events. The structural reading: the gravitational redshift is the differential of the McGucken-framework four-budget coordinate-frame projection between two events at different gravitational potentials. $\square$

### Step 4: GR T14 from the Geometric Channel.

**Theorem 12.1.3.4 (Gravitational Redshift from the Geometric Channel).** Combining (12.1.3.2) and (12.1.3.3) --- with the coordinate-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ being the *same* at both events (by Lemma 12.1.3.1a, the Sphere-flow congruence of successive wavefronts on the static exterior):
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{coord}} / \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1} / \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}}. \tag{T14.1}$$

*Proof.* In three steps from the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, GR T2, and the four-budget partition.

*Step 1: Coordinate-time invariance of the photon's worldline period (Lemma 12.1.3.1a).* By Lemma 12.1.3.1a, the coordinate-time period between successive wave crests is invariant along the photon's null worldline. The Geometric Channel derives this from the *congruence of the two wavefront histories under the iterated Sphere flow*: on the static exterior the Sphere-flow map from $\Sigma_t$ to $\Sigma_{t+dt}$ is the same at every $t$ (universal Sphere radius $c\,dt$ by GR T2, $t$-independent spatial embedding by staticity), so the null Sphere-flow history of the second crest is the rigid coordinate-time translate of the first, and the two arrive at $r_2$ separated by the same coordinate-time interval $\Delta t$ that separated their emissions. No Killing vector, no Noether current, and no conserved $p_t$ is invoked; the Algebraic Channel reaches the same invariance by that entirely different route at Lemma 12.1.2.2 (see Remark 12.1.3.1b).

*Step 2: Time-dilation factors at emission and reception (Lemmas 12.1.3.2 and 12.1.3.3).* By Lemma 12.1.3.3, the emitter's proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$ relates to the coordinate-time frequency by $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}} = \nu_{\mathrm{em}} \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}$. By Lemma 12.1.3.2, the receiver's proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}}$ relates to the coordinate-time frequency by $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} = \nu_{\mathrm{coord}} / \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}$. Both factors descend from GR T13 (gravitational time dilation), which is itself the McGucken-framework expression of the master-equation four-budget partition at the stationary observer.

*Step 3: McGucken-framework structural reading.* Combining (12.1.3.2) and (12.1.3.3) using the invariance of $\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}$ from Step 1:
$$\nu_{\mathrm{rec}} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{coord}}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}} \;=\; \frac{\nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{1 - r_s/r_1}}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_2}} \;=\; \nu_{\mathrm{em}}\, \sqrt{\frac{1 - r_s/r_1}{1 - r_s/r_2}}. \tag{T14.1}$$
The Geometric Channel structural reading: the photon is, in the McGucken framework, a null worldline with the entire four-budget directed into spatial motion at universal rate $c$ (case (ii) of Lemma 7.2.3.1 of Chapter 7: $|u^4| = 0$, $|\vec u| = c$). Its *coordinate-time* period is invariant along the null geodesic because the static metric admits a time-translation Killing vector. What changes is the *coordinate-to-proper-time projection* at emission and reception: at the emitter's location (low potential $r_1$), the proper-time-per-coordinate-time factor is small, so the coordinate-time period corresponds to a shorter-proper-time period (higher proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{em}}$); at the receiver's location (higher potential $r_2$), the proper-time-per-coordinate-time factor is larger, so the same coordinate-time period corresponds to a longer proper-time period (lower proper-time frequency $\nu_{\mathrm{rec}}$). The photon does not "lose energy climbing out of the gravitational well" — it carries the *same* coordinate-time period throughout. The redshift is purely the difference in how emitter and receiver project the coordinate-time period onto their respective proper-time axes. This is the McGucken-framework dissolution of the "photon-loses-energy" intuition: the photon's $x_4$-stationary character (Lemma 7.2.3.1 case (ii)) is preserved along the null geodesic; the frequencies seen by emitter and receiver differ because their respective four-budget partitions differ at their respective gravitational potentials. $\square$

**Conclusion of the Geometric Channel derivation.** GR T14 along the Geometric Channel reads the gravitational redshift as the structural consequence of the budget partition consumed by binding at lower potential: the photon climbs out of the potential well with constant *coordinate-time* frequency, but the receiver's proper-time clock runs faster than the emitter's because less binding-consumption occurs at higher altitude, so the receiver counts fewer wave crests per second of its proper time. The redshift is the algebraic record of the differential budget consumption at the two events.

## 12.1.4 structural disjointness audit of GR T14

**Proposition 12.1.4 (Dual-Channel Disjointness on GR T14).** Let $\Pi_A$ be the Algebraic Channel derivation of §12.1.2 and $\Pi_B$ the Geometric Channel derivation of §12.1.3. The intermediate-machinery sets are
