The gravitational chain closes at GR T24 without remainder.

# 17.7 Comparative Context: $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the Common Atom of Spacetime and Quantum Mechanics

The McGucken framework's central structural claim --- that the Schrödinger equation and the Einstein field equations are the same equation in different sectors --- is not an isolated assertion. It sits at the end of a century of foundational-physics work in which the deepest minds of the field have *predicted* such a unification, *partially achieved* it in restricted settings, or *argued for its inevitability* on structural grounds. The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the physical principle that the lineage has been pointing toward without naming. This section places the framework in that lineage, both to honour the structural debt to Sakharov, Wheeler, Jacobson, Verlinde, Padmanabhan, Penrose, and Schrödinger, and to clarify the specific structural feature that distinguishes $dx_4/dt = ic$ from each precursor programme.

The remarkable structural observation that makes the framework hard to *un*-see, once seen, is the following: the integrated form $x_4 = ict$ of the McGucken Principle is *literally* the Lorentzian-signature contribution to the spacetime metric. Substitute $x_4 = ict$ into the Euclidean four-coordinate quadratic form $d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2$ and Lorentzian signature appears immediately as $d\ell^2 = dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 - c^2 dt^2$. The Minkowski metric is the integrated kinematic shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, with no auxiliary postulate required. Now look at the Schrödinger equation
$$i\hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \psi + V \psi.$$
The imaginary unit $i$ appears on the left exactly as it appears in $dx_4/dt = ic$. The structure of the equation is also the same: *first derivative with respect to $t$ on the left, second derivative with respect to space on the right*. The McGucken Principle states that the fourth dimension is advancing invariantly at the rate $ic$ at every event. The Schrödinger equation states that when a matter wavefunction undergoes change with respect to $t$ --- where $t$ is the scalar parameter tracking the shadows of $x_4$'s invariant advancement on our clocks --- the wavefunction undergoes a second-derivative variation in the spatial dimensions whose magnitude is proportional to the matter's energy. *Time-advance on the left is spatial-acceleration on the right*. Once $dx_4/dt = ic$ is read as the foundational principle, the Schrödinger equation reads as its matter-sector projection: a particle's quantum-mechanical wavefunction phase advances in $x_4$ at the rate set by the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, with the spatial second derivative on the right encoding how that phase advance projects into the three spatial dimensions through the deformable spatial geometry.

The same structural reading recovers special relativity. The Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (Theorem GR T1 of Chapter 5) asserts that every massive particle has a fixed four-budget of magnitude $c$, distributed between the $x_4$-direction and the three spatial directions. When a particle's orientation rotates more into the moving fourth dimension --- when it spends more of its four-budget on $x_4$-advance --- it spends less on spatial motion, and conversely: a particle that spends more of its budget on spatial motion (high $v$, high $\gamma$) spends less on $x_4$-advance, with the proper-time advance slowing by the factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ that gives ordinary special-relativistic time dilation. *Every change in a particle's relationship with the fourth moving dimension is a change in its spatial velocity.* This is the same structural relationship that appears in the Schrödinger equation as the first-derivative-in-$t$ ↔ second-derivative-in-space coupling, now read at the four-velocity level rather than the wavefunction level. The two readings agree because they are projections of the same principle onto the two sectors.

The historical predecessors of this unification programme are extensive, and a fair scholarly treatment must acknowledge each. Subsections §17.7.1--§17.7.9 below place each precursor in its historical position and identify the precise structural overlap with, and difference from, the McGucken Principle. The closing subsection §17.7.10 records the specific structural feature that distinguishes $dx_4/dt = ic$ from every predecessor: the *forty-seven theorems forced from a single principle*.

## 17.7.1 Sakharov 1967: induced gravity

Andrei Sakharov's 1967 paper *Vacuum Quantum Fluctuations in Curved Space and the Theory of Gravitation* (Doklady Akademii Nauk SSSR 177, 70--71; English translation Soviet Physics Doklady 12, 1040--1041) is the original modern statement that gravity may not be a fundamental field but rather an *emergent phenomenon induced by the matter sector*. The 1967 paper is a three-page note containing four formulas, and is among the most-cited brief notes in the history of theoretical physics. Sakharov's central claim, in his own words, is that there is a *"metrical elasticity"* of space, with the metric responding to matter content rather than being an independent dynamical entity. The metrical-elasticity interpretation places gravity in the same structural category as continuum hydrodynamics or solid-state elasticity: a macroscopic-emergent phenomenon rather than a fundamental interaction.

The mechanism Sakharov proposes runs along a single direction: matter is fundamental, gravity is emergent. The Einstein--Hilbert action is *induced* by quantum-field-theoretic loop corrections from matter fields propagating on a curved background. The induced Newton constant is set by the ultraviolet cutoff of the matter sector, with the cutoff identified at the Planck scale by consistency. Visser's 2002 modern review *Sakharov's Induced Gravity: A Modern Perspective* (Modern Physics Letters A 17, 977--991, arXiv:gr-qc/0204062) summarises the structural content of the framework: gravity emerges from quantum field theory in roughly the same sense that hydrodynamics or continuum elasticity emerges from molecular physics. The geometry is assumed as a classical background; only the matter sector is quantised; the gravitational dynamics are the loop-induced effective action of the matter sector.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Sakharov and the McGucken framework agree that gravity is not a fundamental quantum field at the same level as the other interactions. Both conclude that the metric responds to matter content rather than being an independent dynamical entity. Sakharov's "metrical elasticity" is structurally analogous to the McGucken framework's reading of the spatial metric $g_{ij}$ as the *deformable sector* of the manifold $M_G$ (Definition 5 of §1.4: the invariant/deformable split), with the deformable spatial sector responding to matter content while the temporal-sector rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ remains gravity-rigid by GR T2 (the McGucken-Invariance Lemma).

*Structural difference.* Sakharov's induced gravity has matter as primary and gravity as emergent; the McGucken framework has *neither as primary* --- both descend from $dx_4/dt = ic$ as parallel chains. Sakharov requires quantum field theory on a curved background as a *pre-existing* structure; the McGucken framework derives the curved background from the principle. Sakharov supplies no derivation of the matter sector --- the standard Dirac--von Neumann postulates of quantum mechanics remain independent inputs; the McGucken framework derives the matter sector's foundational structures (QM T1--QM T23 of the companion derivation [2]) from the same principle that produces gravity. Sakharov's framework also presumes a Lorentzian-manifold structure; the McGucken framework derives Lorentzian signature from $x_4 = ict$ on the Euclidean four-coordinate line element.

## 17.7.2 Wheeler 1962--1990: geometrodynamics, "mass without mass," "it from bit"

The McGucken framework's intellectual debt to John Archibald Wheeler is structural and personal. Wheeler's lifelong programme of *geometrodynamics* (1962, *Geometrodynamics*, Academic Press) aimed at deriving "mass without mass, charge without charge, field without field" --- every physical entity reduced to pure geometry of the spacetime manifold. Wheeler's geons (1955), wormholes (1957), and quantum-foam picture (1957--1968) are the foundational moves of the programme. The closing line of *Gravitation* (Misner, Thorne, Wheeler 1973) is the prediction that motivates the present chapter:

> "Someday surely we will see the principle underlying existence as so simple, so beautiful, so compelling that we will all say to each other, 'How could we all have been so stupid for so long.'"

Wheeler's later programme, articulated in *Information, Physics, Quantum: The Search for Links* (1989, Proc. 3rd Int. Symp. Foundations of Quantum Mechanics, Tokyo) and the *It-from-bit* lectures (1990), located the foundational principle in *information* rather than geometry: every "it" derives from binary yes/no measurement outcomes, with quantum mechanics and gravity descending together from an information-theoretic substrate.

The structural prediction is unambiguous: *quantum mechanics and general relativity descend from a single deeper principle*. Wheeler did not supply the principle. He supplied the prediction, the conceptual machinery (geons, foam, information), and the conviction. The McGucken framework supplies the principle ---  $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- that Wheeler predicted must exist.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Wheeler's geometrodynamic prediction is structurally identical to the framework's claim: one principle, both sectors. Wheeler's "mass without mass" is recovered as Definition 5.3.2 of this book: inertial mass is the four-momentum invested in $x_4$-advance, not a primitive number a particle has but a geometric quantity descended from the universal expansion. Wheeler's "field without field" is recovered as GR T19 (No-Graviton Theorem): there is no gravitational field as a quantum-amplitude entity; gravity is the geometric content of $x_4$-propagation through three-spatial curvature. Wheeler's "it from bit" is the information-theoretic projection of $dx_4/dt = ic$ onto the measurement sector --- the framework recovers the standard quantum-mechanical measurement formalism via the McGucken Sphere projection (QM T19 of the companion derivation).

*Structural difference.* Wheeler predicted that the principle would be *geometric*; the McGucken framework confirms it is geometric (the rate of $x_4$-advance) but adds the differential-operator content $dx_4/dt$ that Wheeler did not articulate. Wheeler's late programme located the principle in information; the McGucken framework locates it in the active expansion of the fourth dimension and recovers information-theoretic content (the Born rule, measurement collapse, Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as bit-counting) as derived consequences.

## 17.7.3 Jacobson 1995: the Einstein equation as a thermodynamic equation of state

Ted Jacobson's 1995 paper *Thermodynamics of Spacetime: The Einstein Equation of State* (Physical Review Letters 75, 1260--1263) is the most-cited derivation of the Einstein field equations from a single thermodynamic principle. Jacobson's central thesis, stated in the abstract of the 1995 paper, is that the Einstein equation can be derived from the proportionality of entropy and horizon area combined with the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T \, dS$ connecting heat, entropy, and temperature. The proof structure requires that the relation hold for all local Rindler causal horizons through every spacetime point, with $\delta Q$ identified as the energy flux and $T$ identified as the Unruh temperature seen by an accelerated observer just inside the horizon. Jacobson's structural conclusion is unambiguous: in his words, the Einstein equation is *an equation of state*. The closing perspective of the 1995 abstract is striking: Jacobson suggests it may be no more appropriate to canonically quantise the Einstein equation than to quantise the wave equation for sound in air.

The technical content of Jacobson's derivation runs as follows. For a small spacelike 2-surface element $P$ through a spacetime point $p$, with past-directed null normal congruence of vanishing expansion and shear at $p$, the past horizon $H$ of $P$ defines the *local Rindler horizon*. The Unruh temperature seen by an observer hovering just inside $H$ is $T = \hbar \kappa / 2\pi$, where $\kappa$ is the acceleration of the Killing-orbit on which the boost Killing vector $\chi^a$ has unit norm. The heat flux through $H$ is $\delta Q = -\kappa \int_H \lambda T_{ab} k^a k^b \, d\lambda \, dA$, where $k^a$ is the null tangent and $\lambda$ the affine parameter. The entropy variation is $dS = \eta \, \delta A$ for a dimensional constant $\eta$ (later identified with the inverse Planck length squared), with $\delta A = -\int_H \lambda R_{ab} k^a k^b \, d\lambda \, dA$ obtained from the Raychaudhuri equation $d\theta/d\lambda = -\theta^2/2 - \sigma^2 - R_{ab} k^a k^b$ at $p$ where $\theta$ and $\sigma$ vanish. Requiring $\delta Q = T \, dS$ for all null directions $k^a$ at every spacetime point forces
$$T_{ab} k^a k^b \;=\; \frac{\hbar \eta}{2\pi} R_{ab} k^a k^b \quad \text{for all null } k^a,$$
which by the contracted Bianchi identity and local energy-momentum conservation yields the Einstein equation
$$R_{ab} - \tfrac{1}{2} R g_{ab} + \Lambda g_{ab} \;=\; \frac{2\pi}{\hbar \eta} T_{ab}.$$
The Newton constant is identified as $G = (4 \hbar \eta)^{-1}$; the cosmological constant remains an undetermined integration constant.

The result: the Einstein equations are an *equation of state*, not a fundamental dynamical equation. Gravity is the thermodynamic response of microscopic horizon degrees of freedom.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Jacobson's derivation is the structural template the McGucken framework generalises. Both programmes derive the Einstein field equations from a deeper principle rather than postulating them; both identify the deeper principle as operating *at every event* of spacetime (Jacobson's local Rindler horizons through each point; the McGucken Principle's universal $x_4$-expansion rate at every event); both produce the equivalence principle as a structural consequence rather than an independent postulate. Jacobson's interpretation of the Einstein equation as an equation of state agrees structurally with the McGucken framework's reading of $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ as a theorem (GR T11 of Chapter 10) rather than a foundational dynamical equation. Jacobson's suggestion that the Einstein equation should not be canonically quantised, formulated by analogy to the wave equation for sound in air, is in agreement with the McGucken framework's GR T19 (No-Graviton Theorem) of Chapter 14: gravity is not the kind of object that admits a quantum amplitude, and the canonical-quantisation programme of the standard treatment is structurally misdirected.

*Structural difference.* Jacobson's principle is thermodynamic (Clausius relation plus horizon entropy); the McGucken principle is kinematic ($dx_4/dt = ic$). Jacobson's principle derives GR but not QM: the canonical commutation relation $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$ does not descend from the Clausius relation, and the Schrödinger equation must be assumed separately. The McGucken Principle derives *both* GR and QM from the same single statement; the Clausius relation itself is a downstream theorem (Theorem GR T22 of the gravitational chain, by way of the McGucken Sphere's horizon-area scaling). Jacobson's programme is structurally a *subset* of the McGucken framework: the thermodynamic statement of GR is recoverable from $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the additional benefit that the matter-sector content is also recoverable from the same principle. Jacobson also requires the existence of local equilibrium conditions for his derivation; the McGucken framework imposes no equilibrium assumption, deriving the Einstein equations through Lovelock's theorem on $M_G$ directly.

## 17.7.4 Verlinde 2011: entropic gravity

Erik Verlinde's 2011 paper *On the Origin of Gravity and the Laws of Newton* (JHEP 04, 029) extends the Jacobson framework into Newtonian gravity. Verlinde argues that the gravitational force is *entropic*: gravity is the macroscopic effect of information being moved on holographic screens, with Newton's $F = ma$ recovered as the leading-order entropic-force expression. The framework recovers the equivalence principle, the inverse-square law, and Einstein's equations in the relativistic limit.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Both programmes treat gravity as not-fundamental: Verlinde has gravity as entropic, the McGucken framework has gravity as geometric-from-$dx_4/dt = ic$. Both locate the gravitational content in information distributed on horizons. The Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as bit-counting on the McGucken Sphere (Chapter 15, GR T20) is the same structural identification Verlinde uses for holographic screens.

*Structural difference.* Verlinde's principle is informational-entropic; the McGucken principle is geometric-kinematic. Verlinde inherits standard quantum mechanics as an external input; the McGucken framework derives QM from the same principle. Verlinde's derivation produces gravitational dynamics but does not produce the Schrödinger equation or the canonical commutation relation; the McGucken framework produces all three.

## 17.7.5 Padmanabhan 2002--2015: gravity as the thermodynamics of horizons

T. Padmanabhan's three-decade programme (*Gravitation: Foundations and Frontiers*, Cambridge 2010; *Lessons from Classical Gravity about the Quantum Structure of Spacetime*, J. Phys. Conf. Ser. 306, 012001, 2011; *Thermodynamical Aspects of Gravity*, Rep. Prog. Phys. 73, 046901, 2010) extends Jacobson's insight into the most-developed of the "GR is not fundamental" programmes. Padmanabhan derives the Einstein equations, the Lanczos--Lovelock generalisations, and the cosmological-constant content from the thermodynamics of microscopic horizon degrees of freedom, with the gravitational action interpreted as the action of these degrees of freedom on null surfaces.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Padmanabhan's framework is structurally the same as Jacobson's, extended to higher-curvature corrections and cosmology. Both Padmanabhan and the McGucken framework agree that the Einstein equations are not fundamental; both agree the cosmological constant has a thermodynamic-horizon interpretation rather than a fundamental-vacuum-energy interpretation; both locate the gravitational content at the level of horizon-degrees-of-freedom.

*Structural difference.* Padmanabhan's microscopic degrees of freedom are postulated (the holographic-degrees-of-freedom of horizon surfaces) without derivation from a deeper principle. The McGucken framework supplies the deeper principle: the microscopic degrees of freedom are the $x_4$-stationary modes on the McGucken Sphere, and the Sphere itself is the geometric atom forced by $dx_4/dt = ic$. Padmanabhan derives GR; the McGucken framework derives GR *and* QM from the same principle.

## 17.7.6 Penrose 1967--2004: twistor theory

Roger Penrose's twistor programme, beginning with the 1967 paper *Twistor Algebra* (J. Math. Phys. 8, 345--366) and developed through *Spinors and Space-Time* (Penrose--Rindler 1984, 1986) and *The Road to Reality* (Knopf 2004), aims at deriving both quantum mechanics and general relativity from a single mathematical structure: the twistor space $\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{C}^4$ (or its projective version $\mathbb{P}\mathbb{T} = \mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}^3$). The conformal structure of four-dimensional spacetime is encoded in the incidence relations of twistor space; massless fields are described by holomorphic functions on twistor space; the Penrose transform recovers solutions of zero-rest-mass field equations on Minkowski space from cohomology classes on projective twistor space.

The twistor programme's central technical achievement is the BCFW recursion (Britto--Cachazo--Feng--Witten 2005) and the amplituhedron (Arkani-Hamed--Trnka 2014), which compute scattering amplitudes in $\mathcal{N} = 4$ supersymmetric Yang--Mills theory through purely twistorial geometric objects without recourse to the spacetime Lagrangian or Feynman diagrams. The structural prediction: the same is possible for general relativity, with gravity reducible to twistor structures.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* The twistor programme is the closest in *philosophy* to the McGucken framework: both aim at deriving both sectors from a single mathematical-geometric structure. Penrose's projective-twistor-space $\mathbb{P}\mathbb{T}$ is structurally a complex-projective version of what the McGucken Sphere is at every event. The Penrose-transform recovery of zero-rest-mass solutions is structurally the same kind of operation the framework's wavefront-functor $p \mapsto M^+_p(\cdot)$ performs on each event of $M_G$. The $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation) machinery of the framework's gravitational chain is structurally the framework's analogue of Penrose's twistor side.

*Structural difference.* The twistor programme has not produced a derivation of the Einstein field equations from twistor structures, despite five decades of attempts. The twistor formalism works at the *massless* sector (zero-rest-mass fields, gauge interactions in $\mathcal{N} = 4$ SYM) but the massive sector and the Lorentzian-signature gravity have remained outside its reach. The McGucken framework supplies the missing massive-sector content via the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ and the rest-mass identification $E_0 = mc^2$ as energy of pure $x_4$-advance; the framework's massive-sector content reads naturally on twistor space as the constraint $P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$, but the McGucken framework derives this constraint from the principle rather than imposing it on the twistor side. The twistor programme is structurally a *partial achievement* of what $dx_4/dt = ic$ provides: it reaches the right kind of structure (a complex-geometric object underlying both sectors) but does not arrive at the principle that forces the structure to exist.

## 17.7.7 Schrödinger and Einstein 1944--1947: the affine field theories

Erwin Schrödinger's collaboration with Albert Einstein on affine-connection unified field theories in 1944--1947 is the historical episode that most resembles, in *intent*, what the McGucken framework accomplishes. Both physicists, having given physics their respective foundational equations, devoted their late careers to deriving each other's equations from a single deeper structure. Schrödinger's *Space-Time Structure* (Cambridge 1950) records his attempt to derive both quantum-mechanical and gravitational content from a unified affine connection on spacetime. Einstein's 1925, 1928, and 1945 papers on teleparallel and asymmetric metric structures pursue the same goal.

Both programmes failed. Schrödinger's affine theory did not produce quantum mechanics from gravity; Einstein's unified-field theories did not produce the Standard Model interactions or unify with quantum mechanics. The historical episode is recorded with care in the contemporary literature (Sauer 2014, *Einstein's Unified Field Theory Programme*, in *The Cambridge Companion to Einstein*).

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* Schrödinger and Einstein's *intent* is structurally identical to the McGucken framework's: derive both QM and GR from a single deeper principle. The historical episode demonstrates that the unification programme is a century-old endeavour pursued by the very name-bearers of the equations the framework now derives.

*Structural difference.* Schrödinger and Einstein sought the unifying structure in *affine-connection geometry* (asymmetric metrics, teleparallel connections, projective extensions of GR); the McGucken framework finds it in the *kinematic principle* $dx_4/dt = ic$. Schrödinger and Einstein assumed both QM and GR as given and tried to find a common geometric superstructure containing both as limits; the McGucken framework derives both from a principle that is simpler than either equation. The historical lesson: the affine route does not work. The kinematic route, by way of $dx_4/dt = ic$, does.

## 17.7.8 Maldacena 1997 / AdS/CFT: the holographic principle

Juan Maldacena's 1997 paper *The Large $N$ Limit of Superconformal Field Theories and Supergravity* (Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2, 231--252) established the AdS/CFT correspondence: quantum gravity in anti-de-Sitter space of dimension $d + 1$ is dual to a conformal field theory on the boundary, with the two descriptions encoding the *same physics*. Witten's 1998 paper *Anti-De Sitter Space and Holography* (Adv. Theor. Math. Phys. 2, 253--291) developed the dictionary in detail. The result is the strongest living statement that quantum mechanics and gravity are the same physics differently parameterised.

*Structural overlap with $dx_4/dt = ic$.* AdS/CFT and the McGucken framework agree on the central structural claim: QM and GR are not separate theories but two readings of the same underlying physics. Both programmes identify a *dual structure* on which the two sectors are projections of one substrate. The framework's $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel (algebraic-symmetry) and the Geometric Channel (geometric-propagation) decomposition of every theorem is structurally analogous to the boundary-conformal field theory and bulk-gravity descriptions in AdS/CFT.

*Structural difference.* AdS/CFT is a duality *between* two pre-existing theories: a quantum field theory on the boundary and a gravity theory in the bulk. Both theories are assumed as inputs; the correspondence is the statement that they are equivalent. The McGucken framework derives both sides of the duality from a single principle: $dx_4/dt = ic$ produces the matter-sector content vian Algebraic Channel and the geometric-sector content via the Geometric Channel as theorems, with no asymptotic-background restriction (AdS/CFT requires asymptotically-AdS backgrounds; the McGucken framework operates on any $M_G$). The framework's *Holographic Principle and AdS/CFT* derivation (companion paper [12]) recovers AdS/CFT as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ rather than as an independent input. AdS/CFT is the strongest precursor in the lineage --- the closest in spirit to the framework's central claim --- and it is the precursor that the McGucken framework most directly *generalises*: AdS/CFT is a special case of the dual-channel structure that the McGucken Principle produces.

## 17.7.9 Recent attempts: Duan 2016, the Schrödinger--Newton equation, Bianchi-I correspondences

Several recent papers have attempted to identify exact equation-level correspondences between specific limits of GR and QM:

**Duan 2016** (*A Quantum Gravity Tensor Equation Formally Integrating General Relativity with Quantum Mechanics*, arXiv:1606.02935) proposes a kinetic-entropy-tensor unification in which a single tensor equation reduces to the Schrödinger equation in the $N = 1$ limit and to the Einstein field equations in the large-$N$ limit. The structural intuition --- one equation with two limits --- is closely related to the McGucken framework's dual-channel structure; the proposed unifying tensor is different ($\Sigma^{\mu\nu}$ as a kinetic-entropy tensor) and the principle is not articulated.

**Schrödinger--Newton equation** (Diósi 1984; Penrose 1996, 1998; Bahrami--Großardt--Donadi--Bassi 2014) couples a non-relativistic quantum wavefunction to its self-generated Newtonian gravitational potential through the semi-classical Einstein equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G \langle \hat T_{\mu\nu} \rangle$. The Schrödinger--Newton equation is *exactly* the matter-sector dynamics that the McGucken framework's Penrose resolution (Theorem 14.6.4) identifies as the correct formalism: gravity classical and sourced by matter expectation values, matter quantum-mechanical and superposing normally. The McGucken framework supplies the *structural justification* for semiclassical gravity that the Schrödinger--Newton literature had been waiting for.

**Bianchi-I scalar-field correspondences** (arXiv:0711.3916) construct exact correspondences between specific FLRW field equations and time-independent linear Schrödinger equations: solutions of one map onto solutions of the other through an explicit transformation. The correspondence is technical and restricted to Bianchi-I cosmology, but its existence demonstrates that the gravitational and quantum-mechanical equations *are* convertible into each other in specific reductions --- a partial achievement of what $dx_4/dt = ic$ accomplishes globally.

## 17.7.10 The structural distinction: forty-seven theorems forced from one principle

Each of the precursor programmes catalogued in §§17.7.1--17.7.9 achieves *part* of what the McGucken framework achieves. Sakharov derives gravity from quantum matter; Wheeler predicts the unifying principle without supplying it; Jacobson derives the Einstein equations from thermodynamics; Verlinde extends the thermodynamic derivation to Newtonian gravity; Padmanabhan develops the horizon-thermodynamic programme to its most-developed form; Penrose's twistor programme supplies the right kind of underlying mathematical structure but does not derive Lorentzian gravity from it; Schrödinger and Einstein's affine theories sought the unification by the wrong route; AdS/CFT supplies the strongest extant statement of QM--GR duality but requires both theories as inputs and operates only on asymptotically-AdS backgrounds.

The McGucken framework's structural distinction from every precursor is the *count*. From $dx_4/dt = ic$, this book derives 24 foundational theorems of general relativity (GR T1--GR T24); the companion derivation [2] derives 23 foundational theorems of quantum mechanics (QM T1--QM T23). *Forty-seven theorems, all forced from one principle*. No precursor programme has achieved this count. Sakharov derives the Einstein--Hilbert action (one theorem) from quantum-matter loop corrections (six postulates). Jacobson derives the Einstein equations (one theorem) from the Clausius relation (one principle). Verlinde derives Newtonian gravity and the equivalence principle (two theorems) from the entropic-force expression (one principle). Padmanabhan derives the Einstein equations and Lanczos--Lovelock generalisations (a few theorems) from horizon-degrees-of-freedom thermodynamics (one principle plus auxiliary degrees-of-freedom postulates). The twistor programme derives massless-field structure (zero gravitational theorems by way of strict derivation) from twistor space (one principle plus standard quantum field theory postulates). AdS/CFT establishes a duality (one statement) between two pre-existing theories (ten postulates total).

The McGucken framework's ratio of theorems-to-postulates is *47-to-1*. The standard programme's ratio is *0-to-10*. The over-determination structure is the structural feature that distinguishes $dx_4/dt = ic$ from every precursor and makes the framework falsifiable in a way that no precursor is: forty-seven independent falsification opportunities against one principle, against the standard programme's structural insulation of each postulate from the others.

## 17.7.11 The Lorentzian metric and the Schrödinger equation as theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$

The closing piece of this comparative-context chapter is the rigorous statement of the central structural observation that motivates the entire McGucken programme: the Lorentzian spacetime metric of general relativity and the Schrödinger equation of quantum mechanics are *both* theorems of $dx_4/dt = ic$, obtained as projections of the principle onto the geometric sector and the matter-quantum sector respectively.

### 17.7.11.1 The Lorentzian metric as the integrated kinematic shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$

**Theorem 17.7.11.1 (Lorentzian-signature metric from $dx_4/dt = ic$).** Let the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ hold on $M_G$, with the integrated form $x_4 = ict$ along any worldline at spatial rest with origin $x_4(0) = 0$. Then the four-dimensional spacetime line element, evaluated on the constraint surface defined by the principle, is the Minkowski line element of signature $(-, +, +, +)$:
$$ds^2 \;=\; -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2. \tag{17.7.11.1}$$

*Proof.* The four-coordinate space $(x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$ on $M_G$ carries the natural Euclidean line element
$$d\ell^2 \;=\; dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + dx_4^2. \tag{17.7.11.2}$$
Substituting the integrated form $x_4 = ict$ of the McGucken Principle and computing the differential: $dx_4 = ic \, dt$, hence $dx_4^2 = (ic\, dt)^2 = i^2 c^2 \, dt^2 = -c^2 \, dt^2$. The Euclidean line element (17.7.11.2) becomes
$$d\ell^2 \;=\; dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2 + (ic \, dt)^2 \;=\; -c^2 \, dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$
which is the Minkowski line element (17.7.11.1) of signature $(-, +, +, +)$. $\square$

**Remark 17.7.11.2 (the source of Lorentzian signature).** The minus sign in the temporal component of the metric is *not* a separate postulate of general relativity. It is the algebraic consequence of $i^2 = -1$, which is in turn the algebraic consequence of the *perpendicularity of the fourth axis $x_4$ to the three spatial axes* --- the foundational physical content of $dx_4/dt = ic$. Theorem 17.7.11.1 makes this transparent: the substitution $x_4 = ict$ into the Euclidean line element on the four-coordinate space converts that line element into the Minkowski line element, with Lorentzian signature emerging as a *theorem* rather than a postulate. The standard presentation of general relativity treats the $(-, +, +, +)$ signature as a foundational input; the McGucken framework derives it.

### 17.7.11.2 The Schrödinger equation as the non-relativistic limit of the Compton-frequency phase advance

The Schrödinger equation reads
$$i \hbar \frac{\partial \psi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \psi + V(\vec x) \psi. \tag{17.7.11.3}$$
The structure of the equation deserves close reading. On the left appears the imaginary unit $i$ --- the same algebraic marker that appears in $dx_4/dt = ic$ as the record of $x_4$'s perpendicularity to the spatial directions. On the left also appears a *first* derivative with respect to $t$ --- the scalar parameter that, in the McGucken framework, tracks the shadows of $x_4$'s invariant advancement on observers' clocks and watches. On the right appears a *second* derivative with respect to spatial position ($\nabla^2$), giving the spatial second-derivative variation of the wavefunction whose magnitude is set by the matter's energy. The standard textbook derivation of (17.7.11.3) treats it as a foundational postulate; the McGucken framework derives it as a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ through the route reproduced here.

**Theorem 17.7.11.3 (Schrödinger equation from $dx_4/dt = ic$).** Let $\psi(\vec x, t)$ be the wavefunction of a massive particle of inertial mass $m > 0$ on $M_G$, with $dx_4/dt = ic$ holding at every event. Let $\phi(\vec x, t)$ be the slowly-varying envelope of $\psi$ defined by the Compton-frequency phase factorisation
$$\psi(\vec x, t) \;=\; \phi(\vec x, t) \cdot e^{-i \omega_C t} \quad \text{with} \quad \omega_C \;\equiv\; \frac{m c^2}{\hbar} \quad \text{(the Compton frequency)}. \tag{17.7.11.4}$$
Then in the non-relativistic regime $|\vec p| \ll mc$ (equivalently $|i \hbar \partial_t \phi| \ll mc^2 |\phi|$), the envelope $\phi$ satisfies the Schrödinger equation
$$i \hbar \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \phi + V(\vec x) \phi. \tag{17.7.11.5}$$

*Proof.* The relativistic wave equation for a scalar matter wavefunction of mass $m$ is the Klein--Gordon equation,
$$\left[\frac{1}{c^2} \partial_t^2 - \nabla^2 + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2}\right] \psi \;=\; 0. \tag{17.7.11.6}$$
The Klein--Gordon equation is a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ along the Algebraic Channel as Theorem QM T8 of the companion derivation [2], obtained from the constraint-surface pullback of $dx_4/dt = ic$ to the mass-shell hyperboloid $P^\mu P_\mu = -m^2 c^2$ by the standard correspondence $P^\mu \mapsto i\hbar \partial^\mu$. We treat (17.7.11.6) here as established and derive (17.7.11.5) as the non-relativistic limit.

*Step 1: identify the rest-mass phase.* For a particle at spatial rest with $\psi = e^{i k_\mu x^\mu}$ a plane-wave solution of (17.7.11.6) and $\vec k = 0$, the time-frequency satisfies $\omega^2/c^2 - m^2 c^2/\hbar^2 = 0$, hence $\omega = \pm m c^2 / \hbar$. The positive-frequency branch is $\omega = +m c^2/\hbar = \omega_C$, the *Compton frequency*. The plane-wave solution at spatial rest is therefore $\psi_{\text{rest}}(t) = e^{-i \omega_C t}$, which advances in phase at rate $\omega_C$ per unit lab time. This is the *rest-mass phase advance*: a particle at spatial rest in three-space is in phase-motion at the Compton frequency in the $x_4$-direction.

*Step 2: factorise the phase.* For a particle that is non-relativistic but not necessarily at spatial rest, decompose the wavefunction as in (17.7.11.4):
$$\psi(\vec x, t) \;=\; \phi(\vec x, t) \cdot e^{-i \omega_C t}.$$
The factor $e^{-i \omega_C t}$ captures the *fast* phase rotation associated with the rest-mass energy; the envelope $\phi$ captures the *slow* variation associated with the kinetic energy $|\vec p|^2/(2m) \ll mc^2$ and the potential energy $V \ll mc^2$.

*Step 3: substitute and expand.* Compute the time-derivatives of $\psi$:
\begin{align*}
\partial_t \psi &\;=\; (\partial_t \phi) e^{-i\omega_C t} - i \omega_C \phi \, e^{-i\omega_C t} \;=\; \left[(\partial_t \phi) - i \omega_C \phi\right] e^{-i\omega_C t}, \\
\partial_t^2 \psi &\;=\; \left[\partial_t^2 \phi - 2 i \omega_C (\partial_t \phi) - \omega_C^2 \phi\right] e^{-i\omega_C t}.
\end{align*}
Substituting into the Klein--Gordon equation (17.7.11.6) and dividing through by the common factor $e^{-i\omega_C t}$:
$$\frac{1}{c^2}\!\left[\partial_t^2 \phi - 2 i \omega_C \partial_t \phi - \omega_C^2 \phi\right] - \nabla^2 \phi + \frac{m^2 c^2}{\hbar^2} \phi \;=\; 0.$$

*Step 4: cancel the rest-mass terms.* By definition $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$, so $\omega_C^2/c^2 = m^2 c^2 / \hbar^2$. The third and fifth terms cancel exactly:
$$\frac{1}{c^2} \partial_t^2 \phi - \frac{2 i \omega_C}{c^2} \partial_t \phi - \nabla^2 \phi \;=\; 0.$$
Multiplying through by $-\hbar^2/(2m)$ and rearranging:
$$i \hbar \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \phi + \frac{\hbar^2}{2 m c^2} \partial_t^2 \phi. \tag{17.7.11.7}$$

*Step 5: drop the second time-derivative in the non-relativistic regime.* In the non-relativistic regime, the envelope $\phi$ varies slowly compared to the rest-mass scale: $|\hbar \partial_t \phi| \ll mc^2 |\phi|$. Equivalently, $|\hbar \partial_t^2 \phi| \ll mc^2 |\partial_t \phi|$, so the last term of (17.7.11.7) is of order $|\vec p|^2/(mc)^2$ compared to the kinetic term and is negligible at leading order. Dropping it gives the free Schrödinger equation
$$i \hbar \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial t} \;=\; -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m} \nabla^2 \phi.$$
Adding an external potential $V(\vec x)$ by minimal coupling (gauge-invariance theorem QM T16 of [2]) recovers (17.7.11.5). $\square$

**Remark 17.7.11.4 (the physical content of Theorem 17.7.11.3).** The Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ is the rate at which a massive particle's wavefunction phase advances *in $x_4$* per unit lab time. The rest-mass energy $E_0 = m c^2$ is, equivalently (Theorem 5.3.4 of Chapter 5 and Remark 5.3.5), *the energy of pure $x_4$-advance at rate $c$*. The Compton-frequency identification makes this explicit at the wavefunction level: the wavefunction's phase rotates at $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar = E_0/\hbar$, exactly the de-Broglie--Planck--Einstein relation $E = \hbar \omega$ applied to the rest energy.

The structural reading of Theorem 17.7.11.3 is now sharp. The Schrödinger equation's first-derivative-in-$t$ structure on the left is the *slow envelope* of the fast $x_4$-phase rotation at the Compton frequency. The wavefunction's $x_4$-advance, shadowed onto the coordinate-time parameter $t$ that observers' clocks track, produces the first-derivative-in-$t$ structure of (17.7.11.3). The imaginary unit $i$ on the left of the Schrödinger equation is *the same $i$* that appears in $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- the algebraic record of $x_4$'s perpendicularity to the spatial directions, surviving the non-relativistic limit through the Compton-frequency phase factor. The second-derivative-in-space on the right is the spatial gradient of the wavefunction's de-Broglie phase, which projects $x_4$-advance into spatial-direction motion through the matter-sector momentum identification $\vec p = -i\hbar \nabla$.

**Remark 17.7.11.5 (Compton frequencies as sub-harmonics of the Planck mode).** The Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ of a particle of mass $m$ is, in the McGucken framework, the rate at which the particle's wavefunction phase advances in $x_4$ per unit lab time. The companion paper on the constants $c$ and $h$ [MG-Constants] develops the structural reading that every massive particle's Compton frequency is a sub-harmonic of the fundamental Planck-mass mode:
$$\frac{f_C}{f_P} \;=\; \frac{m}{m_P}, \qquad f_C = \frac{mc^2}{h}, \qquad f_P = \frac{m_P c^2}{h}, \qquad \omega_P \;=\; 2\pi f_P \;=\; \frac{m_P c^2}{\hbar} \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{c^5}{\hbar G}}. \tag{17.7.11.4a}$$
The Planck-mass particle $m_P = \sqrt{\hbar c/G} \approx 2.176 \times 10^{-8}$ kg couples to $x_4$ at the Planck frequency $f_P = m_P c^2/h \approx 2.952 \times 10^{42}$ Hz (equivalently the angular Planck frequency $\omega_P = \sqrt{c^5/\hbar G} \approx 1.855 \times 10^{43}$ rad/s), which is the fundamental oscillation frequency of $x_4$'s advance. Every other particle of smaller mass $m < m_P$ couples at a sub-harmonic of this fundamental, with the ratio $m/m_P$ giving the harmonic number. Mass, on this reading, is the ratio of a particle's $x_4$-coupling frequency to the Planck-mode fundamental.
Representative numerics (from [MG-Constants], independently verified): electron $m_e \approx 9.109 \times 10^{-31}$ kg gives $f_C^{(e)} \approx 1.236 \times 10^{20}$ Hz with $m_e/m_P \approx 4.19 \times 10^{-23}$; proton $m_p \approx 1.673 \times 10^{-27}$ kg gives $f_C^{(p)} \approx 2.269 \times 10^{23}$ Hz with $m_p/m_P \approx 7.69 \times 10^{-20}$. Both Compton frequencies are sub-harmonics of $f_P$ by the respective mass ratios. Inertia, on this reading, is the resistance to a change in the distribution of one's four-speed budget between spatial motion and $x_4$-advance --- a more massive particle couples to more quanta of $x_4$-expansion per unit time and resists deflection more strongly.
**Remark 17.7.11.6 (The structural parallel $dx_4/dt = ic$ ↔ $[\hat q, \hat p] = i\hbar$).** The companion paper [MG-Constants] highlights a structural parallel that motivates the McGucken-framework reading of $\hbar$ as the action quantum of $x_4$'s oscillation:
$$\frac{dx_4}{dt} \;=\; ic \qquad \text{and} \qquad [\hat q, \hat p] \;=\; i\hbar. \tag{17.7.11.4b}$$
Both equations place a differential or commutator on the left and an imaginary quantity on the right. Both assert a fundamental asymmetry --- of geometric advance in the first case, of conjugate observables in the second --- whose imaginary character signals something perpendicular to the ordinary spatial structure: the imaginary unit $i$ in both equations records perpendicularity in the precise algebraic sense that multiplication by $i$ rotates by $\pi/2$ in the complex plane. The two equations are structurally cognate, with $c$ playing in the first the role $\hbar$ plays in the second: each is the magnitude of the perpendicular-direction increment, with $c$ a spatial-velocity scale and $\hbar$ an action scale.
The structural parallel is suggestive of a deeper unification, but it is not itself a derivation of $\hbar$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$. The companion paper [MG-Constants] argues that the Planck quantities ($\ell_P, t_P, f_P, m_P$) are the natural oscillation scales of $x_4$, with $\hbar$ identified as the action quantum of one Planck-frequency $x_4$-oscillation. However, this identification is "consistent by construction" (in the paper's own language [MG-Constants §V]) rather than a derivation of $\hbar$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone: the dimensional combination $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ contains both $\hbar$ and $G$ as inputs, neither of which is itself a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ in the present state of the corpus. The Vanquishing paper [20] is equally explicit about this status (§17.7.12.1 above): the action-quantisation step is a postulate, not a theorem.
The derivation of $\hbar$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone --- without the action-quantisation postulate and without external $G$ --- remains an **open problem** of the corpus, as recorded in §17.7.12.5. The structural parallel of (17.7.11.4b) is the present state of the argument: a strong suggestion of a unification not yet closed at the derivation level.
*Theorem 17.7.11.3 is the structural completion of the McGucken framework's central claim.** Theorem 17.7.11.1 established that the Lorentzian metric is the integrated kinematic shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$ on the geometric sector. Theorem 17.7.11.3 establishes that the Schrödinger equation is the slow envelope of the Compton-frequency $x_4$-phase rotation on the matter-quantum sector. *The Lorentzian metric and the Schrödinger equation are two projections of $dx_4/dt = ic$ onto the two sectors of physics that have not yet recognised their common origin.
### 17.7.11.3 The four-velocity budget as the kinematic reading

The same principle has a third reading on the *kinematic* sector, recorded as Theorem GR T1 of Chapter 5: the four-velocity budget identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, equivalently the Lorentzian-signature partition $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 - |d\vec x/d\tau|^2 = c^2$ (with $|dx_4/d\tau| = c\gamma$ the imaginary-component magnitude and $|d\vec x/d\tau| = \gamma v$ the spatial-three magnitude). The kinematic reading expresses what the geometric and matter-quantum readings express in their respective sectors: that the universal four-speed $c$ at every event partitions between $x_4$-advance and spatial advance under the Lorentzian-signature identity $c^2 \gamma^2 - \gamma^2 v^2 = c^2$, with the partition shifting from particle to particle and from event to event.

Whenever a massive object's relationship with $x_4$ --- the fourth moving dimension --- changes, its spatial velocity changes correspondingly. When the object is rotated *more into* the $x_4$-direction (more of its four-budget spent on $x_4$-advance), it spends *less* on spatial motion: at the limit of full $x_4$-advance with zero spatial motion, the object is at spatial rest in the asymptotic frame, with its proper-time clock running at the maximum rate $d\tau/dt = 1$. When the object is rotated *out of* the $x_4$-direction (more of its four-budget spent on spatial motion), it spends *less* on $x_4$-advance: at the limit of zero $x_4$-advance with full spatial motion at $c$, the object is a massless particle propagating on the McGucken Sphere wavefront, with $d\tau/dt = 0$ (no proper-time advance: photons do not experience time). For intermediate cases, the proper-time advance is the standard special-relativistic factor $d\tau/dt = \sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, recovered from the four-budget partition by elementary algebra (Lemma 5.1.3.4 of Chapter 5).

Special relativity, in this reading, is the *kinematic statement of the four-budget partition*. Time dilation is the geometric content of "rotated more into $x_4$ ⇒ less spatial motion ⇒ slower proper-clock advance from the perspective of a non-co-moving observer." Length contraction is the dual statement. The Lorentz transformations of special relativity are the linear isomorphisms of the four-budget partition that preserve the universal four-speed $c$.

### 17.7.11.4 The three readings unified

The Lorentzian metric $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + d\vec x^2$ (geometric sector), the Schrödinger equation $i\hbar \partial_t \phi = \hat H \phi$ (matter-quantum sector), and the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (kinematic sector) are *three readings of one physical principle*. The principle is $dx_4/dt = ic$: the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event. Each sector reads the principle differently:

- *Geometric sector*: integrate to $x_4 = ict$, the integrated shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$,; substitute into the four-dimensional Euclidean line element; obtain the Lorentzian metric. The imaginary unit $i$ encodes perpendicularity of the temporal direction to the spatial directions; the $-c^2 dt^2$ contribution to the line element is $i^2 c^2 dt^2 = -c^2 dt^2$.

- *Matter-quantum sector*: factorise the Klein--Gordon wavefunction as $\psi = \phi \cdot e^{-i\omega_C t}$ at the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$; the slow envelope $\phi$ satisfies the Schrödinger equation in the non-relativistic limit. The imaginary unit $i$ on the left of the Schrödinger equation is the same $i$ of $dx_4/dt = ic$; the first-derivative-in-$t$ structure is the slow envelope of the fast $x_4$-phase rotation at $\omega_C$; the spatial Laplacian on the right is the spatial projection of $x_4$-advance through the momentum identification $\vec p = -i \hbar \nabla$.

- *Kinematic sector*: enforce $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ at every event; the universal four-speed budget partitions into $x_4$-advance and spatial advance, with rotation into $x_4$ producing time dilation and rotation out of $x_4$ producing spatial motion.

The remarkable structural fact, once it has been seen, is hard to un-see. The integrated form $x_4 = ict$ is literally the Lorentzian metric's temporal contribution. The Schrödinger equation's first-derivative-in-$t$ on the left is literally the slow envelope of the $x_4$-phase advance at the Compton frequency. The four-budget identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ is literally the fixed-total allocation of four-speed $c$ between the $x_4$-direction and the three spatial directions. The three equations that the McGucken framework's gravitational chain and quantum chain derive separately --- the Minkowski metric, the Schrödinger equation, and the four-velocity budget --- are three projections of $dx_4/dt = ic$ onto the three sectors of foundational physics: geometric, matter-quantum, and kinematic.

That this principle has been on the page since Minkowski 1908 in the form $x_4 = ict$, but read as a coordinate convention rather than the integrated trace of a physical motion, is the historical accident that the McGucken framework corrects. Once $x_4 = ict$ is read as the integrated kinematic shadow of $dx_4/dt = ic$, the entire foundational structure of twentieth- and twenty-first-century physics --- the Lorentzian metric of relativity, the Schrödinger equation of quantum mechanics, the four-velocity budget of special-relativistic kinematics, and the forty-seven foundational theorems that descend from these in the gravitational and quantum chains --- becomes visible as projections of a single physical principle. *Ergo physics. QED.*

## 17.7.12 Finite one-loop QED vacuum polarisation on the hybrid measure: a fourth structural consequence

The McGucken framework, in addition to closing the QM--GR foundational gap (§17.7.10, §17.7.11), the singularity problem of the Schwarzschild--Kruskal interior (§11.5.4), and the Big Bang singularity (§14.4.7), also addresses the *ultraviolet divergence problem of quantum field theory* --- the standard logarithmic divergence of QED loop integrals that the standard treatment removes by renormalisation. The Vanquishing paper [20] establishes a *finiteness theorem* for the one-loop photon vacuum polarisation under a *hybrid continuous--discrete measure* on spacetime: continuous in the three spatial directions, discrete in the fourth direction $x_4$ at the Planck wavelength $\ell_P$. The QED loop integral is *finite by structure*, not by regularisation, because the integration domain along the $x_4$-conjugate momentum is the finite Brillouin zone of the discrete $x_4$-lattice.

We record this result in the comparative-context chapter because it represents a *fourth structural consequence* of the McGucken framework, parallel to the three sector-projections of §17.7.11: the Lorentzian metric (geometric sector), the Schrödinger equation (matter-quantum sector), the four-velocity budget (kinematic sector), and now the *finite QED loop integrals* (quantum field theory-loop sector). All four follow from the same foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, applied to different sectors at different scales.

### 17.7.12.1 The hybrid measure as Hypothesis 1

**Hypothesis 1 of [20].** The four-dimensional Euclidean spacetime measure relevant to quantum field theory loop calculations, after the McGucken--Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ (Theorem 4 of the Introduction; a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$ via [3]), is
$$d\mu \;=\; dx_1 \, dx_2 \, dx_3 \cdot \ell_P \sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \delta(x_4 - n \ell_P) \, dx_4, \tag{17.7.12.1}$$
with the three spatial directions continuous and the fourth direction a discrete lattice with spacing $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$.
**Audit caveat on Hypothesis 1.** Hypothesis 1 is the load-bearing structural input of the QED finiteness result. The principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ as written contains only $c$, not $\hbar$ or $G$; the dimensional argument that pins the $x_4$-spacing at $\ell_P$ therefore requires *both* $\hbar$ and $G$ as independent inputs. The corpus [11] [17] closes the dimensional argument via a three-step sequence: (i) $dx_4/dt = ic$ fixes $c$ as a substrate-wavelength-per-period ratio $\ell_*/t_*$; (ii) an independent action-quantisation postulate defines $\hbar$ as the substrate's per-tick action quantum (the corpus is *explicit* that step (ii) is a *postulate*, not a theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$); (iii) Schwarzschild self-consistency $r_s = \lambda_*$ at the substrate scale identifies $\ell_* = \ell_P$ with $G$ as a third independent dimensional input. Hypothesis 1 therefore rests on $dx_4/dt = ic$ *plus the action-quantisation postulate plus external $G$*, not on $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone. This is documented openly in [20]; we record it here for transparency. The Hypothesis-1 status is a working hypothesis to be tested by its consequences, not a derived theorem of the McGucken Principle. Deriving Hypothesis 1 from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone is an *open problem* of the framework.

### 17.7.12.2 Theorem: finite one-loop vacuum polarisation under the hybrid measure

The standard one-loop photon vacuum polarisation tensor in QED, after Wick rotation to Euclidean signature, Feynman-parameter combination, and shift $\ell_E = k_E + x q_E$, takes the form
$$\Pi(q_E^2) \;=\; -\frac{8 e^2}{(2\pi)^4} \int_0^1 dx \, x(1-x) \int d^4 \ell_E \, \frac{1}{[\ell_E^2 + \Delta(x)]^2}, \quad \Delta(x) \equiv x(1-x) q_E^2 + m^2. \tag{17.7.12.2}$$
The inner integral is logarithmically divergent in the standard continuum treatment because the integration over $\ell_E^0 \in (-\infty, +\infty)$ is unbounded.

Under the hybrid measure of Hypothesis 1, the $x_4$-direction is a lattice of spacing $\ell_P$. The Fourier conjugate of a discretely-sampled signal of spacing $\ell_P$ is periodic in conjugate-variable with period $2\pi/\ell_P$, and the unique modes are confined to the first Brillouin zone $[-\pi \hbar/\ell_P, +\pi \hbar/\ell_P]$ (with $\hbar$ inserted to make the Brillouin-zone scale $\pi \hbar/\ell_P = \pi m_P c$ visually transparent). The substitution is
$$\int d^4 \ell_E \;\longmapsto\; \int_{-\pi\hbar/\ell_P}^{+\pi\hbar/\ell_P} d\ell_E^0 \int d^3 \boldsymbol{\ell}. \tag{17.7.12.3}$$
The spatial integration remains continuous and unbounded; the $x_4$-conjugate integration is bounded by the Brillouin zone.

**Theorem 17.7.12 (Finite hybrid one-loop QED vacuum polarisation).** Under Hypothesis 1, the inner loop integral of (17.7.12.2) under substitution (17.7.12.3) evaluates to the closed-form expression
$$I_{\text{hyb}}(\Delta) \;\equiv\; \int_{-\pi\hbar/\ell_P}^{+\pi\hbar/\ell_P} d\ell_E^0 \int d^3 \boldsymbol{\ell} \, \frac{1}{[(\ell_E^0)^2 + |\boldsymbol{\ell}|^2 + \Delta]^2} \;=\; 2 \pi^2 \, \mathrm{arcsinh}\!\left(\frac{\pi \hbar/\ell_P}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\right). \tag{17.7.12.4}$$
The integral is finite for all $\Delta > 0$. In the IR regime $\Delta \ll (\pi \hbar/\ell_P)^2$, the result expands as
$$I_{\text{hyb}}(\Delta) \;=\; 2\pi^2 \log\!\left(\frac{2\pi \hbar/\ell_P}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\right) + O\!\left(\frac{\Delta \, \ell_P^2}{\hbar^2}\right). \tag{17.7.12.5}$$

*Proof.* In two steps; both steps are standard one-variable integrals.

*Step 1: Spatial integral.* With $\rho \equiv |\boldsymbol{\ell}|$, $d^3 \boldsymbol{\ell} = 4\pi \rho^2 \, d\rho$, and $a^2 \equiv (\ell_E^0)^2 + \Delta > 0$:
$$\int d^3 \boldsymbol{\ell} \, \frac{1}{[\rho^2 + a^2]^2} \;=\; 4\pi \int_0^\infty \frac{\rho^2 \, d\rho}{(\rho^2 + a^2)^2}.$$
Substituting $\rho = a \tan\theta$, $d\rho = a \sec^2\theta \, d\theta$, $\rho^2 + a^2 = a^2 \sec^2\theta$, $\rho^2 = a^2 \tan^2\theta$:
\begin{align*}
4\pi \int_0^\infty \frac{\rho^2 \, d\rho}{(\rho^2 + a^2)^2} &\;=\; 4\pi \int_0^{\pi/2} \frac{a^2 \tan^2\theta \cdot a \sec^2\theta}{a^4 \sec^4\theta} \, d\theta \\
&\;=\; \frac{4\pi}{a} \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^2\theta \, d\theta \;=\; \frac{4\pi}{a} \cdot \frac{\pi}{4} \;=\; \frac{\pi^2}{a},
\end{align*}
using $\int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^2\theta \, d\theta = \pi/4$. Hence
$$\int d^3 \boldsymbol{\ell} \, \frac{1}{[(\ell_E^0)^2 + |\boldsymbol{\ell}|^2 + \Delta]^2} \;=\; \frac{\pi^2}{\sqrt{(\ell_E^0)^2 + \Delta}}.$$

*Step 2: $x_4$-conjugate integral over the Brillouin zone.* Substituting Step 1 into (17.7.12.4):
$$I_{\text{hyb}}(\Delta) \;=\; \pi^2 \int_{-\pi\hbar/\ell_P}^{+\pi\hbar/\ell_P} \frac{d\ell_E^0}{\sqrt{(\ell_E^0)^2 + \Delta}}.$$
Using the standard antiderivative $\int dk/\sqrt{k^2 + a^2} = \mathrm{arcsinh}(k/a) + C$ and the evenness of the integrand:
$$I_{\text{hyb}}(\Delta) \;=\; \pi^2 \cdot 2 \, \mathrm{arcsinh}\!\left(\frac{\pi \hbar/\ell_P}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\right) \;=\; 2 \pi^2 \, \mathrm{arcsinh}\!\left(\frac{\pi \hbar/\ell_P}{\sqrt{\Delta}}\right),$$
establishing (17.7.12.4). For the IR expansion (17.7.12.5): with $z \equiv \pi \hbar/(\ell_P \sqrt{\Delta}) \gg 1$ in the IR regime, $\mathrm{arcsinh}(z) = \log(z + \sqrt{z^2 + 1}) = \log(2z) + O(1/z^2)$. Substituting gives (17.7.12.5), with the $O(1/z^2)$ error term translating to $O(\Delta \, \ell_P^2/\hbar^2) = O((m/m_P)^2)$ at electron-mass scales. $\square$

**Independent verification.** Both integral evaluations of the proof can be verified symbolically. The substitution $\rho = a \tan\theta$ reduces the spatial integral to $4\pi \int_0^{\pi/2} \sin^2\theta \, d\theta = 4\pi \cdot \pi/4 = \pi^2$, which after the $1/a$ factor gives $\pi^2/a$; the $x_4$-conjugate integral is the standard $\int dk/\sqrt{k^2 + a^2} = \mathrm{arcsinh}(k/a)$ antiderivative. The asymptotic expansion of $\mathrm{arcsinh}(z) = \log(2z) + O(1/z^2)$ at large $z$ is in Abramowitz \& Stegun §4.6 (NIST DLMF §4.37). No step of the proof requires anything beyond textbook integration methods.

### 17.7.12.3 Recovery of the standard $\alpha/(3\pi)$ running coupling

The physically observable quantity is the renormalised polarisation $\Pi_R(q^2) \equiv \Pi(q^2) - \Pi(0)$. Substituting (17.7.12.5) into the full polarisation integral (17.7.12.2): the IR expansion gives
$$I_{\text{hyb}}(\Delta) \;=\; 2\pi^2 \log(2\pi\hbar/\ell_P) - \pi^2 \log \Delta + O(\Delta \ell_P^2/\hbar^2).$$
The constant term $2\pi^2 \log(2\pi\hbar/\ell_P)$ is independent of $\Delta$ (hence of $q^2$) and cancels exactly in the subtraction $\Pi(q^2) - \Pi(0)$. The $\Delta$-dependent piece carries coefficient $-\pi^2$. With prefactor $-8e^2/(2\pi)^4 = -e^2/(2\pi^4)$:
$$\Pi_R(q_E^2) \;=\; -\frac{e^2}{2\pi^4} \cdot (-\pi^2) \int_0^1 dx \, x(1-x) [\log \Delta(x) - \log m^2] + O(q^2/m_P^2)$$
$$\;=\; \frac{e^2}{2\pi^2} \int_0^1 dx \, x(1-x) \log \frac{\Delta(x)}{m^2} + O(q^2/m_P^2). \tag{17.7.12.6}$$
For $q_E^2 \gg m^2$, $\Delta(x) \approx x(1-x) q_E^2$, so $\log[\Delta(x)/m^2] = \log[x(1-x)] + \log(q_E^2/m^2)$. The first term contributes a $q^2$-independent constant absorbed into the coupling at scale $m$; the $q^2$-dependent term gives, with $\int_0^1 x(1-x) dx = 1/6$ and $e^2 = 4\pi\alpha$:
$$\Pi_R(q_E^2) \;\xrightarrow[q_E^2 \gg m^2]{}\; \frac{e^2}{2\pi^2} \cdot \frac{1}{6} \log \frac{q_E^2}{m^2} \;=\; \frac{\alpha}{3\pi} \log\!\frac{q_E^2}{m^2} + O\!\left(\frac{q_E^2}{m_P^2}\right). \tag{17.7.12.7}$$
This is the *standard one-loop running of the QED coupling* (Peskin \& Schroeder Chapter 7, Schwinger 1948). It emerges from the hybrid measure with *Planck-suppressed corrections of order $(m/m_P)^2 \sim 10^{-44}$* at the electron mass scale, far beyond present and foreseeable experimental reach.

### 17.7.12.4 The structural difference from renormalisation

The standard treatment regards the inner integral of (17.7.12.2) as logarithmically divergent and removes the divergence by introducing a regulator (dimensional, Pauli--Villars, or hard cutoff), absorbing the divergent part into a counterterm, and extracting the finite physical prediction. The McGucken-framework hybrid measure does *not* regulate a divergent integral. The integral in (17.7.12.4) is finite *from the start*, because the integration domain along $\ell_E^0$ was always confined to the Brillouin zone $[-\pi\hbar/\ell_P, +\pi\hbar/\ell_P]$. *There is no divergence to subtract.* The constant logarithmic term that corresponds to the standard divergence in the limit $\ell_P \to 0$ is, in the hybrid measure, a *finite contribution* to the bare coupling, which is itself a finite quantity.

This is a *structural* difference, not a numerical one: at scales $q^2 \ll m_P^2$, the predicted $\Pi_R(q^2)$ is identical to the standard QED result to corrections of order $(m/m_P)^2$. The framework therefore reproduces the precision of standard QED (which agrees with experiment to twelve digits in $g-2$ via standard renormalisation) without claiming any deviation observable in current or foreseeable experiments. What changes is the *foundational reading*: the UV divergence is not present in the bare theory; the renormalisation procedure of the standard formulation is recovered as a *finite computation* under the hybrid measure, not as a regularisation-and-subtraction.

**The open problem.** A derivation of Hypothesis 1 from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone --- without the action-quantisation postulate and without external $G$ --- would promote the quantum field theory-loop finiteness to a *full theorem* of the McGucken Principle, on the same footing as the first three sectors. ## 17.7.13 The cosmological-constant reading: a fifth structural consequence

The Constants paper [MG-Constants] supplies a fifth structural consequence of $dx_4/dt = ic$, complementing the four of §17.7.12.5: a physical reading of the standard *cosmological-constant problem* of quantum field theory in which the textbook $120$-order-of-magnitude discrepancy acquires a natural interpretation rather than being a $120$-decade failure.

### 17.7.13.1 The standard problem

Standard quantum field theory predicts a vacuum energy density of order $\rho_{\text{QFT}} \sim 10^{113}$ J/m$^3$, obtained by summing zero-point energies of all field modes up to a Planck-scale cutoff. The observed cosmological constant corresponds to an energy density of $\rho_{\text{obs}} \sim 5 \times 10^{-10}$ J/m$^3$. The ratio is approximately $10^{123}$ --- in Weinberg's characterisation, "the worst theoretical prediction in the history of physics."

### 17.7.13.2 The Constants-paper reading

The Constants paper [MG-Constants, §VII] reads this discrepancy as a *misidentification of the vacuum state of $x_4$*. The structural argument:

(i) If $x_4$ expands at the Planck frequency $f_P = \sqrt{c^5/(\hbar G)} \approx 1.855 \times 10^{43}$ Hz in its fundamental mode (by the Constants-paper hypothesis that the Planck quantities are $x_4$'s natural oscillation scales), then the zero-point energy of $x_4$'s fundamental Planck-frequency mode is
$$E_0^{(P)} \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} \hbar \omega_P \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2} m_P c^2 \;\approx\; 9.8 \times 10^8~\text{J}. \tag{17.7.13.1}$$

(ii) Distributed over one Planck volume $\ell_P^3 \approx 4.22 \times 10^{-105}$ m$^3$, this gives an energy density
$$\rho_{x_4}^{\text{Planck mode}} \;=\; \frac{E_0^{(P)}}{\ell_P^3} \;\sim\; 10^{113}~\text{J/m}^3, \tag{17.7.13.2}$$
which matches the standard quantum field theory prediction $\rho_{\text{QFT}}$ to order of magnitude.

(iii) The observed cosmological constant corresponds to an energy density $\rho_{\text{obs}} \sim 5 \times 10^{-10}$ J/m$^3$ which is *one quantum of $x_4$-expansion per observable-universe volume*. (Observable-universe volume $V_{\text{univ}} \sim 4 \times 10^{80}$ m$^3$; $E_0^{(P)}/V_{\text{univ}} \sim 10^{-72}$ J/m$^3$, which together with a degeneracy factor reaches the observed value; see [MG-Constants §VII] for the detailed estimate.)

### 17.7.13.3 The structural reading

The standard quantum field theory vacuum-energy calculation, on this reading, counts all modes of $x_4$'s oscillation up to the Planck cutoff. The physically realised vacuum state is the *ground state* of $x_4$'s expansion: one quantum of expansion distributed over the spatial extent of the observable universe.

The cosmological-constant "problem" is then not a failure of quantum field theory but a *misidentification of the vacuum*. Both $\rho_{\text{QFT}} \sim 10^{113}$ J/m$^3$ and $\rho_{\text{obs}} \sim 10^{-10}$ J/m$^3$ are correct on their own terms: the former is the energy density of $x_4$'s highest-frequency mode (Planck mode, occupied at one quantum); the latter is the ground-state energy density (one quantum spread over cosmological volume). The $123$-decade ratio between $\rho_{\text{QFT}}$ and $\rho_{\text{obs}}$ has a natural interpretation as the ratio of mode densities of the respective sectors: the Planck-scale modes occupy roughly one per Planck volume $\ell_P^3 \approx 4.22 \times 10^{-105}$ m$^3$; the cosmological-ground-state mode is one per observable-universe volume $V_{\text{univ}} \approx 4 \times 10^{80}$ m$^3$. The bare ratio is $V_{\text{univ}}/\ell_P^3 \sim 10^{185}$; the additional factor needed to reach the observed $10^{-123}$ comes from the mode-degeneracy and ground-state-energy-distribution structure of the cosmological McGucken Sphere, detailed in [21]. The structural reading is qualitative at the level of [MG-Constants §VII]: the discrepancy is the ratio of UV-cutoff-mode density to ground-state mode density, with the detailed numerics requiring the full McGucken cosmology of [21].

### 17.7.13.4 Status and relation to the earlier treatment of $\Lambda$

The Constants-paper reading is *complementary* to the earlier treatment of the cosmological constant (Chapter 10 of this book and the companion McGucken Cosmology paper [21]). In Chapter 10 and [21], $\Lambda$ enters the field equations as a *geometric integration constant* in both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel derivations, not as a vacuum-energy density. The empirical value $\Lambda \approx 1.1 \times 10^{-52}$ m$^{-2}$ is recovered as the cosmological-scale curvature parameter of $M_G$, with the McGucken Cosmology of [21] producing first-place agreement against $\Lambda$CDM in twelve independent observational tests with zero free dark-sector parameters.

The two readings are *not in conflict*: $\Lambda$ as a geometric integration constant (Algebraic Channel/B derivation in Chapter 10) is the *what*; $\Lambda$ as the ground-state of $x_4$'s oscillatory expansion (following [MG-Constants]) is the *why*. The geometric integration constant takes the value it does because the McGucken vacuum is the ground state of $x_4$'s Planck-frequency oscillation, with the observed $10^{-10}$ J/m$^3$ corresponding to one quantum per observable-universe volume. The two readings combine to dissolve the cosmological-constant problem along independent paths: by the geometric channel (Chapter 10) the value is the integration constant of the field equations; by the mode-counting channel (§17.7.12.5) the value is the ground-state of $x_4$.

**Status caveat.** The Constants paper [MG-Constants §VII] is explicit that the cosmological-constant calculation is "speculative, and detailed calculation is required." We record the structural reading here at the level the corpus supports: the McGucken framework supplies a *physical picture* in which both the quantum field theory estimate and the observed value have natural homes, rather than a $120$-decade calculational failure. Promotion to a rigorous theorem would require: (a) a full McGucken-framework derivation of the observable-universe mode count from the cosmological scale of $x_4$-expansion in [21]; (b) a tight numerical bound on the ground-state energy density rather than an order-of-magnitude estimate. Both are deferred to the McGucken Cosmology paper [21] and a future companion paper on the cosmological vacuum.

# 18.1 The Bidirectionality of Gravity $\leftrightarrow$ Thermodynamics in the McGucken Duality {#sec:bidirectionality}

## 18.1.1 The historical order: gravity $\to$ thermodynamics was the first direction

Jacobson 1995 [37] is celebrated as the *thermodynamics-to-gravity* derivation that established the Einstein field equations as the equation of state of spacetime. The McGucken framework's $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel derivation of GR T11 (Chapter 10 of this textbook) is the McGucken-Duality refinement of Jacobson's chain, with the area law, Unruh temperature, and Second Law derived as theorems of $(\mathrm{McP})$ rather than imported as postulates.

What is sometimes lost in the celebration of Jacobson is that the reverse direction --- *gravity-to-thermodynamics* --- was the canonical achievement of the preceding two decades and the structural foundation Jacobson stood on. The historical sequence is:

\begin{enumerate}
\item **Bekenstein 1973** [33]. From the second law of thermodynamics and the irreversibility of black-hole formation, Bekenstein argued that a black hole must carry entropy proportional to its horizon area: $S_{BH} = \eta\, k_B\, A/\ell_P^2$ for some constant $\eta$ of order unity. The argument was *gravity-to-thermodynamics*: classical-GR area theorems combined with the second law of thermodynamics forced an entropy assignment to the horizon.
\item **Bardeen, Carter, Hawking 1973** [BCH73]. *The Four Laws of Black Hole Mechanics.* This paper proved, purely from classical general relativity (Killing horizons, surface gravity $\kappa$, the Raychaudhuri equation, Hawking's area theorem), four theorems with the exact mathematical structure of the four laws of thermodynamics:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{2.0cm}p{5.5cm}p{5.5cm}}
\hline
\textbf{Law} & \textbf{BCH (GR theorem)} & \textbf{Thermodynamic correlate} \\
\hline
0th & $\kappa = \mathrm{const}$ on stationary horizon & $T = \mathrm{const}$ in equilibrium \\
1st & $dM = (\kappa/8\pi G) dA + \Omega dJ + \Phi dQ$ & $dU = T dS + \text{work}$ \\
2nd & $dA/dt \geq 0$ (area theorem) & $dS/dt \geq 0$ \\
3rd & $\kappa \to 0$ unattainable in finite steps & $T \to 0$ unattainable \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

At this stage the correspondence was *purely formal*: pure geometric theorems of GR exhibiting the structure of thermodynamic laws.
\item **Hawking 1975** [35]. Particle creation by black holes: a black hole radiates a thermal spectrum at temperature $T_H = \hbar \kappa / (2\pi c k_B)$. The derivation was *gravity-to-thermodynamics* via quantum field theory on a black hole background: the surface gravity $\kappa$ from classical GR, combined with the analytic structure of quantum fields, forced the thermal-spectrum identification.
\item **Unruh 1976** [36]. Extended the Hawking-temperature relation to accelerated observers in flat spacetime: a uniformly accelerated observer experiences a thermal bath at $T_U = \hbar a/(2\pi c k_B)$. Again *gravity-to-thermodynamics*: the acceleration was the GR input, the thermal bath was the thermodynamic output.
\item **Jacobson 1995** [37]. Reversed the direction: take the area law, Unruh, and Clausius as inputs; recover the Einstein field equations at every event. *Thermodynamics-to-gravity*.
\item **Ryu-Takayanagi 2006** [52], **Verlinde 2010** [53], **Van Raamsdonk 2010** [53], **Maldacena-Susskind 2013** [MS13]. Each instance is a *gravity $\leftrightarrow$ thermodynamics* equivalence at the level of holography, entanglement, or geometric connectivity: $S_{\text{ent}} = A_{\text{min}}/(4G)$ (Ryu-Takayanagi); gravity as an entropic force (Verlinde); spacetime connectivity from boundary entanglement (Van Raamsdonk); $ER = EPR$ (Maldacena-Susskind).
\end{enumerate}

# 18.2 Quantum Mechanics as a Bi-Channel Theory: Unitary Schrödinger Evolution as the Algebraic Channel of the McGucken Duality, Born Rule and Measurement Collapse as the Geometric Channel {#sec:QM-bichannel}

## 18.2.1 The orthodox two-evolution-rule structure of quantum mechanics

The orthodox formulation of quantum mechanics (von Neumann 1932 [40], Dirac 1930 [43]) contains *two structurally distinct evolution rules*, traditionally treated as conceptually independent components of the theory:

\begin{itemize}
\item **Evolution Rule I --- Unitary Schrödinger evolution.** Between measurements, the state vector $|\psi(t)\rangle$ evolves according to the Schrödinger equation
$$i\hbar \frac{\partial}{\partial t} |\psi(t)\rangle \;=\; \hat H\, |\psi(t)\rangle, \tag{18.2.1.1}$$
with $\hat H$ the Hamiltonian operator. The evolution generated by (18.2.1.1) is *deterministic, linear, unitary, and time-reversible*: the time-evolution operator $\hat U(t, t_0) = \exp[-i \hat H (t - t_0)/\hbar]$ satisfies $\hat U^\dagger \hat U = \hat U \hat U^\dagger = \hat I$, and the inverse evolution $\hat U^{-1} = \hat U^\dagger$ exists and is itself unitary.
\item **Evolution Rule II --- Measurement collapse and the Born rule.** Upon measurement of an observable $\hat O$ with eigenstates $\{|o_k\rangle\}_{k=1}^\infty$ and eigenvalues $\{o_k\}_{k=1}^\infty$, the state $|\psi\rangle = \sum_k c_k |o_k\rangle$ undergoes a *non-unitary, irreversible, stochastic* transition to one of the eigenstates $|o_{k^*}\rangle$, with probability
$$P(k^*) \;=\; |c_{k^*}|^2 \;=\; |\langle o_{k^*} | \psi \rangle|^2 \tag{18.2.1.2}$$
(the Born rule). The collapse $|\psi\rangle \to |o_{k^*}\rangle$ is *not* generated by any Hamiltonian; it is an external postulate of the theory.
\end{itemize}

The two evolution rules have structurally opposite characters along five separate axes:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{3.0cm}p{5.0cm}p{5.0cm}}
\hline
\textbf{Property} & \textbf{Rule I (Schrödinger)} & \textbf{Rule II (collapse)} \\
\hline
Determinism & Deterministic & Stochastic \\
Linearity & Linear in $|\psi\rangle$ & Nonlinear (projection) \\
Unitarity & Unitary, $\hat U^\dagger \hat U = \hat I$ & Non-unitary, projector $\hat P_k$ \\
Time-reversibility & Reversible & Irreversible \\
Continuity in $t$ & Continuous & Discontinuous (instantaneous) \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

The orthodox quantum mechanics literature has spent ninety years (since Heisenberg-Schrödinger 1925-1926) attempting to reconcile these two evolution rules within a single framework. The *measurement problem* of quantum mechanics is the structural question: *when does Rule I cease and Rule II begin, and what determines the transition?* The orthodox theory does not specify when, and the answers proposed in the literature --- the Copenhagen interpretation, Bohmian mechanics, many-worlds, GRW spontaneous collapse, decoherence-based interpretations, QBism --- each take a stance on the question but none derive Rule II from Rule I or vice versa.

The temporal succession of Rule I followed by Rule II, in the orthodox picture, is the *appearance* of switching between channels when only one channel is at any moment being read by the observer; the underlying dynamics is bi-channel throughout. The "measurement problem" of orthodox QM dissolves: there is no problem because the question --- when does Rule I cease? --- is malformed in the McGucken Duality. Rule I never ceases (Algebraic Channel operates always); Rule II is not a temporal addition (Geometric Channel has been operating in parallel throughout); the observer's identification of the outcome at measurement is the structural event of the Geometric Channel becoming visible. $\square$
