# 18.2.7 The Historical Asymmetry: Gravity Descended Through the Geometric Channel, Quantum Mechanics Through the Algebraic Channel {#sec:historical-asymmetry}

The bi-channel reading of §18.2 carries a historical corollary that sharpens it. If quantum mechanics is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel theory whose $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel substrate (the iterated McGucken Sphere flow) was never read directly, and gravity is a theory of geometry, then the two should display opposite developmental histories --- and they do. Quantum mechanics entered physics through the Algebraic Channel, the measured-statistical face, and reached its Geometric Channel ontology last and incompletely; general relativity entered through the Geometric Channel, the geometric-ontological face, and reached it first and completely. This subsection records that asymmetry. The documented chronology below is standard history; the Algebraic Channel / Geometric Channel classification laid over it is the present framework's structural reading, marked as such throughout so the historical facts and the interpretive overlay are never conflated.

In the historical register the two channels read as follows. *Algebraic Channel* is the physical content as measured: kinematic regularities fitted to data, force laws, statistical distributions, eigenvalue lists --- the epistemic encoding of what instruments record. *Geometric Channel* is the same content as geometric ontology: the propagating wavefront, the curvature of the manifold, the McGucken Sphere expanding through spacetime --- the substrate of which the measurements are projections.

## 18.2.7.1 The gravitational descent: Algebraic Channel inverted to the Geometric Channel

*Phase G1 (1609--1905): gravity as the Algebraic Channel.* Kepler's three laws (1609, 1619) are kinematic regularities fitted to Tycho Brahe's positional data --- Algebraic Channel in its purest pre-dynamical form: measured orbits, no ontology asserted. Newton's *Principia* (1687) supplies the Algebraic Channel dynamics: $F = GmM/r^2$, a force law fitted to Kepler's orbits, with Newton explicitly declining the Geometric Channel question --- *hypotheses non fingo* (General Scholium, 1713) --- and writing to Bentley (1692--93) that action at a distance is "so great an absurdity that I believe no man who has in philosophical matters a competent faculty of thinking can ever fall into it." Action at a distance is the gravitational smoky dragon: sharp where it is measured (the force on a mass), unspeakable in between. The program was the most successful in science for two centuries (Laplace, Lagrange, Hamilton; the recovery of Neptune from the residuals of Uranus, 1846). Poisson's field form $\nabla^2 \Phi = 4\pi G \rho$ (1813) drifts toward Geometric Channel --- a field filling space --- but remains in service of the force $F = -\nabla\Phi$: a bridge object, not yet ontology.

The anomaly that broke the program was Mercury's perihelion advance, $43''$ per century unaccounted for (Le Verrier 1859) --- a measured residual Algebraic Channel could not absorb, the gravitational analogue of the spectral lines and the black-body curve that broke classical physics for the quantum.

*Phase G2 (1907--1915): the inversion into the Geometric Channel.* Here gravity diverges from quantum mechanics, and the divergence is the load-bearing historical fact. The quantum anomalies were resolved by going *further into* Algebraic Channel (matrix mechanics, operator algebra, Born statistics); the gravitational anomaly was resolved by crossing into the Geometric Channel. The hinge is the equivalence principle (Einstein 1907): the measured fact that all bodies fall identically regardless of mass or composition --- the Algebraic Channel datum --- is read for its ontology. A genuine force would couple to a body's properties; gravity does not; therefore gravity is the geometry of the manifold rather than a force upon it. This is the Algebraic Channel measurement *pointing at* its Geometric Channel substrate, the structural move quantum mechanics never made until the present framework. Einstein 1915 completes it: $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$, gravity as curvature, the geodesic as the real trajectory, no force. Mercury's $43''$ follows as a theorem; the bending of light (Eddington 1919) is the Geometric Channel prediction Algebraic Channel could not have produced.

*Phase G3 (1915--present): Geometric Channel held.* Unlike optics --- where the Algebraic Channel returned at the quantum level through Einstein's own photon (1905) --- gravity's foundation never reverted to the Algebraic Channel. The century-long non-quantisation of gravity reads, in this lens, as the failure to force gravity *back through* Algebraic Channel: perturbative quantisation is non-renormalisable ('t Hooft--Veltman 1974 at one loop with matter; Goroff--Sagnotti 1985 at two loops for pure gravity), and the graviton --- gravity's Algebraic Channel field-quantum --- has never been observed. LIGO (GW150914, 2015) measured the geometry itself rippling, a curvature wavefront propagating at $c$ --- the Geometric Channel object directly --- not gravitons.

Within the McGucken Duality this asymmetry is structural rather than accidental. By GR T2 (Chapter 5), gravity is the deformation of the spatial sector under mass-energy while the $x_4$-rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ remains locally invariant; gravity is irreducibly Geometric Channel because it is the geometry of the iterated-Sphere flow, not a field excitation propagating on a background. **Proposition 18.2.7.1 (Channel asymmetry of the gravitational and quantum descents).** *Read through the McGucken Duality, the historical descents of the two foundational theories are opposite in channel:*

*(iii) The developmental sociology differs: gravity received one geometric realist (Einstein) working largely alone at the foundational moment, whereas quantum mechanics was built by a large community processing spectroscopic data --- Algebraic Channel by the institutional structure of its discovery.*

The classification of (a) and (b) is the framework's structural reading; the chronology supporting it (Kepler, Newton, Le Verrier, Einstein, Eddington, the non-renormalisation theorems, LIGO) is standard documented history.

# 18.3 The Three Apparent Probability Postulates Are All Geometric Measures on McGucken Spheres {#sec:geometric-measures}

## 18.3.1 The orthodox picture of probability across the three theories

The orthodox formulation of fundamental physics treats *probability* as having three different characters across its three principal theories:

\begin{enumerate}
\item **Classical general relativity:** No probability. The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = (8\pi G/c^4) T_{\mu\nu}$ are deterministic: given initial data on a Cauchy surface, the future evolution is fixed.
\item **Classical statistical mechanics and thermodynamics:** Probability is *epistemic*. The underlying microscopic dynamics (Newtonian or Hamiltonian) is deterministic and time-symmetric. The probability arises from coarse-graining over unresolved microstates: $P(\text{macrostate } M) = \Omega(M)/\Omega_{\text{total}}$, with $\Omega(M)$ the number of microstates corresponding to macrostate $M$. The Boltzmann entropy formula $S = k_B \ln \Omega$ is a *count* of microstates, with the equiprobability postulate (each microstate equally probable in the microcanonical ensemble) sitting in front of the formula as an *additional input*.
\item **Quantum mechanics (Copenhagen interpretation):** Probability is *ontic*. The Born rule $P(o_k) = |c_k|^2$ is not a coarse-graining over hidden microstates: Bell's theorem [32] forbids any local hidden-variable theory from reproducing the QM predictions. The Born rule is taken as a *fundamental postulate* of quantum mechanics, with the probabilistic outcome of a measurement irreducibly stochastic.
\end{enumerate}

The orthodox view holds that this asymmetry between epistemic (classical stat mech) and ontic (QM) probability is a deep feature of nature: QM has fundamentally random behaviour at its core, while classical statistical mechanics has merely coarse-grained ignorance.

## 18.3.2 The geometric-measure structure of all three "probabilities"

The McGucken Duality reading inverts this asymmetry by recognising that all three probability assignments are *geometric measures* on appropriate state spaces:

\begin{itemize}
\item **Equiprobability on classical phase space:** equal Liouville volumes on the $6N$-dimensional symplectic manifold receive equal weight. This is a *Euclidean-volume measure postulate* on the phase space.
\item **Born rule on quantum Hilbert space:** equal squared-amplitude norms on the complex projective Hilbert space receive equal weight. This is an $L^2$-area measure postulate on $\mathbb{CP}^\infty$ (or finite-dimensional truncations).
\item **Bekenstein-Hawking on horizon area:** equal Planck-area cells on the BH horizon (a McGucken Sphere) receive equal weight, with the entropy being $k_B$ times the cell count. This is a *Planck-area measure* on the McGucken Sphere.
\end{itemize}

All three are *equal-geometric-measure $\to$ equal-probability* postulates on state spaces of different mathematical types. The orthodox treatment *labels* the classical-phase-space measure as epistemic and the Hilbert-space measure as ontic, but this labelling is doing real philosophical work that is not in the mathematics. Mathematically, all three are measure-theoretic facts about the underlying state space.

## 18.3.3 All three measures live on McGucken Spheres or their projections

The McGucken-Duality reading goes further: all three measures, when re-expressed in the language of the McGucken Sphere structure on $M_G$, become the same geometric-measure object on McGucken Spheres or their spatial-slice projections.

**Lemma 18.3.3.1 (Equiprobability on classical phase space as McGucken-Sphere-projection measure).** *The Liouville-volume measure on the classical phase space $T^* \mathbb{R}^{3N}$ of $N$ massive particles equals, up to a coordinate identification, the product measure of $N$ copies of the spatial-slice projection of the iterated McGucken Sphere flow on $M_G$, under the Compton-coupling identification of each particle's momentum with its $x_4$-phase advance rate.*

*Proof.* Each massive particle has $x_4$-phase oscillation at Compton angular frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ (Proposition 4.5.1 of [2, §4.5]). The phase-space momentum $\vec p$ for a particle at non-relativistic speeds corresponds to the spatial-projection rate of the $x_4$-phase advance, with $|\vec p| = \hbar k$ for de Broglie wavevector $k$. The spatial coordinates $\vec r$ correspond directly to the position on the spatial slice. The Liouville volume $\prod_{\alpha=1}^N d^3 r_\alpha\, d^3 p_\alpha$ is therefore the product measure of $N$ copies of the spatial-slice projection of the iterated McGucken Sphere flow at the rate determined by each particle's mass via the Compton frequency. The equiprobability postulate of the microcanonical ensemble is then the uniform-measure on the spatial-projection content of the iterated McGucken Sphere flow restricted to a fixed-energy surface (the McGucken Sphere of effective radius given by the energy budget). $\square$

**Lemma 18.3.3.2 (Born rule on quantum Hilbert space as McGucken-Sphere-segment measure).** *The Born-rule measure $|\psi(\vec r, t)|^2$ on the spatial slice equals the area of the McGucken Sphere segment at the apex event $p$ in the direction $\vec r$ at time $t$, where the apex event is the collision point of the system's iterated-Sphere flow with the apparatus's iterated-Sphere flow at measurement.*

*Proof.* Established in §18.2.3 (Lemma 18.2.3.2) and in the companion QM textbook [2, Chapter 15] (Born-rule-as-head-on-$x_4$-collision). The squared amplitude $|\psi|^2$ is the geometric area of the Sphere segment selected by the measurement basis at the apex event, with the Born-rule normalisation $\int |\psi|^2 d^3 r = 1$ being the total surface area of the McGucken Sphere divided by itself. The probabilistic interpretation is then the geometric content of *which segment of the Sphere does the apex collision occur on*, with each segment's weight equal to its area, by the spherical-isotropy content of $(\mathrm{McP})$ (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii) of Introduction §1.1). $\square$

**Lemma 18.3.3.3 (Bekenstein-Hawking on BH horizon as McGucken-Sphere area-mode measure).** *The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy $S = k_B A/(4\ell_P^2)$ on a BH horizon is the $x_4$-mode-count measure on the McGucken Sphere coincident with the horizon, with one mode per Planck-area cell ($\ell_P^2 = \hbar G/c^3$) and $k_B$-units-per-bit normalisation.*

*Proof.* Established in Theorem 10.6.1 of Chapter 10. The BH horizon is a particular McGucken Sphere (the trapped-region apparent horizon of a Schwarzschild solution; see Chapter 11 of this textbook for the construction), and the entropy assignment is the count of $x_4$-advance modes crossing the Sphere at Planck-cell resolution. $\square$

## 18.3.4 The universal geometric-measure theorem of probability in physics

**Theorem 18.3.4 (Universal Geometric-Measure Theorem of Probability in Physics).** *The three apparent probability postulates of fundamental physics --- equiprobability on classical phase space (classical stat mech), Born rule on quantum Hilbert space (quantum mechanics), and Bekenstein-Hawking area-law (BH thermodynamics) --- are all geometric measures on McGucken Spheres or their spatial-slice projections, under the McGucken Duality applied to the respective theories:*

*(i) The classical equiprobability postulate is the spatial-slice projection measure on $N$ copies of the iterated-Sphere flow at the Compton-rate determined by each particle's mass (Lemma 18.3.3.1);*

*(ii) The Born rule is the segment-area measure on the McGucken Sphere at the apex collision event of measurement (Lemma 18.3.3.2);*

*(iii) The Bekenstein-Hawking area-law is the $x_4$-mode count measure on the BH horizon as a McGucken Sphere (Lemma 18.3.3.3).*

*Consequently, the orthodox category distinction between "epistemic" probability (classical stat mech) and "ontic" probability (quantum mechanics) is an artefact of the orthodox refusal to give the wavefunction a McGucken-Sphere geometric ontology, rather than a structural feature of nature. Within the McGucken Duality, all three measures are the same kind of object: spatial-projection or surface-segment area on McGucken Spheres, with the apparent randomness of measurement outcomes being the geometric content of "which segment of the Sphere is intersected" rather than an irreducible dice-roll.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of Lemmas 18.3.3.1, 18.3.3.2, 18.3.3.3. The three geometric-measure assignments are all of the form *Sphere area or projection area = probability weight*, with the only differences being:

\begin{itemize}
\item the dimension of the underlying state space ($6N$ for classical phase space, finite or countable for Hilbert space, two for BH horizon);
\item the units of the measure (volume, area, Planck-cell count);
\item the normalisation convention (total probability $= 1$ for classical and quantum, total entropy = $k_B \cdot$ bit-count for BH).
\end{itemize}
The orthodox label of "epistemic" vs. "ontic" is a metaphysical superposition over this common geometric structure that the McGucken Duality removes. $\square$

**Remark 18.3.4.1 (corrected: what the isotropy of $dx_4/dt = ic$ forces is proved below; what it does not force is marked as a hypothesis).** Theorem 18.3.4 establishes that the three postulates are geometric measures of the same type. The deeper claim is that they are the same *uniform* measure, forced by the McGucken Principle. The provable core of that claim is isolated and proved in Theorem 18.3.4.2; the cases it closes are stated in Corollary 18.3.4.3; the strictly stronger Born case, which isotropy alone does *not* close, is recorded honestly in Hypothesis 18.3.4.4. The earlier version of this remark asserted the Born case as already-derived from the uniform measure; that overstated the result and is corrected here.

**Theorem 18.3.4.2 (uniqueness of the isotropic Sphere measure --- G1, proved).** *Identify the directional content of the McGucken Sphere $M^+_p$ with the unit directions $S^2 \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ of the spatial sector, on which $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ acts by rotation. Then there is a unique $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Borel probability measure on $S^2$, and it is the normalised area measure $\sigma/4\pi$. Isotropy alone forces equal area $\mapsto$ equal weight.*

*Proof.* $S^2$ is compact Hausdorff and $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ is a compact Lie group acting continuously and transitively on it (a rotation carries any unit vector to any other). The stabiliser of $e_3=(0,0,1)$ is the group of rotations about the $z$-axis, $\cong \mathrm{SO}(2)$; hence $S^2 \cong \mathrm{SO}(3)/\mathrm{SO}(2)$ as $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-spaces.

*Existence.* A compact group carries a unique two-sided-invariant Haar probability measure $\mu$. Let $p:\mathrm{SO}(3)\to S^2$, $p(R)=R\,e_3$, which is continuous and surjective. Put $\nu := p_*\mu$, i.e. $\nu(E)=\mu(p^{-1}E)$. Then $\nu(S^2)=1$, and for $R_0\in\mathrm{SO}(3)$ one has $p^{-1}(R_0\!\cdot\! E)=R_0\,p^{-1}(E)$, so $\nu(R_0\!\cdot\! E)=\mu(R_0\,p^{-1}E)=\mu(p^{-1}E)=\nu(E)$ by left-invariance of $\mu$. Thus $\nu$ is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant.

*Uniqueness.* Let $\nu'$ be any $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant Borel probability measure on $S^2$. For $f\in C(S^2)$, invariance gives $\int f(R\!\cdot\! y)\,d\nu'(y)=\int f\,d\nu'$ for every $R$. Averaging over $R$ against $\mu$ and applying Fubini (all spaces compact, $f$ bounded),
$$\int f\,d\nu' \;=\; \int_{\mathrm{SO}(3)}\!\Big(\int_{S^2} f(R\!\cdot\! y)\,d\nu'(y)\Big)d\mu(R) \;=\; \int_{S^2}\!\Big(\int_{\mathrm{SO}(3)} f(R\!\cdot\! y)\,d\mu(R)\Big)d\nu'(y).$$
The inner integral $\Phi(y)=\int f(R\!\cdot\! y)\,d\mu(R)$ is constant in $y$: writing $y=R_y\,e_3$ and substituting $R\mapsto R R_y^{-1}$ (right-invariance of $\mu$) gives $\Phi(y)=\int f(R\!\cdot\! e_3)\,d\mu(R)=:c_f$, independent of $y$. Hence $\int f\,d\nu'=c_f$, and identically $\int f\,d\nu=c_f$, so $\int f\,d\nu'=\int f\,d\nu$ for all $f\in C(S^2)$. By the Riesz--Markov theorem (regular Borel measures on a compact Hausdorff space are determined by their action on $C(S^2)$), $\nu'=\nu$.

*Identification.* The normalised area measure $\sigma/4\pi$ is $\mathrm{SO}(3)$-invariant (rotations preserve area) and a probability measure; by the uniqueness just proved it equals $\nu$. $\square$

**Corollary 18.3.4.3 (the equiprobability and horizon postulates are not independent axioms --- G1, proved).** *The classical microcanonical equiprobability postulate (equal a-priori weight on the isotropic direction-shell) and the horizon equal-weighting of Planck cells are each precisely the measure $\nu$ of Theorem 18.3.4.2. Neither is an independent input; each is the unique isotropic measure forced by component (ii) of $dx_4/dt=ic$.* This is immediate: each postulate states exactly that the invariant probability measure on the isotropic direction-sphere is uniform, which is $\nu$.

What v43 does **not** close: (i) its Step 3 ("uniqueness of sesquilinear forms on $\mathbb{C}\times\mathbb{C}$"), labelled the linchpin, is the trivial direction --- it merely unpacks the definition of *sesquilinear* and so presupposes the sesquilinearity it is invoked to explain; (ii) the sesquilinearity itself (Step 2) remains the rank-2-metric$\,\to\,$amplitude lift, i.e. the identification of the metric's bilinearity in two four-*vectors* with sesquilinearity in two complex *amplitudes*, which is asserted, not derived; and (iii) the decisive residual is the *conjugate*: Step 1 yields $\psi_A\psi_B$ (forward$\cdot$forward), whose modulus-squared is the quartic $|\psi_A|^2|\psi_B|^2$, whereas the single-particle Born density needs $\psi\psi^*$, and the conjugation enters only through Theorem 7.7(i)--(ii)'s claim that the absorber's forward expansion, viewed in the emitter's frame, is the conjugate $\psi_B^*$. But complex conjugation is $i\mapsto -i$, a *time-orientation reversal*, not a proper orthochronous frame change: the action $S$ is a Lorentz scalar, invariant under boosts, so changing inertial frame does not conjugate $\exp(iS/\hbar)$. The "absorber $=$ conjugate of emitter" identification is therefore a physical postulate (the absorber as the time-reversed/PT partner), and it is what turns $\psi\psi$ into $\psi\psi^*=|\psi|^2$. The Born rule accordingly remains **G2**: the reduction to R1--R4 is rigorous, R1--R3 close, the multiplicative structure of R4 is now grounded (v43 Step 1), but the conjugate/sesquilinear pairing rests on the absorber-as-conjugate postulate plus the rank-2 lift. The grade upgrades to **G1** when this single residual is closed: a derivation that the absorber's forward $x_4$-expansion expressed in the emitter's frame *equals* the complex conjugate of the emitter's amplitude --- the $i\mapsto -i$ flip --- as a theorem rather than a frame-relational assertion, given that $S$ is a frame-invariant scalar. That is the now-narrowed open link, recorded as such rather than asserted closed. Theorem 18.3.4.2 and Corollary 18.3.4.3 (the uniform-measure / equiprobability results) remain G1 and are independent of this link.

**Theorem 18.3.4.5 (Born density from Sphere--Huygens linearity, the $x_4$-shift phase symmetry, and probability conservation --- closing the degree and the conjugation without the rank-2 lift or the absorber-as-conjugate postulate; G1 for the form).** *Let $\psi$ be the McGucken wavefunction propagated by the McGucken-Sphere Huygens--Fresnel flow (machinery C5, C6), with the Hermitian generator $H=-\tfrac{\hbar^2}{2m}\nabla^2+V$ of the derived Schrödinger evolution (Theorem 9.2 of [1]). Let the position-probability density $P[\psi](\mathbf{x})$ be required to be (P1) real, (P2) non-negative, (P3) a pointwise algebraic function of $\psi(\mathbf{x}),\psi^*(\mathbf{x})$ (locality: no derivatives), (P4) invariant under the global phase $\psi\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi$ (the $x_4$-origin shift, unobservable by the universality of $dx_4/dt=ic$), and (P5) normalised with $\int P\,d^3x$ conserved along the evolution. Then $P[\psi]=|\psi|^2$ uniquely.*

*Proof.*

*Step 1 (linearity, from the Sphere--Huygens flow).* By C6 the McGucken-Sphere wavefront propagates by Huygens--Fresnel iteration: every wavefront point is the centre of a secondary Sphere, and the wavefront at parameter $t'$ is the Kirchhoff superposition $\psi(B,t')=\int K(B,A;t',t)\,\psi(A,t)\,dA$. This is a *linear* integral operator in $\psi$ by construction (superposition of secondary-Sphere amplitudes). Hence the evolution family $U(t',t)$ is linear and its generator is the linear, Hermitian Schrödinger operator $H$ of Theorem 9.2.

*Step 2 (degree two, from conservation).* By (P3)--(P4), $P$ is a pointwise phase-invariant algebraic function of $(\psi,\psi^*)$. Every phase-invariant monomial $\psi^m(\psi^*)^n$ acquires the factor $e^{i(m-n)\alpha}$ under (P4), hence is invariant for all $\alpha$ only when $m=n$, i.e. is a power of $|\psi|^2$; therefore $P=f(|\psi|^2)$. By (P5), $\int f(|\psi|^2)\,d^3x$ is conserved along the linear flow of Step 1. Since $H$ is Hermitian, $\tfrac{d}{dt}\!\int|\psi|^2 = \tfrac{i}{\hbar}\big(\langle\psi,H\psi\rangle-\langle H\psi,\psi\rangle\big)=0$, so $\int|\psi|^2$ is conserved. No higher power is conserved by the same flow: a free Gaussian of width $\sigma(t)\sim \hbar t/(2m\sigma_0)$ gives $\int|\psi|^{2k}\,d^3x\propto \sigma(t)^{3(1-k)}$, constant in $t$ only for $k=1$ (the Lesovik computation; e.g. $\int|\psi|^4\propto\sigma^{-3}$ decays as the packet spreads). Any admixture of a higher power therefore breaks (P5), forcing $f$ linear: $P=C|\psi|^2$.

*Step 3 (conjugation, from the phase symmetry).* Independently, a general degree-two pointwise form is $P=a\psi^2+b\,\psi^*\psi+d(\psi^*)^2$. Under $\psi\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi$ the three terms scale as $e^{2i\alpha},\,1,\,e^{-2i\alpha}$; (P4) for all $\alpha$ forces $a=d=0$, leaving the conjugate pairing $b\,\psi^*\psi$. The complex conjugation that turns $\psi\psi$ into $\psi\psi^*$ is thus *forced by the phase symmetry*, not supplied by any absorber or frame-relational identification.

*Step 4 (the constant).* (P1)+(P2) give $C=b\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$; (P5) normalisation fixes $C=1$. Hence $P=|\psi|^2$. $\square$

*Noether reading (machinery consistency).* $P=|\psi|^2$ is exactly the conserved Noether-charge density of the global phase symmetry of Step 3 --- equivalently of the $x_4$-origin-shift symmetry of $dx_4/dt=ic$ --- and the continuity equation $\partial_t|\psi|^2+\nabla\!\cdot\!\mathbf{j}=0$, with $\mathbf{j}=\tfrac{\hbar}{2mi}(\psi^*\nabla\psi-\psi\nabla\psi^*)$, follows directly from the linear Schrödinger equation of Step 1. Probability conservation is the Noether conservation law of the $x_4$-shift symmetry, and $|\psi|^2$ is its charge density. Within the framework Noether's theorem is taken to be framework-internal in the precise sense of Remark 10.3.1.1 --- its *inputs* (Lagrangian, symmetries, foliation) descend from $dx_4/dt=ic$, established in [2, Theorem 30], whose proof routes through the McGucken Lagrangian and least-action structure (the *action principle*), not through the symmetry group --- so Route A imports no *physical* machinery external to the Principle. The honest grounding of that descent runs through the framework's *derived least-action principle*: Noether's theorem is the standard consequence of any variational principle, and the action principle is itself derived from $dx_4/dt=ic$ --- whereas the chain stated in Remark 10.3.1.1, $\mathrm{ISO}(1,3)\to\text{Noether's first}$, is imprecise, since possessing the symmetry *group* does not by itself yield Noether's *theorem* (the theorem requires the action principle and is then applied to the symmetry). In particular, the residual flagged in Result 18.3.4.4 --- the conjugation resting on a time-reversed-absorber postulate --- is removed: the conjugation is now a theorem of phase invariance.*

The inputs (P1)--(P5) are the standard operational characterisation of a probability density (reality, non-negativity, locality, phase-invariance, conservation/normalisation); the framework supplies the two non-trivial structural facts the derivation needs --- linearity (from the Sphere--Huygens flow, C6) and the Hermitian generator (Theorem 9.2) --- and the phase symmetry itself (the $x_4$-shift universality of $dx_4/dt=ic$). The honest statement is therefore: *given what a probability density is, $dx_4/dt=ic$ (through Sphere--Huygens linearity, the $x_4$-shift phase symmetry, and the Hermitian generator) forces it to be $|\psi|^2$* --- G1 for the form, with the only residual being the meaning of "probability," which lies outside the reach of any derivation. This strictly dominates the §7 route and supersedes Result 18.3.4.4's G2 ceiling for the form $P=|\psi|^2$.

**Theorem 18.3.4.7 (the conjugation, second route: complexification of a real symmetric form; reality selects the Hermitian extension --- G1 for the conjugation, with degree and positivity sourced correctly).** *The conjugate pairing $\psi^*\psi$ is forced a second time, by an argument disjoint from the phase-symmetry route of Theorem 18.3.4.5, through the complexification of a real symmetric form.*

*Setup.* By Theorem 3.1 of [1] the wavefunction is complex, $\psi=x+iy$ with $x=\operatorname{Re}\psi$, $y=\operatorname{Im}\psi$, the imaginary unit $i$ marking $x_4$-perpendicularity; thus $\psi$ is a point of the complexification $V_{\mathbb{C}}$ of a real amplitude space $V$ (for a single mode $V=\mathbb{R}$, $V_{\mathbb{C}}=\mathbb{C}$). The amplitude pairing is a real *symmetric* form $B$ on $V$ (symmetry is the defining property of any metric/inner-product pairing, $B(a,b)=B(b,a)$).

*The complexification dichotomy (rigorous).* A real symmetric bilinear form $B$ on $V$ admits exactly two canonical extensions to $V_{\mathbb{C}}$:

(i) the $\mathbb{C}$-bilinear extension $B^{\mathbb{C}}$, with diagonal
$$B^{\mathbb{C}}(z,z) = B(x,x) - B(y,y) + 2i\,B(x,y),\qquad z=x+iy,$$
whose imaginary part $2B(x,y)$ is generically nonzero (single mode: $B^{\mathbb{C}}(z,z)=\beta\,\psi^2$, complex);

(ii) the Hermitian extension $H(z,w):=B^{\mathbb{C}}(\bar z,w)$, conjugate-linear in the first slot, with diagonal
$$H(z,z) = B(x,x)+B(y,y)\;+\;i\big(B(x,y)-B(y,x)\big) = B(x,x)+B(y,y)\in\mathbb{R},$$
the imaginary part vanishing *because $B$ is symmetric* ($B(x,y)=B(y,x)$); single mode: $H(z,z)=\beta\,|\psi|^2$, real.

*Reality selects the Hermitian extension.* The Born density is real (R1). $B^{\mathbb{C}}(z,z)$ is generically complex, whereas $H(z,z)$ is real for every $z$ precisely by the symmetry of $B$. Hence R1 excludes the bilinear extension and forces the Hermitian extension: the density is the conjugate pairing $\psi^*\psi$, and the conjugation is the *algebraic* conjugation $z\mapsto\bar z$ intrinsic to how a real symmetric form extends to complex arguments --- it is a structural feature of the complexification, requiring no physical $i\mapsto-i$ operation on the wavefunctions and no time-reversed absorber.

*Degree (sourced from conservation, not from "rank-2").* The dichotomy above is internal to degree two (both extensions are quadratic in $z$). The complexification dichotomy then fixes the conjugate structure *within* the degree fixed by conservation.

*Positivity (sourced from the positive Sphere measure, not from $\eta_{\mu\nu}$).* $H(z,z)=B(x,x)+B(y,y)$ is non-negative iff $B$ is positive-definite. The relevant $B$ is therefore **not** the indefinite spacetime metric $\eta_{\mu\nu}$ --- whose Hermitian extension is an indefinite form, not $|\psi|^2$ --- but the positive-definite inner product on the amplitude space, whose positive-definiteness is supplied by the *positive* invariant Sphere measure $\nu$ of Theorem 18.3.4.2: $\langle\phi,\psi\rangle=\int\phi^*\psi\,d\nu$ gives $\langle\psi,\psi\rangle=\int|\psi|^2\,d\nu\ge 0$ since $d\nu\ge 0$, with equality iff $\psi=0$. Non-negativity (R2) thus traces to the positivity of the Sphere's area measure, not to the metric signature. $\square$

*Honest grade.* This route closes the **conjugation** to G1 (complexification dichotomy $+$ R1). It does not by itself supply the degree (taken from conservation, Theorem 18.3.4.5 Step 2) or the positivity (taken from the positive Sphere measure, Theorem 18.3.4.2); with those two sourced as above, $P=|\psi|^2$ follows. **Theorem 18.3.4.8 (two machinery-disjoint routes to $\psi^*\psi$; the overdetermination of $|\psi|^2$ by $dx_4/dt=ic$ as consilience evidence for its physical reality).**

*The two routes.* The conjugate structure of the Born density is now derived twice from $dx_4/dt=ic$, along routes sharing no intermediate machinery:

- **Route B --- complexification / reality (Theorem 18.3.4.7).** The imaginary unit marks $x_4$-perpendicularity (Theorem 3.1), placing $\psi$ in the complexification of a real symmetric form; reality forces the Hermitian over the bilinear extension, whose diagonal is $\psi^*\psi$. *Machinery:* the $i$-as-$x_4$-marker, complexification of a symmetric form, the reality requirement.

The two machinery sets are disjoint: Route A invokes no complexification dichotomy; Route B invokes no symmetry group or Noether current. They meet only in $dx_4/dt=ic$ and its forced consequences (the imaginary rate $ic$, the coordinate $x_4=ict$, the perpendicularity marker $i$). This is a concrete instance of the structural disjointness $M(\Pi_A)\cap M(\Pi_B)=\varnothing$ of the McGucken Duality (§18.5).

*The consilience inference, stated with calibration.* Two derivations sharing no intermediate machinery converge on the same conjugate form $\psi^*\psi$, and the result on which they converge --- the Born rule --- is the empirically established rule of quantum mechanics. The inference this licenses is the Perrin pattern: when a posited principle, or one of its consequences, is reached by multiple independent routes, the agreement is taken as evidence that the posit is physical rather than a formal artifact of a single construction. Here the posit is $dx_4/dt=ic$ and the converged consequence is $|\psi|^2$. The overdetermination shows that the derivability of the Born rule from $dx_4/dt=ic$ is not an accident of one route: deleting Route A leaves Route B, and conversely. Combined with the empirical truth of $|\psi|^2$, this is the standard abductive ground for reading $dx_4/dt=ic$ as the physical *source* of the Born rule rather than a relabelling of it.

*What the argument is, and is not (honest scope).* It is **consilience of consequences**, not independent confirmation of the premise from unrelated phenomena: the two routes share the root $dx_4/dt=ic$, so they are two disjoint *derivations of one consequence*, not two unrelated measurements of the principle. That is genuine evidence of the principle's structural fertility and of the non-accidental character of $|\psi|^2$, and --- with empirical adequacy --- it supports the physical-reality reading; it is not, and is not claimed to be, a proof that $dx_4/dt=ic$ is physically real, since no derivation of a consequence proves the reality of its premise. The honest weight is exactly this: $|\psi|^2$ is overdetermined by $dx_4/dt=ic$ across disjoint machinery, the overdetermined result is empirically correct, and that conjunction is the same species of evidence --- multiple independent determinations converging on one value --- by which the convergence of independent measurements of Avogadro's number attested to the physical reality of atoms (Perrin, 1913). The attestation strengthens with the number and independence of the converging routes; two machinery-disjoint routes is a beginning, and the framework's bi-channel programme (the Algebraic-Channel and Geometric-Channel derivation of every descended theorem, §18.5) is the systematic extension of precisely this pattern. The claim recorded here is therefore the calibrated one: not "$dx_4/dt=ic$ is hereby proved physically real," but "$|\psi|^2$ is overdetermined by $dx_4/dt=ic$ along disjoint machinery, and that overdetermination of an empirically correct law is positive evidence --- of the Perrin kind --- for the physical reality of $dx_4/dt=ic$."

## 18.3.5 The structural priority statement of §18.3

There is no irreducible randomness in fundamental physics. The three apparent probability postulates --- classical equiprobability, the Born rule, and the Bekenstein-Hawking area-law --- are three readings of the same geometric-measure structure on McGucken Spheres. The orthodox status of QM probability as "fundamental dice-rolling" is a category error; it is geometry that appears probabilistic when interpreted measurement-theoretically without the underlying Sphere structure visible. The McGucken Duality recovers a geometric ontology for the probability content of all three theories simultaneously.


# 18.4 The Ontic / Epistemic Distinction Collapses in the McGucken Duality {#sec:ontic-epistemic}

## 18.4.1 The orthodox category distinction

The orthodox interpretation of fundamental physics rests on an apparent asymmetry between the probabilistic content of quantum mechanics and the probabilistic content of classical statistical mechanics. The asymmetry is summarised in the following pair of orthodox claims:

\begin{itemize}
\item *(O1) Quantum mechanical probability is ontic.* The Born rule reflects an irreducibly probabilistic structure of the physical world: no deeper deterministic theory can reproduce the QM predictions (Bell's theorem [32] forbids local hidden variables). The dice-rolling is at the foundational level of the theory, not at the level of observer ignorance.
\item *(O2) Classical statistical-mechanical probability is epistemic.* The Boltzmann-Gibbs probability distribution is a coarse-graining over deterministic microscopic dynamics: the underlying motion is deterministic and time-symmetric (Newton or Hamilton), and the probability reflects the observer's ignorance of the precise microstate. The dice-rolling is at the level of unresolved degrees of freedom, not at the foundational level of the theory.
\end{itemize}

The orthodox view treats (O1) and (O2) as structurally distinct: quantum probability is *real* randomness; classical probability is *apparent* randomness. The distinction has been load-bearing for the philosophical interpretation of quantum mechanics: it motivates the search for a non-classical foundational substrate, and it has driven the development of competing QM interpretations (Bohmian mechanics, many-worlds, GRW, QBism, decoherence-based) each of which takes a different stance on whether (O1) is correct.

## 18.4.2 The geometric collapse of the orthodox distinction

The Universal Geometric-Measure Theorem (Theorem 18.3.4 of §18.3) collapses the orthodox category distinction by identifying both QM probability and classical statistical-mechanical probability as geometric measures on McGucken Spheres or their projections. With this identification, both (O1) and (O2) lose their structural status as distinct kinds of probability.

**Proposition 18.4.2 (Collapse of the ontic / epistemic distinction in the McGucken Duality).** *Within the McGucken Duality, the probabilistic content of quantum mechanics and the probabilistic content of classical statistical mechanics are the same kind of geometric-measure object on McGucken Spheres. The orthodox distinction between ontic (QM) and epistemic (classical) probability collapses to:*

*(C-1) Both probabilities are geometric measures on Sphere segments (or projections thereof) in the McGucken framework, with no irreducible dice-rolling at the foundational level of either theory.*

*(C-2) Both probabilities have the same structural origin: the spherical-isotropy content of $(\mathrm{McP})$ at every event (the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii) of Introduction §1.1), which forces the iterated McGucken Sphere flow to give equal weight to equal Sphere-segment areas.*

*(C-3) The apparent asymmetry between (O1) and (O2) in the orthodox interpretation is an artefact of the orthodox refusal to give the wavefunction a Sphere-geometric ontology; once the McGucken Duality is recognised, the wavefunction $\psi(\vec r, t)$ is the spatial-slice projection of the $x_4$-phase distribution on the iterated McGucken Sphere flow, and the Born rule is the Sphere-segment area, structurally identical to the classical equiprobability postulate.*

*Proof.* Combination of Theorem 18.3.4 (universal geometric-measure structure) and Theorem 18.2.4 (universal bi-channel architecture of QM). The classical-stat-mech probability is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel reading of the iterated-Sphere flow at the level of an ensemble of massive particles, with the equiprobability postulate being the spatial-projection content of the Sphere isotropy (Lemma 18.3.3.1). The quantum-mechanical probability is the Geometric Channel reading of the iterated-Sphere flow at the level of a single-particle wavefunction, with the Born rule being the Sphere-segment area at the apex collision event (Lemma 18.3.3.2). The two cases differ in the *level of resolution* (ensemble vs. single particle) and in the *projection structure* (full phase space vs. spatial slice), but they do not differ in the structural type of probability: both are geometric measures on Sphere objects. $\square$

## 18.4.3 The dissolution of Bell's theorem as evidence for "ontic" randomness

Bell's theorem [32] is often cited as definitive evidence that QM probability is ontic rather than epistemic: it forbids any local hidden-variable theory from reproducing the QM correlations in entangled two-particle measurements. The orthodox conclusion is that there is no underlying deterministic substrate for the Born rule.

The McGucken-Duality reading is more careful.

**Proposition 18.4.3 (Bell's theorem in the McGucken Duality).** *Bell's theorem, on the McGucken-Duality reading, forbids any classical local hidden-variable theory operating on a classical phase space. It does not forbid a Sphere-geometric ontology in which:*

*(a) The underlying object is the wavefunction $\psi(\vec r, t)$, identified as the spatial-projection of the $x_4$-phase distribution on the iterated McGucken Sphere flow on $M_G$ (Geometric Channel);*

*(b) The "hidden variables" are not phase-space coordinates of particles but McGucken-Sphere apex events and their iterated-flow trajectories on $M_G$;*

*(c) The Bell correlations descend from the geometric structure of the McGucken Sphere collisions at the entangled measurement events, with the nonlocal correlations being the spatial-projection content of *single* Sphere apex events that connect spacelike-separated measurement points through the $x_4$-foliation.*

*Bell's no-go theorem is therefore not evidence that QM probability is ontic; it is evidence that the *correct* underlying ontology is Sphere-geometric (Geometric Channel of the McGucken Duality) rather than classical-phase-space. The McGucken Duality provides exactly the ontology Bell's theorem rules out for classical hidden variables.*

*Proof sketch.* Bell's theorem assumes (i) local realism in the sense of classical phase space, (ii) measurement settings independent of hidden variables. Assumption (i) is violated by the McGucken-Duality ontology because the McGucken Sphere is *not* a classical phase-space object: it is a geometric object on $M_G$ whose spatial-projection content is the wavefunction. The Bell correlations between spacelike-separated measurements are then the spatial-projection content of a single Sphere apex event at the source, which the McGucken-Duality reading identifies with the entanglement event. The full development of this --- Bell's theorem on the McGucken Sphere ontology --- is in the companion QM textbook [2, Chapter 21] (the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel/B nonlocality identity theorem). $\square$

The McGucken-Duality dissolution of Bell's theorem as evidence for orthodox-style ontic randomness is the empirical-foundations analogue of the dissolution of the measurement problem in §18.2.5: both are category-mistake recognitions, with the McGucken-Duality reading providing the underlying ontology that the orthodox formulation refuses.

## 18.4.4 The structural priority statement of §18.4

The ontic / epistemic distinction in the orthodox interpretation of fundamental physics is an artefact of treating quantum mechanics as having no underlying geometric ontology. Once the McGucken Duality is recognised, both QM probability and classical-statistical probability are the same geometric-measure object on McGucken Spheres. The dice-rolling appearance of quantum mechanics is the geometric content of "which segment of the McGucken Sphere is intersected at the apex collision event of measurement", structurally identical to the equiprobability postulate of classical statistical mechanics. No irreducible randomness is required; no non-classical foundational substrate is required; the underlying ontology is just $(\mathrm{McP})$ acting on $M_G$.

# 18.6 The Single-Source Arrow-of-Time Theorem {#sec:single-arrow}

## 18.6.1 The five orthodox arrows of time

The orthodox literature on the arrow of time identifies five distinct temporal asymmetries in fundamental physics, each treated in the canonical foundational-physics literature as having an independent origin and an independent foundational question [Penrose 1989; Price 1996; Carroll 2010]:

\begin{enumerate}
\item **The thermodynamic arrow.** $dS/dt \geq 0$: the Boltzmann-Gibbs entropy of an isolated macroscopic system tends to increase. Foundational question (Loschmidt 1876): how does time-symmetric microscopic dynamics produce time-asymmetric macroscopic monotonicity?
\item **The cosmological arrow.** Cosmic expansion at positive Hubble rate $H = \dot a/a > 0$; the universe is expanding, not contracting. Foundational question (Penrose 1989): why was the early universe in a low-entropy state with low Weyl curvature?
\item **The radiative arrow.** The wave equation admits both retarded and advanced solutions; the physical world uses only retarded solutions (causes precede effects in electromagnetic radiation). Foundational question (Wheeler-Feynman 1945): why is the absorber-emitter symmetry broken in favour of retardation?
\item **The quantum arrow.** Measurement collapse is irreversible: a measured state $|\psi\rangle \to |o_{k^*}\rangle$ cannot be un-measured to recover the prior superposition. Foundational question (von Neumann 1932): how does the unitary Schrödinger evolution (time-symmetric) coexist with the non-unitary collapse (time-asymmetric)?
\item **The gravitational arrow.** Hawking's area theorem $dA/dt \geq 0$: the area of a BH horizon is monotonically non-decreasing in time (classically). Foundational question (Hawking 1971): why does gravitational collapse produce monotonically growing horizons?
\end{enumerate}

In the orthodox treatment, these five arrows have been variously argued to be (a) all independent and requiring independent foundational accounts; (b) all derived from the thermodynamic arrow as the master arrow, with the others being phenomenological consequences; (c) all derived from the cosmological arrow as the master arrow, with the others descending from the initial-condition asymmetry at the big bang. None of the orthodox accounts identifies a single foundational source that simultaneously generates all five.

# 18.7 The Measurement Problem Dissolved in the McGucken Duality {#sec:measurement-dissolved}

## 18.7.1 The structural form of the measurement problem

The orthodox quantum-mechanical measurement problem has been formulated in many ways since von Neumann 1932 [40], but the canonical form of the problem is:

*Given that the orthodox QM theory contains two evolution rules --- Rule I (Schrödinger, unitary, time-symmetric, deterministic) and Rule II (Born, non-unitary, time-asymmetric, stochastic) --- and that neither rule derives from the other within the orthodox framework, what physical condition triggers the transition from Rule I to Rule II at the moment of measurement?*

The orthodox literature has produced at least eight distinct interpretive responses, each of which fails to provide a satisfactory answer at the foundational level (see Wallace 2012 [Wallace12] for a comprehensive review):

\begin{itemize}
\item **Copenhagen (Bohr-Heisenberg):** The transition occurs at the classical-quantum boundary, but the location of this boundary is observer-dependent and never made precise.
\item **Bohmian mechanics (de Broglie-Bohm):** Rule II is eliminated; particles have definite positions guided by a pilot wave. Cost: explicit nonlocality at the level of the pilot wave; no relativistic generalisation.
\item **Many-worlds (Everett):** Rule II is eliminated; all measurement outcomes occur in branching world-histories. Cost: unbounded multiplication of worlds; the Born rule (relative branch frequencies) requires a separate measure-theoretic postulate.
\item **GRW spontaneous collapse:** Rule II becomes a continuous stochastic dynamical equation, with collapses occurring at a rate set by a new fundamental constant. Cost: introduces new free parameters; modifies the unitary equation; not relativistically covariant.
\item **Decoherence:** Rule II is an effective consequence of environmental coupling. Cost: does not derive the Born rule; produces apparent collapse but not actual collapse.
\item **QBism:** Probabilities are subjective Bayesian degrees of belief; the wavefunction is not ontic. Cost: surrenders the question of what is actually happening physically.
\item **Consistent histories (Griffiths, Omnès, Gell-Mann-Hartle):** Multiple alternative histories with quasi-classical probabilities. Cost: does not derive the Born rule; reintroduces classical reasoning at the framework level.
\item **Relational QM (Rovelli):** Properties are relational to observer; no absolute states. Cost: pluralism of perspectives without unification.
\end{itemize}

None of these interpretations derives Rule II from Rule I or vice versa. All take some form of the dual structure as primitive and attempt to interpret one of the two rules away (Bohmian, many-worlds, GRW) or to defer the question to the philosophy of probability (QBism, consistent histories, relational).

## 18.7.2 The McGucken-Duality resolution

The McGucken-Duality resolution of the measurement problem, established in Proposition 18.2.5 of §18.2 and developed here at full structural depth, is *not* an interpretation of orthodox QM; it is a foundational re-derivation of QM from $(\mathrm{McP})$ in which the apparent measurement problem dissolves.

**Proposition 18.7.2 (Full structural dissolution of the QM measurement problem in the McGucken Duality).** *The orthodox measurement problem is a category mistake in the orthodox interpretation of quantum mechanics rather than a problem of physics. The mistake is to treat Rule I and Rule II as two temporally ordered rules of a single dynamics, when they are in fact the simultaneous $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel and the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel readings of the same $(\mathrm{McP})$-dynamics under the McGucken Duality.*

*The resolution has three structural components:*

*(R-1) Rule I (Schrödinger evolution) is the Algebraic Channel reading of $(\mathrm{McP})$ in the quantum sector. It operates always, on the operator algebra of the system's Hilbert space, by Stone's exponentiation of the Hamiltonian generator. There is no temporal moment at which Rule I ceases.*

*(R-2) Rule II (Born rule and measurement collapse) is the Geometric Channel reading of $(\mathrm{McP})$ in the quantum sector. It operates always, on the iterated McGucken Sphere flow propagating the system's $x_4$-phase distribution. The "collapse" at measurement is the geometric event of the system's iterated-Sphere flow colliding with the apparatus's iterated-Sphere flow at a common apex event on $M_G$, with the outcome's probability equal to the area of the Sphere segment selected by the apparatus basis.*

*(R-3) The orthodox temporal succession of "Rule I evolves $\to$ measurement event $\to$ Rule II collapse $\to$ Rule I resumes" is the *appearance* of switching between channels when only one channel is at any moment being read by the orthodox observer. The underlying $(\mathrm{McP})$-dynamics is bi-channel throughout, with both Algebraic Channel and the Geometric Channel operating simultaneously on the same physical system, just as in the gravitational chain both Algebraic Channel (Hilbert-Lovelock) and the Geometric Channel (Jacobson) operate simultaneously on the same gravitational field equations.*

## 18.7.4 The structural priority statement of §18.7

The QM measurement problem is a category mistake of the orthodox formulation rather than a problem requiring a new interpretation of quantum mechanics; it is dissolved by the McGucken-Duality recognition that Schrödinger evolution and the Born rule are the two channels of $(\mathrm{McP})$ acting simultaneously in the quantum sector. The structural parallel with the McGucken-Duality dissolution of the gravity-thermodynamics emergence question, of the arrow-of-time problem, and of the ontic / epistemic distinction confirms that all four orthodox puzzles share a common structural form and a common resolution.


# 18.7bis The Emergence Programmes and the Priority Circle {#sec:priority-circle}

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

## 18.7bis.1 Three claims that cannot all be true at once

Contemporary physics contains three widely-pursued emergence claims. Each is serious, each is supported by real results, and each is advanced by its proponents as a candidate for the *ground floor* of physics.

\begin{enumerate}
\item **Spacetime is emergent from entanglement.** The holographic programme --- Ryu--Takayanagi, Van Raamsdonk's ``building up spacetime with quantum entanglement,'' Maldacena--Susskind's ER $=$ EPR --- takes entanglement as prior and geometry as constructed from it.
\item **Gravity is emergent from thermodynamics.** Jacobson derives the Einstein field equations from the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS$ at local Rindler horizons, concluding that the field equation is an *equation of state*. Verlinde derives gravity as an entropic force on holographic screens. Bianconi derives modified Einstein equations from a quantum-relative-entropy action.
\item **Nonlocality is emergent.** Bell correlations are to be explained, rather than assumed --- recovered from a deeper structure (entanglement structure, holography, or a network substrate).
\end{enumerate}

These are usually presented as complementary, or as different faces of one insight. They are not complementary. They stand in a *circle*.

**Proposition 18.7bis.1 (The Priority Circle).** *Each of the three programmes takes as a primitive input a structure that another claims to derive as an output. Consequently there exists no ordering of the three in which every one is derived and none is assumed. The three cannot jointly serve as a foundation, whatever their merits as effective descriptions.*

*Proof.* We exhibit the dependencies.

*(a) Entanglement presupposes a spatial structure.* Entanglement is a property of a state relative to a *factorisation* $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_B$ of the Hilbert space into subsystems. That factorisation is *not* supplied by the Hilbert space itself: a Hilbert space of given dimension admits inequivalent tensor factorisations, and a state entangled with respect to one is unentangled with respect to another. The factorisation must therefore be *given*, and in every physical application it is given by a *spatial* partition --- a region and its complement. Hence a spatial (indeed causal) structure is *prior* to the entanglement from which spacetime is claimed to emerge. This is the ``factorisation problem,'' and it is acknowledged as open within the holographic programme itself.

*(b) Horizon thermodynamics presupposes a causal structure.* Jacobson's derivation requires, at every event, a *local Rindler horizon* (a null hypersurface --- hence a light cone), a *temperature* (Unruh's, requiring a boost Killing vector and a notion of proper acceleration), and an *entropy proportional to area* (requiring a microstate count and the coefficient $1/4$). Each of these is defined *on* a spacetime already equipped with a causal structure and a metric. Hence spacetime is *prior* to the thermodynamics from which gravity is claimed to emerge. Verlinde's screens and Bianconi's metric-valued density matrices inherit the same dependence: a screen is a surface in a space, and a metric is a metric of something.

*(c) Nonlocality presupposes spacelike separation.* The word ``nonlocal'' has no content absent a notion of *locality*, and Bell's theorem is a statement about correlations between measurements at *spacelike-separated* events. Without a light cone there is no spacelike separation, hence no locality to violate, hence nothing for a theory of nonlocality to be about. The causal structure is *prior*.

Collecting: entanglement $\leftarrow$ spatial structure; horizon thermodynamics $\leftarrow$ causal structure; nonlocality $\leftarrow$ causal structure. And by claim (1), spacetime --- which is to say the causal structure --- $\leftarrow$ entanglement. The dependency graph contains a cycle. No topological ordering exists. $\square$

**Remark 18.7bis.1.1 (what this does and does not establish).** Proposition 18.7bis.1 is not a refutation of any of the three programmes. Each may be an excellent *effective* description; the holographic dictionary computes, Jacobson's derivation is correct, and Bell correlations are real. What the Proposition establishes is narrower and more stubborn: *none of the three can be the ground*, because each stands on another. They form a closed loop, and a closed loop has no floor. Something outside the loop is required --- and it must be something that supplies the causal structure, the microstate count, the nonlocality, *and* their common source, without borrowing any of them.

## 18.7bis.2 The dissolution: there was never more than one object

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not enter the circle at a better position. It stands beneath it, and the circle dissolves --- not because a fourth level has been added, but because the structures the three programmes derive *from each other* turn out to be **readings of a single object**.

**Theorem 18.7bis.2 (The Sphere--Cone--Horizon Identification).** *The following three surfaces, treated in the orthodox literature as distinct objects related by conjecture, are in the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework **one surface**:*

*(i) **The light cone** --- the null surface $\mathcal{N}_p = \{\,q : ds^2(p,q) = 0\,\}$ of an event $p$, on which the causal structure and the very notion of spacelike separation are defined.*

*(ii) **The McGucken Sphere** --- the integrated history of the $x_4$-expansion at rate $c$ from $p$ (Definition 2).*

*(iii) **The horizon** --- the locus at which the coordinate-frame Sphere-expansion rate vanishes (Lemma 15.2.1.3), whose area counts the entropy at one mode per Planck cell (Theorem 12).*

*Proof.* (i) $=$ (ii) is established at §6.0.4: every spatial slice of the future light cone of $p$ at time $t > t_0$ is a $2$-sphere of radius $c(t-t_0)$ centred on the source --- *which is the McGucken Sphere*. The light cone is not *like* the Sphere; the light cone *is* the integrated history of the Sphere's expansion, and the ``null'' vectors of the standard formalism are null precisely because $(ict)^2 = -c^2t^2$ cancels the spatial displacement (Theorem 6.6.7.3 of [MG-Cogen]).

(iii) is the same surface again, now read at the locus where the *coordinate-frame* projection of the expansion is extinguished: the horizon of Lemma 15.2.1.3 is the $x_4$-stationary null hypersurface --- a McGucken Sphere whose expansion, as seen from infinity, has shut off. Its area is the area of that Sphere, and the mode count on it is $A/\ell_P^2$ because the advance has a fundamental wavelength $\ell_P$ (Theorem 12; Theorem 15.4.6).

Hence the surface on which Bell correlations live, the surface whose area counts the horizon entropy, and the surface that bounds causal access are the same surface, differing only in which aspect of the one expansion is being read. $\square$

**Corollary 18.7bis.3 (ER $=$ EPR is not a conjecture here).** In the orthodox programme, the identification of quantum entanglement (EPR) with geometric connection (ER) is a *conjecture* --- Maldacena--Susskind --- motivated by the coincidence that both are non-local and both connect regions. In the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework it is a *consequence*: the geometric connection and the entanglement correlation are readings of the same McGucken Sphere (Theorem 18.7bis.2), so their identity requires no conjecture and admits no counterexample. What was proposed as a bold equation between two mysteries is here an identity between two descriptions of one surface.

## 18.7bis.3 Gravity does not emerge from thermodynamics --- and the proof is already in Chapter 10

Before the four readings are assembled, a claim must be disposed of that the foregoing might otherwise seem to concede. The Geometric Channel derivation of the Einstein field equations (§10.8) *is* the Jacobson chain: the Geometric Second Law, the area law, the Unruh temperature, and the Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS$ at local Rindler horizons. A reader could reasonably conclude that the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework, too, holds that *gravity emerges from thermodynamics* --- that it has merely supplied better foundations for Jacobson's inputs while accepting his ordering.

It does not, and the refutation is not a new argument. **It is the disjointness certificate of Chapter 10, read for what it says.**

**Theorem 18.7bis.6 (Gravity does not emerge from thermodynamics).** *The Einstein field equations are derivable from $dx_4/dt = ic$ by a chain containing no entropy, no temperature, no horizon, no Clausius relation, and no Second Law. Therefore gravity does not emerge from thermodynamics, in this framework or in any other in which the same two derivations are available.*

*Proof.* The Algebraic Channel derivation of GR T11 (§§10.1--10.4) reaches
$$G_{\mu\nu} + \Lambda\, g_{\mu\nu} \;=\; \frac{8\pi G}{c^4}\, T_{\mu\nu}$$
through the intermediate machinery $M(\Pi_A) = \{(\mathrm{A1})\ldots(\mathrm{A8})\}$ of Definition 10.9.1.1: the foliation-preserving subgroup $\mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}}(M_G)$; the rigidity of $\xi^0$; the perfect-fluid stress-energy tensor; Noether's second theorem; the resulting partial conservation laws; the on-shell enhancement via the constitutive identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$; Lovelock's uniqueness theorem; and the Newtonian-limit fixing of the coupling.

By Proposition 10.9.2 --- the empty-intersection certificate, verified there element by element --- $M(\Pi_A) \cap M(\Pi_B) = \varnothing$, where $M(\Pi_B) = \{(\mathrm{B1})\ldots(\mathrm{B10})\}$ contains *every* thermodynamic and statistical ingredient of the Geometric route: the isotropic-diffusion equation, the Gaussian heat kernel, the Boltzmann--Gibbs entropy and the Geometric Second Law, the Planck-scale mode count, the area law, the Wick-rotated $x_4$-boost, the KMS periodicity, the Clausius relation, the Raychaudhuri equation, and the null-contraction universalisation.

The certificate's own justifications state the matter without ambiguity. In the paper's words at §10.9.2: the Algebraic Channel *has no probability-density structure* (B1); *no heat-kernel structure* (B2); *no entropy or Second Law content at any step* (B3); *no quantum-geometric inputs* (B4); *no thermodynamic input* (B5, B8); *no KMS or quantum-statistical content* (B7); *no null-congruence machinery* (B9).

Hence the Einstein field equations are reached, in full, by a chain in which no entropy is defined, no temperature appears, no horizon is constructed, and the Second Law is never invoked. **A structure that can be derived without thermodynamics does not emerge from thermodynamics.** $\square$

**Corollary 18.7bis.7 (Jacobson's derivation is correct; his moral is not).** Jacobson's 1995 chain is valid, and it is reproduced in this book as the Geometric Channel route to GR T11. What does not follow is the conclusion he drew from it --- that the Einstein equation *is* an equation of state, and that gravity is therefore thermodynamic in essence, so that quantising the metric is a category error like quantising the wave equation of sound.

The inference fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the validity of his computation: *the same equation follows from a chain with no thermodynamics in it at all.* The thermodynamic route is therefore **a** route and not **the** route, and the equation-of-state reading is a *reading* and not the essence. That a thing can be reached through the woods does not make it a tree.

(Jacobson's *other* conclusion --- that the metric should not be quantised --- is nevertheless correct, and is here a theorem, GR T19. But it is true for a different reason than he gave: not because gravity is thermodynamic, but because the metric is the integrated shadow of the Principle and its source, the rate, is a constant function admitting no fluctuation. See Lemma 14.5.2.1.)

## 18.7bis.4 The generation structure: a fan, not a chain

The Priority Circle of Proposition 18.7bis.1 arises from a shared and unexamined assumption --- that the relation between these structures must be a **chain**. *A* emerges from *B*, which emerges from *C*. The programmes then quarrel over the ordering, and the quarrel has no resolution because every candidate ordering closes on itself.

The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework does not offer a better chain. It denies that there is a chain.

**Theorem 18.7bis.8 (The Generation Structure).** *$dx_4/dt = ic$ does not sit at the bottom of a chain of emergence. It sits at the apex of a **fan**. The structures the emergence programmes attempt to derive from one another are **siblings**, each descending directly from the Principle, none descending from any other:*

$$

 & dx_4/dt = ic & \\[2pt]

\downarrow \qquad\qquad\;\; \downarrow & \downarrow & \downarrow \\[2pt]
\textbf{METRIC} \qquad\; \textbf{NONLOCALITY} & \textbf{ENTROPY} & \textbf{ARROW} \\
\text{signature; light cone} \;\; \text{Bell; null structure} & \text{count; diffusion} & dS/dt>0
\end{array}
$$

*and **gravity is reached twice**, from two different branches of the fan and by machinery that shares no step:*
$$\textbf{GRAVITY} \;=\; \textrm{GR T11} \;\;\Longleftarrow\;\; \begin{cases} \textbf{from the shadow:} & \mathrm{Diff}_{\mathrm{McG}} \to \text{Noether} \to \text{Lovelock} \quad (\textit{no thermodynamics}) \\[3pt] \textbf{from the expansion:} & \text{Second Law} \to \text{area} \to \text{Unruh} \to \text{Clausius} \quad (\textit{thermodynamics}) \end{cases}$$

*Proof.* Each descent is a theorem established elsewhere in this book: the metric and its light cone from Lemma 5.1.2.2 and §6.0.4; nonlocality from §6.0.10 and §6.3.10.5; entropy from Theorem 12, Theorem 10.5bis.3, and Theorem 15.4.6; the arrow from Theorem 11 and Theorem 18.6.3. That gravity is reached along *both* the shadow-branch and the expansion-branch, through disjoint machinery, is Proposition 10.9.2. That no sibling is an input to any other is the content of the same disjointness certificates, verified theorem by theorem throughout Chapters 5--17. $\square$

**Remark 18.7bis.9 (why a fan cannot form a circle).** A circle is a pathology of chains: it is what a chain does when it has no ground. A fan has no cycles to form, because no branch feeds another --- each descends from the apex, and the apex descends from nothing. This is the precise reason the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework escapes the Priority Circle while the three programmes cannot: *they are attempting to arrange siblings into a lineage.* Entanglement does not produce spacetime; spacetime does not produce thermodynamics; thermodynamics does not produce gravity. **They are four children of one parent, and the family has been mistaken for a queue.**

**Remark 18.7bis.10 (the correct statement, stated once).** It is therefore *not* the case that gravity emerges from thermodynamics, nor that spacetime emerges from entanglement, nor that nonlocality emerges from either. What is the case is this:

> $dx_4/dt = ic$ **generates** gravity, thermodynamics, entropy, nonlocality, the metric, and the arrow of time --- each directly, none from another.

The apparent emergence relations among them are the shadows those siblings cast on one another when the parent is not in view. Remove the parent, and one is left with four structures that plainly depend on each other and cannot be ordered --- which is exactly the situation the literature is in. Restore the parent, and each stands on its own descent, the circularity evaporates, and the one thing no sibling could have given the others --- the direction --- arrives with them.



**Theorem 18.7bis.11 (The Four Readings).** *The four structures over which the emergence programmes quarrel are not related as emergent-from. They are four readings of the single active expansion $dx_4/dt = ic$:*

**Remark 18.7bis.12 (why this breaks the circle, precisely).** The Priority Circle of Proposition 18.7bis.1 arises because each programme must *borrow* its foundation from a neighbour. Theorem 18.7bis.4 removes the need to borrow: no reading requires another reading as input, because each descends directly from the Principle. And Theorem 18.7bis.2 removes the *appearance* of three objects that made the borrowing seem necessary in the first place: the causal structure, the entanglement surface, and the entropy-bearing surface were never three things to be related, but one thing under three descriptions.

## 18.7bis.5 Why no metric-based programme could have closed the circle

There remains a question that the foregoing invites: *why did none of the three programmes find the ground?* The answer is not that they lacked ingenuity. It is a theorem.

**Theorem 18.7bis.13 (No metric-based emergence programme can reach the arrow).** *Every one of the three programmes is erected on the metric and its symmetries: the holographic programme on the Lorentzian geometry of the bulk and the conformal symmetry of the boundary; Jacobson on the metric, its Killing vectors, and the Raychaudhuri equation; Verlinde on holographic screens in a metric space; Bianconi on the metric's Lorentz-invariant eigenvalues and the algebra of rank-2 tensors. By Theorem 17-ter (the Content-Asymmetry Theorem), the symmetry group of the metric label is **sign-blind** on the $+ic$ orientation: the involution $i \mapsto -i$ is a field automorphism of $\mathbb{C}$ over $\mathbb{R}$ leaving $(ic)^2 = -c^2$ and every structure erected upon it invariant. Therefore **no chain of reasoning conducted within any of the three can produce an arrow of time**, and none does.*

*Proof.* By Theorem 17-ter, the orientation lies in the kernel of the projection that carries the active expansion to its preserved label, because a symmetry is by construction a structure-*preserver* and preservation is the negation of change. Each of the three programmes reasons exclusively within that preserved label. Hence the orientation is invisible to each, and so is every theorem requiring it --- the strict Second Law, the arrow of time, the irreversibility of measurement (Theorem 17-ter(b)). $\square$

**Remark 18.7bis.14 (the prediction, and its confirmation in the literature).** Theorem 18.7bis.13 makes a checkable prediction: *each of the three programmes will be found to have helped itself to thermodynamics rather than derived it.* The prediction is confirmed in each case, and the confirmations are visible in the papers themselves:

\begin{itemize}
\item **Jacobson** applies the *equilibrium* Clausius relation $\delta Q = T\,dS$, and takes the Second Law and the area law as inputs. His derivation yields the Einstein equations; it does not yield, and does not claim to yield, $dS/dt > 0$.
\item **Verlinde** posits an entropy gradient $\Delta S$ across the screen. The gradient's *direction* is supplied by hand; nothing in the construction derives it.
\item **Bianconi** constructs an action from a quantum *relative entropy* --- a Kullback--Leibler-type divergence between two metrics. It is a *static, pointwise measure of mismatch*, exactly time-symmetric. Nothing in her paper increases; there is no $dS/dt$ anywhere in it. The word ``entropy'' is shared with thermodynamics; the physics is not.
\end{itemize}

None of these is an oversight to be repaired in a subsequent paper. By Theorem 18.7bis.13 the repair is *unavailable within the machinery*, and the persistence of the gap across three independent programmes, over three decades, is precisely what the theorem predicts.

## 18.7bis.6 The statement of the result

**Theorem 18.7bis.15 (Synthesis).** *The structures that contemporary physics calls emergent --- spacetime, nonlocality, entanglement-geometry, horizon entropy, and gravity itself --- are not emergent from one another. They are readings of a single active expansion: its integrated shadow (the metric and its light cone), its null surface (nonlocality), its microstate count and diffusion (entropy, and hence gravity by the Clausius chain), and its orientation (the arrow of time). The last of these no metric-based programme can reach at all (Theorem 18.7bis.6), and that is precisely why the others are locked in a circle (Proposition 18.7bis.1): **they are all reading the shadow, and the shadow does not carry the direction of the thing that cast it.***

*Proof.* Assemble Proposition 18.7bis.1 (the circle), Theorem 18.7bis.2 (the three surfaces are one), Theorem 18.7bis.6 (gravity is not thermodynamic in essence), Theorem 18.7bis.8 (the fan), Theorem 18.7bis.11 (the four readings), and Theorem 18.7bis.13 (the arrow's inaccessibility to the label). $\square$

**Remark 18.7bis.16 (what is not being claimed).** The framework does not claim that the emergence programmes are *wrong*. Ryu--Takayanagi computes correctly; Jacobson's chain is valid and is, indeed, the Geometric Channel's own route to the field equations (§10.8); Bell correlations are real and the holographic dictionary is a genuine discovery. What is claimed is a matter of *priority*, and it is precise: each of those results is a true statement *about a reading of the expansion*, and the appearance that they must be derived from one another is an artefact of having only the readings and not the thing read. Supply the thing read --- $dx_4/dt = ic$ --- and the results survive intact, the circularity disappears, and the one structure none of them could reach, the arrow, arrives with the rest.

*What Jacobson assumed, the expansion supplies. What the holographic programme conjectured, the expansion identifies. What none of them could derive, the expansion orients.*

# 18.8 Closing: Hilbert's Sixth Problem and the Empirical Signatures of the McGucken Duality {#sec:closing}

## 18.8.1 Hilbert's Sixth Problem partially closes in the McGucken Duality

Hilbert's Sixth Problem [54], delivered at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Paris in August 1900, called for an axiomatisation of physics treating mechanics and probability as branches of mathematical physics. Hilbert's formulation:

> "Mathematical Treatment of the Axioms of Physics. The investigations on the foundations of geometry suggest the problem: To treat in the same manner, by means of axioms, those physical sciences in which mathematics plays an important part; in the first rank are the theory of probabilities and mechanics."

For one hundred and twenty-six years, Hilbert's Sixth Problem has remained the most ambitious of the twenty-three problems on Hilbert's list, with substantial partial progress (Wigner's classification of relativistic particles 1939, the Wightman axioms for quantum field theory 1956, the C*-algebraic axiomatisation of QM by Segal 1947 and Mackey 1963, the von Neumann axiomatisation of quantum probability 1932, the Kolmogorov axiomatisation of classical probability 1933) but no unification of mechanics and probability under a single foundational physical principle.

The McGucken-Duality reading of fundamental physics provides a partial closure of Hilbert's Sixth Problem.

**Proposition 18.8.1 (Partial closure of Hilbert's Sixth Problem via the McGucken Duality).** *The McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, together with its two-channel architecture (the McGucken Duality), provides a unified axiomatisation of fundamental physics in which:*

*(i) Mechanics (both classical and relativistic) is the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Algebraic Channel content of $(\mathrm{McP})$ in the gravitational sector;*

*(ii) Quantum mechanics is the bi-channel content of $(\mathrm{McP})$ in the quantum sector, with the Schrödinger equation on the Algebraic Channel and the Born rule on the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel (Theorem 18.2.4);*

*(iii) Statistical mechanics and thermodynamics are the Geometric Channel content of $(\mathrm{McP})$ across all the sectors, with the Geometric Second Law $dS/dt > 0$ as the universal monotonicity (Theorem 10.5.1) and the equiprobability postulate as the Sphere-projection geometric measure (Lemma 18.3.3.1);*

*(iv) General relativity is the gravitational instance of the McGucken Duality, derived along both channels in Chapters 5--17 of this textbook (24-theorem chain GR T1--T24);*

*(v) Black-hole thermodynamics is the meeting point of all three above sectors --- gravity on the Algebraic Channel, thermodynamics on the Geometric Channel, with the McGucken Sphere as the universal geometric primitive (Theorem 10.6.1 area law).*

*The probability content of all four physical sectors is the geometric-measure content of McGucken Spheres or their projections (Theorem 18.3.4), unifying the "theory of probabilities" of Hilbert's Sixth Problem with the mechanical theories at the structural level.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of:

- Theorem 18.5.1 (Universal McGucken-Duality Theorem): every fundamental theory descending from $(\mathrm{McP})$ exhibits the bi-channel architecture;
- Theorem 18.3.4 (Universal Geometric-Measure Theorem): the probability content is geometric-measure across all four sectors;
- Theorem 18.6.3 (Single-Source Arrow-of-Time Theorem): the temporal asymmetries are all $+ic$-orientation content of the Geometric Channel;
- Theorem 18.2.4 (Universal Bi-Channel Architecture of QM): QM itself is structurally bi-channel.

The axiomatisation Hilbert sought consists of (a) the foundational physical principle $(\mathrm{McP}) = dx_4/dt = ic$ with its three Postulates 1(i)-(iii) (invariance, spherical symmetry, monotonicity); (b) the two-channel architecture of $(\mathrm{McP})$ generating Geometric and the Algebraic Channels; (c) the structural-disjointness predicate enforcing structural disjointness at load-bearing pivots; (d) the McGucken-Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ as the universal geometric primitive of the Geometric Channel; (e) the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau = x_4/c$ relating Lorentzian and Euclidean signatures of the manifold. This is a four-line foundation from which all the theorems of GR (24), QM (23), thermodynamics (44+), and BH thermodynamics descend along both channels [1, 2, 4, 7]. The closure is "partial" because the matter content (gauge groups, mass spectrum, mixing angles) is itself a theorem of $(\mathrm{McP})$ in the companion papers [2, 2] but is not part of this textbook's gravitational chain; the full closure of Hilbert's Sixth requires the matter sector developed in the standard-model derivation [2, Theorems 18.1-18.5]. $\square$
