# 19.0 Chapter Overview

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

At theorem grade, the Higgs mechanism, the inertia content of mass, the equivalence principle, and the principle of least action are four readings of the single foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. The orthodox tradition has carried an open structural problem for over sixty-five years: the Higgs mechanism gives fundamental fermions their inertial mass via Yukawa coupling to the Higgs vacuum expectation value, but no derivation within the Standard Model explains why this Higgs-generated inertial mass should also be the gravitational mass appearing in the geodesic equation of general relativity. The problem is documented at primary-source grade across the contemporary literature by Synge (1960), Ostoma and Trushyk (1999), Unnikrishnan and Gillies (2015), and Bin Li (2025).

The chapter imports the load-bearing theorems of [MG-Higgs-EP] and its extension [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple] (the McGucken Higgs--Equivalence-Principle--Inertia--Least-Action papers of the present author's 2026 corpus) and renders them in the textbook's chapter format. Theorem 160 identifies the Higgs field as the field-theoretic pointer to the local $+ic$ direction at each spacetime event. Theorem 173 identifies the Yukawa coupling as the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate. Theorem 187 identifies rest mass as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at the Compton frequency. Theorem 189 (the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem) identifies the inertia content of mass as the resistance to rotating the four-velocity between two extreme kinematic states: perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest, and carried-by-$x_4$-expansion (the photon state). Theorem 191 (the Equivalence Principle Theorem) closes the orthodox open problem: inertial mass and gravitational mass are not two quantities that happen to be equal, but the same fundamental quantity --- the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude --- appearing in two structurally distinct roles. Theorem 192 (Mass-Bends-Space, $dx_4/dt = ic$-Locally-Invariant) establishes the structural compatibility of curved global geometry with the local-Lorentz-invariance of the substrate at every event. Theorem 193 (Principle of Least Action as Wavefront Constructive Interference) identifies the principle of least action and the equivalence principle as two readings of the same structural content: the classical path is the geodesic; the geodesic is the constructive-interference path; both are the path of no four-velocity rotation in the local-inertial-frame sense; both descend from the McGucken-Sphere wavefront content of $dx_4/dt = ic$.

Theorem 194 (the Triple Structural Identity Theorem) closes the chain at its deepest structural layer: the Compton-coupling rate, the inertia content of mass, and the action quantity that the principle of least action varies are not three distinct quantities related by empirical correspondence but one structural content of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront viewed from three angles. Inertia is resistance to changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation in four-space; the principle of least action minimizes precisely this change; the Compton-coupling rate itself is the wavefront-phase advance rate the McGucken-Sphere supplies from every event. Theorem 197 (Composite-State Mass Theorem) with Corollary 198 (Wilczek's "Mass Without Mass") extends the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of rest mass from elementary fermions to composite bound states (hadrons, nuclei), with the proton's mass arising approximately 99% from non-Higgs sources (gluon-field energy, quark kinetic energy, sea-quark fluctuations) and approximately 1% from the Higgs-mediated valence-quark winding. Theorem 201 (Gravitational-Compton-Clock Theorem) is the bridge theorem making the full structural chain explicit: inertia is rapidity-modulation of the Compton-$x_4$-clock (Theorem 189); gravity is gravitational-modulation of the same Compton-$x_4$-clock; the equivalence principle is the structural identification of inertial mass and gravitational mass as the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude; the principle of least action is the constructive-interference content of the same Compton-frequency phase accumulation along the worldline. All four phenomena are projections of one quantity --- the Compton-$x_4$-clock --- modulated by three different physical contexts (boost, gravity, free worldline), with $dx_4/dt = ic$ strictly invariant at every event in all cases.

# 19.1 The Orthodox Open-Problem Status, Documented at Primary-Source Grade {#sec:OpenProblemStatus}

Four primary-source documentations establish the open-problem status across sixty-five years of orthodox-tradition recognition.

## 19.1.1 Synge 1960

Synge, *Relativity: The General Theory* [Synge1960], Preface, pp. IX--X, verbatim:

> "I have never been able to understand this Principle. Does it mean that the effects of a gravitational field are indistinguishable from the effects of an observer's acceleration? If so, it is false. In Einstein's theory, either there is a gravitational field or there is none, according as the Riemann tensor does not or does vanish. This is an absolute property; it has nothing to do with any observer's world-line. Space-time is either flat or curved... The Principle of Equivalence performed the essential office of midwife at the birth of general relativity... I suggest that the midwife be now buried with appropriate honours and the facts of absolute space-time faced."

Synge's structural identification: the equivalence principle, in its post-1916 orthodox formulation, is a foundational postulate that has never been derived from a deeper principle. Synge's proposal to "bury the midwife" with honour reflects the orthodox-tradition recognition that the equivalence principle, while empirically extraordinarily well-confirmed (Eötvös experiments, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017 confirming the universality of free fall to one part in $10^{15}$), is structurally a postulate rather than a theorem in the orthodox framework.

## 19.1.2 Ostoma and Trushyk 1999

Ostoma and Trushyk [OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary] §B, verbatim:

> "IN GENERAL RELATIVITY, THE PRINCIPLE OF EQUIVALENCE MUST BE ACCEPTED ONLY AS A POSTULATE, AND CANNOT BE DERIVED. Why should there be equivalence between inertial and gravitational mass? After all, both these mass types are defined differently in conventional Newtonian physics. Inertial mass involves accelerated motion, but there appears to be no motion involved in the definition of gravitational mass. In general relativity, equivalence has still remained a postulate as first proposed by Einstein, in spite of 70 years of investigation, albeit a very well tested postulate."

The Ostoma--Trushyk electromagnetic-quantum-gravity programme [OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP; OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary] attempts a quantum-vacuum-fluctuations derivation of the equivalence principle; the present chapter records the Ostoma--Trushyk primary-source recognition of the open-problem status while noting that the EMQG programme has not been adopted in mainstream physics.

## 19.1.3 Unnikrishnan and Gillies 2015

Unnikrishnan and Gillies [UnnikrishnanGillies2015], Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and University of Virginia, Gravity Research Foundation 2015 Awards (honourable mention), published in *International Journal of Modern Physics D* **24**(14):1544009 (2015). The paper's title verbatim: "Is the Higgs Mechanism true to the Equivalence Principle?" Verbatim abstract:

> "We raise and discuss the fundamental issue whether the interaction-induced inertia in the Higgs mechanism is the same as the charge of gravity, or the gravitational mass. True physical mass has to fulfill the dual role of inertia and the gravitational charge and should respect the weak equivalence principle. *This is not yet addressed in the standard model that does not incorporate gravity.* Hence the Higgs scenario still requires a gravitational completion."

The technical argument of Unnikrishnan--Gillies (verbatim from the body of the paper):

> "interaction-induced inertia need not always generate equivalent gravity, as we now argue from a familiar example... the effective mass of an electron in a solid can be negative or even diverge in magnitude, seemingly without any gravitational signature, signifying that the inertia generated by interaction in that case is only a pseudo-mass without a gravitational implication... This fact immediately instructs us to be cautious about any scheme that merely provides inertia in the sense of enhanced reluctance to free motion, without generating enhanced gravitational field."

Their conclusion verbatim:

> "Inertia that does not contribute its full gravitational equivalence is not true mass. Gravitational mass could be more fundamental than inertial mass and the hardest task of the theory is to explain the origin of the gravitational mass."

## 19.1.4 Bin Li 2025

Bin Li [BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory], "Revisiting Mass Generation: Higgs Mechanism and a Topological Alternative via Chronon Field Theory," Preprints.org 202506.2073 (June 2025), DOI 10.20944/preprints202506.2073.v1, §3.4 verbatim:

> "Another deep shortcoming of the Higgs mechanism is its failure to illuminate the equivalence between inertial and gravitational mass... in the SM framework, mass arises from interactions with the Higgs field, a scalar field that does not couple to spacetime curvature in any fundamental way. The mechanism is agnostic about gravity: it describes how particles resist acceleration due to Higgs-mediated interactions, but not how they gravitate. *There is no derivation within the SM showing why a particle's inertial mass, generated by the Higgs field, should also be the quantity appearing in the geodesic equation of GR.*"

Bin Li's Chronon Field Theory proposal --- a unit-norm future-directed timelike vector field $\Phi^\mu$ with $\Phi^\mu \Phi_\mu = -1$ as the ontological substrate, with mass arising from solitonic excitations producing both inertial and gravitational mass --- is the contemporary primary-source articulation closest in structural spirit to the McGucken framework: both treat the fourth (temporal) direction as the foundational structural source, and both propose that inertial and gravitational mass coincide because they have a common foundational origin. The two frameworks are structurally distinct: Chronon Field Theory has a unit-norm timelike vector field with no derivation of $c$ or $\hbar$ from the principle, no McGucken-Sphere wavefront content, no dual-channel architecture, and no unification with the Standard Model gauge content; the McGucken framework has the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ from which $c$ and $\hbar$ are derived ([MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]), the McGucken-Sphere wavefront, the dual-channel architecture, and theorem-grade derivation of $U(1)_Y \times \mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times \mathrm{SU}(3)_c$ and the Higgs sector. The two frameworks share the structural insight that the equivalence problem is closed by identifying inertial and gravitational mass as the same fundamental thing under a common foundational principle, with distinct technical content.

# 19.2 The Higgs as Field-Theoretic Pointer to $+ic$, and the Yukawa Coupling as Species-Specific $x_4$-Winding Rate {#sec:HiggsPointer-Yukawa}

The McGucken framework supplies a foundational physical interpretation of the Higgs field, absent from every prior treatment: the Higgs field $H$ is the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$ direction at each spacetime event. The Higgs is not an additional postulated field but the field-theoretic record of the foundational physical principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. Its four real components are the three orientation angles plus one magnitude of the unit vector specifying the $+ic$ direction in 4-space; its vacuum expectation value $\langle H\rangle \neq 0$ records the direction in which $x_4$ is locally expanding at each event; its Yukawa couplings to fermions determine the species-specific rate at which each fermion species winds perpendicular through $x_4$.

## 19.2.1 Theorem 160: The Higgs as Pointer to $+ic$

**Theorem 160 (Higgs as $+ic$-pointer [MG-Higgs2026; MG-Higgs-EP]).** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and the global uniformity postulate. Assume further:

- The local symmetry group acting on field-theoretic encodings of the $+ic$ direction is a Lie group $G_{\mathrm{or}}$ containing $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ as the universal cover of the spatial-frame rotation subgroup orthogonal to $+ic$.
- Among $G_{\mathrm{or}}$-modules, the chosen encoding $H$ realises the smallest-dimensional faithful complex representation.

Then the Higgs field $H$:

1. is a doublet of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factor of $G_{\mathrm{or}}$;
2. has four real components splitting as three orientation parameters plus one magnitude;
3. satisfies $|\langle H\rangle|(p) > 0$ for every $p \in \mathcal{M}$.

The chirality of the surviving $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ factor is identified with $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ rather than with $\mathrm{SU}(2)_{\mathrm{diag}}$ via the stabilizer-reduction route of [MG-Higgs-EP Theorem 56].

*Proof outline.* The McGucken Principle specifies, at each $p \in \mathcal{M}$, a one-dimensional real subspace of $T_p \mathcal{M}$: the $+ic$ direction. Recording this direction in field-theoretic data requires three real parameters specifying the orientation of this 1D subspace within the 4D tangent space (a point in the coset $S^3/\mathbb{Z}_2 \cong \mathbb{R}P^3$, whose universal cover is $S^3 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ as a manifold) plus one real parameter for magnitude, totalling $3 + 1 = 4$ real components. This matches $\dim_\mathbb{R} H = 4$. The smallest faithful complex representation of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the fundamental $\mathbf{2}$, of complex dimension 2 and real dimension 4. By the smallest-representation assumption, $H$ is in this representation: $H \in \mathbb{C}^2$ as a $\mathbf{2}$ of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. The non-vanishing follows by contradiction: if $|\langle H\rangle|(p) = 0$ at some $p$, the encoding records no orientation at $p$, contradicting the foundational specification of $+ic$ at every $p$ with $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$. Full proof at [MG-Higgs-EP §5.1].

**Lemma 160.2 (directedness selects $S^3\cong\mathrm{SU}(2)$ with no quotient and no cover --- G1, proved).** *Component (iii) of $(\mathrm{McP})$ (Monotonicity: the advance is $+ic$, not $-ic$) makes the local advance a directed unit four-vector --- a specific unit vector in $\mathbb{R}^4$, not identified with its negative. The space of directed unit four-vectors is the 3-sphere $S^3=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^4:|v|=1\}$, which under unit-quaternion multiplication is a Lie group isomorphic to $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. No quotient by $\pm 1$ and no passage to a universal cover is required.*

*Proof.* By definition $\{v\in\mathbb{R}^4:|v|=1\}=S^3$. Directedness means $v$ and $-v$ are distinct, so the parametrising space is $S^3$ itself, not the antipodal quotient. Identify $\mathbb{R}^4$ with the quaternions $\mathbb{H}$; the unit quaternions form a group under multiplication, and $q=\alpha+\beta j\;(\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{C},\,|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1)\mapsto\left(\begin{smallmatrix}\alpha&\beta\\-\bar\beta&\bar\alpha\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ is a Lie-group isomorphism onto $\mathrm{SU}(2)$. The antipodal map $q\mapsto-q$ generates the kernel $\mathbb{Z}_2$ of the double cover $\mathrm{SU}(2)\to\mathrm{SO}(3)$; identifying $v$ with $-v$ would land in $\mathrm{SO}(3)=\mathbb{R}P^3$, the very identification directedness forbids. Hence the directed object is $S^3\cong\mathrm{SU}(2)$ directly, while only an *undirected* line ($1$D subspace) would be a point of $\mathbb{R}P^3$ and require the cover $S^3\to\mathbb{R}P^3$ to recover $S^3$. $\square$

This corrects and sharpens the proof outline's "$\mathbb{R}P^3$-plus-cover" route: the framework's own directedness (Monotonicity) makes $S^3$ immediate, and ties it to the same component of $(\mathrm{McP})$ that orients the temporal arrow (Theorem 18.6.3).

**Hypothesis 160.3 (identification of the orientation $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ with the electroweak gauge $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ --- G3, marked, not proved).** *The framework further identifies the orientation group $S^3\cong\mathrm{SU}(2)$ of Lemma 160.2 with the electroweak weak-isospin gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ that carries the Higgs doublet, reading the Higgs's four real components as the three orientation angles plus one magnitude of the $+ic$ direction, and the fundamental $\mathbf{2}$ as the smallest faithful complex representation in which these four reals sit.* Honest scope statement: Lemma 160.2 is rigorous, but it does **not** establish this identification. The two $\mathrm{SU}(2)$'s enter in different roles --- $S^3\cong\mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the manifold/group of orientations of a single four-vector, whereas $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L$ is an internal *local gauge* symmetry acting on isospin doublets --- and the coincidence of real dimension ($4=4$) does not by itself identify a manifold of orientations with a gauge group, nor a group element with a vector in its representation space. The identification (the Higgs as the field-theoretic $+ic$ pointer) is a physical postulate of the framework, recorded here as a marked hypothesis. The earlier wording --- "the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ structure carrying the Higgs doublet is read straight off," "the electroweak $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ doublet structure of the Higgs descends" --- asserted the identification as established and is hereby downgraded to this hypothesis.

**Remark 161 (The physical content of the Higgs).** The Higgs's role in the Standard Model is mathematically defined (it is the field whose vev breaks $\mathrm{SU}(2)_L \times U(1)_Y \to U(1)_{\mathrm{em}}$ and supplies fermion masses via Yukawa coupling) but physically opaque: *what is the Higgs?* Standard physics has no answer. The McGucken framework supplies one: the Higgs is the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$ direction --- the McGucken pointer. Its four real components are the three orientation angles plus one magnitude of the unit vector specifying the $+ic$ direction in 4-space. Its non-vanishing vev encodes the fact that $|dx_4/dt| = c \neq 0$ everywhere. *The Higgs is the pointer; the McGucken Principle supplies what it points to.*

## 19.2.2 Theorem 173: Yukawa Coupling as Species-Specific $x_4$-Winding Rate

**Theorem 173 (Yukawa as winding rate [MG-Higgs2026; MG-Higgs-EP]).** Assume the matter orientation condition (M) and the broken phase $\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$. The Yukawa coupling $y_f$ of each fermion species $f$ is identified as the dimensionless coefficient setting the species-specific Compton-frequency $x_4$-winding rate:
$$k_C^{(f)} \;=\; \frac{m_f c}{\hbar} \;=\; \frac{y_f v c}{\sqrt{2}\hbar}. \tag{19.2.1}$$
The wavefunction of species $f$ in the broken phase is therefore
$$\Psi^{(f)}(\mathbf{x}, x_4) \;=\; \Psi_0^{(f)}(\mathbf{x}) \cdot \exp\!\left(+I \cdot \frac{y_f v c}{\sqrt{2}\hbar} \cdot x_4\right), \tag{19.2.2}$$
winding around $x_4$ at the species-specific rate $k_C^{(f)} \propto y_f$.

*Proof.* By the matter orientation condition (M), a matter field of mass $m$ satisfies $\Psi(\mathbf{x}, x_4) = \Psi_0(\mathbf{x}) \exp(+I k_C x_4)$ with $k_C = mc/\hbar$. The standard Higgs-mechanism mass formula in the broken phase gives $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$ from the vev $\langle H\rangle = (0, v/\sqrt{2})^\top$. Substituting yields (19.2.1) and (19.2.2). $\square$

**Remark 174 (Interpretive content of the Yukawa coupling).** Theorem 173 converts the Standard-Model Yukawa coupling $y_f$ from an opaque dimensionless parameter into a structurally interpreted quantity: $y_f$ is the dial that, in the broken phase $\langle H\rangle \neq 0$, sets the rate at which species $f$'s wavefunction winds around the fourth dimension. The empirical Yukawa hierarchy $y_e \approx 3 \times 10^{-6}$ through $y_t \approx 1$ becomes the empirical $x_4$-winding-rate hierarchy: the electron's wavefunction winds slowly around $x_4$, the top quark's wavefunction at the McGucken-pointer rate $vc/(\sqrt{2}\hbar)$. The Yukawa hierarchy is the $x_4$-winding-rate hierarchy. The numerical values of the individual $y_f$ remain empirical inputs; the structural interpretation does not derive them.

# 19.3 Rest Mass as Perpendicular-$x_4$-Winding Rate; the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem {#sec:RestMass-MassEnergyGeometry}

The central physical-content theorem of the McGucken framework's treatment of mass is now established: rest mass is the rate at which a particle at three-rest winds perpendicular through $x_4$, observed in three-space as the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$.

## 19.3.1 Theorem 187: Rest Mass as Perpendicular-$x_4$-Winding Rate at the Compton Frequency

**Theorem 187 (Rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate [MG-Higgs-EP]).** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (Theorem GR T1, Chapter 5), the four-fold ontology of [MG-Higgs2026; MG-McGSpace], and Theorems 160 and 173. Then for any massive fermion species $f$ of rest mass $m_f$:

1. **Perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest.** The fermion at absolute three-rest has its four-velocity entirely in the perpendicular $x_4$-direction: $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the $(\hat x_4, \hat x_1, \hat x_2, \hat x_3)$ decomposition aligned with the local $+ic$ orientation. The fermion moves through $x_4$ at velocity $c$.

2. **Compton-frequency winding.** The fermion's wavefunction phase advances at angular frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$ along $x_4$: at three-rest, $\psi(p, x_4) \sim \exp(i m_f c/\hbar \cdot x_4)$, where the factor $i$ is the perpendicularity marker $i = (dx_4/dt)/c$ of [MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]. The Compton frequency is the rate of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding of the fermion at three-rest.

3. **Higgs-vev establishes the perpendicular direction.** The local $+ic$ direction at the fermion's spacetime location is encoded by $\langle H(p)\rangle$ via Theorem 160: $\langle H\rangle$ records which direction $x_4$ is locally expanding, equivalently which direction the fermion at three-rest is locally winding through.

4. **Yukawa coupling sets the species-specific winding rate.** The Yukawa coupling $y_f$ determines the rate at which species $f$ winds through this perpendicular direction at three-rest: $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$, where $v \approx 246$ GeV is the Higgs vev magnitude. The rest mass $m_f$ *is* the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, with units restored via $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar = (y_f v/\sqrt{2}) c^2/\hbar$.

5. **$E = m_0 c^2$ as the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion.** The total energy of a massive particle at three-rest is the energy of its perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$: $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$. The famous mass-energy equivalence relation $E = mc^2$ is the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion through the expanding fourth dimension; the factor $c^2$ is the velocity-squared of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion (with one $c$ from the magnitude of the four-velocity and one $c$ from the perpendicular-direction unit).

6. **Photon limit.** A field with $y_f = 0$ (Yukawa coupling vanishes) has $m_f = 0$ and therefore no perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate. Such a field is stationary in $x_4$: it does not move perpendicular through $x_4$ but rather is carried by $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$. This is the photon state. The masslessness of the photon is the field-theoretic consequence of vanishing Yukawa-type coupling to the Higgs-encoded perpendicular direction; equivalently, the photon is at absolute rest in $x_4$, with $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$ carrying the photon outward on the wavefront.

*Proof.* Property (i) follows from the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ applied at three-rest: the four-velocity has magnitude $c$, and three-rest means the spatial three-components vanish, leaving $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local frame aligned with $x_4$-expansion at $+ic$. The fermion's worldline at three-rest is parametrised by $x_4$-advance at rate $c$: $dx_4/d\tau = c$. Property (ii) follows from Property (i) plus the quantum-mechanical phase identification of [MG-CCR Theorem 3.1]: the wavefunction phase along the timelike direction advances at angular frequency $mc^2/\hbar$, the Compton frequency. The factor $i$ is the perpendicularity marker per [MGWick Theorem 21.6bis.1]. Property (iii) is Theorem 160 restated. Property (iv) is Theorem 173 restated together with the standard Higgs-mechanism mass formula. Property (v): the four-velocity of a rest particle has magnitude $c$, entirely in the $x_4$-perpendicular direction; the rest energy is the energy of this motion; standard relativistic kinematics gives $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$, with the McGucken-framework reading that the $c^2$ factor decomposes as one factor of $c$ from the magnitude of the four-velocity component in the perpendicular direction and one factor of $c$ from the rate at which the perpendicular direction itself is expanding. Property (vi): a field with $y_f = 0$ has $m_f = 0$ by the Yukawa-mass formula; vanishing winding rate means the field is not perpendicular-winding through $x_4$; it is stationary in $x_4$; the field's worldline rides $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$, the photon state. Equivalently, the four-velocity becomes a null vector $p^\mu p_\mu = 0$. $\square$

**Remark 188 (The Einstein 1905 anchor).** The identification of Property (v) --- $E = mc^2$ as the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion --- deserves explicit emphasis. The Einstein 1905 relation, empirically confirmed in countless nuclear and particle-physics experiments, is in the McGucken framework not a mysterious mass-energy equivalence but a direct statement of the energy of a massive particle's perpendicular motion through $x_4$ at velocity $c$. The factor $c$ appears twice because the perpendicular-motion is at the velocity-of-light magnitude in the perpendicular direction: one factor of $c$ from the magnitude of the four-velocity component in the perpendicular direction, one factor of $c$ from the rate at which the perpendicular direction itself is expanding (the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Principle). The combination $c^2$ is the velocity-magnitude-squared of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion that the particle is performing at three-rest. Nuclear binding energies, mass defects in fission and fusion, and the energy released in matter-antimatter annihilation are all measurements of the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion --- a deep physical content that the standard reading of $E = mc^2$ as "mass-energy equivalence" does not articulate.

## 19.3.2 Theorem 189: The Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem

We now establish the geometric source of all relativistic phenomena: every relativistic phenomenon descends from the geometry of four-velocity rotation between two extreme kinematic states, both intrinsic to the $x_4$-expanding ontology of the McGucken Principle.

**Theorem 189 (Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem [MG-Higgs-EP]).** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, the four-fold ontology, and Theorems 160, 173, 187. Then the four-velocity of any particle in the McGucken framework lies between two extreme kinematic states:

**State (i): perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest.** The particle moves perpendicular through $x_4$ at velocity $c$; the spatial three-velocity vanishes; the four-velocity is $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local frame aligned with $x_4$-expansion. The particle has the maximum perpendicular-$x_4$-motion permitted by the Master Equation. Energy: $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_0 c^2$. This is the state of a massive particle at three-rest.

**State (ii): carried-by-$x_4$-expansion (photon).** The particle is at absolute rest in $x_4$; $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$ carries it outward on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront. Its four-momentum is null: $p^\mu p_\mu = 0$. The particle has zero perpendicular-$x_4$-motion. Energy: $E_{\mathrm{photon}} = h\nu$. This is the photon state.

The two states are dual in a precise sense: in state (i), the particle moves through $x_4$ at velocity $c$ with $x_4$ providing the substrate; in state (ii), the particle is fixed in $x_4$ and $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$ carries the particle. In both cases, the relative velocity between particle and $x_4$ is the velocity of light.

For a massive particle at intermediate three-velocity $0 < v < c$, the four-velocity is rotated from state (i) toward state (ii) by the rapidity
$$\phi = \operatorname{arctanh}(v/c), \tag{19.3.1}$$
with the rotation acting in the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane where $\hat v$ is the unit vector along the three-velocity direction. The four-velocity decomposes as
$$u^\mu = (\gamma c, \gamma v) = (c \cosh\phi, c \sinh\phi \cdot \hat v), \tag{19.3.2}$$
with $\gamma = \cosh\phi = (1-v^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. The total energy at three-velocity $v$ is
$$E(v) = \gamma m_0 c^2, \tag{19.3.3}$$
which decomposes into the rest-mass component $m_0 c^2$ (the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion energy) and the kinetic component $(\gamma - 1) m_0 c^2$ (the energy of the rotated four-velocity in the wavefront-direction component).

The following relativistic phenomena descend from this four-velocity rotation geometry as direct kinematic consequences:

1. **$E = mc^2$ at rest.** State (i) energy. The energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$.
2. **$E = \gamma m_0 c^2$ at intermediate velocity.** Total energy of the rotated four-velocity at rapidity $\phi$.
3. **Relativistic momentum $p = \gamma m_0 v$.** The spatial component of the four-momentum after the rapidity rotation.
4. **Length contraction $L = L_0/\gamma$.** The proper length of a particle defined in its rest frame as an extended perpendicular-$x_4$-winding object is foreshortened in the lab frame by the projection of the rest-frame perpendicular-$x_4$-extent onto the lab-frame three-space, with projection ratio $\cos\phi_{\perp} = 1/\gamma$ for the longitudinal direction.
5. **Time dilation $\tau_{\mathrm{proper}} = t/\gamma$.** The rate of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding (Compton clock) measured in the lab frame is slowed by $1/\gamma$ relative to the proper-frame rate, because in the lab frame part of the four-velocity has been rotated away from $x_4$ and toward the spatial direction; the lab-frame projection of the Compton-clock rate onto the $x_4$-direction is reduced.
6. **Velocity-of-light asymptotic limit.** As $v \to c$, $\phi \to \infty$, $\gamma \to \infty$. The four-velocity rotates asymptotically toward state (ii). Reaching state (ii) would require complete rotation, which requires infinite rapidity and infinite energy. Massive particles can approach but never reach state (ii).
7. **Masslessness of the photon.** A photon is permanently in state (ii). It has no rest frame; zero perpendicular-$x_4$-motion; it is stationary in $x_4$; $x_4$'s expansion carries it on the wavefront. Its rest mass is zero because, having no perpendicular-$x_4$-motion in any frame, it has no rest-energy from that motion. Its energy $h\nu$ is the energy of being carried by $x_4$'s expansion at the wavefront frequency $\nu$.
8. **Mass as resistance to four-velocity rotation.** Rotating the four-velocity from state (i) toward state (ii) costs energy. The energy cost scales with the magnitude of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component being rotated, which is $m_0 c$. A more massive particle has a larger perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component, and rotating it costs proportionally more energy. Hence higher rest mass corresponds to higher inertia against three-acceleration --- the standard identification of mass with inertia, given a geometric grounding in the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion picture.

*Proof.* Properties (i)--(iii) are the direct relativistic energy-momentum relations applied at rapidity $\phi$. Property (iv) follows from the rapidity rotation acting in the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane: the proper-length extent of a particle defined as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding has a spatial-frame projection reduced by the cosine of the rotation angle, which is $1/\gamma$ for the longitudinal direction in standard relativistic kinematics. Property (v) follows similarly: the Compton-clock rate is the rate of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding, and its lab-frame projection onto the $x_4$-direction is reduced by $1/\gamma$ when the four-velocity is rotated by rapidity $\phi$ from state (i). Property (vi) is the standard $\gamma \to \infty$ limit as $v \to c$. Property (vii) follows from the photon's four-momentum being null: $p^\mu p_\mu = 0$ corresponds to state (ii) directly. Property (viii) follows from the fact that rotating a vector requires energy proportional to its magnitude; the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion component has magnitude $m_0 c$, hence rotation costs scale with $m_0$. The McGucken-framework content is in the *identification* of the two extreme states as the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion state and the carried-by-$x_4$-expansion state, with all relativistic phenomena as kinematic consequences of rotation between them. The rotation is in real geometric space-time (specifically, the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane), not in any abstract or formal sense. $\square$

**Remark 190 (Why the Higgs is necessary for mass).** Theorems 187 and 189 together establish the deep physical reason why the Higgs is necessary for fermion mass. Without the Higgs vev, no perpendicular direction reference is established at each spacetime event. Without the perpendicular direction reference, there is no direction for fermions to wind through; the only available kinematic states are state (ii) (stationary in $x_4$, carried by $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$). All fermions in such a Higgs-vev-less framework would be photon-like (massless and travelling at $c$). The Higgs vev creates the possibility of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion by establishing the $+ic$-direction reference at every spacetime event. The Yukawa coupling then sets the species-specific rate at which each fermion species winds through this perpendicular direction. The resulting winding rate is the species' rest mass, observed as the Compton frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$. **In the McGucken framework, the Higgs gives mass by creating the perpendicular direction for fermions to wind through. Without the Higgs, there would be no perpendicular direction --- and therefore no mass for any fermion.**

# 19.4 The Equivalence Principle as Theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$: Closure of the Synge--Ostoma-Trushyk--Unnikrishnan-Gillies--Bin-Li Open Problem {#sec:EquivalencePrincipleTheorem}

The McGucken framework establishes, at theorem grade, four structural identifications that together close the equivalence-principle / Higgs-inertia / principle-of-least-action open problem documented in §19.1:

1. Theorem 160 (Higgs as pointer to $+ic$): the Higgs field $H$ is the field-theoretic encoding of the local $+ic$ direction at each spacetime event.
2. Theorem 173 (Yukawa as $x_4$-winding rate): each fermion species $f$ acquires Compton frequency $k_C^{(f)} = y_f v c / (\sqrt{2}\hbar)$ in the broken phase, with $y_f$ the species-specific Yukawa coupling.
3. Theorem 187 (rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate): the rest mass $m_f$ of any fermion species is identified with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate at Compton frequency $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$. *Rest mass is the $x_4$-winding rate.*
4. Theorem 189 (Mass-Energy-Geometry, four-velocity rotation): the four-velocity of any particle lies between two extreme kinematic states; inertia is the resistance to rotating the four-velocity away from straight-line motion in four-space, with the energy cost of rotation proportional to the $x_4$-component magnitude $m_0 c$.

The framework also has the principle of least action descending from $x_4$-wavefront constructive interference at the McGucken-Sphere (per [31; MG-Lagrangian; MG-SingularMechanism2026]).

What the existing framework content does not yet establish explicitly is an Equivalence Principle Theorem stating that inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing because both *are* the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude. The present section closes this gap.

**Theorem 191 (The Equivalence Principle as theorem of $dx_4/dt = ic$: inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing because both ARE the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude) [MG-Higgs-EP].** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$; the Higgs pointer identification (Theorem 160); the Yukawa-as-winding-rate identification (Theorem 173); the rest-mass identification as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate (Theorem 187); the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem (Theorem 189); the four-velocity budget $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ (Theorem GR T1, Chapter 5); and the McGucken framework's derivation of the Einstein field equations from $dx_4/dt = ic$ (Theorem GR T11, Chapter 10). Then:

1. **The inertial mass identified by the framework is the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude.** Per Theorems 187 and 189, the inertial mass of any massive fermion species $f$ is identified with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude at Compton frequency $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$. Inertia (resistance to acceleration) is the energy cost of rotating the four-velocity away from the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding state, with the cost proportional to the $x_4$-component magnitude $m_f c$.

2. **The gravitational mass that sources spacetime curvature is the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude.** The stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$ that sources the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ encodes the energy density and momentum density of matter. For a perfect-fluid description of a localised mass distribution, $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ where $\rho$ is the rest-mass density. The rest-mass density is, per (i), the integrated perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude density. *The gravitational mass that sources spacetime curvature IS the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude content of matter, the same content identified as inertial mass in (i).*

3. **Inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing in the framework: both ARE the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude.** The orthodox-tradition equivalence-principle postulate "inertial mass equals gravitational mass" is, in the McGucken framework, not a postulate of equality between two separate quantities but the structural identity: *inertial mass = gravitational mass = perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude*, all three names refer to the same physical content. The empirical universality of free fall (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017) is the empirical signature of this structural identity.

4. **The equivalence principle is a theorem, not a postulate, in the framework.** The orthodox open problem (documented in §19.1 at [Synge1960; OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary; UnnikrishnanGillies2015; BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory]) is the absence of a foundational derivation explaining why inertial and gravitational mass should be the same. The McGucken framework supplies the foundational derivation: they are the same because both are names for the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude under the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the Higgs as the pointer encoding the $+ic$ direction (Theorem 160), the Yukawa coupling as the species-specific winding rate (Theorem 173), and the four-velocity-rotation cost as the inertia content (Theorem 189).

5. **The Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015 heavy-fermion counterexample is structurally engaged.** Unnikrishnan and Gillies argue that interaction-induced inertia (the effective mass of an electron in a solid, which can be $1000\times$ the bare mass, negative, or divergent) need not generate equivalent gravity. The framework's reading: heavy-fermion effective masses arise from condensed-matter electron-lattice-electron interactions *within* a continuum-field effective theory at energies well below the substrate scale; they do not modify the fundamental perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude of the underlying electron (which is the bare Yukawa-induced rest mass $m_e \approx 0.511$ MeV/$c^2$). The effective mass in condensed matter is an effective-theory parameter describing the band-structure response to external fields; it is not a perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude. The framework's identification (i)--(iii) therefore correctly distinguishes *true* inertial mass (perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, identical to gravitational mass) from *effective-theory band-structure* inertial mass (a condensed-matter response parameter, not identical to gravitational mass). The Unnikrishnan--Gillies counterexample does not falsify the framework's identification; it confirms that the framework's identification operates at the fundamental-mass level, with band-structure effective masses correctly treated as effective-theory parameters that do not source proportionally enhanced gravity.

**The structural conclusion:** the orthodox open problem documented by Synge 1960, Ostoma--Trushyk 1999, Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015, and Bin Li 2025 is closed at theorem grade in the McGucken framework. The equivalence principle is not a postulate but a structural identity: inertial mass and gravitational mass are the same thing because both are the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, with the Higgs supplying the $+ic$ direction reference and the Yukawa coupling supplying the species-specific winding rate.

*Proof.* Property (i) is documentary at Theorems 187 and 189. G1 grade for the rest-mass identification; G2 grade for the structural identification of inertia as resistance to four-velocity rotation. Property (ii) is structural identification: the stress-energy tensor of matter at rest is $T^{00} = \rho c^2$ with $\rho$ the rest-mass density; the rest-mass density of localised matter is, per (i), the integrated perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude density. The Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ are themselves derived in the framework's GR corpus (Theorem GR T11, Chapter 10); the present section does not re-derive them. Property (iii) follows from combining (i) and (ii): the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude that supplies the four-velocity-rotation-resistance of (i) also supplies the stress-energy-tensor source of (ii). Property (iv) is the synthesis closure: the orthodox open problem is documented at primary-source grade, and Properties (i)--(iii) supply the structural derivation. Property (v) is the framework's engagement of the Unnikrishnan--Gillies heavy-fermion counterexample. $\square$

**Remark 191.1 (the equivalence principle as the two read-offs of one four-momentum component).** The structural identity of Theorem 191 has a single-object grounding in the four-momentum $p^\mu = m_0 u^\mu$. At three-rest $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$, so $p^\mu = (m_0 c, 0, 0, 0)$: the entire four-momentum sits in its $x_4$-component $p^4 = m_0 c = \hbar\, k_C^{(f)}$, exactly $\hbar$ times the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of Theorem 187. The two roles of mass are two read-offs of this one component:

\begin{itemize}
\item *Inertial role.* By Theorem 189, property (viii), the cost of rotating the four-velocity away from the perpendicular-$x_4$ state scales with the magnitude of the $x_4$-component being rotated --- that magnitude is $p^4 = m_0 c$. Inertia is the resistance to rotating $p^4$ toward the null (photon) state.
\item *Gravitational role.* The rest-frame stress-energy is $T^{00} = \rho c^2$; for number density $n$ this is $T^{00} = n\, p^4 c$, so the source of curvature in $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G\, T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ is the density of the same $x_4$-component $p^4$.
\end{itemize}

Inertial mass and gravitational mass are therefore not two quantities that happen to be equal but two ways of reading the $x_4$-component of one four-momentum --- which is, by Theorem 187, $\hbar$ times the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate that the Higgs pointer (Theorem 160) and the Yukawa coupling (Theorem 173) fix. The equivalence principle is the statement that a single four-vector has a single fourth component, read once as resistance-to-rotation and once as curvature-source. The Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ --- whose $-c^2$ is the $(ic)^2$ of the principle --- guarantees that this fourth component is, frame-covariantly, the same object in every local inertial frame, so the identity holds not at one event by stipulation but at every event $p \in \mathcal{M}_G$ by the invariance of the four-velocity budget. This is the matter-sector companion of the McGucken-Invariance Lemma (GR T2): there the *rate* $dx_4/dt = ic$ is metric-rigid at every event; here the *winding* of matter through that rate, $p^4 = \hbar k_C$, is the one component whose two read-offs are inertia and gravitation.

**Honest scope of Theorem 191.** The framework establishes the equivalence principle as a structural identity at the foundational-principle level. *The framework does not derive the numerical magnitudes of the Yukawa couplings $y_e$ through $y_t$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$*; the numerical magnitudes remain honest-open. *The framework does not derive Newton's constant $G$ from $dx_4/dt = ic$*; $G$ is the third fundamental dimensional input alongside $c$ and $\hbar$ (with $c$ and $\hbar$ derived from $dx_4/dt = ic$ per [MG-Sphere2026 §5.2, §11.2]). The equivalence-principle theorem operates at the structural-identification level, identifying inertial and gravitational mass as the same fundamental thing; the analytic-numerical content remains open at the same level it is open in standard physics.

# 19.5 Mass Bends Space, $dx_4/dt = ic$ Locally Invariant: Structural Compatibility of Curved Global Geometry with Invariant Local $x_4$-Expansion {#sec:MassBendsSpaceX4Invariant}

**Theorem 192 (Mass bends space, but $dx_4/dt = ic$ is locally invariant: the structural compatibility of curved global geometry with invariant local $x_4$-expansion) [MG-Higgs-EP].** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$; the Einstein field equations $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$ as theorems of the framework (Theorem GR T11, Chapter 10); the Equivalence Principle Theorem (Theorem 191); and the Lorentz-covariance of the McGucken Sphere substrate at every event ([MG-Sphere2026 §11.2.3]). Then:

1. **Mass-energy curves the global spacetime geometry via the Einstein field equations.** The stress-energy tensor $T_{\mu\nu}$, sourced by the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate-magnitude content of matter (Theorem 191 (ii)), enters the right-hand side of $G_{\mu\nu} = 8\pi G T_{\mu\nu}/c^4$, producing curvature of the global four-dimensional spacetime metric $g_{\mu\nu}$. This is the McGucken-framework realisation of Wheeler's "matter tells spacetime how to curve."

2. **The local rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is invariant at every spacetime event.** At each spacetime event $p \in \mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{G}}$, every observer in their local inertial rest frame at $p$ observes $x_4$ expanding spherically symmetrically at velocity $c$. The Lorentz-covariance of the substrate guarantees that the same $x_4$-expansion at the same rate $c$ is seen by every inertial observer in their own local frame. The principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ holds locally at every event with the same $c$.

3. **The geodesic motion of freely falling particles in curved spacetime is the structural realisation of inertia under $dx_4/dt = ic$.** In flat spacetime, free particles follow straight lines (geodesics of Minkowski metric), corresponding to constant four-velocity, corresponding to no rotation of the four-velocity, corresponding to no inertia work done against the rotation cost identified in Theorem 189. In curved spacetime, free particles follow geodesics of the local metric, corresponding to constant four-velocity in the local-inertial-frame sense (with the four-velocity parallel-transported along the geodesic), corresponding to no rotation of the four-velocity relative to the local frame, corresponding to no inertia work done. *Geodesic motion in curved spacetime IS the curved-spacetime generalisation of straight-line motion in flat spacetime*, with the inertia content (resistance to four-velocity rotation) preserved as the same structural quantity in both cases.

## 19.7.1 The Depth of the Triple Identification

In the orthodox tradition, three foundational features of physics --- the inertia content of mass (Newton's $F = ma$), the rate-of-coupling of matter to the Higgs field (the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ inherited via Yukawa coupling), and the principle of least action ($\delta S = 0$ supplying the equations of motion for classical and quantum mechanics) --- are treated as three distinct postulates. Newton postulated $F = ma$ in 1687. The Higgs mechanism was constructed in 1964 by Englert, Brout, Higgs, and Guralnik-Hagen-Kibble, and the Yukawa coupling rate that determines the Compton frequency was inserted by hand for each fermion species. The principle of least action was developed by Maupertuis, Euler, Lagrange, and Hamilton over the 18th and 19th centuries, and elevated to the foundation of all of physics by Hamilton in 1833 and by Feynman in 1948. Across nearly three and a half centuries of foundational physics, these three were never identified as the same structural content.

The McGucken framework identifies them as one structural quantity --- the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate vector on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront --- viewed from three angles. Inertia is the resistance to rotating this vector; the Compton-coupling rate is its magnitude; the action the principle of least action varies is the accumulated phase of its wavefront along the worldline. Acceleration is the rate of change of its orientation, and the principle of least action selects the path that minimizes this rate of change, equivalent to constructive interference of the wavefront phases, equivalent to geodesic motion in the curved spacetime sourced by the very same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate content via the Einstein field equations.

Within the primary-source literature reviewed at full-read grade in [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple], no programme other than the McGucken framework has stated this triple identity. Newton did not have the Compton frequency (the Compton frequency requires both $\hbar$ from quantum mechanics and $c$ from special relativity, neither of which existed in Newton's framework). Einstein did not unify inertia with the principle of least action via Compton-frequency content (the equivalence principle was a postulate in his treatment, the principle of least action remained a variational principle, and the Compton frequency was not yet identified when general relativity was completed in 1915). Feynman's path-integral construction unified the principle of least action with quantum-mechanical wavefunction phase but did not identify the wavefunction phase as Compton-frequency winding tied to the Higgs-pointer-encoded $+ic$ direction of $x_4$-expansion. The orthodox modern textbook treatments (Weinberg, Peskin and Schroeder, Schwartz, Srednicki, Tong) state Newton's $F = ma$, the Higgs mechanism with Yukawa couplings, and the principle of least action as three distinct postulates without identifying them as one structural content.

## 19.7.2 The Equivalence Principle Tied to Inertia at a Depth Never Previously Reached

The framework's identification of inertial and gravitational mass (Theorem 191) as the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude becomes, via Theorem 194, a deep structural identity rather than a surface coincidence. Specifically:

- *Inertial mass is the resistance to changing the Compton-coupling rate's orientation in four-space* (Property (ii) of Theorem 194).
- *Gravitational mass is the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude that sources spacetime curvature via the Einstein field equations* (Theorem 191, Property (ii)).
- *The equivalence principle's empirical universality of free fall* (Eötvös, lunar laser ranging, MICROSCOPE 2017 confirming the equivalence at one part in $10^{15}$) *is the empirical signature of the fact that gravitational sourcing and inertial resistance are not two distinct physical effects with a numerical match imposed by postulate; they are the same structural content (perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude) acting in two roles* --- the source role (entering the right-hand side of the Einstein field equations) and the inertia role (resisting four-velocity rotation under applied force).
- *The principle of least action's selection of geodesic motion* (Theorem 193, Property (v)) *is the same identity in dynamics: the path that minimizes the rate of change of the Compton-coupling rate's orientation is the geodesic of the metric sourced by the same Compton-coupling rate's magnitude content.*

In the orthodox tradition, the equivalence principle is the empirical fact $m_I = m_G$, with the universality of free fall as its dynamical content; in the McGucken framework, the equivalence principle is the structural identity $m_I = m_G$ = perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude, with the universality of free fall as the dynamical content that descends because the principle of least action minimizes the rate of change of the Compton-coupling rate's orientation, and the change-rate cost is proportional to the magnitude, and the magnitude is the same content that sources the curvature; so the geodesic is the path of minimum change-rate-cost, and the change-rate-cost is proportional to the same magnitude that sources the curvature; so all freely-falling particles follow the geodesic regardless of magnitude (which would be an empirical mystery in the orthodox treatment) because the change-rate-cost-to-magnitude ratio is unity, the magnitude factors out, and the geodesic is independent of the magnitude. *The universality of free fall is the universality of the geodesic; the universality of the geodesic is the magnitude-independence of the change-rate-minimization condition; the magnitude-independence is the consequence of the change-rate cost being proportional to the magnitude; the proportionality is the consequence of all three (inertia, Compton-coupling rate, accumulated action) being the same structural content of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront.*

The equivalence principle, in the McGucken framework, is no longer an empirical postulate but a deep structural consequence of the triple identity of Theorem 194.

## 19.7.3 The Framework's Structural Priority in One Sentence

In the McGucken framework, inertia is not a separate postulate, mass is not a separate parameter, the Compton frequency is not a separate empirical scale, the principle of least action is not a separate variational principle, the equivalence principle is not a separate empirical postulate, and the Higgs mechanism is not a separate field-theoretic construction --- all six are projections of a single foundational physical-geometric law, $dx_4/dt = ic$, with the McGucken-Sphere wavefront supplying the action-carrying content, the Higgs sector supplying the field-theoretic encoding of the $+ic$ direction, the Yukawa couplings supplying the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rates, the Compton frequency supplying the rate magnitude, the four-velocity rotation supplying the inertia content, and the Einstein field equations supplying the curved-spacetime extension --- all six unified at theorem grade by the triple identity of Theorem 194.

# 19.8 Composite-State Mass as Integrated Perpendicular-$x_4$-Winding Rate: The Framework's Reading of Wilczek's "Mass Without Mass" {#sec:CompositeStateMass}

Theorem 187 establishes the framework's identification of rest mass with the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate for elementary fermions, with the Higgs vev as the $+ic$-direction encoder and the Yukawa coupling as the species-specific winding-rate dial. This covers the elementary fermions (electrons, charged leptons, quarks) and the gauge bosons that acquire mass through electroweak symmetry breaking ($W^\pm$, $Z$). It does not yet address the dominant numerical contribution to the mass of ordinary visible matter: the proton's mass, of which only a small fraction is contributed by the valence-quark Yukawa-induced winding. Wilczek's three foundational treatments [Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI; Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII; Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass] establish the empirical fact: the bulk of the mass of ordinary matter arises from the back-reaction of color gluon fields in the QCD vacuum upon the confined quarks, not from the quarks' intrinsic Higgs-induced masses.

## 19.8.1 Wilczek's Three Foundational Statements (Verbatim)

For self-containment, we record the three primary statements from [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple §H11.5]:

*Wilczek 1999* [Wilczek1999MassWithoutMassI p. 11]: "The bulk of the mass of ordinary matter (better than 99%) comes from the masses of protons and neutrons. ... Let us set [the up and down quark masses] to zero. Now our resulting truncated, approximate version of QCD contains no mass terms at all. ... Yet, if we use it to calculate the mass of protons and neutrons --- the mass of ordinary matter --- we find it is accurate to within 10%! ... The energy in this field is ... what mostly makes us weigh. It thus provides, quite literally, 'mass without mass.'"

*Wilczek 2000* [Wilczek2000MassWithoutMassII p. 13]: "Most of the mass of ordinary matter, for sure, is the pure energy of moving quarks and gluons. The remainder, a quantitatively small but qualitatively crucial remainder --- it includes the mass of electrons --- is all ascribed to the confounding influence of a pervasive medium, the Higgs field condensate."

*Wilczek 2012* [Wilczek2012OriginsOfMass §III, pp. 10--11]: "Most ($\sim 95\%$) of the mass of protons and neutrons, and thus of ordinary matter, is due to the back-reaction of color gluon fields resisting accelerated motion of the quarks and gluons inside."

The empirical fact recorded by Wilczek across these three sources is unambiguous: of the proton mass $m_p \approx 938.3$ MeV, the contribution from the valence quarks' Higgs-induced rest masses ($2 m_u + m_d \approx 8.99$ MeV) is approximately $1\%$, with the remaining $\sim 99\%$ arising dynamically from the QCD vacuum's interaction with the confined quarks and gluons.

## 19.8.2 Theorem 197: Composite-State Mass as Integrated Perpendicular-$x_4$-Winding Rate

**Theorem 197 (Composite-state mass as integrated perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate of internal degrees of freedom) [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple].** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, Theorem 187 (rest mass as perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate), Theorem 189 (mass-energy as four-velocity rotation), and the validity of relativistic energy-momentum conservation for bound states. Let $|B\rangle$ be a bound state of internal degrees of freedom (constituent fields, gauge-field configurations, vacuum-fluctuation modes), with total four-momentum $P^\mu$. Define the rest mass $m_B$ of the bound state by $P^\mu P_\mu = -m_B^2 c^2$ in the bound-state's rest frame. Then:

1. **Composite Compton frequency.** The bound state's wavefunction (centre-of-energy wavefunction) winds at the composite Compton frequency $\omega_C^B = m_B c^2/\hbar$. This is Theorem 187, Property (ii), applied to the bound state as a localised quantum entity with definite rest mass $m_B$.

2. **Composite four-velocity is perpendicular to three-space at three-rest.** By the Master Equation $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ applied to the centre-of-energy four-velocity, the bound state at three-rest has $u^\mu_B = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local $(\hat x_4, \hat x_1, \hat x_2, \hat x_3)$ decomposition.

3. **Energy accounting in the bound-state rest frame.** The total energy of the bound state at three-rest decomposes into the contributions of its internal degrees of freedom in the centre-of-energy frame:
$$E_B^{\rm rest} = m_B c^2 = \sum_{\rm constituent\ fermions} \left[ m_f c^2 + K_f \right] + E_{\rm gauge-fields} + E_{\rm vacuum-fluctuations} + E_{\rm potential}, \tag{19.8.1}$$
where $K_f$ is the kinetic energy of constituent fermion $f$ in the bound-state rest frame, $E_{\rm gauge-fields}$ is the energy stored in the gauge fields binding the constituents (for the proton, the colour-electric and colour-magnetic gluon-field energies), $E_{\rm vacuum-fluctuations}$ is the energy of virtual-particle fluctuations, and $E_{\rm potential}$ encodes binding-potential contributions.

4. **Each internal degree of freedom contributes its own perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.** By Theorem 187, each constituent fermion at instantaneous rest in some local frame contributes a winding-rate term $m_f c^2/\hbar$ at the Compton frequency, and contributes total $x_4$-winding-relevant energy $\sqrt{(m_f c^2)^2 + (p_f c)^2}$. The gauge-field configurations contribute through the field-theoretic identification $T^{00}_{\rm gauge} = (E_a^2 + B_a^2)/2$ for the colour electric and magnetic gluon-field components. The vacuum-fluctuation contributions are field-theoretic interaction-energy contributions evaluated in the QCD vacuum.

5. **Composite winding rate is the integrated internal-degree winding rate.** Combining (iii) and (iv) with $E_B^{\rm rest} = m_B c^2$:
$$\omega_C^B = \frac{m_B c^2}{\hbar} = \frac{1}{\hbar} \sum_{\rm internal\ d.o.f.} E_i^{\rm rest-frame}. \tag{19.8.2}$$
*The composite Compton frequency is the sum of the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate equivalents of all internal degrees of freedom in the bound-state rest frame.* In particular, the gauge-field-energy contributions (gluon-field energies, for the proton) contribute directly to the composite winding rate, even though the gauge-field quanta themselves (gluons) carry no Yukawa-induced winding rate at the elementary level.

*Proof.* Standard relativistic-bound-state kinematics composed with the framework's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate identification of Theorem 187. Property (i) applies Theorem 187 Property (ii) to any state with definite rest mass $m$ in its rest frame, including composite bound states. Property (ii) is the Master Equation applied to the centre-of-energy four-velocity. Property (iii) is the standard relativistic decomposition of bound-state total energy in the rest frame; this is QCD's textbook accounting of proton mass into quark-rest-mass, quark-kinetic, and gluon-field-energy contributions per Yang et al. 2018 lattice-QCD decomposition. Property (iv) follows from standard relativistic energy-mass equivalence: a contribution of energy $E_i$ in the rest frame contributes $E_i/c^2$ to the composite mass and $E_i/\hbar$ to the composite Compton winding rate. Property (v) is the direct sum: $\omega_C^B = m_B c^2/\hbar = E_B^{\rm rest}/\hbar = \sum_i (E_i^{\rm rest}/\hbar)$. $\square$

## 19.8.3 Corollary 198: Wilczek's "Mass Without Mass" in the McGucken Framework

**Corollary 198 (Wilczek's "mass without mass" is the McGucken-framework statement that internal-degree perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate contributions can dominate the composite-state perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate) [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple].** For the proton $|p\rangle$, Theorem 197 Property (v) specialised to the QCD bound state:

# 19.9 Gravitational Redshift as Gravitational Slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-Clock: The Bridge Theorem Closing the Inertia ↔ Equivalence Principle ↔ Least Action Chain {#sec:GravitationalComptonClock}

Theorems 187 and 189 established the framework's identification of rest mass as the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate observed as the Compton frequency, with the Higgs vev as the $+ic$-direction encoder. The same identification carries through into curved spacetime: *gravitational redshift is the gravitational slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-clock.* This is the bridge theorem closing the structural chain: inertia is rapidity-modulation of the Compton clock (Theorem 189); gravity is gravitational-modulation of the same Compton clock (Theorem 201, below); the equivalence principle is the structural identification of inertial mass and gravitational mass as the same perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate magnitude (Theorem 191); the principle of least action is the constructive-interference content of the same Compton-frequency phase accumulation along the worldline (Theorem 193). All four phenomena are projections of one quantity --- the Compton-$x_4$-clock --- modulated by three different physical contexts (boost, gravity, free worldline), with $dx_4/dt = ic$ strictly invariant at every event in all cases.

## 19.9.1 The Photon-Clock Mechanism: Foundational Physical Content of Gravitational Time Dilation

A photon clock consists of a photon bouncing between two mirrors a fixed proper distance $L$ apart in $x_1 x_2 x_3$, with the tick rate set by the round-trip transit time $2L/c$. In flat space, $L$ equals the coordinate distance between the mirrors and the tick rate is the flat-space rate. Near a mass $M$, with the mirrors at coordinate-fixed positions separated by $dr$ in the radial direction, the proper distance between the mirrors is stretched relative to the coordinate distance:
$$L_{\mathrm{proper}} = \int \frac{dr}{\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}} > L_{\mathrm{coord}} = \int dr, \tag{19.9.1}$$
where $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ is the Schwarzschild radius. The photon, propagating at the invariant speed $c$ in proper-distance terms (because $dx_4/dt = ic$ forces null worldlines to satisfy $ds^2 = 0$ in the full four-dimensional geometry), therefore takes longer to complete a round trip when measured against coordinate-time at infinity. *The wristwatch at the mass-proximate event ticks slower not because $dx_4/dt = ic$ has changed (it has not; it is strictly invariant) but because the photon has more stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ to traverse while maintaining its invariant $ic$ expansion through $x_4$. The principle stays invariant; the wristwatch responds to the stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$.*

This is the foundational physical mechanism of gravitational time dilation per [5 §X.3b.2], supplying the physical content that the standard general-relativistic derivation lacks. The standard derivation accepts the metric coefficient $N^2(r) = (1 - r_s/r)$ as the source of time dilation through the proper-time relation $d\tau = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\,dt$ without further geometric content; the McGucken-framework derivation identifies time dilation as the wristwatch-rate response to the photon traversing locally-stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ while $dx_4/dt = ic$ stays invariant.

## 19.9.2 The Compton-$x_4$-Clock Identification with the Photon Clock

A massive fermion at three-rest is itself a Compton clock: by Theorem 187, the fermion winds perpendicular through $x_4$ at angular frequency $\omega_C = m_f c^2/\hbar$, with the wavefunction phase advancing along $x_4$ at this rate. The Higgs vev establishes the $+ic$ direction in which the winding occurs; the Yukawa coupling sets the species-specific winding rate. Each oscillation cycle of the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding is one tick of the fermion's internal clock; the wristwatch-rate of the fermion at three-rest is its Compton frequency.

**The structural identification:** *The photon clock of the gravitational-redshift mechanism and the Compton-$x_4$-clock of the rest-mass mechanism are the same clock, viewed at different time scales.* The photon clock has tick rate $2L/c$ for round-trip transit between mirrors at proper distance $L$; the Compton clock has tick rate $\hbar/(m_f c^2)$ for one cycle of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding at the species-specific rate. Both clocks are governed by the same invariant: $dx_4/dt = ic$ remains invariant at every event; the wristwatch-rate response is to the local $x_1 x_2 x_3$ geometry in both cases.

## 19.9.3 Theorem 201: Gravitational Redshift as Gravitational Slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-Clock

**Theorem 201 (Gravitational redshift as gravitational slowing of the Compton-$x_4$-clock) [MG-Higgs-EP-Triple].** Assume the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, the four-fold ontology, Theorems 160 and 187, and the Schwarzschild Theorem of [5 Theorem 12]. Let $M$ be a localized mass producing the standard Schwarzschild-domain metric stretching of $x_1 x_2 x_3$ around it. Then for any massive fermion species $f$ of rest mass $m_f$ located at coordinate-fixed radial position $r$ from $M$:

1. **Compton-frequency dilation.** The Compton frequency of the fermion, measured against coordinate-time at infinity, is dilated by the Schwarzschild factor:
$$\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}}(r) = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \frac{m_f c^2}{\hbar}. \tag{19.9.2}$$
The fermion's perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate, measured at infinity, is reduced by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ because the fermion's wristwatch is ticking more slowly (by the same factor) due to the locally-stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ that the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding must traverse.

2. **Gravitational redshift identification.** A photon emitted by the fermion via a Compton-frequency transition (e.g., an atomic transition whose frequency depends on rest-mass-energy differences via $\Delta E = \hbar \omega = \Delta(mc^2)$) is emitted at frequency $\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}}(r)$ as measured at infinity. A photon received at infinity from emission at radius $r$ is therefore redshifted by the factor $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ relative to a photon emitted at infinity with the same proper-frequency emission. *The gravitational redshift is the frequency-domain shadow of the Compton-clock dilation.*

3. **Equivalence-principle consistency.** A freely-falling observer at radius $r$ accumulates proper time at the rate $d\tau_{\mathrm{local}}/dt_{\mathrm{coord}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ relative to coordinate-time at infinity, by the standard Schwarzschild result. The freely-falling fermion's Compton clock ticks at the local proper rate $\omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}} = m_f c^2/\hbar$; an observer at infinity records this clock as ticking at $\omega_C^{\mathrm{lab}} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega_C^{\mathrm{proper}}$.

4. **The mass-energy of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion is preserved under gravitational redshift.** The rest-mass energy $E_{\mathrm{rest}} = m_f c^2$ is the energy of the fermion's perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$ (Theorem 187(v)). The infinity-observer measures this energy as $E_{\infty} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, m_f c^2$, reduced by the gravitational redshift factor. *In the McGucken framework, it is the dilation of the perpendicular-$x_4$-motion frequency as seen by the infinity-observer.*

5. **Photon limit consistency.** A photon emitted at radius $r$ with proper frequency $\omega$ is received at infinity with frequency $\omega_{\infty} = \sqrt{1 - r_s/r}\, \omega$. The photon, at rest in $x_4$ ($v_{x_4} = 0$; Theorem 187(vi)), is carried by $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$. The redshift arises because the proper-distance traversal of the photon through stretched $x_1 x_2 x_3$ takes more coordinate time than in flat space; the photon's wavefront-riding rate is fixed at $c$ in proper-distance terms but the relation between proper-distance and coordinate-distance is modified by the metric stretching.

*Proof.* Each property follows from the photon-clock theorem of [5 §X.3b.3] together with the Compton-$x_4$-clock identification of Theorem 187. The two clocks are governed by the same invariant ($dx_4/dt = ic$ stays strictly invariant) and the same response mechanism (the local $x_1 x_2 x_3$ stretching modulates the wristwatch rate). Property (i) is the Compton-clock formulation of the standard gravitational-time-dilation result; properties (ii)--(v) are direct consequences of Property (i) combined with the standard relations between Compton frequency, rest mass, and atomic-transition energies. $\square$

**The novel structural content of Theorem 201 relative to the standard gravitational-redshift result:** the dilation is identified as the dilation of the fermion's *perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate* (the Compton clock), with the Higgs vev as the unchanged direction encoder (the $+ic$ direction is locally unchanged at every event; what is modulated is the rate at which the fermion winds through this direction). *The Higgs vev does not change under gravitational stretching; the Compton-frequency winding rate does.* The fermion's mass-content $m_f c^2$ is the proper-frame energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion; the infinity-observer's measurement of this energy is gravitationally redshifted by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$.

# 19.10 Comparative Position in the Primary-Source Literature {#sec:ComparativePosition}

**Remark 194 (The McGucken framework as the first programme to derive Higgs + Inertia + Principle of Least Action + Equivalence Principle from a single foundational principle).** Per the primary-source literature review documented at §19.1:

- **Standard Model** (with the Higgs mechanism postulated): supplies the Higgs and Yukawa-induced inertial mass, but not the equivalence principle (open problem per [UnnikrishnanGillies2015; BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory]), not the principle of least action (postulated variational principle), and not inertia from a foundational principle.

- **General relativity** (with the equivalence principle postulated): supplies the geodesic-equation content of gravitational mass, but not the Higgs mechanism (separate physics) and not the equivalence principle's foundational derivation (it is a postulate per [Synge1960; OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary]).

- **Chronon Field Theory** ([BinLi2025ChrononFieldTheory], June 2025 preprint, not yet peer-reviewed): proposes inertial-and-gravitational mass coincidence via solitons in a unit-norm timelike vector field; structurally closest in spirit to the McGucken framework on this specific point but lacks the McGucken framework's derivation of $c, \hbar$, McGucken-Sphere wavefront, dual-channel architecture, and Standard Model gauge content from a single foundational principle.

- **TEGR/STEGR** (Mancini, Tino, and Capozziello 2025 [Capozziello2025EquivalenceGravities], *Foundations of Physics* 55:69): the equivalence principle is recovered a posteriori in teleparallel formulations of gravity, not postulated a priori; the foundational problem "how we can justify the coincidence between gravitational and inertial mass" is explicitly listed by the authors as one of eight foundational equivalence-principle problems associated with GR; the Higgs mechanism is not engaged.

- **EMQG** ([OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGEP; OstomaTrushyk1999EMQGSummary], 1999): attempts a quantum-vacuum-fluctuations derivation of the equivalence principle; not adopted in mainstream physics; the Higgs mechanism is not engaged.

- **Other proposals** (Dehnen 1991, Chiatti 2025, Supanyo 2021): partial engagements; none derives the Higgs mechanism, the principle of least action, the inertia content, AND the equivalence principle from a single foundational principle.

*Within the primary-source literature reviewed, no programme other than the McGucken framework has derived the Higgs mechanism, the principle of least action, the inertia content of mass, and the equivalence principle from a single foundational principle.* The McGucken framework's existing content (Theorems 160, 173, 175, 187, 189, the McGucken-Huygens derivation of the principle of least action, and the present chapter's Theorems 191, 192, 193) supplies the four-fold structural unification from one foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$.

This is the framework's structural advance on the open problem documented by Synge 1960, Ostoma--Trushyk 1999, Unnikrishnan--Gillies 2015, and Bin Li 2025. The advance is at the structural-identification level; the analytic-numerical content (Yukawa magnitudes, Newton's $G$) remains open at the same level it is open in standard physics.
