# 19.12 The McGucken Principle and the McGucken Sphere: How $dx_4/dt = ic$ and Its Wavefront Relate Compton Coupling, Inertia, the Equivalence Principle, the Principle of Least Action, and Gravity in a Single Geometric Fact {#sec:McGuckenSphere-Synthesis}

Theorems 160, 173, 187, 189, 191, 192, 193, 194, and 201 of §§19.2–19.9 establish, theorem by theorem, the structural pieces of a unification that has no precedent in the primary-source physics literature. The present section states the unification as a single integrative synthesis with the foundational principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ and its geometric realisation, the McGucken Sphere $M^+_p(t)$ of Definition 2 of §1.2, as the explicit protagonists. The five concepts named in the section title — Compton coupling, inertia, the Equivalence Principle, the Principle of Least Action, and gravity — are *five readings of one geometric fact*: the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, from every spacetime event of $M_G$. The dynamics were in the premise. Everything else is what that means.

## 19.12.1 The Foundational Geometric Fact

**The McGucken Principle, $dx_4/dt = ic$.** At every spacetime event $p \in M_G$, the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light, in a spherically symmetric manner, with the imaginary unit $i$ as the algebraic marker of perpendicularity between the fourth axis and the three spatial axes. This is the foundational physical-geometric principle of the framework. Stated as the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ of §1.1, with components the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (i) — universality of the rate $c$ at every event — and the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$, component (ii) — spherical symmetry of the expansion.

**The McGucken Sphere, $M^+_p(t)$.** From every event $p = (x_0, t_0) \in M_G$ and every coordinate time $t > t_0$, the McGucken Sphere generated by $p$ is the spherically-symmetric two-sphere of radius $c(t - t_0)$ on the spatial slice $\Sigma_t$. This is Definition 2 of §1.2. The Sphere is the *geometric realisation* of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ at each event: what the principle looks like when drawn at $p$ at time $t$. Proposition 3 of §1.2 establishes the iterated structure: every point of $M^+_p(t)$ is itself the apex of a new McGucken Sphere; iterating generates Huygens' Principle and the path content of $M_G$.

**The wavefront's geometric necessities.** The McGucken Sphere carries five properties as immediate geometric consequences, not as additional postulates:

- *Rate* $c$ — the universal expansion velocity (Lemma 6, the McGucken-Invariance Lemma, which establishes that the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is independent of the spatial-sector metric).
- *Wavelength* $\ell$ — the Planck length $\ell_P = \sqrt{\hbar G/c^3}$ at the substrate scale; the Compton wavelength $\lambda_C = \hbar/(mc)$ when a massive particle of rest mass $m$ rides the Sphere.
- *Frequency* $f$ — the Planck frequency $f_P = c/\ell_P$ at the substrate scale; the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/\hbar$ when a massive particle of rest mass $m$ rides the Sphere.
- *Phase* $\varphi$ — accumulated along $x_4$-advance, with the imaginary unit $i$ marking perpendicularity to the spatial three-axes.
- *Action* $\hbar$ — one quantum per Planck-frequency oscillation of the wavefront.

The four-budget identity $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$ at every event of every massive worldline (Lemma 11 of §1.4.1; equivalent to Theorem GR T1 of Chapter 5) is the algebraic record of the Sphere's universal-rate property: every massive object moves through spacetime at total magnitude $c$, with the four-budget partitioned between $x_4$-advance and spatial motion.

This is the entirety of the structure. The five concepts named in the title of this section are five readings of what this structure does.

## 19.12.2 Reading One: Compton Coupling

A massive fermion of rest mass $m_f$ at spatial rest IS the apex of a McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ along its $x_4$-direction. Its wavefunction phase advances at the Compton frequency $\omega_C^{(f)} = m_f c^2/\hbar$ — *the rate of perpendicular-$x_4$-winding of the fermion at three-rest* (Theorem 187, Property (ii)). The Compton frequency is what the McGucken Sphere does at the apex of a particle of rest mass $m_f$.

The Higgs vev encodes the $+ic$ direction at the fermion's spacetime location (Theorem 160) and the Yukawa coupling $y_f$ sets the species-specific winding rate $m_f = y_f v/\sqrt{2}$ (Theorem 173). The composite-state mass (proton, nucleus) is the integrated perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate over the bound state, with the ~99% gluon-field-energy contribution to proton mass identified at theorem grade (Theorem 197 with Wilczek's "Mass Without Mass" Corollary 198).

*Compton coupling is the Sphere's apex cycle rate at the species-specific perpendicular-$x_4$-winding rate.* It is what de Broglie 1923–1924 identified empirically as the internal-clock frequency; it is what Feynman 1948 and Bordé 1989–2008 identified as the proper-rate of wavefunction phase advance along the worldline ($S/\hbar = \int \omega_C\, d\tau$); it is what the McGucken framework grounds geometrically as the Sphere wavefront's frequency at the apex of a massive particle.

## 19.12.3 Reading Two: Inertia

A massive particle's inertia is its resistance to having its four-velocity rotated away from the perpendicular-$x_4$-winding orientation. Theorem 189 (the Mass-Energy-Geometry Theorem) establishes the two extreme kinematic states between which any four-velocity must lie:

- *State (i):* perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at three-rest. $u^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in the local frame aligned with $x_4$-expansion. The particle moves through $x_4$ at velocity $c$. Energy $E_{\rm rest} = m_f c^2$.
- *State (ii):* carried-by-$x_4$-expansion (the photon state). The particle is at absolute rest in $x_4$; $x_4$'s expansion at velocity $c$ carries it outward on the McGucken-Sphere wavefront. Four-momentum is null. Energy $E_{\rm photon} = h\nu$.

For a massive particle at intermediate three-velocity $0 < v < c$, the four-velocity is rotated from state (i) toward state (ii) by rapidity $\phi = \operatorname{arctanh}(v/c)$, with the rotation acting in the $(\hat x_4, \hat v)$ plane. The energy cost of this rotation is proportional to the magnitude $m_f c$ of the $x_4$-component being rotated (Theorem 189, Property (viii)). *That is the inertia of the particle:* the resistance to changing the orientation of its perpendicular-$x_4$-winding-rate vector in four-space.

Newton's $F = ma$, in the framework's reading, is the four-space-rotation cost of changing the Compton-coupling-rate vector's orientation: $F$ supplies the rotation work; $a$ at small velocities is $d\phi/dt$, the rate of change of the orientation; $m$ is the magnitude of the vector being rotated. The mass-energy equivalence $E = m c^2$ is, equivalently, the energy of perpendicular-$x_4$-motion at velocity $c$: the factor $c^2$ decomposes as one $c$ from the magnitude of the four-velocity component in the perpendicular direction and one $c$ from the rate at which the perpendicular direction itself is expanding (Theorem 187, Property (v); Remark 188).

## 20.1 Theorem 18: The Twins Paradox via $x_4$-Path Length, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §23] {#sec:TwinsParadox}

**Theorem 18 (Twin Paradox via $x_4$-Path Length, Grade 2 [Time, Theorem 18 of §23]; consolidates [MG-GRChain, Theorem 6 and Corollary 1.1], the four-velocity-budget content of Theorem 2 Part (iii) of [Time], and [MG-GPS-Andromeda, Theorem 5] (GPS asymmetry as continuous empirical realization); the differential-aging asymmetry traces structurally to $dx_4/dt = ic$ — the physical, geometric fact of the fourth dimension's velocity-$c$ expansion in a spherically symmetric manner — recorded in integrated form as $x_4 = ict$).** *The twin paradox of special relativity — that the traveling twin returns younger than the stay-at-home twin despite each twin's apparent right to consider the other moving — is resolved in the McGucken framework by computing the $x_4$-path length along each twin's worldline. The traveling twin spends more of her four-velocity budget on spatial motion and less on $x_4$-advance, so she accumulates less $x_4$ over the round-trip — equivalent to the standard time-dilation result.*

*Proof.* From [MG-GRChain, Theorem 6 and Corollary 1.1], every massive observer has a four-velocity satisfying $u^\mu u_\mu = -c^2$, which decomposes as $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |d\vec x/d\tau|^2 = c^2$. For the stay-at-home twin, $d\vec x/d\tau = 0$ (no spatial motion), so $|dx_4/d\tau| = c$ — the entire four-velocity budget goes into $x_4$-advance. For the traveling twin, $|d\vec x/d\tau| > 0$ during the journey, so $|dx_4/d\tau| < c$ — some of the four-velocity budget is diverted from $x_4$-advance to spatial motion.

Over the round-trip from event $p_1$ (departure) to event $p_2$ (return), both twins occupy the same starting and ending events, but their worldlines differ. The stay-at-home twin's worldline is the $x_4$-aligned straight line from $p_1$ to $p_2$; the traveling twin's worldline detours through space. The total $x_4$-advance along each worldline is
$$\Delta x_4^{\mathrm{stay}} = ic \cdot \tau_{\mathrm{stay}} = ic(t_2 - t_1)$$
(the stay-at-home twin's proper time equals coordinate time), while
$$\Delta x_4^{\mathrm{travel}} = ic \cdot \tau_{\mathrm{travel}} < ic(t_2 - t_1)$$
(the traveling twin's proper time is reduced by the time-dilation factor). The traveling twin returns having advanced less along $x_4$ — having lived less *durée* — than the stay-at-home twin. $\square$

**Comparison with standard treatments [Time, §23].** The standard SR derivation of the twin paradox uses Lorentz transformations between inertial frames or proper-time integrals along worldlines; the result is the same. The McGucken framework supplies a more direct geometric reading: the twins are racing in $x_4$, and the traveler's spatial detour costs her $x_4$-advance. Durée is the proper-time experience of $x_4$-advance; less $x_4$-advance means less durée. The twin paradox is a direct consequence of the four-velocity budget.

**Empirical confirmation: GPS as continuous laboratory verification [Time, §23].** The twins paradox has direct empirical realization in the GPS satellite constellation, which has been operationally verifying the asymmetric four-velocity-budget partition continuously since 1978. The special-relativistic component of GPS time dilation is $-7.214$ μs/day for the satellite relative to the Earth-surface clock, computed from $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ with $v \approx 3.874$ km/s the orbital speed; this is precisely the four-velocity-budget partition of Theorem 18 applied to the satellite-vs-ground worldlines. The asymmetry is empirical and continuous: the satellite ages less than the ground clock by a definite, non-reciprocal amount, with the GPS pre-launch frequency offset built in to compensate. The full development of GPS as direct empirical refutation of strict frame-reciprocity and direct empirical confirmation of $dx_4/dt = ic$ is the subject of Theorem 38 of §20.2 below. The twins paradox is no abstract thought-experiment; it is in continuous laboratory operation in every GPS satellite overhead, with the asymmetry built into the satellite oscillator at manufacture and verified daily by every GPS receiver.

**The deeper ontological content [Time, §23].** The standard SR resolution of the twins paradox via proper-acceleration is operationally correct but ontologically incomplete: it tells us which twin ages less but does not say *why* there exists a fact of the matter about which one is "really" moving in a theory that allegedly forbids absolute motion. ## 20.2 Theorem 38: The GPS Asymmetry as Definitive Empirical Confirmation of $dx_4/dt = ic$ and Refutation of Strict Frame Reciprocity, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §49] {#sec:GPSAsymmetry}

The McGucken framework provides definitive empirical proof that a preferred kinematic frame exists. The block-universe liberation of [Time, §§46–48] has rested on structural argument from the $dx_4/dt = ic$ Geometric Channel; the present section establishes the direct empirical confirmation. The operational time-dilation pattern of the Global Positioning System constitutes a continuous, forty-seven-year (1978–2025) laboratory refutation of strict reciprocal frame relativity and a continuous laboratory confirmation of $dx_4/dt = ic$. The asymmetric structure that block-universe eternalism must deny is observed, sustained, and engineered against every day of every year since 1978.

### 20.2.1 The Empirical Fact

GPS satellite atomic clocks in approximately 20,200 km circular orbits with orbital speed $v \approx 3.874$ km/s exhibit two distinct relativistic frequency shifts relative to Earth-surface clocks:

1. *Special-relativistic slowing* of approximately $-7.214$ μs/day due to $v$.
2. *General-relativistic speeding* of approximately $+45.85$ μs/day due to weaker gravitational potential at altitude.

Net: satellite clocks tick *faster* by $+38.6$ μs/day in the rotating ECEF frame. To compensate, satellite clock frequencies are pre-corrected at manufacture from $10.23$ MHz to $10.22999999543$ MHz. The pre-launch frequency offset has been verified empirically by continuous GPS operation since 1978; without it, GPS would accumulate kilometer-scale positioning errors per day.

We focus on the special-relativistic component (1), since this is what is conventionally said to be "frame-reciprocal."

### 20.2.2 Theorem 38: GPS Refutes Strict Frame Reciprocity

**Theorem 38 (Non-Reciprocity of GPS Special-Relativistic Time Dilation, Grade 1 [Time, Theorem 38 of §49]; consolidates [MG-GPS-Andromeda, Theorem 5]).** *Let $T_1$ denote the strict Einstein 1905 reading absent further structure: "All inertial frames are physically equivalent, and time dilation between them is reciprocal." Let $T_2$ denote the McGucken reading: "There exists a preferred kinematic structure — $x_4$-advance per $dx_4/dt = ic$ — against which spatial motion is operationally distinguishable, and time dilation is governed by the loss of $x_4$-advance to spatial motion." Then the empirical fact of GPS operability with a fixed pre-launch frequency offset implies $\neg T_1$ and is consistent with $T_2$.*

*Proof [Time, §49.2].*

*$\neg T_1$*: Suppose $T_1$. Then for every pair (ground clock $G$, satellite clock $S$) and every comparison protocol, the dilation must be symmetric: $\tau_S/\tau_G = \tau_G/\tau_S = \gamma^{-1}$. This is a contradiction unless $\gamma = 1$, which is empirically false ($\gamma - 1 \approx 8.3 \times 10^{-11}$ for the GPS satellite's orbital speed in the ECI frame). Hence $\neg T_1$.

The standard escape — "$S$ is non-inertial, hence $T_1$ does not apply" — fails because the SR component of GPS dilation is computed from $v$ alone, independent of any acceleration: the formula $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ depends only on instantaneous spatial speed, not on the centripetal acceleration. The satellite's instantaneous comoving frame is inertial to the precision of GPS measurement. The escape requires invoking exactly the kind of privileged structure (the set of timelike geodesics, or equivalently the timelike Killing field of the ECI frame) that $T_1$ disavows.

*Quantitative consequence*: if reciprocity held — if from the satellite's "frame" the ground clock ran slow by the same factor — then no fixed pre-launch offset could correct both directions of time comparison simultaneously, and the system would accumulate inconsistencies of order $(v^2/2c^2) \times (\text{orbital period}) \approx 10^{-10} \cdot 43{,}000\text{s} \approx 4$ μs per orbit. After forty-seven years of GPS operation, accumulated drift would exceed $10^9$ μs $\approx 1000$ seconds, rendering the system inoperable. *The system is operational. Therefore the dilation is asymmetric with the satellite as the dilated party.*

*Consistency with $T_2$*: From Theorem 18 of §20.1, the dilation ratio is $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$ where $v$ is unambiguously the speed of the clock through the frame in which $dx_4/d\tau$ is maximal. By the four-velocity-budget partition $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |\vec v|^2 = c^2$, the frame in which $|dx_4/d\tau|$ is maximal is the unique frame in which the clock has no spatial motion — *the CMB rest frame at cosmic scale, idealized in the GPS context as the ECI frame to the precision of orbital speeds*. The asymmetry of GPS is precisely the asymmetry of the absoluteness index $\mathcal{A}(F) \equiv |dx_4/d\tau|_F / c = \sqrt{1 - v_F^2/c^2}$:
$$\mathcal{A}(\text{Earth surface}) \approx 1 - 7.6 \times 10^{-7}, \qquad \mathcal{A}(\text{GPS satellite}) \approx 1 - 7.6 \times 10^{-7} - 8.3 \times 10^{-11},$$
where the $v_\odot \approx 370$ km/s contribution to both is the Solar System's peculiar velocity in the CMB rest frame, and the additional $8.3 \times 10^{-11}$ to the satellite is the orbit-averaged contribution of its $v_{\mathrm{orb}} \approx 3.87$ km/s orbital speed in the ECI frame. (The instantaneous cross-term $2\vec v_\odot \cdot \vec v_{\mathrm{orb}}/c^2 \sim 3 \times 10^{-8}$ averages to zero over the orbit, since $\vec v_{\mathrm{orb}}$ rotates relative to the fixed direction $\vec v_\odot$; the orbit-averaged contribution is $v_{\mathrm{orb}}^2/(2c^2) = 8.3 \times 10^{-11}$.) The Earth-surface clock has higher $\mathcal{A}$; the satellite clock has lower $\mathcal{A}$; the clock with more $x_4$-advance ages faster. The pre-launch frequency offset is operationally a calibration of the satellite to the ground's higher $\mathcal{A}$. $\square$

**Corollary 38.1 (The GPS offset fixes the *sign* of $ic$, not merely the magnitude of the asymmetry).** *Theorem 38 establishes non-reciprocity --- that a preferred kinematic structure exists and that the dilation is asymmetric. It is cited elsewhere in this book (§6.1, axis $(\gamma)$; Theorem 18.6.3) for a stronger claim: that GPS empirically anchors the **forward** orientation $+ic$ as against $-ic$. That stronger claim requires a separate argument, which is given here, because the four-velocity budget itself is silent on the sign.*

*Why the budget alone cannot fix the sign.* The budget partition $|dx_4/d\tau|^2 + |\vec v|^2 = c^2$ is invariant under the substitution $ic \mapsto -ic$, since $|-ic| = |ic| = c$: it constrains the *magnitude* of the $x_4$-advance and is blind to its direction. So too is the dilation factor $\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}$, which is even in the rate. Every quantity appearing in the statement of Theorem 38 has this character. The five empirical strands of §6.1 --- CHSH-saturation, rotational invariance, distance-independence, $c$-isotropy, Huygens propagation --- are sign-symmetric for the same reason: each is a statement about a magnitude or an invariance, and by Theorem 17-ter no such statement can distinguish $+ic$ from $-ic$. Something *linear and directional* is required.

*What GPS supplies that is directional.* It is this. The proper-time relation is
$$\frac{d\tau}{dt} \;=\; \pm\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2},$$
and the two roots correspond exactly to the two orientations: $+ic$ selects the positive root ($\tau$ *accumulates* as $t$ advances), $-ic$ the negative root ($\tau$ *unwinds*). The budget cannot choose between them; an experiment must. GPS does, and does so continuously:

\begin{enumerate}
\item The satellite clock's offset is $+38.6\ \mu\mathrm{s}/\mathrm{day}$: it runs *ahead*, accumulating *more* elapsed proper time than the ground clock, day after day, in one direction, monotonically.
\item The pre-launch correction is applied in *one* direction only --- the oscillator is *slowed*, from $10.23$ MHz to $10.22999999543$ MHz. Under the $-ic$ orientation, with $\tau$ unwinding, the required correction would carry the opposite sign; the manufactured offset would be wrong by twice itself, and the system would fail at once and permanently.
\item The system has been operational since 1978. The correction is therefore not merely of the right magnitude but of the right *sign*, continuously confirmed for forty-seven years.
\end{enumerate}

Hence GPS measures the sign of $d\tau/dt$, and thereby the sign of the $x_4$-advance. The observed offset is *linear* in the rate --- it is an accumulation, with a direction --- where the budget is *quadratic* in it, and this is precisely why it can do what the five strands cannot. $\square$

**Remark 38.1.1 (why the arrow may not be used here, and what is being claimed).** It must be stressed that the orientation is *not* being fixed by the thermodynamic arrow, and could not be: the arrow is *derived from* the $+ic$ orientation as the Geometric Second Law (Theorem 11 of §1.5.2), so to fix the orientation by the arrow would be to argue in a circle. Nor is it fixed by fiat. What Corollary 38.1 supplies is an *independent, directional, continuously-verified empirical measurement of the sign* --- an engineering fact, checked every day by every GPS receiver on Earth. The logical order is therefore: the GPS offset fixes $+ic$; $+ic$ generates the arrow (Theorem 11); the arrow's five apparent forms are its five projections (Theorem 18.6.3). Each step runs one way only.

*What is not claimed.* Corollary 38.1 does not claim that GPS *explains* why the fourth dimension advances forward rather than backward --- no experiment could, any more than an experiment explains why the electron's charge is what it is. It claims only that the sign is *measured*, not stipulated, and that the framework therefore takes it from nature rather than assuming it. The foundational question ``why $+ic$?'' remains, as it should, a question about the world and not about the theory.

The standard textbook resolution of the twin paradox appeals to the traveling twin's proper acceleration at turnaround. This resolution is operationally correct but ontologically incomplete. ## 20.3 Theorem 39: The McGucken Cloaking Theorem, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §50] {#sec:McGuckenCloaking}

We now address the deeper question: if $dx_4/dt = ic$ furnishes a physically real frame of absolute motion against a physically real frame of spatial rest, why did this structure escape detection for a century? *The operational definitions of length and time have been constructed in such a way that the absolute motion of $x_4$ and the absolute rest of $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ are systematically rendered invisible to any local measurement.*

### 20.3.1 The Two-Loop Tautology of Metrology

The SI definitions of the meter and the second form a closed loop:

- **The second** (since 1967): the duration of $9{,}192{,}631{,}770$ periods of a particular cesium-133 transition. A second is operationally the count of a clock cycle.
- **The meter** (since 1983): the distance light travels in vacuum in $1/299{,}792{,}458$ of a second. A meter is operationally a defined fraction of $c \times \text{second}$.
- *The speed of light is therefore defined to be $299{,}792{,}458$ m/s exactly. It is no longer a measured quantity.*

**Proposition 20.3.1 (Ruler–Light Circularity [Time, §50.1, Proposition 50.1]).** *Any measurement of a length $L$ returns $L = c \cdot \Delta t$, where $\Delta t$ is read off a clock and $c$ is fixed by definition. Hence "the velocity of light measured by ruler-and-clock" is*
$$c_{\mathrm{measured}} = \frac{L}{\Delta t} = \frac{c \cdot \Delta t}{\Delta t} = c.$$
*The invariance of $c$ under local measurement is therefore not only a physical fact — it is partly a tautology baked into the metrological definitions.*

**Proposition 20.3.2 (Clock–Ruler Circularity [Time, §50.1, Proposition 50.2]).** *The length of a ruler is operationally the round-trip light-time divided by $2c$. The "speed of light" measured along this ruler is therefore $(2 \cdot \text{ruler-length})/(\text{round-trip time}) = c$ by construction. Conversely, the rate of a clock is calibrated against the cesium transition, which is itself an electromagnetic frequency — a process whose rate is governed by $c$ via $E = \hbar\omega$ and $\omega = ck$ for the relevant atomic transition. Clocks tick by light; rulers measure by light; light is defined by both.*

**Corollary 20.3.3 (Local Metrology is Constitutionally Blind to Absolute Motion [Time, Corollary 50.3]).** *Any local measurement using SI-defined clocks and rulers is constitutionally incapable of detecting absolute motion in $x_4$ or absolute rest in $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$. The measurement apparatus has been built from the very quantity ($c$) that defines the partition.*

### 20.3.2 The Fatal Conflation: $x_4$ vs $t$

Minkowski 1908 wrote, explicitly: $x_4 = ict$. This identity is the *integrated form* of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$. Note: not $x_4 = t$. The fourth coordinate carries an explicit factor of $ic$, which is geometric content, not a unit conversion. The $i$ is the rotation-generator; the $c$ is the rate of advance. Together they encode the statement $dx_4/dt = ic$, made literal by differentiating $x_4 = ict$ with respect to $t$.

Within two decades of Minkowski 1908, the $i$ had been "absorbed" into the metric signature, and physicists adopted the convention $x^0 = ct$ (real-valued). By the 1950s, common practice further simplified to $x^0 = t$ with $c = 1$ in natural units. *The geometric content of $i$ — that $x_4$ is the spatial-like axis along which the universe advances at rate $ic$ via the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ — was lost.*

**Proposition 20.3.4 (The Conflation [Time, §50.2, Proposition 50.4]).** *In the modern convention, physicists write the metric as*
$$ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + dx_1^2 + dx_2^2 + dx_3^2,$$
*and read $t$ as "time." This obscures three distinct objects:*

1. *$t$ is a coordinate label assigned by an observer to events.*
2. *$\tau$ (proper time) is what a clock reads, which is a path-dependent integral.*
3. *$x_4$ is a geometric axis along which the manifold advances at rate $ic$, the active expansion of $dx_4/dt = ic$.*

*Conflating $x_4$ with $t$ erases (3) and forces the principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ into incoherence ("$dt/dt = ic$"). Minkowski's $x_4 = ict$ encodes all three correctly; the modern $x^0 = t$ convention erases the third by absorbing $ic$ into the signature.*

### 20.3.3 Theorem 39: The McGucken Cloaking Theorem

**Theorem 39 (McGucken Cloaking, Grade 2 [Time, Theorem 39 of §50]; consolidates [MG-GPS-Andromeda, §7]).** *Three tautological identifications systematically render $x_4$'s absolute motion and $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$'s absolute rest invisible to local measurement:*

| Geometric content | Operational definition | Tautology that hides the geometry |
|---|---|---|
| $x_4$ (axis advancing at $ic$) | $t$ (clock reading) | "$x_4 = t$" makes $dx_4/dt = ic$ incoherent rather than geometric |
| Length $L$ (geometric extent) | $c \cdot \Delta t$ (light-time) | Ruler-length tautologously yields $c$ when used to measure light |
| Frequency $\omega$ (rate) | Clock tick (cesium transition rate) | Clock rate tautologously yields $c$ when used to time light |

*Once the three identifications are in place, the four-velocity-budget structure — which is the actual geometric content of special relativity — becomes invisible to every local experiment. It surfaces only in non-local protocols (GPS, Hafele-Keating asymmetric residuals, CMB-frame dipole measurement) and in cosmology (the CMB rest frame itself).*

*Proof [Time, §50.3].* Each identification is a tautology by construction:

(1) The $x_4 \to t$ identification is the modern convention's substitution $x^0 = t$ with $c = 1$, which loses the factor $ic$ that distinguishes the geometric $x_4$-axis from the coordinate-label $t$.

(2) The $L \to c\Delta t$ identification is the SI 1983 definition of the meter as a fixed fraction of $c \cdot \text{second}$. Any local measurement of $L$ using a ruler calibrated by light returns $L = c \cdot \Delta t$ by construction. "The speed of light measured by ruler-and-clock" is therefore $c$ tautologously (Proposition 20.3.1).

(3) The $\omega \to \text{clock-tick}$ identification is the SI 1967 definition of the second as a fixed count of cesium-133 transitions. The transition frequency is governed by $E = \hbar\omega$ and $\omega = ck$ for the atomic transition; the clock rate is therefore set by $c$ via the atomic transition itself. Clocks tick at a rate proportional to $c$ by construction (Proposition 20.3.2).

The three identifications jointly close the local-metrology loop on itself, making the absolute motion of $x_4$ and the absolute rest of $(x_1, x_2, x_3)$ undetectable by any local experiment using SI-defined clocks and rulers. The local Lorentz invariance of physics, expressed operationally, is a partial consequence of the tautological closure rather than a complete physical fact.

*Detection of the absolute structure requires non-local protocols that escape the tautological loop*: (i) the GPS pre-launch frequency offset, whose maintenance over decades of operation is empirically asymmetric (Theorem 38 of §20.2); (ii) the CMB dipole measurement, which identifies the cosmic-comoving rest frame at $v_\odot \approx 369.82$ km/s peculiar velocity (Planck 2018); (iii) the prospective PTA kinematic dipole of the gravitational-wave background; (iv) cosmological age coherence across six independent observational methods, all of which converge on the cosmic-comoving age within the cosmological-rest frame (the McGucken Cosmology paper). Each of these protocols breaks the reciprocal-calibration loop and thereby exposes the absolute structure. $\square$

*Minkowski's $x_4 = ict$ — read as the integrated form of the physical, geometric fact $dx_4/dt = ic$ that the fourth dimension is expanding at the velocity of light in a spherically symmetric manner — was the open door. The community closed it.*

## 20.4 Theorem 40: The McGucken Absolute Simultaneity Theorem, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §51] {#sec:AbsoluteSimultaneity}

The Cloaking Theorem of §20.3 addressed how clocks and rulers, calibrated by $c$ and used to define $c$, hide the geometric content of $x_4$-advance. The same cloaking applies to the notion of simultaneity itself.

**Definition 20.4.1 (Einstein Simultaneity [Time, Definition 51.1]).** *For an inertial observer $O$ with worldline parametrized by proper time $\tau_O$, two events $E_1, E_2 \in \mathcal{M}$ are Einstein-simultaneous in $O$'s frame if the operational light-signal protocol — sending light signals from $E_1$ and $E_2$ to their spatial midpoint as measured in $O$'s frame — yields coincident arrival in $O$'s frame. The relation is reflexive and symmetric but frame-dependent: events Einstein-simultaneous in $O$'s frame are generally not Einstein-simultaneous in a frame moving relative to $O$.*

**Definition 20.4.2 (McGucken Absolute Simultaneity [Time, Definition 51.2]).** *Two events $E_1, E_2 \in \mathcal{M}$ are McGucken-absolutely-simultaneous if they share the same value of $x_4$ as measured along the cosmic-comoving worldline — i.e., if they lie on the same $x_4$-slice through $\mathcal{M}$. The relation is reflexive, symmetric, transitive, and frame-independent: it is a property of the manifold geometry itself, not of any observer's coordinate system.*

The McGucken absolute simultaneity slices are the level sets of $x_4$ along the cosmic-comoving worldline — equivalently, the cosmic-comoving hypersurfaces of the FLRW foliation, with the CMB rest frame as their operational identifier.

**Theorem 40 (McGucken Absolute Simultaneity, Grade 2 [Time, Theorem 40 of §51]; consolidates [MG-GPS-Andromeda, Theorem 18]).** *For an inertial observer $O$ with peculiar velocity $\vec v$ relative to the CMB rest frame:*

*(i) Einstein simultaneity in $O$'s frame coincides with McGucken absolute simultaneity if and only if $|\vec v| = 0$.*

*(ii) For $|\vec v| \neq 0$, $O$'s Einstein simultaneity slices are tilted relative to the McGucken absolute simultaneity slices by angle $\theta = \arctan(v/c)$ in the local Minkowski tangent space. Two events $E_1, E_2$ Einstein-simultaneous in $O$'s frame are at McGucken $x_4$-coordinate values differing by*
$$\Delta x_4 = (ic) \cdot \gamma v \cdot \Delta x_\parallel / c^2 = i\gamma v \Delta x_\parallel / c,$$
*where $\Delta x_\parallel$ is their spatial separation projected along $\vec v$.*

*(iii) The CMB rest frame is the unique inertial frame in which operational Einstein-simultaneity slices coincide with physical McGucken-simultaneity slices.*

*Proof [Time, §51.2].* By the McGucken Principle and sphere-surface $x_4$-locality ([17]), the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma^+(p)$ at any event $p$ has $x_4(q; p) = 0$ for every $q$ on its surface. The cosmic-comoving worldline through $p$ is the unique worldline whose $x_4$-coordinate advances at rate $ic$ from $p$ in the absence of spatial motion; its orthogonal three-space at $p$ is the slice of constant $x_4(q; p) = 0$ in the rest frame of the cosmic-comoving observer.

For an observer $O$ moving with peculiar velocity $\vec v$ in the CMB rest frame, the Einstein clock-synchronization protocol defines simultaneity in $O$'s frame by light-signal exchange. By the standard Lorentz boost from the CMB rest frame to $O$'s frame, the slices of constant $O$-frame time are tilted relative to the slices of constant CMB-frame time. Specifically, two events at spatial separation $\Delta \vec x$ in the CMB rest frame that are simultaneous in $O$'s frame (i.e., share $O$-frame coordinate time) have CMB-frame time difference $\Delta t_{\mathrm{CMB}} = \gamma \vec v \cdot \Delta \vec x / c^2$. Translating to McGucken $x_4$-coordinate via the integrated form $x_4 = ict$ of the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$:
$$\Delta x_4 = (ic) \cdot \gamma \vec v \cdot \Delta \vec x / c^2 = i\gamma v \Delta x_\parallel / c.$$
The tilt angle $\theta$ between $O$'s simultaneity slice and the CMB-rest slice is $\arctan(v/c)$ in the local Minkowski tangent space. For $v = 0$ the tilt vanishes and the two simultaneity slices coincide. For $v \neq 0$, the slices differ by a non-zero angle. The CMB rest frame is therefore the unique inertial frame in which Einstein simultaneity and McGucken absolute simultaneity coincide. $\square$

## 20.5 Theorem 41: The McGucken Invariance, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §51.6] {#sec:McGuckenInvariance}

Theorem 40 establishes the existence of the simultaneity tilt; we now exhibit an explicit Lorentz-covariant measurement procedure by which any moving observer, using only quantities measurable in their own frame, can recover the absolute-simultaneity verdict of a designated privileged frame.

**Setup [Time, §51.6].** Let $S$ denote a designated privileged frame (the embankment in the lightning-train setting; the CMB rest frame in the cosmological setting), and let two source events $\mathcal{E}_A, \mathcal{E}_B$ occur at positions $x_A = -L, x_B = +L$ symmetric about the origin of $S$, with identical intrinsic emission frequency $f$ and intensity $I$ in $S$. For each inertial observer $T_i$ with peculiar velocity $v_i = \beta_i c$ relative to $S$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma_i = (1 - \beta_i^2)^{-1/2}$, whose midpoint coincides with $S$'s origin at the emission epoch, three quantities are locally measurable in the observer's own frame:

1. the arrival-time interval $\tau_{X,i}$ from emission to reception of light from source $X \in \{A, B\}$ at the observer's midpoint;
2. the Doppler-shifted frequency $f'_{X,i}$ at reception;
3. the observed intensity $I'_{X,i}$ at reception.

The *McGucken Invariance* is the Lorentz-covariant combination
$$\mathcal{M}_{X,i} \equiv \frac{\tau_{X,i} \cdot (f'_{X,i})^2}{(I'_{X,i})^{1/4}}.$$

**Theorem 41 (McGucken Invariance, Grade 2 [Time, Theorem 41 of §51.6]; consolidates [MG-Invariance-2026, Theorem A] and [MG-GPS-Andromeda, Theorem 22]).** *Under the standard relativistic kinematics of light propagation, the relativistic Doppler relations, and the intensity transformation $I' = I D^4$ where $D = \sqrt{(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)}$ is the Doppler factor (B-side approaching) or its inverse (A-side receding), the McGucken combination satisfies, for every inertial observer $T_i$:*
$$\mathcal{M}_{A,i} = \mathcal{M}_{B,i} = L \gamma_i \frac{f^2}{c I^{1/4}}.$$
*The two source-side values coincide for every observer, despite the manifestly asymmetric arrival times, Doppler shifts, and intensities individually observed for the $A$ and $B$ sides.*

*Proof [Time, §51.6].* For the B-side (approaching, $\beta_i > 0$):
$$\tau_{B,i} = \frac{L}{c(1+\beta_i)}, \qquad f'_{B,i} = f \sqrt{\frac{1+\beta_i}{1-\beta_i}}, \qquad I'_{B,i} = I \left(\frac{1+\beta_i}{1-\beta_i}\right)^2.$$
Substituting:
$$\mathcal{M}_{B,i} = \frac{L}{c(1+\beta_i)} \cdot f^2 \cdot \frac{1+\beta_i}{1-\beta_i} \cdot \left(\frac{1-\beta_i}{1+\beta_i}\right)^{1/2} \cdot \frac{1}{I^{1/4}} = \frac{L f^2}{c I^{1/4}} \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{(1-\beta_i)(1+\beta_i)}} = L \gamma_i \frac{f^2}{c I^{1/4}}.$$
The A-side computation is identical with $\beta_i \to -\beta_i$, and the same factor $\sqrt{(1-\beta_i)(1+\beta_i)} = 1/\gamma_i$ emerges. The two source-side values coincide for every observer. $\square$

**Operational recovery of $x_4$-endowed simultaneity [Time, §51.6].** The empirical content of Theorem 41 is the following: any inertial observer in any moving frame, using only quantities locally measurable in their own frame (their own clocks, their own spectrometer, their own intensity-measuring apparatus), can compute $\mathcal{M}_{A,i}$ and $\mathcal{M}_{B,i}$ and test whether they are equal. *The equality $\mathcal{M}_{A,i} = \mathcal{M}_{B,i}$ is the operational signature that the two source events were simultaneous in the privileged frame $S$.* The observer does not need to know their own velocity $\beta_i$, does not need to perform any Lorentz transformation, and does not need to adopt $S$'s clock-synchronization convention; the equality test is intrinsic to their own local measurements.

This is the operational realization of the abstract simultaneity-tilt theorem. Theorem 40 establishes that the moving observer's Einstein-simultaneity is tilted relative to McGucken-absolute simultaneity; the McGucken Invariance constructs a Lorentz-covariant quantity that compensates exactly for this tilt.

## 20.6 Theorem 42: The Andromeda Paradox Dissolved, Imported Verbatim from [MG-Time, §52] {#sec:AndromedaParadox}

The Andromeda Paradox (Penrose 1989, Rietdijk 1966, Putnam 1967) is the historically strongest argument for the four-dimensional block-universe interpretation of relativity. Two observers in essentially the same place, moving relative to each other at walking speed, disagree by days or weeks about whether a distant event has happened.

### 20.6.1 The Standard Andromeda Argument

Let $\mathcal{E}_W$ denote the encounter-event of two observers $W$ (walking toward Andromeda) and $M$ (walking away from Andromeda) on Earth, moving with peculiar velocities $\pm v$ in the local inertial frame at walking speed $v \approx 1$ m/s. Let $\mathcal{E}_A$ denote a vote-event in an Andromedan war room at spatial distance $L \approx 2.5 \times 10^6$ light-years from $\mathcal{E}_W$. By direct Lorentz-transformation calculation, the temporal offset along the Andromedan worldline between the two intersection events is:
$$\Delta t_{W,M} = \gamma \cdot \frac{2vL}{c^2} \approx \frac{2vL}{c^2},$$
where $\gamma \approx 1$ for walking speeds. With $v = 1$ m/s and $L = 2.5 \times 10^6$ light-years $= 2.4 \times 10^{22}$ m, this yields $\Delta t_{W,M} \approx 5.3 \times 10^5$ s $\approx 6.1$ days.

The Penrose–Rietdijk argument runs:

- **(P1)** $W$'s Einstein-now-slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$ includes a definite event on the Andromedan worldline that is approximately three days after the vote.
- **(P2)** $M$'s Einstein-now-slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$ includes a definite event on the Andromedan worldline that is approximately three days before the vote.
- **(P3)** By the principle of frame-equivalence (no inertial frame is ontologically privileged), $W$'s now and $M$'s now are equally physically real.
- **(P4)** Therefore the vote-event and the not-yet-vote-event are equally physically real components of a single reality.
- **(P5)** Therefore reality is a four-dimensional block in which past, present, and future events coexist as equally real.

### 20.6.2 The McGucken Resolution: Premise (P3) is False

**Theorem 42 (Andromeda Paradox Dissolution, Grade 2 [Time, Theorem 42 of §52]; consolidates [MG-GPS-Andromeda, Theorem 24]).** *Under the McGucken Principle $dx_4/dt = ic$ with sphere-surface $x_4$-locality, premise (P3) of the Penrose–Rietdijk argument is false. The Einstein-simultaneity-slices of $W$ and $M$ are equally valid as operational coordinates in their respective frames, but they are not equally physically real as simultaneity slices. The physically real simultaneity slice is the McGucken absolute $x_4$-slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$, which is the cosmic-comoving hypersurface containing the encounter event. The Einstein-now-slices of $W$ and $M$ are operational projections of this single underlying slice onto their respective coordinate three-spaces, tilted in opposite directions by $\theta_W = -\theta_M = \arctan(v/c)$. The vote on Andromeda has either happened or has not happened in the McGucken absolute sense, at a fact-of-the-matter level independent of which observer is asking. Reality is the cosmic-comoving $x_4$-slice at the current cosmic-comoving epoch; the future does not yet exist; reality is not a block.*

*Proof [Time, §52.2].* By Theorem 40 of §20.4, Einstein-simultaneity in any moving observer's frame coincides with McGucken absolute simultaneity (the physical $x_4$-slice) only when the observer's peculiar velocity relative to the CMB rest frame is zero. For $W$ moving at $+v$ and $M$ moving at $-v$ in the local inertial frame (both with non-zero peculiar velocities relative to the CMB rest frame, modulo the Solar-System barycentric peculiar velocity already documented at $v_\odot \approx 369.82$ km/s), neither $W$'s Einstein-simultaneity-slice nor $M$'s Einstein-simultaneity-slice coincides with the McGucken absolute simultaneity slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$.

Let $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$ denote the McGucken absolute simultaneity slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$, defined as the cosmic-comoving hypersurface (the set of events sharing $\mathcal{E}_W$'s $x_4$-coordinate value as measured along the cosmic-comoving worldline through $\mathcal{E}_W$). By the McGucken Sphere Uniqueness Theorem ([17]), $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$ is a single physical hypersurface, observer-independent, with all events on it sharing a common $x_4$-value.

Let $\Sigma_W$ and $\Sigma_M$ denote the Einstein-simultaneity-slices through $\mathcal{E}_W$ in $W$'s and $M$'s rest frames respectively. By the standard relativistic kinematics of Lorentz boost from the cosmic-comoving frame, $\Sigma_W$ and $\Sigma_M$ are three-dimensional hyperplanes tilted from $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$ by angles $\theta_W = +\arctan(v/c)$ and $\theta_M = -\arctan(v/c)$ respectively. The vote-event $\mathcal{E}_A$ on the Andromedan worldline lies either on $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$ or it does not; this is the McGucken absolute simultaneity fact about whether the vote-event is McGucken-simultaneous with $\mathcal{E}_W$.

$W$'s claim that "the vote has happened" is the statement that the vote-event is in the causal past of $\Sigma_W$ as $W$ sees it. $M$'s claim that "the vote has not yet happened" is the statement that the vote-event is in the causal future of $\Sigma_M$ as $M$ sees it. Both claims are correct as statements about each observer's Einstein-simultaneity-slice. Neither claim is the statement of physical fact about whether the vote-event is on $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$.

Premise (P3) of the Penrose–Rietdijk argument asserts that $\Sigma_W$ and $\Sigma_M$ are equally physically real as simultaneity slices. Under the McGucken framework, this is false. $\Sigma_W$ and $\Sigma_M$ are operationally valid as coordinate maps but are not physically real as simultaneity slices; the physically real simultaneity slice through $\mathcal{E}_W$ is $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\mathcal{E}_W)$, and there is exactly one such slice through any event.

With premise (P3) false, the inference (P4)–(P5) does not go through. *The vote-event has either happened or has not happened in the McGucken absolute sense, and this is a single fact of the matter rather than two simultaneously real readings. Reality at the current cosmic-comoving epoch is the cosmic-comoving $x_4$-slice $\Sigma_{\mathrm{CMB}}(\text{now})$; the future does not yet exist; reality is not a block.* $\square$

## 20.7 Bell's Spaceship Paradox: The String Snaps because Length Contraction is Real {#sec:BellsSpaceship}

The remaining sections of this chapter (§§20.7–20.9) establish three new paradox-resolution theorems descending from Lemma 12 of §1.4.1.4 (Lorentz contraction as rotation-into-motion). Each is derived here at full theorem grade from existing framework lemmas.

### 20.7.1 The Setup

Two identical spaceships $A$ and $B$, separated by distance $L_0$ in the launch frame, each starting at relative rest with respect to the launch frame at time $t = 0$. Both spaceships have identical proper-acceleration profiles: each accelerates with proper acceleration $a$ along the $+\hat x$-direction starting at $t = 0$ in the launch frame, with the launch-frame separation $L_0$ maintained throughout (by the identical-profile setup, both ships have the same launch-frame velocity at every launch-frame time). A string of rest length $L_0$ connects $A$ and $B$ at $t = 0$.

The classical puzzle: in standard SR analyses the string snaps as the ships accelerate, despite the launch-frame separation $L_0$ remaining constant. The McGucken framework's reading: the string snaps because the proper-frame separation between the ships grows as $L_0 \gamma$ while the string's rest length is fixed at $L_0$.

### 20.7.2 Theorem 20.7: Bell's Spaceship as Material Consequence of Lemma 12

**Theorem 20.7 (Bell's Spaceship Paradox via Lemma 12, Grade 1).** *Let $A$ and $B$ be two spaceships separated by launch-frame distance $L_0$ at $t = 0$, each undergoing identical proper acceleration $a$ along the $+\hat x$-direction starting at $t = 0$. Let a string of rest length $L_0$ connect them at $t = 0$. Then under Lemma 12 of §1.4.1.4 (Lorentz contraction as rotation-into-motion):*

*(i) The launch-frame separation between $A$ and $B$ remains $L_0$ at every launch-frame time $t$.*

*(ii) The proper-frame separation between $A$ and $B$ in their instantaneous co-moving frame at launch-frame time $t$ grows as*
$$L_{\mathrm{proper}}(t) = L_0 \gamma(t), \qquad \gamma(t) = \cosh(\phi(t)), \qquad \phi(t) = \operatorname{arcsinh}(at/c).$$

*(iii) The string's rest-frame proper length is fixed at $L_0$ by construction.*

*(iv) The string is under proper-frame tensile strain $L_0(\gamma(t) - 1)$, which grows monotonically with rapidity $\phi(t)$. When the strain exceeds the string's material yield strength, the string snaps.*

*Proof.* (i) By construction: identical proper-acceleration profiles applied at the same launch-frame time give identical launch-frame trajectories displaced by $L_0$.

(ii) By Lemma 12 of §1.4.1.4: Lorentz contraction is the *rotation of spatial extent into the moving $x_4$-direction* by rapidity $\phi$. The contraction factor $1/\gamma$ is the cosine of the rapidity-rotation angle. *Equivalently, a launch-frame separation $L_0$ corresponds to a proper-frame separation of $L_0 \gamma$* — the proper-frame spatial extent is the un-rotated source of the launch-frame's contracted projection. Specifically, at launch-frame time $t$, both ships have rapidity $\phi(t) = \operatorname{arcsinh}(at/c)$ in the launch frame. In the ships' instantaneous co-moving frame at this $t$, the launch frame's $x_4$-axis is rotated by $-\phi(t)$ relative to the co-moving $x_4$-axis. By Lemma 12, the launch-frame spatial separation $L_0$ in this rotated configuration corresponds to a proper-frame separation $L_0 \cosh(\phi(t)) = L_0 \gamma(t)$, with the launch-frame measurement being the $\cos\theta = 1/\gamma$ projection of the proper-frame extent.

(iii) The string is a material object with fixed rest-frame proper length $L_0$. Its rest-frame proper length is the measurement of its spatial extent in its own instantaneous co-moving frame at any event of its worldline.

(iv) The string's instantaneous co-moving frame coincides with that of the ships at every $t$ (since the string is attached to both ships). At launch-frame time $t$, the proper-frame separation between the ships' attachment points is $L_0 \gamma(t)$ by (ii), while the string's proper rest length is $L_0$ by (iii). The proper-frame tensile strain is therefore
$$\epsilon(t) = \frac{L_0 \gamma(t) - L_0}{L_0} = \gamma(t) - 1,$$
which grows monotonically with $\phi(t)$. When $\gamma(t) - 1$ exceeds the string's material yield strain $\epsilon_{\mathrm{yield}}$, the string fractures. $\square$

**Structural reading.** *The string snaps because length contraction is real, not perspectival.* The launch-frame's "constant separation $L_0$" is the un-rotated projection of a growing proper-frame separation $L_0 \gamma(t)$. The proper-frame separation grows because both ships have rotated their four-velocity $K^\mu$ into the spatial direction by rapidity $\phi(t)$: by Lemma 12, the spatial axes of their proper frames have been partially rotated into $x_4$. The launch-frame measurement of constant $L_0$ corresponds to a proper-frame extent of $L_0 \gamma(t)$ that the string cannot accommodate without stretching beyond its yield strain. The McGucken framework's reading is that the material consequence is real because *spatial extent has been partially rotated into the moving $x_4$-direction by rapidity $\phi$, and the launch-frame projection $L_0$ corresponds to a proper-frame extent $L_0 \gamma$ that grows as the ships accelerate.*

### 20.7.3 Corollary: Any Extended Object at High $v$ Has the Same Strain

**Corollary 20.7.1 (Universal Bell Strain at High Velocity).** *Any extended material object accelerated from rest to high velocity $v$ has every internal element undergoing the same Bell-mechanism strain as Bell's string. The object survives the acceleration if and only if its internal speed-of-sound $c_s$ can equilibrate the rapidity-rotation-induced proper-frame stresses faster than the acceleration timescale $c/a$ — i.e., if $a \ll c c_s / L_0$ where $L_0$ is the object's rest length. For slow (adiabatic) acceleration, the object Born-rigidly contracts and atomic bonds re-equilibrate; for fast (sudden) acceleration, the object fractures or fragments.*

*Proof.* Each internal element of the object has its own worldline with $K^\mu$ rotating by rapidity $\phi(t)$ during acceleration. The proper-frame distance between any two internal elements at rest separation $L_0$ in the original rest frame becomes $L_0 \gamma(t)$ during acceleration, by the same Lemma 12 reading of Bell's string. The material's internal binding (atomic bonds, lattice forces, etc.) communicates at speed-of-sound $c_s$; equilibration timescale is $\tau_{\mathrm{eq}} \sim L_0 / c_s$. The acceleration timescale is $\tau_{\mathrm{acc}} \sim c/a$. Survival requires $\tau_{\mathrm{eq}} \ll \tau_{\mathrm{acc}}$, i.e., $a \ll c c_s / L_0$. $\square$

**Empirical confirmation.** This is why high-energy particle beams in synchrotrons require *adiabatic* acceleration: protons at the LHC are accelerated over many seconds, not in a single kick. Sudden acceleration would tear the bunch apart through exactly the Bell mechanism. Composite particles (protons, nuclei, atoms) survive ultra-relativistic motion because their internal binding ($\sim$ GeV scale for QCD) vastly exceeds per-constituent rapidity-rotation energies at achievable accelerator scales. Macroscopic objects (spacecraft, rotors) accelerated to relativistic speeds would fracture unless the acceleration profile is carefully managed to maintain Born rigidity.

## 20.8 Ehrenfest's Paradox: The Rotating Disk as Continuous-Radius Bell Scenario {#sec:EhrenfestParadox}

### 20.8.1 The Setup

A rigid disk of radius $R$ rotating at angular velocity $\omega$ about its center, with rim tangential velocity $v(r) = \omega r$ at radius $r$. The lab frame measures circumference $2\pi r$ at each radius. The rotating frame's spatial sector is non-Euclidean: by direct application of Lorentz contraction to the tangential extent, the proper circumference is $2\pi r \gamma(r)$ where $\gamma(r) = (1 - \omega^2 r^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$. The ratio $C/D$ in the rotating frame exceeds $\pi$ by factor $\gamma$.

The classical puzzle: Born rigidity is impossible (Herglotz-Noether 1909-1910); the rotating-frame spatial geometry is genuinely non-Euclidean; what happens to a real material disk at relativistic rotation?

### 20.8.2 Theorem 20.8: Rotating Disk as Continuous-Radius Bell Scenario

**Theorem 20.8 (Ehrenfest's Rotating Disk via Lemma 12, Grade 1).** *Let $D_R$ be a material disk of radius $R$ rotating at angular velocity $\omega$ about its center. Under Lemma 12 of §1.4.1.4 (Lorentz contraction as rotation-into-motion) and Lemma 6 of §1.4 (McGucken-Invariance Lemma):*

*(i) Each annulus at radius $r$ has tangential rapidity $\phi(r) = \operatorname{arctanh}(\omega r / c)$ rotating the tangential spatial axis into $x_4$ by angle $\phi(r)$. Different radii have different rotations.*

*(ii) The proper-frame circumference at radius $r$ is $C_{\mathrm{proper}}(r) = 2\pi r \gamma(r)$, while the lab-frame circumference is $C_{\mathrm{lab}}(r) = 2\pi r$.*

*(iii) The rotating-frame spatial sector has $C/D = \pi \gamma(r) > \pi$ at radius $r$ — genuinely non-Euclidean, not a coordinate artifact.*

*(iv) The temporal axis $dx_4/dt = ic$ is metric-rigid by Lemma 6: each rim element's local inertial frame sees the McGucken Sphere expanding at the same rate $c$ regardless of the rotation. The non-Euclidean spatial geometry of the rotating frame is the integrated record of the radius-dependent rapidity rotation of tangential spatial axes into $x_4$.*

*(v) Born rigidity is impossible: a rigid disk cannot have its different radii rotated by different rapidity angles in $x_4$ without violating the rigid-body constraint. The material must deform — stretch tangentially, deform radially, or fracture.*

*(vi) At $\omega R \to c$, the tangential-stretch requirement $\gamma(R) \to \infty$ diverges. No material survives in the rigid-body sense at the rim; the disk fragments at the relativistic limit.*

*Proof.* (i) Each rim element at radius $r$ has tangential velocity $v(r) = \omega r$ in the lab frame. By Theorem 189 of §19.3 (four-velocity rotation by rapidity), the element's four-velocity is rotated by rapidity $\phi(r) = \operatorname{arctanh}(v(r)/c) = \operatorname{arctanh}(\omega r/c)$ from the lab's $x_4$-axis toward the tangential spatial direction.

(ii) By Lemma 12: the rotation rotates the tangential spatial axis into $x_4$ by angle $\phi(r)$, with the lab-frame measurement of the rim element's tangential extent being the $\cos\phi(r) = 1/\gamma(r)$ projection of its proper-frame extent. Equivalently, a proper-frame infinitesimal tangential element $d\ell_{\mathrm{proper}}$ at radius $r$ projects to lab-frame $d\ell_{\mathrm{lab}} = d\ell_{\mathrm{proper}}/\gamma(r)$. Integrating around the rim at radius $r$: $C_{\mathrm{lab}}(r) = 2\pi r$ (the un-rotated projection), $C_{\mathrm{proper}}(r) = \oint d\ell_{\mathrm{proper}} = \oint \gamma(r)\, d\ell_{\mathrm{lab}} = 2\pi r \gamma(r)$.

(iii) The radial direction has zero rotation (no radial motion at constant orbital radius), so $D_{\mathrm{proper}}(r) = D_{\mathrm{lab}}(r) = 2r$. Hence $C_{\mathrm{proper}}(r)/D_{\mathrm{proper}}(r) = \pi \gamma(r) > \pi$ for $\omega r > 0$. The spatial sector of the rotating frame is genuinely non-Euclidean.

(iv) By Lemma 6 (McGucken-Invariance), the rate $dx_4/dt = ic$ is metric-independent. Each rim element's local inertial frame sees the McGucken Sphere expanding at rate $c$ regardless of the rotation. The non-Euclidean spatial geometry observed in the rotating frame is the *integrated record* of radius-dependent $K^\mu$-rotations into $x_4$ at different radii.

(v) Born rigidity would require all elements of the disk to maintain fixed proper-frame separations from one another. But by (i), different radii have different rapidity rotations $\phi(r)$ of $K^\mu$ into $x_4$. The proper-frame separation between two rim elements at the same radius but different angles is $r\, d\theta\, \gamma(r)$ (by Lemma 12), which is radius-dependent. Different radii rotate by different angles in $x_4$; the rigid-body constraint that all separations remain constant in some frame cannot be satisfied because the rotations into $x_4$ have non-zero holonomy around any closed loop on the disk. By the Herglotz-Noether theorem (1909-1910), no rigid rotation exists in special relativity; the material must deform.

(vi) As $\omega R \to c$, $\gamma(R) \to \infty$, so $C_{\mathrm{proper}}(R) \to \infty$ at the rim. The required tangential stretching of the rim material diverges; no real material has divergent tensile strength. The disk must either fragment (at the relativistic limit) or deform radially (dishing inward to relieve tangential stress at sub-relativistic limits). $\square$

**Structural reading.** *The rotating disk is the continuous-radius generalisation of Bell's spaceship paradox.* Each annulus has its own rapidity rotation; the rotations are radius-dependent; the rigid-body constraint is incompatible with radius-dependent rotation into $x_4$. The non-Euclidean spatial geometry of the rotating frame is the material-frame signature of this incompatibility: the proper circumference at each radius exceeds $2\pi r$ by factor $\gamma(r)$ because the tangential spatial axes have been partly rotated into $x_4$, and this rotation is real material content, not coordinate artifact.

**Empirical applications.** Spinning hard drives at $\omega R \sim 100$ m/s are non-relativistic ($\gamma - 1 \sim 10^{-14}$) and indistinguishable from classical centrifugal stress. Pulsars at $\omega R \sim 0.3c$ have $\gamma - 1 \sim 5\%$ tangential stretch; the neutron-star material survives because of its extreme tensile strength. Black-hole accretion disks near the innermost stable circular orbit have $\omega R \to c$; the differential rotation between annuli sources viscous heating, part of which is the accretion-disk luminosity. *The Ehrenfest paradox is the structural source of accretion-disk thermodynamics at relativistic radii.*

## 20.9 The CMB-Anchored Cosmological Asymmetry of Lorentz Contraction {#sec:CMBAsymmetry}

The McGucken framework resolves the *cosmological asymmetry of Lorentz contraction* that standard SR formalism systematically buries. The structural fact: when two observers compare Lorentz contraction in an absolute frame setting (CMB-anchored), the local Einstein-relativity reciprocity is preserved (each sees the other contracted by $1/\gamma$), but the *cosmological-rest-frame energy content, the CMB dipole signature, the material strain history, and the $K^\mu$-rotation angle relative to cosmological $\hat x_4$* are all asymmetric. This asymmetry is invisible to local protocols (by the Cloaking Theorem of §20.3) but exposed by non-local protocols (CMB dipole, GPS asymmetry, cosmological age coherence).

### 20.9.1 The Comparison: Static Rotated Rulers vs Moving Ships

Consider two parallel rulers $A$ and $B$ of rest length $L_0$ in a static $(x, y)$ plane with no moving dimension. Ruler $A$ lies along the $x$-axis; ruler $B$ is rotated by angle $\theta$ in the $(x, y)$ plane. The projection of $B$ onto $A$'s direction is $L_0 \cos\theta$; the projection of $A$ onto $B$'s direction is $L_0 \cos\theta$. *The symmetry is exact and purely geometric*: no material strain, no energy difference, no breaking; each ruler sees the other foreshortened by the same factor.

Now consider two ships $A$ and $B$ passing one another with relative velocity $0.9c$. By standard SR formalism, the situation looks identical to the rotated-rulers case: each ship measures the other's spatial extent foreshortened by $1/\gamma \approx 0.436$. Standard SR reads the symmetry as exact.

**But there is a structural asymmetry that the standard analysis cannot surface and the McGucken framework makes explicit.** When ship $A$ is at rest in the CMB rest frame and ship $B$ has peculiar velocity $0.9c$ relative to the CMB rest frame, four asymmetric quantities arise that distinguish the two cases.

### 20.9.2 Theorem 20.9: The Four Cosmological-Asymmetric Quantities

**Theorem 20.9 (CMB-Anchored Cosmological Asymmetry of Lorentz Contraction, Grade 2).** *Let $A$ and $B$ be two ships with peculiar velocities $\vec v_A = 0$ and $\vec v_B = 0.9c\,\hat x$ relative to the CMB rest frame. Both ships have identical rest mass $M$ and rest length $L_0$. Then:*

*(i) The local Lorentz-symmetry of length contraction is preserved: $A$ measures $B$'s length as $L_0/\gamma_B \approx 0.436\, L_0$; $B$ measures $A$'s length as $L_0/\gamma_B \approx 0.436\, L_0$. Each ship in its own rest frame sees the other foreshortened by the same factor.*

*(ii) The cosmological-rest-frame kinetic energy content is asymmetric: $E_{\mathrm{kin}}^{\mathrm{CMB}}(A) = 0$ while $E_{\mathrm{kin}}^{\mathrm{CMB}}(B) = (\gamma_B - 1) M c^2 \approx 1.29\, M c^2$.*

*(iii) The CMB dipole signature is asymmetric: $A$ measures isotropic CMB at $T_0 = 2.725$ K; $B$ measures a CMB dipole with hot pole $T_+ = T_0\sqrt{(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)} \approx 11.88$ K and cold pole $T_- = T_0\sqrt{(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)} \approx 0.625$ K.*

*(iv) The material strain history is asymmetric: ship $A$'s internal structure has never undergone the Bell-mechanism rotation of $K^\mu$ into spatial direction; ship $B$'s internal structure has undergone $K^\mu$-rotation from cosmological-rest alignment to rapidity $\phi_B = \operatorname{arctanh}(0.9) \approx 1.472$ during its history of acceleration to its current peculiar velocity.*

*(v) The $K^\mu$-rotation angle relative to cosmological $\hat x_4$ is asymmetric: ship $A$'s $K_A^\mu$ is aligned with cosmological $\hat x_4$ ($\phi_A = 0$); ship $B$'s $K_B^\mu$ is rotated by rapidity $\phi_B \approx 1.472$ relative to cosmological $\hat x_4$.*

*Proof.* (i) By standard Lorentz contraction in each ship's instantaneous co-moving frame: each sees the other foreshortened by $1/\gamma_B$. This is the *local* Lorentz symmetry preserved by Lemma 6 (McGucken-Invariance) at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$. Each ship's local inertial frame is a valid local inertial frame; the McGucken Sphere expands at rate $c$ in each ship's local frame.

(ii) By standard relativistic kinematics in the CMB rest frame: $E_{\mathrm{kin}} = (\gamma - 1)Mc^2$ with $\gamma$ being the Lorentz factor relative to the CMB rest frame. For $\vec v_A = 0$: $\gamma_A = 1$, $E_{\mathrm{kin}}^{\mathrm{CMB}}(A) = 0$. For $\vec v_B = 0.9c$: $\gamma_B \approx 2.294$, $E_{\mathrm{kin}}^{\mathrm{CMB}}(B) \approx 1.294\, Mc^2$. *This energy is real cosmological-frame content; it is the energy that was supplied to accelerate $B$ from rest to $0.9c$ relative to the CMB.*

(iii) By the relativistic-Doppler analysis of the CMB temperature field. The CMB rest frame measures isotropic temperature $T_0 = 2.725$ K. An observer moving with $\beta = 0.9$ relative to the CMB rest frame sees the temperature field Doppler-shifted in their own frame: $T(\theta) = T_0 \gamma_B^{-1}(1 - \beta\cos\theta)^{-1}$. At the hot pole $\theta = 0$ (direction of motion): $T_+ = T_0\sqrt{(1+\beta)/(1-\beta)} \approx 11.88$ K. At the cold pole $\theta = \pi$ (opposite direction): $T_- = T_0\sqrt{(1-\beta)/(1+\beta)} \approx 0.625$ K. The CMB dipole is real, measurable, and a signature of $B$'s peculiar velocity in the cosmic-comoving frame (cf. Theorem 38(O4) of §20.2.3).

(iv) By Corollary 20.7.1 of §20.7.3 (Universal Bell Strain at High Velocity): every extended material body accelerated from rest to relativistic velocity has every internal element undergoing $K^\mu$-rotation from rest alignment to rapidity $\phi$. Ship $A$ has been at rest in the CMB rest frame throughout its history; its internal elements have $K^\mu$ aligned with cosmological $\hat x_4$; no accumulated Bell-strain. Ship $B$ was accelerated from rest in the CMB rest frame to $\vec v_B = 0.9c$ at some point in its history; during that acceleration, every internal element of $B$ underwent $K^\mu$-rotation from cosmological-$\hat x_4$ alignment to rapidity $\phi_B \approx 1.472$. *The acceleration was either sudden (in which case $B$ fragmented and is not a coherent ship in its current state) or adiabatic (in which case Born-rigidity-approximate equilibration allowed the material to survive, but the rotation occurred).* In the adiabatic case, $B$'s internal structure has the memory of the rotation in its atomic-bond configurations.

(v) Direct application of Theorem 189 of §19.3 (four-velocity rotation by rapidity). Ship $A$ at rest in the CMB rest frame has $u_A^\mu = (c, 0, 0, 0)$ in cosmological coordinates aligned with $\hat x_4$: $K_A^\mu$ is along $\hat x_4$, $\phi_A = 0$. Ship $B$ at $\vec v_B = 0.9c\hat x$ has $u_B^\mu = \gamma_B(c, v, 0, 0)$: $K_B^\mu$ is rotated by rapidity $\phi_B = \operatorname{arctanh}(0.9) \approx 1.472$ from cosmological $\hat x_4$ toward $\hat x$. $\square$

### 20.9.3 The Structural Resolution

The local symmetry (each ship sees the other Lorentz-contracted by $1/\gamma_B$) is preserved by the McGucken framework because $dx_4/dt = ic$ is universal at every event of $\mathcal{M}_G$ (Lemma 6); each ship has its own valid local inertial frame in which the McGucken Sphere expands isotropically at rate $c$. *Local Lorentz invariance holds in the McGucken framework as a theorem*, not a postulate.

The cosmological asymmetry (different kinetic energy, CMB dipole, material strain history, $K^\mu$-rotation angle) is preserved because the cosmological McGucken Sphere expansion has an absolute structural realization: *the CMB rest frame is the unique frame in which the cosmological-Sphere expansion is locally most isotropic*. Ships at relative velocity to this frame have their $K^\mu$ rotated relative to cosmological $\hat x_4$; their cosmological-frame kinetic energy is real; their CMB dipole is real; their material had to absorb real Bell-strain during the acceleration that produced this state. *The McGucken framework holds the local Lorentz symmetry and the cosmological asymmetry simultaneously, with each operating at its own structural level: local Lorentz symmetry at every event by Lemma 6, cosmological asymmetry at the global level by the cosmological McGucken Sphere expansion having an absolute structural realization in the CMB rest frame.*

The rotated-rulers comparison in static $(x, y)$ space shows what *pure projection symmetry* looks like with no moving dimension: each ruler is foreshortened in the other's frame, but no energy difference, no CMB dipole, no material strain, no asymmetric rotation. The two-ships-with-CMB scenario shows what *projection symmetry plus a moving fourth dimension* looks like: locally symmetric in the projections (Lorentz contraction is reciprocal in each local frame), but cosmologically asymmetric in the four observable quantities of Theorem 20.9. *The McGucken framework's $dx_4/dt = ic$ supplies the moving fourth dimension that distinguishes the two cases.*

### 20.9.4 Empirical Consequences

The four cosmological-asymmetric quantities of Theorem 20.9 are all empirically measurable:

(i) **Cosmological kinetic energy** is measurable as the energy required to bring an object from rest in the CMB rest frame to its current peculiar velocity; for the Solar System ($v_\odot \approx 369.82$ km/s), the cosmological kinetic energy per unit mass is $v_\odot^2/2 \approx 6.84 \times 10^{10}$ J/kg, real energy not visible in local mechanics.

(ii) **CMB dipole** is measured continuously by satellite missions: COBE 1990s, WMAP 2003, Planck 2013-2018, all consistent with $v_\odot \approx 369.82$ km/s.

(iii) **Material strain history** is preserved in the internal stress configurations of accelerated bodies; for slowly accelerated bodies (Born-rigid-approximate), the strain is small but non-zero and in principle measurable as a deviation from rest-frame equilibrium.

(iv) **$K^\mu$-rotation angle** is measurable as the rapidity inferred from peculiar velocity via $\phi = \operatorname{arctanh}(v/c)$; for the Solar System, $\phi_\odot \approx 1.23 \times 10^{-3}$ rad, small but non-zero.

All four are *invisible to local reciprocally-calibrated protocols* (by the Cloaking Theorem of §20.3) but *exposed by non-local protocols* (CMB dipole measurement, GPS asymmetry, the McGucken Invariance procedure of §20.5).

## 20.9bis The Even–Odd CMB Parity Asymmetry as a Zero-Parameter Signature of the $+ic$ Orientation, and Comparison with the Direct-Sum (Einstein–Rosen-Bridge) Program

The McGucken Principle asserts that the fourth dimension $x_4$ is expanding at the velocity of light: $dx_4/dt = ic$, with $x_4 = ict$, as a spherically symmetric McGucken Sphere whose wavelength sets the action $h$ and whose volume defines a nonlocality.

The CMB-anchored asymmetry of §20.9 has a second, sharper empirical face: the **even–odd parity asymmetry** of the CMB temperature power spectrum. This subsection shows that the McGucken Principle predicts the *magnitude* of that asymmetry with zero free parameters, and contrasts the resulting one-principle account with the direct-sum (Einstein–Rosen-bridge) program of Gaztañaga, Kumar & Marto (*A new understanding of Einstein–Rosen bridges*, arXiv:2512.20691v2, 2026), which reaches the same observable through a substantially heavier construction.

### 20.9bis.1 The observed anomaly

The CMB temperature field $T(\hat n)$ on the sky expands in spherical harmonics, $T(\hat n) = \sum_{\ell m} a_{\ell m} Y_{\ell m}(\hat n)$. Under the antipodal reflection $\hat n \to -\hat n$ — parity $P$ on the sphere — the harmonics satisfy
$$Y_{\ell m}(-\hat n) = (-1)^{\ell}\, Y_{\ell m}(\hat n),$$
so the **even-$\ell$** multipoles are parity-symmetric and the **odd-$\ell$** multipoles parity-antisymmetric. A statistically parity-symmetric sky (the scale-invariant $\Lambda$CDM baseline) carries equal even and odd power in expectation. The standard parity estimator
$$R_{TT} \;=\; \frac{\sum_{\ell}\ell(\ell+1)\,C_\ell^{\,\text{even}}}{\sum_{\ell}\ell(\ell+1)\,C_\ell^{\,\text{odd}}}$$
therefore has expectation $R_{TT}=1$ under the baseline. The Planck data give $R_{TT}\approx 0.79$ on the largest angular scales ($\ell \lesssim 20\text{–}30$): a real parity asymmetry, with the odd multipoles carrying excess power.

*The two quoted figures reconciled.* The single number $R_{TT}=0.79$ admits two reference readings: the even sector is $1-0.79 = 0.21$ **below** the odd (the "$\sim\!20\%$" stated in prose in the direct-sum paper), while the odd sector is $1/0.79 - 1 = 0.27$ **above** the even. Same $R_{TT}$, two denominators. The reference-independent measure is the modulation amplitude $|1-R_{TT}| \approx 0.21$, with the odd-excess reading giving $0.27$.

### 20.9bis.2 The McGucken prediction: the oriented dimension sets the modulation amplitude

A parity asymmetry on the sky is, by construction, a failure of symmetry under $\hat n \to -\hat n$. The McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework contains exactly one parity-breaking structure, and it fixes the amplitude.

**Assumptions.**

- **(A1)** The primordial fluctuation content rides the four-dimensional McGucken-Sphere wavefront $\mathcal{M}_E(t)$: the three spatial directions $x_1 x_2 x_3$ and the oriented advance $x_4$ along $+ic$.
- **(A2)** Under the antipodal map $\hat n \to -\hat n$ — the spatial realization of the McGucken-Sphere $PT$ operation ([MG-Cogen], §6.6, §7.11) — the three spatial directions are parity-symmetric: the spatial expansion is isotropic and carries no orientation. The single advance $x_4$ carries the $+ic$ orientation, which is the unique parity-breaking element of the structure: by Theorem 4.6.4 of [MG-Cogen], the involution $i \mapsto -i$ is otherwise an exact symmetry, and only the $+ic$ advance selects a direction.
- **(A3)** Equipartition: the four dimensions of the wavefront carry equal shares of the fluctuation power.

**Proposition 20.9bis (Parity-modulation amplitude from the four-velocity budget).** *Under (A1)–(A3), the parity-odd modulation of the CMB temperature power spectrum has fractional amplitude equal to the oriented dimension's share of the four-dimensional budget,*
$$\delta_P \;=\; \tfrac14 \;=\; 0.25,$$
*appearing as a sign-alternating modulation*
$$C_\ell \;=\; C_\ell^{\,\text{baseline}}\big[\,1 + (-1)^{\ell+1}\,\delta_P\,\big],$$
*which suppresses even-$\ell$ and enhances odd-$\ell$ power, yielding a predicted even–odd imbalance $|1 - R_{TT}| \approx \delta_P = 0.25$.*

*Proof.* The parity-symmetric baseline has $C_\ell^{\text{even}} = C_\ell^{\text{odd}}$ in expectation, i.e. no modulation. By (A2) the only structure that breaks the antipodal symmetry is the $+ic$ orientation carried by $x_4$; the three spatial directions contribute solely to the parity-symmetric (even) sector. The parity-**odd** sector is therefore sourced by the oriented dimension alone, and by (A3) its weight in the four-dimensional fluctuation budget is $1/4$. Hence the fractional amplitude of the parity-odd modulation is $\delta_P = 1/4$, carried with the sign $(-1)^{\ell+1}$ because the odd-$\ell$ multipoles constitute the parity-odd sector. The even–odd imbalance is then $|1-R_{TT}| = \delta_P = 1/4$. $\square$

*Comparison with observation.* Planck at $\ell \lesssim 20\text{–}30$ gives $|1-R_{TT}| \in [0.21,\,0.27]$ across the even-deficit and odd-excess readings. The prediction $\delta_P = 0.25$ brackets both, with **zero free parameters**: the value $1/4$ is fixed entirely by the count of one oriented dimension among four.

*Status and the completing calculation.* Proposition 20.9bis fixes the *amplitude* of the modulation from the dimensional budget. Its *$\ell$-dependence* — the envelope of $\delta_P(\ell)$ across multipoles — requires projecting the $x_4$-oriented source onto the spherical-harmonic basis on the last-scattering sphere via the line-of-sight integral against the radiation transfer function. That projection is the analog of the direct-sum program's Hankel-function modulation (their Eqs. 172, 179); Proposition 20.9bis supplies its overall scale, $1/4$, as a parameter-free prediction, and the multipole envelope is the completing calculation, left open here.

### 20.9bis.3 Model content compared with the direct-sum (ER-bridge) program

The direct-sum program reaches the *same* observable — the $(-1)^{\ell+1}$ even–odd modulation — through the following construction (Gaztañaga, Kumar & Marto 2026): (i) a doubled Hilbert space $\mathcal{H} = \mathcal{H}_+ \oplus \mathcal{H}_-$ carrying two arrows of time (their Eqs. 94–96); (ii) an inflaton field with potential and slow-roll parameters $\epsilon,\eta$; (iii) a $PT$-asymmetric quasi-de Sitter vacuum $|0\rangle_{q\text{dS}}$ obtained by breaking $\tau \to -\tau$ in the vacuum (their Eqs. 174–175); (iv) the resulting modulation $C_\ell^{\text{DSI}} = C_\ell^{\text{SI}}[1+(-1)^{\ell+1}\Delta C_\ell]$ with $\Delta P_v \propto (1-n_s)$ (their Eqs. 191, 179), reaching a $650\times$ posterior-odds improvement over scale-invariant inflation (their Table 2).

The McGucken account obtains the identical modulation from $dx_4/dt = ic$ alone. The difference is the ingredient count:

| Ingredient | Direct-sum (ER-bridge) program | McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ |
|---|---|---|
| Arrow of time | Two ($\mathcal{H}_+ \oplus \mathcal{H}_-$), kept symmetric, then broken in the vacuum | One: the $+ic$ orientation (derived) |
| Source of parity asymmetry | $PT$-asymmetric quasi-dS vacuum imposed ($\tau\to-\tau$ broken by hand) | $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$ (the Principle's component (iii)) |
| Auxiliary structure | inflaton field + potential, slow-roll $\epsilon,\eta$, doubled vacuum | none beyond $dx_4/dt=ic$ |
| Amplitude of asymmetry | fitted through $\Delta P_v \propto (1-n_s)$ | predicted $\delta_P = 1/4$, zero parameters |
| Nonlocality | inherited from standard QM (ER=EPR realized, not derived) | derived in-paper (§6.0.10, §6.3.10.5; formalized [MG-Cogen], Cor. 6.6.7.5) |

Both target the same Planck data. The direct-sum program assembles a doubled Hilbert space, an inflaton sector, and a hand-broken vacuum; the McGucken $dx_4/dt = ic$ framework uses one oriented advance and a dimensional count.

### 20.9bis.4 Nonlocality: assumed there, derived here

The direct-sum program is *built on* entanglement across horizons — its realization of ER=EPR through geometric superselection sectors (their §6.2.1, Table 1). But the nonlocality is **inherited** from standard quantum mechanics: the direct-sum reorganizes where the entanglement is housed; it does not generate it from the construction. This is precisely the defect the present textbook diagnoses in the orthodox formulation at §6.3.10.5 — *quantum non-locality forced into the formulation by hand, with no source in the formalism* — where general relativity and quantum mechanics, as there noted, "do not share a foundational source for their respective structural commitments."

The present framework supplies that source in-paper: the same $dx_4/dt = ic$ that fixes the arrow (§6.3.10.7) and sets the parity-asymmetry amplitude (§20.9bis.2) **generates** the nonlocality — *derivation, not postulate* (§6.3.10.5). The mechanism is the dual-channel crystallisation of §6.0.10,

> *Relativity is $x_4$'s nonlocality, read along the Algebraic Channel; $x_4$'s nonlocality is relativity's null structure, read along the Geometric Channel.*

The Bell-test correlations live on the null surface $\mathcal{N}_{E} = \{\,p : ds^2(E,p)=0\,\}$, and that null surface *is* the McGucken Sphere — the integrated history of $x_4$'s expansion at $c$ from $E$ (§6.0.3–6.0.4, §6.3.10.6), so that $(ict)^2 = -c^2 t^2$ is what supplies the null vectors in the first place. The empirical record — Aspect 1982, Hensen et al. 2015, the Big Bell Test 2018 — is then one fact in two registers, and the Disjunctive Forcing Theorem (Theorem 26, §6.1.5) closes the case-exhaustion: every alternative to $dx_4/dt = ic$ violates either the Algebraic-Channel null structure or the Geometric-Channel expansion. The companion paper formalizes the identical chain as $\text{Born rule} \Leftarrow \text{nonlocal coupling} \Leftarrow \text{Lorentzian null structure} \Leftarrow dx_4/dt = ic$ ([MG-Cogen], Cor. 6.6.7.5). Either way, the nonlocality the direct-sum program presupposes is a downstream theorem of the same principle that predicts the parity asymmetry.

### 20.9bis.5 Synthesis

One oriented advance does three things for which the direct-sum program requires three separate constructions. The $+ic$ orientation of $x_4$ (a) fixes a single arrow of time, removing the need for a doubled Hilbert space; (b) predicts the CMB even–odd parity-asymmetry amplitude at $\delta_P = 1/4$ with zero free parameters, removing the need for a $PT$-asymmetric vacuum and a slow-roll fit; and (c) generates, via the Lorentzian null structure of the McGucken Sphere (§6.0.10, §6.3.10.5), the quantum nonlocality on which the program's entanglement architecture rests, removing the need to borrow it from standard quantum mechanics.
